DW-B28-02 P1 Cancel, Trim, and Flatten buttons are silent no-ops when no rule is applied.

Root cause (HIGH confidence — code audit 2026-07-16):
Trim(Instrument), Flatten(Instrument), and CancelPendingEntries(Instrument) all route through AllAccounts(instrument) → FindRule(instrument).
FindRule returns null when _rules is empty or has no entry matching instrument.FullName.
AllAccounts immediately yield break on null rule → the foreach loop iterates zero accounts.
No order is submitted, no error is raised, no StatusUpdate message fires.

Reproduction (Director session 2026-07-16):
Both panels showed "COPY OFF". "Apply Rule" had NOT been clicked. _rules was empty. Every button click executed zero account iterations silently.

Proposed fix — two options:
Option A (preferred — direct account path for UI buttons): Add a leader-account overload to Trim, Flatten, and CancelPendingEntries that accepts Account leader as the first argument. The panel passes _leaderAccount. The engine operates on the leader directly without requiring a rule entry. This mirrors the BreakEven(Account leader, Instrument, int) pattern already established at CopyEngine.cs:1216.
Panel call sites change from: _engine.Trim(_instrument) to _engine.Trim(_leaderAccount, _instrument).
Engine new overloads: operate on leader directly, then optionally fan-out via AllAccounts for followers (if rule exists).
Option B (guard + warning): Add a guard at the top of Trim/Flatten/Cancel: if AllAccounts returns empty, emit StatusUpdate("No rule applied — apply rule first"). This surfaces the problem immediately without changing the architecture. Does NOT fix the underlying gap (buttons still don't act on leader-only sessions).

Director decision required: Option A or B?
Option A requires 3 new engine overloads + 3 panel call site changes = ~30 lines.
Option B requires 3 guard additions = ~9 lines. Simpler but incomplete. 		CLOSED — leader-direct overloads shipped in B28 Lane B. F5 GREEN 2026-07-16.

Step 2 — CopyEngine.cs: add three leader-account overloads (after existing Flatten at ~L928):

// B28 T2 -- Trim(Account,Instrument): leader-direct + follower fan-out.
// CYC=4: null(1), leader direct, foreach(2), leader skip(3), TrimOneAccount(4).
// JS-021: no lock. Mirrors BreakEven(Account,Instrument,int) at L1216.
internal void Trim(Account leader, Instrument instrument)
{
    if (leader == null) { Trim(instrument); return; }
    TrimOneAccount(leader, instrument);
    foreach (var acc in AllAccounts(instrument))
    {
        if (acc == leader) continue;
        TrimOneAccount(acc, instrument);
    }
}

// B28 T2 -- Flatten(Account,Instrument): same pattern. CYC=4.
internal void Flatten(Account leader, Instrument instrument)
{
    if (leader == null) { Flatten(instrument); return; }
    FlattenOneAccount(leader, instrument);
    foreach (var acc in AllAccounts(instrument))
    {
        if (acc == leader) continue;
        FlattenOneAccount(acc, instrument);
    }
}

// B28 T2 -- CancelPendingEntries(Account,Instrument): same pattern. CYC=4.
internal void CancelPendingEntries(Account leader, Instrument instrument)
{
    if (leader == null) { CancelPendingEntries(instrument); return; }
    CancelOneAccount(leader, instrument);
    foreach (var acc in AllAccounts(instrument))
    {
        if (acc == leader) continue;
        CancelOneAccount(acc, instrument);
    }
}

// B28 T2 -- Trim(Account,Instrument,int,double,double): leader-direct 4-arg.
// CYC=5: null(1), ask/bid guard(2), leader direct, foreach(3), leader skip(4), TrimOneAccount(5).
internal void Trim(Account leader, Instrument instrument, int exitBuffer, double ask, double bid)
{
    if (leader == null) { Trim(instrument, exitBuffer, ask, bid); return; }
    if (ask <= 0 || bid <= 0 || exitBuffer == 0) { Trim(leader, instrument); return; }
    TrimOneAccountLimit(leader, instrument, exitBuffer, ask, bid);
    foreach (var acc in AllAccounts(instrument))
    {
        if (acc == leader) continue;
        TrimOneAccountLimit(acc, instrument, exitBuffer, ask, bid);
    }
}

// B28 T2 -- Flatten(Account,Instrument,int,double,double): same. CYC=5.
internal void Flatten(Account leader, Instrument instrument, int exitBuffer, double ask, double bid)
{
    if (leader == null) { Flatten(instrument, exitBuffer, ask, bid); return; }
    if (ask <= 0 || bid <= 0 || exitBuffer == 0) { Flatten(leader, instrument); return; }
    FlattenOneAccountLimit(leader, instrument, exitBuffer, ask, bid);
    foreach (var acc in AllAccounts(instrument))
    {
        if (acc == leader) continue;
        FlattenOneAccountLimit(acc, instrument, exitBuffer, ask, bid);
    }
}

DW-B31-01 P0 BE button kills ATM bracket — cancel+replace destroys OCO link.
B29 introduced acc.Cancel() + acc.CreateOrder() as a workaround for the silent acc.Change() failure on ATM stops. This cancels the ATM-owned stop, severs the OCO link, and orphans the ATM targets. The ATM's built-in trail and auto-BE are also destroyed.

Root cause: B29 used the wrong acc.Change() overload (account-level multi-param), which NT8 silently rejects for ATM-owned orders. The correct call is the same property-set + single-array pattern already used by SyncFollowerBracket: order.StopPrice = newStop; acc.Change(new Order[] { order });

wrapped in try/catch (JS-001). StatusUpdate messages updated to reflect in-place move.

Same substitution — replace TryCreateStopWithRetry(...) call with:

● Block 33  ·  PTT-COPIER-B33  ·  Modular Independence Architecture  ·  ✓ COMPLETE
B33 implements the PttBus + IPttModule architecture approved by Director on 2026-07-19. Each feature (BE, Trim, Flatten, Cancel, Copier) becomes a fully independent module — usable standalone, sold separately, and compatible when combined. The copier is no longer required for BE to function. Three architect subagents reviewed and converged on the same design (2026-07-19).
B33 ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS — LOCKED (2026-07-19)
  • PttBus (static event hub): BE fires PttBus.BeFired after submitting the OCO bracket-replace (PTT-BE-Stop + PTT-BE-Target-N) and cancelling the ATM bracket. Copier subscribes and fans out to followers. Neither module imports the other. No lock() — subscription always on UI thread during Initialize().
  • IPttModule interface: Every feature implements IPttModule (ModuleId, IsEnabled, Initialize, Teardown). Panel holds List<IPttModule> only — no concrete feature types. Adding/removing a feature = one AddModule() line.
  • Two-layer activation: Layer 1 = NT8 Properties (bool IsBeLicensed etc.) — hides button entirely. Layer 2 = runtime toggle buttons on panel face — instant on/off mid-session. No indicator reload required.
  • Hot potato stays: PTT submits a fresh OCO bracket (PTT-BE-Stop + PTT-BE-Target-N) via CreateOrder and cancels the ATM bracket, fires PttBus.BeFired, then is done. PTT owns the replacement orders; no PTT trail, no trailing-stop sync. (B35 bracket-replace confirmed live PA 2026-07-24.)
  • ATM constraint respected: Stop\d+ filter (DW-B32-07) stays in all feature modules. PTT can only move PTT-created stops. ATM-owned stops managed by NT8 ATM template BE logic.
  • Standalone BE path (B35 bracket-replace): PttBreakEven.Execute() calls SubmitBeStop(leader,...) directly — CancelStaleBrackets() first, then OCO group with stop + targets. No FindRule(). Followers reached only via PttBus subscription in PttCopier. (DW-B36-01 fix: Execute() must loop AllAccounts() — see B36.)
  • JS-021 compliant: No lock() anywhere. PttBus uses CLR events subscribed/unsubscribed on UI thread only.
  • CYC ≤ 8: Each module method: null guard (1) + IsEnabled check (1) + position check (1) + long/short branch (1) = CYC 4 max per method.

▶ APPROVED APPROACH — NEW-STOP BE (DW-B33-01)
Instead of moving the existing ATM-owned stop (blocked by NT8-046), submit a new independent StopMarket order at the BE price via account.CreateOrder(). The ATM stop remains live. When the new BE stop fills, NT8 sees position = 0 and auto-cancels the ATM stop. If anything else closes the position first, the orphan cancel guard cancels the pending BE stop immediately.
Runtime flow
── Normal case (BE fires, position closes clean) ────────────────────────
Long 1 MES @ 5000.00  |  ATM Stop1 @ 4998.00
User arms BE (buffer = 0 ticks)
Price dips to 4999.00 → engine armed, waiting
Price recovers → crosses 5000.00
  SubmitBeStop() fires:
    CreateOrder(instrument, Sell, StopMarket, 5000.00, qty=1, "PTT-BE")
    _pendingBeStop = submitted order
Now live: ATM Stop1 @ 4998.00  +  PTT-BE Stop @ 5000.00
Price ticks down to 5000.00:
  PTT-BE Stop fills → position = 0
  ATM engine detects flat → cancels Stop1 automatically ✅

── Orphan case (position closed by something else first) ────────────────
User manually flattens  OR  ATM Stop1 hits first (fast market)
  OnPositionUpdate fires: position.Quantity == 0
  OrphanCancelGuard():
    if (_pendingBeStop != null && _pendingBeStop.OrderState == Working)
      account.Cancel(new[] { _pendingBeStop })  ← cancels orphan immediately
    _pendingBeStop = null

B33 live-test bug (2026-07-20): Original pseudocode passed args in wrong order: (type, signalName, modifier, bePrice, 0, qty). NT8 accepted silently — order appeared with Limit=0, Stop not set, qty=13 (all accounts summed), account=Sim102 (wrong).
Three fixes applied (NT8-049): (1) arg order corrected to NT8-007 spec: (instr, action, type, OrderEntry.Manual, TimeInForce.Day, qty, 0, bePrice, "", "PTT-BE-Stop", DateTime.MaxValue, (CustomOrder)null) (2) acc must be leader account only -- not iterated (3) qty from leaderAcc.Positions[instr].Quantity -- not passed in from outer loop 
// NT8-007 confirmed arg order (12 args, zero-indexed):
//  0  Instrument      instr
//  1  OrderAction     action        (Sell or BuyToCover)
//  2  OrderType       type          (StopMarket)
//  3  OrderEntry      entry         (OrderEntry.Manual)
//  4  TimeInForce     tif           (TimeInForce.Day)
//  5  int             quantity
//  6  double          limitPrice    (0 for StopMarket -- NOT the stop price)
//  7  double          stopPrice     (bePrice goes here)
//  8  string          oco           ("")
//  9  string          signalName    ("PTT-BE-Stop")
// 10  DateTime        gtd           (DateTime.MaxValue)
// 11  CustomOrder     customOrder   ((NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null)

private void SubmitBeStop(Account leaderAcc, Instrument instr, double bePrice)
{
    // Read qty from leader's own live position -- never passed in from outer loop
    var pos = leaderAcc.Positions[instr];
    if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) return;  // Guard: flat

    // Guard: no duplicate pending BE stop already working
    if (_pendingBeStop != null && _pendingBeStop.OrderState == OrderState.Working) return;

    var direction = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long
        ? OrderAction.Sell
        : OrderAction.BuyToCover;

    // NT8-007: limitPrice=0 at arg6, stopPrice=bePrice at arg7
    _pendingBeStop = leaderAcc.CreateOrder(
        instr, direction, OrderType.StopMarket, OrderEntry.Manual,
        TimeInForce.Day, pos.Quantity,
        0,        // arg6: limitPrice -- MUST be 0 for StopMarket
        bePrice,  // arg7: stopPrice  -- bePrice goes HERE, not arg6
        "", "PTT-BE-Stop", DateTime.MaxValue,
        (NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null);

    leaderAcc.Submit(new[] { _pendingBeStop });
    Print($"[BE] SubmitBeStop {direction} {pos.Quantity} @ {bePrice:F2}");
}

private void OrphanCancelGuard(Account leaderAcc, Instrument instr)
{
    if (_pendingBeStop == null) return;
    if (_pendingBeStop.OrderState != OrderState.Working) { _pendingBeStop = null; return; }
    leaderAcc.Cancel(new[] { _pendingBeStop });
    _pendingBeStop = null;
    Print("[BE] OrphanCancelGuard fired -- PTT-BE-Stop cancelled");
}

Manual flatten before BE fires OnPositionUpdate qty==0 → OrphanCancelGuard ✓ PTT-BE stop cancelled immediately
ATM Stop1 fills first (fast market) OnPositionUpdate qty==0 → OrphanCancelGuard ✓ PTT-BE stop cancelled. No reverse position.
BE button clicked twice _pendingBeStop != null guard in SubmitBeStop ✓ Second call is no-op. One stop only.
Position already flat when BE arms Positions[instr].Quantity==0 guard ✓ Early return. No order submitted.
Short position MarketPosition == Short → BuyToCover ✓ Direction auto-detected from position.

BUG-B33-02 fix — CancelStaleBrackets (new helper, insert after OrphanCancelGuard)
// B33 BUG-B33-02: cancel ATM bracket orders that remain Working after PTT-BE fills.
// NT8 ATM engine auto-cancels on real brokers; internal sim (Sim101/Sim102) does NOT.
// Called from TryFirePositionState when !hasPos (after OrphanCancelGuard).
// JS-021: no lock -- acc.Cancel is NT8 API call. CYC=3: null guard(1), Where(2), Count==0(3).
private void CancelStaleBrackets(Account leaderAcc, Instrument instr)
{
    if (leaderAcc == null || instr == null) return;   // (1) null guard
    var stale = leaderAcc.Orders
        .Where(o => o.Instrument?.FullName == instr.FullName  // null-safe per NT8-043
                 && (o.OrderState == OrderState.Working
                     || o.OrderState == OrderState.Accepted)
                 && o.Name != "PTT-BE-Stop")   // don't cancel our own stop
        .ToList();                                             // (2) filter
    if (stale.Count == 0) return;                           // (3) empty guard
    leaderAcc.Cancel(stale);
    NinjaTrader.Code.Output.Process(
        "[BE] CancelStaleBrackets: cancelled " + stale.Count + " bracket orders",
        PrintTo.OutputTab1);
}

// Hook site in TryFirePositionState (after OrphanCancelGuard call at line ~741):
// BEFORE:
if (!hasPos)
    OrphanCancelGuard(e.Order.Account, e.Order.Instrument);

// AFTER:
if (!hasPos)
{
    OrphanCancelGuard(e.Order.Account, e.Order.Instrument);        // cancel PTT-BE stop
    CancelStaleBrackets(e.Order.Account, e.Order.Instrument);      // cancel ATM brackets
}

private volatile Order _pendingBeStop = null;

// JS-021: ConcurrentDictionary TryGetValue/TryRemove are lock-free (no volatile needed)
// NT8-003: ConcurrentDictionary provides memory barrier -- volatile banned on non-primitives anyway
private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, Order> _pendingBeStop
    = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, Order>();

leaderAcc.Submit(new[] { _pendingBeStop });
// AFTER:

_pendingBeStop[leaderAcc.Name] = beStop;

ID Priority Bug + Evidence
DW-B33-05 P0 Wrong action direction on short accounts. Sim102 (Short) received Action='Sell' PTT-BE-Stop — same direction as its short position. Filled 13 more Sell → position doubled to 26 Short instead of being protected. For short accounts, PTT-BE-Stop must be Action='Buy to cover'.
Root cause: SubmitBeStopLocal derives action from a hard-coded direction or from the leader's MarketPosition, not from acc.MarketPosition per account.
Fix: isLong = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long per account in the loop — then Action = isLong ? OrderAction.Sell : OrderAction.BuyToCover.
DW-B33-06 P0 BE price uses leader fill for all accounts. Both PTT-BE-Stop orders landed at 7501.50 (Sim101's fill price). Sim102 fill was 7501.25 — its PTT-BE-Stop should be 7501.25 − 0.25 (short, buffer −1 tick) = 7501.00. Instead it received 7501.50 — 1 tick higher than its entry, immediately inside the money on a short.
Root cause: pos.AveragePrice or bePrice is computed once (for leader) and reused in the loop — not re-read from FindPositionLocal(acc, instr) per iteration.
Fix: Compute pos = FindPositionLocal(acc, instr) inside the AllAccounts loop per account. Buffer sign must flip: Long → +N ticks, Short → −N ticks.
DW-B33-07 P0 OCO targets not submitted for Sim101 (leader). Sim101 PTT-BE-Stop: Oco='' — no PTT-BE-Target-1/2 submitted. Sim102 correctly received PTT-BE-Target-1 (qty=6 @ 7498.75) + PTT-BE-Target-2 (qty=7 @ 7498.25) OCO'd together. Sim101's ATM targets were cancelled but never replaced — no take-profit protection after BE on the leader.
Root cause: SnapshotTargets / target resubmit path in SubmitBeStopLocal runs for follower accounts but not for the leader, OR the leader's target orders were not present in the snapshot at the time of cancel (timing race).
Fix: Verify SnapshotTargets(acc, instr) is called BEFORE CancelStaleBrackets for every account in the loop, and that target resubmit runs for the leader account identity explicitly.

Q2: What Can "Custom Orders" Actually Define?
NT8's Custom orders section (Tools → Hot Keys → Order Entry → Custom orders → Add) lets you define a named order with these parameters:
Parameter Options Notes
Instrument Current chart instrument (default) Uses whatever is on the active chart. This is what we want — works on any instrument without re-configuring.
Action Buy · Sell · BuyToCover · SellShort Direction must be specified. No "close position" option — you must know if you're long or short when defining the order. One key per direction needed.
Order type Market · Limit · StopMarket · StopLimit Limit is available ✓
Quantity Fixed integer (e.g., 2) FIXED ONLY. No formula. No position-relative sizing. Cannot compute ceil(N/2) dynamically. If Director always trades 4 contracts → Trim qty = 2 (hardcoded). Works. If size varies → this approach breaks silently (submits wrong qty).
Price (for Limit) Ask · Bid · Last · Fixed price Ask and Bid ARE supported as dynamic price types. "Sell Limit at Ask" = you become the offer; filled immediately by buyers at that price. "Buy Limit at Bid" = you become the bid; filled immediately by sellers. This IS the "free tick" behavior. NT8 Custom Orders can do limit@ask/bid. ✓
Accounts Active chart account only Single account — the account selected in ChartTrader. Does NOT fire across follower accounts simultaneously. For multi-account use, PTT button is required.
OPEN QUESTION for Director (blocks Trim + Flatten hotkey design):

If YES: Custom Orders can define Trim as a fixed-qty sell limit at ask. Works today. Zero code.
If NO (variable size): Trim requires PTT code to compute ceil(N/2) dynamically. Custom orders will submit wrong qty on non-standard entries.
MULTI-ACCOUNT LIMITATION (fundamental):
NT8 Custom orders fires on the active chart's account only. If Director has Sim101 + Sim102 (or Live + Sim), a custom orders hotkey presses on the Sim101 chart will NOT affect Sim102. For multi-account Trim/Flatten, PTT TrimEngine + FlattenEngine (code path) is the only solution.

NT8 CUSTOM ORDERS: LONG vs SHORT DIRECTION PROBLEM
NT8 custom orders require you to specify the ORDER ACTION (Buy or Sell) at define-time. There is no "opposite of current position" option. This means you need TWO custom orders for each action: one for when long (Sell) and one for when short (BuyToCover). If you press the wrong direction key (e.g., Sell when already flat or short), NT8 opens a NEW SHORT position — dangerous.
Mitigation: Assign Trim-Long and Trim-Short to DIFFERENT keys (e.g., Numpad1 for Long trim, Numpad4 for Short trim). Know your position direction before pressing. PTT TrimEngine handles this automatically (position-aware direction detection).

A2 — Auto Direction Detection: NEEDS CLARIFICATION
Director asks: will the Custom Order key know to use Sell Ask vs Buy Bid based on entry direction automatically?

Answer: NO for NT8 Custom Orders. Custom orders require the ORDER ACTION (Buy/Sell/BuyToCover/SellShort) to be hardcoded at define-time. NT8 does NOT auto-flip the direction based on position. If you define "Sell · Limit · Ask · 3" and press it while short, NT8 adds to the short — it doesn't treat it as a cover.

Three paths to solve this:
Path A — Two-key per qty Define pairs: key 4 = Sell@Ask·3 (Long trim), key Shift+4 or separate numpad = BuyToCover@Bid·3 (Short trim). Director uses the correct key based on direction. Zero code. Risk: wrong key = new position. Zero code
Path B — TrimEngine code TrimEngine.cs reads pos.MarketPosition (Long → Sell Limit@Ask, Short → BuyToCover Limit@Bid). Auto-detects direction. One key, always correct. Same pattern as BeEngine direction detection. This is the fully correct solution. Planned B34+. Needs code (B34+)
Path C — NT8 "Buy Bid/Sell Ask"
ChartTrader buttons		 NT8's ChartTrader has native "Sell Ask" and "Buy Bid" buttons. These ARE direction-neutral in the sense that they just submit at the current ask/bid without caring about position. They do NOT auto-detect direction — they are always Buy or always Sell. Same problem. Same limitation
ARCH DECISION A2: For zero-code bridge: use Path A (two keys per qty level — one for Long, one for Short). For permanent solution: TrimEngine (B34+) with auto direction detection. Key ladder becomes: Numpad1-6 = Long trim qty 1–6, Numpad7-9+0 = Short cover qty 1–4 (or separate key rows).

Director idea: use keys 4–9 for different contract counts. Each key = a specific fixed qty. Since direction cannot be auto-detected by Custom Orders, each qty needs TWO entries — one for Long exit (Sell Limit@Ask) and one for Short cover (BuyToCover Limit@Bid).

Simplest zero-code layout using number row + modifier:
Key (Long / short) Action (Long exit) Action (Short cover) Qty Use case
4 / Alt+4 Sell · Limit · Ask BuyToCover · Limit · Bid 1 Exit/trim 1 contract
5 / Alt+5 Sell · Limit · Ask BuyToCover · Limit · Bid 2 Exit/trim 2 contracts (half of SL4)
6 / Alt+6 Sell · Limit · Ask BuyToCover · Limit · Bid 3 Exit/trim 3 contracts (half of SL6)
7 / Alt+7 Sell · Limit · Ask BuyToCover · Limit · Bid 4 Exit/trim 4 contracts (half of SL8 / full SL4)
8 / Alt+8 Sell · Limit · Ask BuyToCover · Limit · Bid 5 Exit/trim 5 contracts (half of SL10)
9 / Alt+9 Sell · Limit · Ask BuyToCover · Limit · Bid 6 Exit/trim 6 contracts (half of SL12+ or full SL6)
DANGER WARNING — Direction keys must be different. Key 5 = Sell 2 contracts. If pressed while FLAT or SHORT → NT8 opens or adds to a SHORT position (2-contract short entry). This is NOT a cover. The plain number keys should ONLY be pressed when Long. Alt+number (or a separate key row) ONLY when Short. If confused, press Esc immediately (Close position = market flatten, guaranteed).

Mitigation: The TrimEngine code path (B34+) eliminates this entirely — it reads pos.MarketPosition before submitting and always picks the correct direction. The key-ladder is a temporary zero-code bridge only.

HOW THE QTY FIELD REPLACES THE KEY-LADDER
"Sell ask" and "Buy bid" native actions submit whatever qty is in the ChartTrader quantity field at press time.
So the workflow for a Trim is:
  1. Look at your position size (e.g., Long 6 via SL6 ATM)
  2. Type 3 in the ChartTrader qty field (half of 6)
  3. Press Ctrl+Shift+S → Sell Limit @ Ask · 3 contracts fires
  4. Position reduces to Long 3. ATM bracket still shows original size — cancel or adjust manually.
This is exactly the same ergonomics as typing the qty before any order in ChartTrader. No key-ladder needed. No Custom Orders needed. The qty field IS the variable-qty selector.

Direction caveat still applies: "Sell ask" is always a Sell. If you're Short and press it, you add to Short. For Short positions, use Ctrl+Shift+B (Buy bid = Buy Limit @ Bid = cover at bid price). The permanent solution remains TrimEngine code (B34+) which auto-detects direction.

NT8 Warning: "All hot keys are inactive when a modal form has focus."
NT8 shows this warning when the Hot Keys dialog (or any modal/dialog box) is open and has focus. All hotkeys are globally disabled whenever any NT8 modal dialog has focus. This means pressing Ctrl+B or Ctrl+Z while the Hot Keys settings window is open will do nothing — the keystrokes are swallowed by the dialog, not the chart.

Fix: Close the dialog (click OK) → click the chart window → hotkeys are active again.
Live trading rule: If you accidentally open any NT8 dialog during a trade, hotkeys are dead until you dismiss the dialog and click the chart to return focus. This is a NT8 architectural constraint — cannot be changed. Must be aware of it.
NT8 Rule documented: NT8-052
All NT8 Order Entry hotkeys are globally suspended whenever a modal form (dialog, settings window, order entry popup) has WPF focus. Hotkeys resume only after the modal is dismissed and a chart window regains focus. No workaround from AddOn — this is baked into NT8's keyboard routing at the application level.

Order Entry Hotkeys: Ctrl+B / Ctrl+Z CONFIRMED NOT FIRING — Focus Problem
Director confirmed: pressed Ctrl+B and Ctrl+Z with chart focused and dialog closed — neither fired. Root cause: Order Entry category hotkeys require the ChartTrader order entry sub-panel to have WPF keyboard focus — specifically the panel containing the qty field and Buy/Sell buttons. Clicking the chart canvas gives the Chart context focus, not the Order Entry sub-panel. These are distinct WPF focus targets inside the same window.

Practical impact: During live trading you cannot reliably pre-focus the ChartTrader sub-panel before pressing a panic key. This makes Order Entry category hotkeys unsafe for time-critical actions.

Conclusion: Order Entry category hotkeys (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+Z) are NOT suitable for live trading panic actions without a code-based solution. The only zero-code hotkeys that are reliable for trading are in the Global category — they fire regardless of which window or sub-panel has focus.
Global Category — What's Available (from screenshot)
Flatten everything Orders section. Closes ALL positions on ALL instruments across ALL accounts. Nuclear button. Unassigned. Fires globally — no focus required.
Cancel all orders Orders section. Cancels all working orders globally. Unassigned.
Breakeven ATM strategy NOT present in Global category. Only available under Order Entry. Cannot be made a global zero-code hotkey.
NT8 Rule documented: NT8-053
"Breakeven ATM strategy" is only available under the Order Entry hotkey category. It is NOT available in Global. There is no zero-code way to fire BE from a reliable global hotkey. A code-based solution (PreviewKeyDown wired at the chart window level) is required for a reliable BE keyboard shortcut.

Decision Required — Two Paths
Action Zero-code option Caveat Code option
Flatten (panic) Global "Flatten everything" — assign any Ctrl/Shift/Alt combo. Fires everywhere. Kills ALL positions on ALL instruments. If only one chart active at a time → fine. Multi-instrument → dangerous. FlattenEngine (B34+) — scoped to one instrument, fires across N accounts
Breakeven No reliable zero-code option. Order Entry category requires ChartTrader sub-panel focus — unreliable in practice. Not available in Global. Use PTT button (mouse click) until code solution. ⚠ "Flatten everything" — Full Scope Warning
Global "Flatten everything" is the most powerful destructive action in NT8's hotkey system. One keypress closes every open position on every instrument on every account simultaneously — MES, MGC, NQ, Gold, everything.
When it is safe: Director trades one instrument at a time, one account per session. In that scenario "Flatten everything" = "flatten my one position" and is safe.
When it is dangerous: Two charts open, both in a trade (e.g., MES long Sim101 + MGC short Sim102). Pressing the key exits both simultaneously — no recovery.

Recommendation: Assign to a deliberately inconvenient key combo (e.g., Ctrl+Alt+Z — requires three fingers) to prevent accidental fire. Do NOT use Ctrl+Z (undo muscle memory).
New ticket: DW-B33-HK-03 — PreviewKeyDown BE keyboard shortcut
Wire chart.PreviewKeyDown in the PTT AddOn to intercept a configurable key combo and call BeEngine.Arm() or SubmitBeStop(). PreviewKeyDown fires at the chart window level before WPF routing — no sub-panel focus required, works regardless of which element has focus inside the chart window. This is the only reliable zero-code-free keyboard BE path. Scope: B33 Phase 2 or standalone ticket after Phase 1b closes.
Key suggestion: Ctrl+Shift+B (three fingers = deliberate, not accidental). Fallback: F-key (F9, F10) which fire at OS level and cannot be intercepted by NT8.

Key pseudocode — SnapshotTargets + SubmitBeStop changes
// C1: SnapshotTargets -- reads ATM Target orders before cancel.
// CYC=3: null guard(1), foreach(2), IsAtmTargetName filter(3).
// NT8-014: signal names start "PTT-". NT8-006: requires System.Linq.
// JS-021: no lock. JS-002: returns empty list, never null.
private List<(double Price, int Qty, OrderAction Action)> SnapshotTargets(
    Account leaderAcc, Instrument instr)
{
    var result = new List<(double, int, OrderAction)>();
    if (leaderAcc == null || instr == null) return result;  // (1)
    foreach (var o in leaderAcc.Orders.ToList())              // (2)
    {
        if (o.Instrument?.FullName != instr.FullName) continue;
        if (o.OrderState != OrderState.Working
            && o.OrderState != OrderState.Accepted) continue;
        if (!IsAtmTargetName(o.Name)) continue;              // (3)
        result.Add((o.LimitPrice, o.Quantity, o.OrderAction));
        NinjaTrader.Code.Output.Process(
            "[BE] Snapshot target: " + o.Name
            + " " + o.OrderAction + " " + o.Quantity + " @ " + o.LimitPrice.ToString("F2"),
            PrintTo.OutputTab1);
    }
    return result;
}

// C2: IsAtmTargetName -- target-only slot detection.
// CYC=2: null/short guard(1), Target prefix + digit check(2).
internal static bool IsAtmTargetName(string name)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(name) || name.Length < 7) return false;  // (1)
    return name.StartsWith("Target", StringComparison.Ordinal)
           && char.IsDigit(name[6]);                                   // (2)
}

// C3: additions inside SubmitBeStop try-block, after existing beStop submission.
// Step 1: snapshot already done BEFORE cancel (see full method below).
// Steps 3–6 inside the try block:
var targets = SnapshotTargets(leaderAcc, instr);            // Step 1: snapshot
string ocoId = "PTT-BE-"
    + (leaderAcc.Name.Length >= 4 ? leaderAcc.Name.Substring(0,4) : leaderAcc.Name)
    + "-" + (DateTime.Now.Ticks % 10000L).ToString();           // Step 2: ocoId
CancelStaleBrackets(leaderAcc, instr);                       // Step 3: cancel ATM

// Step 4: PTT-BE-Stop (update arg8 from "" to ocoId)
var beStop = leaderAcc.CreateOrder(
    instr, direction, OrderType.StopMarket, OrderEntry.Manual,
    TimeInForce.Day, pos.Quantity,
    0, bePrice, ocoId, "PTT-BE-Stop", DateTime.MaxValue,
    (NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null);
if (beStop == null) { /* log + return -- no stop = no bracket */ return; }
_pendingBeStop[leaderAcc.Name] = beStop;
leaderAcc.Submit(new[] { beStop });

// Step 5–6: PTT-BE-Target-N (one per snapshot entry)
for (int i = 0; i < targets.Count; i++)
{
    var t = targets[i];
    var tOrd = leaderAcc.CreateOrder(
        instr, t.Action, OrderType.Limit, OrderEntry.Manual,
        TimeInForce.Day, t.Qty,
        t.Price,   // arg6: limitPrice for Limit orders
        0,         // arg7: stopPrice = 0 for Limit
        ocoId, "PTT-BE-Target-" + (i + 1), DateTime.MaxValue,
        (NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null);
    if (tOrd != null)
        leaderAcc.Submit(new[] { tOrd });
    else
        NinjaTrader.Code.Output.Process(
            "[BE] Target-" + (i+1) + " CreateOrder null -- skip (stop still live)",
            PrintTo.OutputTab1);
}

// C4: CancelStaleBrackets filter update (1 changed line).
// BEFORE: && o.Name != "PTT-BE-Stop"
// AFTER:  && !o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-")
// Rationale: when called at submit time (Step 3), excludes our own PTT-BE orders.
// When called at flat event (TryFirePositionState !hasPos), PTT-BE orders ARE included
// in the cancel because they should be cleaned up when position is gone.
// WAIT -- this is WRONG for the flat path. See unknowns below for resolution.

U2 — CancelStaleBrackets dual-role CancelStaleBrackets is called at two points: (A) submit time — must NOT cancel own PTT-BE orders; (B) flat event — MUST cancel own PTT-BE orders. Current single filter cannot serve both. Fix: add a boolean parameter cancelPttBe (default false). Set true only at flat event call site.
U3 — Limit order arg order NT8-049 confirmed arg6=limitPrice, arg7=stopPrice for StopMarket. For Limit orders: same arg positions apply — arg6=limitPrice, arg7=0. Confirm via sim (no prior Limit submission in PTT-BE path).
U4 — TimeInForce for targets ATM targets use Gtc. PTT-BE-Stop uses Day. Should PTT-BE-Target-N use Day or Gtc? On sim this is irrelevant. On live, Day targets expire at session end — may close position mid-trade next day. Use TimeInForce.Gtc for targets to match ATM behavior.
RESOLVED DESIGN DECISIONS (pre-implementation)
  • U2 fix: CancelStaleBrackets(Account, Instrument, bool cancelPttBe = false) — add optional bool param. Submit path: cancelPttBe=false (default). Flat path: cancelPttBe=true. Filter: cancelPttBe ? true : !o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-"). CYC stays ≤ 4.
  • U3 fix: Limit orders use arg6=limitPrice, arg7=0. Confirmed from NT8-007 signature reference (arg6=limitPrice, arg7=stopPrice — for Limit, stopPrice=0).
  • U4 fix: PTT-BE targets use TimeInForce.Gtc to match ATM behavior and survive overnight.
  • U1 gate: OCO is a bonus — if it works, stop auto-cancels when target fills. If not, CancelStaleBrackets(cancelPttBe:true) at flat event handles cleanup. Either way is safe.

B36 LaneB shipped SubmitBeTargetsLocal() and SnapshotTargetsLocal() correctly, but both the button-press path (PttBreakEven.SubmitBeTargetsLocal) and the armed path (CopyEngine.SubmitBeStop) put all orders — stop + every target — into one shared OCO group. NT8 OCO semantics: when any order in the group fills or triggers, NT8 cancels all others. For a 2-target ATM this means Target-1 fills → OCO cancels Stop AND Target-2 → position left with N short/long contracts, no stop, no remaining upside. Position is unprotected.

Confirmed by sim 2026-07-27 10:24 PM: OCO group PTT-BE-Sim1-5271 contained PTT-BE-Stop (13) + PTT-BE-Target-1 (6) + PTT-BE-Target-2 (7). Target-1 filled → OCO cancelled both Stop and Target-2. 7 contracts left short, unprotected.
Correct Architecture — One OCO Pair Per Target
Mirror the NT8 ATM's own layout: each target is paired with its own proportional stop. When Target-1 fills, OCO-1 cancels only Stop-1 (protecting that tranche). OCO-2 (Stop-2 + Target-2) remains Working — the remaining contracts are still protected. 
// WRONG (B36): all orders in one OCO group
ocoId = BuildBeOcoId(acc, bePrice, tick, 0);   // single id
SubmitBeStopLocal(acc, instr, bePrice, qty, ocoId);  // stop for full qty
foreach target[i]: SubmitLimit(target[i].Qty, target[i].Price, ocoId); // all targets same ocoId

// CORRECT (B37): one OCO pair per target (mirrors NT8 ATM layout)
// 0 targets → single bare stop (unchanged edge case)
if (targets.Count == 0)
{
    SubmitBeStopLocal(acc, instr, bePrice, pos.Quantity, string.Empty);
    return;
}
foreach (int i, target in targets)
{
    string ocoId_i = BuildBeOcoId(acc, bePrice, tick, i);   // unique per pair
    SubmitBeStopLocal(acc, instr, bePrice, target.Qty, ocoId_i);  // stop for this tranche
    SubmitBeTargetLimit(acc, instr, target.Price, target.Qty, ocoId_i, i + 1); // target for same tranche
}
// Result: OCO-0 = (Stop-1, Target-1), OCO-1 = (Stop-2, Target-2), ...
// Each pair is independent — Target-1 fill cancels ONLY Stop-1

For each targets[i]: generate ocoId_i = BuildBeOcoId(acc, bePrice, tick, i), call SubmitBeStopLocal(acc, instr, bePrice, targets[i].Qty, ocoId_i), call new helper SubmitBeTargetLimit(acc, instr, targets[i].Price, targets[i].Qty, ocoId_i, i+1). Remove the single pre-loop SubmitBeStopLocal call from Execute(). Execute() CYC stays = 8.
CopyEngine.cs Refactor SubmitBeStop() lines ~1602–1617: same per-pair architecture. Replace: single-stop submit + shared-OCO target loop. With: 0-targets guard (bare stop), then per-target-pair loop generating unique ocoId_i for each targets[i]. Each pair: PTT-BE-Stop-{i+1} (qty=targets[i].Qty) + PTT-BE-Target-{i+1} (qty=targets[i].Qty) share ocoId_i.
Edge Cases
Case Behaviour
0 targets in snapshot Submit single PTT-BE-Stop for full position qty, ocoId = string.Empty. No target loop. Unchanged from pre-B36 behaviour.
1 target in snapshot 1 pair: PTT-BE-Stop-1 (targets[0].Qty) + PTT-BE-Target-1 (targets[0].Qty) share ocoId_0. Same net behaviour as B36 for 1-target ATMs — regression safe for PA live path. ✓
2 targets in snapshot 2 independent pairs. Target-1 fills → OCO-0 cancels only Stop-1. OCO-1 (Stop-2 + Target-2) remains Working. Position protected until Target-2 or Stop-2 trigger. ✓
N targets (N ≥ 3) Scales linearly — N pairs, N OCO groups. Each independent. Max realistic N is 3–4 (NT8 ATM limit). No special handling needed.

B36 section kept as defect record + live PA test baseline. Next live test required: same trade with 1+ followers enabled.
B35 confirmed the BE bracket-replace on the leader account only — live PA test passed 2026-07-24 (1 contract MES, PA-APEX-422136-08, buffer 0: stop exact match, target exact match, OCO correct, zero orphaned orders). The single remaining architectural gap: pressing BE only protects the leader. Follower accounts keep their original ATM stop prices until their own ATM stop-strategy triggers automatically. If the ATM has no auto-BE trigger, followers are exposed from the moment the leader presses BE until the ATM engine independently decides to move their stop.

B36 fix: the BE button fires once per account in the rule — leader first, then every enabled follower — using each account's own live fill price as the BE price. Each account gets an independent PTT-BE bracket (its own OCO group, its own PTT-BE-Stop, its own PTT-BE-Target-N set mirroring its own ATM target prices at the time BE is pressed). Identical safety, per account.
Why each follower uses its own fill price — not the leader's
Followers are independent market orders. On a fast move the leader may fill at 7437.50 while follower PA-08 fills at 7437.75. Setting BE at the leader's price on a follower account would place the stop at a price the follower never traded at — either 1 tick inside (too tight, immediate stop-out) or 1 tick outside (not true BE). Each account's own position.AveragePrice is the correct and only safe anchor.
B36 Defect — DW-B36-01
ID Priority Title Root cause
DW-B36-01 P0 BE button only fires on leader — followers unprotected BreakEven(Account leader, Instrument instr, int bufferTicks) calls SubmitBeStop(leaderAcc, instr, bePrice) once — no loop over follower accounts. Followers retain original ATM stop prices after leader presses BE.
Architecture — BE fires on all accounts in the rule
The existing BreakEven(Instrument instrument, int bufferTicks) path already calls AllAccounts(instrument) to iterate all accounts in the rule (leader + followers). The fix is to call SubmitBeStop inside that loop for every account rather than only for the leader, using each account's own position average price as the BE anchor.

Trim and Flatten already follow this exact pattern — the B36 change brings BE into alignment with them. 
// BEFORE (B35): only leader account
internal void BreakEven(Account leader, Instrument instrument, int bufferTicks)
{
    var pos     = FindPositionPublic(leader, instrument);
    double bePrice = pos.AveragePrice
                   + (isLong ? bufferTicks : -bufferTicks) * tickSize;
    SubmitBeStop(leader, instrument, bePrice);   // leader only
}

// AFTER (B36): leader + all followers via AllAccounts() loop
internal void BreakEven(Instrument instrument, int bufferTicks)
{
    foreach (var acc in AllAccounts(instrument))        // leader + followers
    {
        var pos = FindPositionPublic(acc, instrument);
        if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) continue; // skip flat accounts
        bool isLong    = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long;
        double tick    = instrument.MasterInstrument?.TickSize ?? 0.25;
        double bePrice = Math.Round(
            (pos.AveragePrice + (isLong ? bufferTicks : -bufferTicks) * tick) / tick
        ) * tick;
        SubmitBeStop(acc, instrument, bePrice);          // per-account, per-fill-price
    }
}
Order of execution: Leader fires first (it is always first in AllAccounts()). Each follower's SubmitBeStop is independent — cancels that account's own ATM bracket, submits that account's own PTT-BE-Stop + PTT-BE-Target-N at that account's own fill price. Failure on one account does not block others (each wrapped in its own try/catch per existing pattern).
What SubmitBeStop already handles — no changes needed inside it
Behaviour How
Flat account skip Guard at top of SubmitBeStop — returns early if pos.Quantity == 0
Duplicate BE guard _pendingBeStop[acc.Name] — if a Working PTT-BE-Stop already exists for that account, skip
ATM bracket cancel before submit CancelStaleBrackets(acc, instr) fires per account, cancels that account's ATM bracket only
Target snapshot SnapshotTargets(acc, instr) reads that account's live ATM target prices before cancelling — each follower preserves its own targets
OCO group per account OCO ID = "PTT-BE-" + acc.Name[0..4] + "-" + ticks — each account gets a unique group ID, no cross-account OCO coupling

Change Plan — PttBreakEven.cs
// NEW HELPER C1: SnapshotTargetsLocal
// Reads all Working/Accepted ATM Target orders (Target1..Target9) for the account
// before CancelStaleBracketsLocal destroys them.
// Returns List<(double Price, int Qty, OrderAction Action)>
private static List<(double Price, int Qty, OrderAction Action)> SnapshotTargetsLocal(
    Account acc, Instrument instr)
{
    var targets = new List<(double, int, OrderAction)>();
    if (acc == null || instr == null) return targets;
    foreach (Order o in acc.Orders)
    {
        if (o == null) continue;
        bool stateOk = o.OrderState == OrderState.Working
                    || o.OrderState == OrderState.Accepted;
        bool instrOk = o.Instrument != null
                    && o.Instrument.FullName == instr.FullName;
        bool isTarget = IsAtmTargetName(o.Name);   // "Target1".."Target9"
        if (stateOk && instrOk && isTarget)
            targets.Add((o.LimitPrice, o.Quantity, o.OrderAction));
    }
    return targets;
}

// NEW HELPER C2: IsAtmTargetName
// "Target1".."Target9" — same pattern as CopyEngine
private static bool IsAtmTargetName(string name)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(name)) return false;
    if (!name.StartsWith("Target")) return false;
    string suffix = name.Substring(6);
    int n;
    return int.TryParse(suffix, out n) && n >= 1 && n <= 9;
}

// NEW HELPER C3: SubmitBeTargetsLocal
// Submits PTT-BE-Target-N Limit orders (one per snapshot entry) with the same ocoId
// as the PTT-BE-Stop. Uses GTC (DateTime.MaxValue) to match ATM target behaviour.
// NT8-049: arg6=limitPrice=targetPrice, arg7=stopPrice=0
// NT8-007: arg11=(NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null
private static void SubmitBeTargetsLocal(
    Account acc, Instrument instr, string ocoId,
    List<(double Price, int Qty, OrderAction Action)> targets)
{
    if (acc == null || instr == null || targets == null) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < targets.Count; i++)
    {
        var t = targets[i];
        try
        {
            var order = acc.CreateOrder(
                instr,
                t.Action,                               // same action as snapshot (Sell / BuyToCover)
                OrderType.Limit,
                OrderEntry.Manual,
                TimeInForce.Gtc,
                t.Qty,
                t.Price,                                // arg6: limitPrice (NT8-049)
                0,                                      // arg7: stopPrice=0 (NT8-049)
                ocoId,                                  // arg8: OCO group
                "PTT-BE-Target-" + (i + 1),             // arg9: signal name
                DateTime.MaxValue,                      // arg10: GTC (NT8-013)
                (NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null);      // arg11: not string (NT8-007)
            if (order != null)
                acc.Submit(new[] { order });
        }
        catch { /* non-fatal: log but don't block remaining targets */ }
    }
}

// MODIFY C4: Execute() — add snapshot + ocoId before CancelStaleBracketsLocal
// and add SubmitBeTargetsLocal call after SubmitBeStopLocal.
// Execute() CYC stays at 8 — no new branches added (helpers do the work).

// INSIDE foreach, BEFORE CancelStaleBracketsLocal:
var targets = SnapshotTargetsLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument);
string ocoId = "PTT-BE-"
    + (acc.Name.Length >= 4 ? acc.Name.Substring(0, 4) : acc.Name)
    + "-" + ((int)(bePrice / ctx.Instrument.MasterInstrument.TickSize)).ToString();

CancelStaleBracketsLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument);
SubmitBeStopLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument, bePrice, isLong, ocoId);  // add ocoId param
SubmitBeTargetsLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument, ocoId, targets);        // NEW

Snapshot both targets Target1 + Target2 captured ✓ Both captured correctly ✓ PASS
4 ATM orders cancelled 4 cancelled ✓ 4 cancelled ✓ PASS

Target-1 fill leaves Stop + Target-2 working Stop + Target-2 remain Working after Target-1 fills (partial exit) ✗ OCO cancelled both Stop AND Target-2 when Target-1 filled. Position 7S left unprotected with zero upside. ✗ FAIL
Root cause: All 3 PTT-BE orders share one OCO group. NT8 OCO semantics: when any order in the group fills, NT8 cancels all others. This is correct for a 1-target bracket (target fills → stop cancelled). For a 2-target bracket it is wrong — Target-1 fills → Stop AND Target-2 are cancelled.

The armed path (CopyEngine.SubmitBeStop) has the identical architecture. It worked on the PA live test 2026-07-24 because that ATM had only 1 target, so no Target-2 to orphan. Both paths share this defect for ATMs with 2+ targets.

Correct architecture (mirrors NT8 ATM's own OCO layout):
Each target gets its own OCO group paired with the stop for that partial qty:
OCO-1: PTT-BE-Stop-1 (qty=6) + PTT-BE-Target-1 (qty=6)
OCO-2: PTT-BE-Stop-2 (qty=7) + PTT-BE-Target-2 (qty=7)
Target-1 fills (6) → OCO-1 cancels Stop-1. Target-2 and Stop-2 in OCO-2 remain Working. ✓

ROOT CAUSE — LIVE SIM BUGS (2026-07-26 Fires 1 & 2)

Three P0 bugs were observed when two independent accounts (Sim101 long + Sim102 short) were both in position simultaneously and BE was pressed with COPY OFF. The Execute() method in PttBreakEven.cs reads leaderPos once before the loop and passes isLong and bePrice from the leader to every account in the loop — failing to re-read direction and price per account.

A fourth issue (DW-B33-02/04) is that IPttHostContext exposes no buffer properties, so PttBreakEven uses a hard-coded bePrice = entryPrice (buffer=0) and PttTrim / PttFlatten submit plain market orders instead of limit-at-ask/bid orders.

DW-B33-07 P0 PttBreakEven.cs:74 — CancelStaleBracketsLocal(acc, ...) moved inside foreach before each submit CancelStaleBracketsLocal called once for leader only → leader got bare stop (Oco='') CLOSED B34

✓ B34-01 — DW-B33-05/06/07 — Fix AllAccounts Loop in PttBreakEven.Execute() — VERIFY_PASS

File: Features/PttBreakEven.cs
Scope: Rewrite the body of Execute() to move all per-account reads inside the loop. Remove the pre-loop leaderPos variable. Each iteration reads pos.AveragePrice, pos.MarketPosition, and pos.Quantity from its own account. The leader guard (skip if leader has no position) is preserved as a pre-loop early return.

APPROVED PATTERN — Execute() rewrite
public void Execute(IPttHostContext ctx)
{
    if (!IsEnabled) return;                                               // guard (1)

    // Leader guard: only fire if leader has an active position.
    Position leaderPos = FindPositionLocal(ctx.LeaderAccount, ctx.Instrument);
    if (leaderPos == null || leaderPos.Quantity == 0) return;             // guard (2)

    double tickSize = ctx.Instrument.MasterInstrument.TickSize;
    double buf      = ctx.BeBuffer;                                       // ticks (B34-02 adds BeBuffer)

    foreach (Account acc in ctx.AllAccounts)                             // loop (3)
    {
        Position pos = FindPositionLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument);            // per-account
        if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) continue;

        bool   isLong  = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long;       // per-account direction
        double bePrice = pos.AveragePrice
                       + (isLong ? +buf : -buf) * tickSize;               // per-account price + sign flip

        SnapshotTargetsLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument);                        // save existing targets
        CancelStaleBracketsLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument);                    // per-account cancel
        SubmitBeStopLocal(acc, ctx.Instrument, bePrice, isLong);          // correct direction
    }

    PttBus.RaiseBe(this, new BeEventArgs(
        ctx.Instrument,
        leaderPos.AveragePrice + (leaderPos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long ? +buf : -buf) * tickSize,
        leaderPos.AveragePrice, leaderPos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long, string.Empty));
}
KEY CHANGES vs B33
  • isLong derived from pos.MarketPosition inside loop — not from leader (fixes DW-B33-05)
  • bePrice = pos.AveragePrice ± buf*tick computed per account — not from leaderPos (fixes DW-B33-06)
  • CancelStaleBracketsLocal(acc, ...) called inside loop before each SubmitBeStop — not before loop (fixes DW-B33-07)
  • Buffer sign flipped for short accounts: isLong ? +buf : -buf
  • SnapshotTargetsLocal replaces separate pre-loop snapshot call — moves per-account
NT8 COMPILER CONSTRAINTS
  • NT8-049: CreateOrder arg6=limitPrice=0, arg7=stopPrice=bePrice — never swap
  • NT8-007: arg11 = (NinjaTrader.Cbi.CustomOrder)null — not a string
  • NT8-013: DateTime.MaxValue for GTC — not DateTime.Now
  • NT8-006: No LINQ — explicit foreach over acc.Positions
  • NT8-050: FindPositionLocal foreach — never acc.Positions[instr]
  • JS-021: No lock() anywhere
  • JS-033: synchronous void only — no async void
  • CYC target: Execute() ≤ 6, helpers ≤ 4 each

DW-B34-01 (P1) — ROOT CAUSE

SubmitBeStopLocal() wraps acc.Submit() in a try/catch for Exception. NT8 stop rejections do not throw — they arrive as an OrderUpdate event with state=Rejected after the call returns. The catch block is blind to them. The success log line also never fires because Submit() succeeds at the API level — NT8 rejects asynchronously.

Live evidence (2026-07-26 Fire 3, Sim101): Entry @ 7506.00, BE +1 tick → bePrice = 7506.25. Market already above 7506.25 at submission time. NT8 Output: "Sell stop or sell stop limit orders can't be placed above the market." Panel _statusText: nothing. Position left unprotected with zero user feedback.

B35-02 PttBreakEven.cs:75-92 Price guard in Execute() foreach. Reads ctx.Ask/ctx.Bid. Long: skip if bePrice > ask. Short: skip if bePrice < bid. On skip: OutputTab1 warning + ctx.WarnUser() + continue. No-data fallback: ask/bid <= 0.0 allows submission. CYC(Execute)=8. VERIFY_PASS

ⓘ BE ACTIVATION DEBUG NOTE — 2026-07-28  ·  Live PA MES (3 accounts)

Observed: Pressed BE button during a live MES trade (3 PA accounts). Price moved at least 1 tick in favor after clicking BE but the SL did not move. Position was closed manually.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS — source-verified

The BE button has two distinct paths depending on whether price is already at/past BE at click time:

  • Path A — "price already at BE" (IsPriceAlreadyAtBe returns true): Calls DispatchModule("BE") immediately. Stop moves right now. No arming needed.
    Condition: Long: bid >= entry + buffer×tick  |  Short: ask <= entry - buffer×tick
  • Path B — "price NOT yet at BE" (IsPriceAlreadyAtBe returns false): Arms a watcher via ArmPendingBe. Button turns amber ("BE Armed"). BE fires when OnPendingBeAccountUpdate detects price crossing the target.
    Trigger: Long: bid >= entry + buffer×tick  |  Short: ask <= entry - buffer×tick
LIKELY CAUSE — B35 Guard Silent Rejection

The most probable reason BE fired (path went through) but the SL did not move: the B35 guard (priceOk check in PttBreakEven.Execute) silently rejected the stop. The guard requires: Long: bePrice <= ask at the moment BE fires. If the stop was submitted with the old TimeInForce.Day (pre-B38 build), it would have expired at session close — but that alone doesn't explain no movement at click time.

More likely scenario: You clicked BE when price was not yet at BE level (Path B — armed). The button turned amber. Price then touched 1 tick in your favor — but bid (for long) must reach entry + buffer×tick. If the + value on the button was set to e.g. +1, price needed bid ≥ entry + 1 tick. A momentary 1-tick ask touch does not move bid by 1 tick simultaneously — bid would need to be ≥ entry + buffer×tick, not just ask.

THE "+ VALUE" ON THE BE BUTTON — WHAT IT DOES
  • _beBuffer (default 1) = the number of ticks beyond entry price the stop is placed.
  • BE+0: stop placed exactly at entry price. Trigger threshold = bid ≥ entry (long).
  • BE+1: stop placed at entry + 1 tick. Trigger threshold = bid ≥ entry + 1 tick (long). This is also the minimum price must reach for BE to fire.
  • BE+2: stop at entry + 2 ticks. Price must reach bid ≥ entry + 2 ticks before BE fires.
  • There is no separate activation buffer. The same value controls both the stop placement and the trigger threshold.
WHY "1 TICK IN FAVOR" MAY NOT FIRE BE+1
  • Bid vs Ask: For a Long, trigger uses bid, not ask. If ask touched entry+1 but bid was still at entry+0, BE+1 does not fire. (MES spread is 0.25 = 1 tick — bid must close above entry+1 tick.)
  • AveragePrice vs entry: bePrice = pos.AveragePrice ± buf×tick. If you were filled at a slightly worse average (slippage across 3 PA accounts), the effective threshold is higher than you perceived.
  • Path B timing: If you clicked BE before price moved (armed path), OnPendingBeAccountUpdate fires on NT8 account background thread. There can be a 1–2 tick delay between market price and the AccountItemUpdate event callback. The price may have briefly touched the level but the NT8 event fired before or after the threshold was crossed.
  • B35 guard pre-B38: If running a pre-B38 build, the stop TIF was Day. The stop itself should still have been submitted and cancelled at session close — not at click time. TIF does not affect whether the stop is placed.
NEXT STEPS / DIAGNOSTIC
  1. Check NT8 Output Tab1 after the next BE attempt — [BE] WARNING: ... BE stop @ ... rejected means the B35 guard fired (stop above ask for long — position was underwater at BE time).
  2. Check NT8 Output Tab1 for [BE] SubmitBeStopLocal line — if present, BE fired and submitted. If absent, OnPendingBeAccountUpdate never crossed threshold.
  3. Use BE+0 for a test: this fires immediately when bid ≥ entry (no buffer). If it fires, the arming and stop submission are working. Then increase buffer.
  4. For intraday MES scalps: BE+0 is the most practical setting — stop goes to entry, fires as soon as price returns to entry. BE+1 requires bid to reach entry+0.25 before arming fires.
  5. With B38 now deployed (TIF.Gtc), stops will survive session rollover — the Day expiry root cause is eliminated.

● Block 39  ·  PTT-COPIER-B39  ·  Global BE All  ·  No-Copier Multi-Account Break Even  ·  PLANNED
B39 — Global BE All: One Button Protects Every Open Position
The existing BE button (B4–B38) operates within a copy rule's instrument scope — it fires on the leader account and all followers registered under that rule for the chart's current instrument. This is correct behaviour when the copier is active.

The gap: When trading 3+ accounts manually with the copier OFF (no rule configured), pressing BE on one chart only protects that chart's account. The other accounts remain fully exposed. Today there is no single action that fires BE across all open positions on all accounts.

B39 closes this gap: a new [BE ALL] button that scans Account.All × positions, fires SubmitBeStop for every account that has a non-zero position on any instrument, requires zero copy rule configuration, and works whether the copier is ON, OFF, or never set up.

A matching own module is created: src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttGlobalBreakEven.cs — following the same modular pattern as PttBreakEven.cs, PttTrim.cs, and PttFlatten.cs established in B33. Each button, its own file.
Panel Layout Change — ChartTrader Panel (B39)
The existing B12 locked layout is 3 rows + ATR row. B39 changes Row 2 and Row 3 only — Row 1 (Trim / Flatten) and Row 4 (Risk/ATR) are unchanged.

Change summary:
• Row 2 (previously BE | Cancel) → becomes BE | BE ALL — Cancel moves down
• Row 3 (previously ● COPY ON/OFF full-width) → becomes Cancel | ● COPY ON/OFF — two equal-width buttons sharing one row
• Row 4 (Risk $ / ATR %) — unchanged

Constraint respected: Cancel stays reachable one row below its previous position. Copy ON/OFF shrinks from full-width to half-width (same height, same row) so both fit in a single ChartTrader row. Copy toggle is used less frequently during a trade than Cancel is — the trade-off is acceptable.

Follows the exact same modular pattern as PttBreakEven.cs. No inheritance, no shared base class — just a standalone class with a single public method. Panel and Window each hold a reference; both call Execute(bufferTicks). The class does not know which surface called it. 
// src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttGlobalBreakEven.cs
// JS-021: no lock(). JS-002: no return null. JS-033: no async void.
// CYC target: Execute()=4, helper=2. ~55 lines total.
internal sealed class PttGlobalBreakEven
{
    // Shared buffer (UI thread only — volatile per JS-023)
    private volatile int _globalBeBuffer = 0;   // default 0 = exact entry price

    // Called from Panel OnGlobalBeClick / Window OnGlobalBeClick
    internal void Execute(int bufferTicks)
    {
        foreach (var acc in Account.All)
        {
            foreach (var pos in acc.Positions)          // live positions snapshot
            {
                if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) continue; // flat — skip
                ExecuteOne(acc, pos.Instrument, bufferTicks);
            }
        }
    }

    // CYC=2: direction branch only. B35 market-guard inherited from SubmitBeStop.
    private void ExecuteOne(Account acc, Instrument instr, int bufferTicks)
    {
        var pos = acc.Positions.FindByInstrument(instr);
        if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) return;
        bool   isLong  = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long;
        double tick    = instr.MasterInstrument?.TickSize ?? 0.25;
        double bePrice = Math.Round(
            (pos.AveragePrice + (isLong ? bufferTicks : -bufferTicks) * tick) / tick
        ) * tick;
        CopyEngine.Instance?.SubmitBeStop(acc, instr, bePrice);  // B35 guard inside
    }

    // Buffer ▲▼ — called from Panel/Window RepeatButton handlers
    internal int  GlobalBeBuffer  => _globalBeBuffer;
    internal void IncrementBuffer() => _globalBeBuffer++;
    internal void DecrementBuffer() { if (_globalBeBuffer > -10) _globalBeBuffer--; }
}
Design note — buffer range: Unlike the per-instrument BE (range −10 to +10), the global BE default is 0 (exact entry price, no buffer). A buffer of 0 means the stop lands exactly at your average fill price — the safest default for a "panic protect all" action. The ▲▼ spinners allow adjustment from −10 to +10 exactly like the existing BE button, but the starting point is 0 not +1.
B35 guard is inherited — no extra code needed: SubmitBeStop() already rejects a stop if it would be placed on the wrong side of the market (underwater position). The global loop defers to that guard. Each account gets its own warning in the Output window if its BE price is adverse.

⚠ Open Design Question — Shared vs Separate Instance
The Panel and Window each display a BE ALL button with its own ▲▼ buffer spinner. Should they share a single PttGlobalBreakEven instance (buffer stays in sync across both surfaces) or hold independent instances (each surface tracks its own buffer)?

Option A — Shared instance via CopyEngine.Instance: Panel and Window both reference CopyEngine.Instance.GlobalBe. Adjusting ▲▼ on the panel changes the buffer shown in the window too — consistent, same as how CopyEngine.Instance.BreakEven works today.

Option B — Independent instances: Each surface holds its own PttGlobalBreakEven instance. Panel buffer and Window buffer are independent. Simpler — no cross-surface sync needed. Slight inconsistency risk: press BE ALL on panel at buffer+2, window still shows 0.

Recommended: Option A — mirrors the existing Live Map pillar: "Toggle Copy ON from the Panel — the Window goes green simultaneously." BE ALL buffer should stay in sync. Add CopyEngine.GlobalBe property returning the singleton PttGlobalBreakEven. Fire a GlobalBeBufferChanged event on CopyEngine whenever buffer changes — both surfaces subscribe and update their label. CYC impact: +1 to CopyEngine.

⚠ MULTI-ACCOUNT LIVE TEST — 2 defects found — B40 scope
Test setup: Sim101 + Sim102 both in long position, COPY OFF, clicked BE ALL.

DW-B39-OCO-01 (P0) — OCO ID collision across accounts with same name prefix

Error: Sim102 Order 'b527c7...' can't be submitted: The OCO ID 'PTT-BE-Sim1-30541-1' cannot be reused.

Root cause: ocoId is built as "PTT-BE-" + acc.Name[0..4] + "-" + ticks + "-" + pairIndex. acc.Name[0..4] for Sim101 = "Sim1" and for Sim102 = "Sim1" — identical prefix. When Execute() loops Sim101 then Sim102 in rapid succession, Environment.TickCount (or equivalent) returns the same value for both calls, producing the same ocoId. NT8 rejects Sim102's submission with OCO reuse error.

Cascade effect: The OCO error triggers NT8 error events / position state re-fires, causing Execute() to run again — visible as the same ocoId block repeating 3–4 times in the log for both accounts.

Fix: Replace acc.Name[0..4] with a per-Execute monotonic counter combined with more account name characters. Two safe options:
Option A (simplest): Use a volatile int _ocoSeq field in PttGlobalBreakEven, incremented once per Execute() call. ocoId = "PTT-BE-G" + _ocoSeq.ToString("D5") + "-" + pairIndex. Globally unique across all accounts per button press.
Option B (more readable): Use enough of the account name to distinguish: acc.Name.Replace(" ","").Replace("-","")[0..Math.Min(6,acc.Name.Length)] → "Sim101" vs "Sim102" (6 chars). Combined with ticks: unique for all practical account names.

Recommended: Option A — counter is 100% collision-free regardless of account names. CYC unchanged. One new volatile int _ocoSeq = 0 field.
DW-B39-BEHAVIOR-01 (P1) — BE ALL fires immediately; does not wait for price to reach entry

Observed: Clicking BE ALL submits the stop order immediately at the entry price, regardless of whether current market price has reached the entry level. If price is still below entry (for a long), the stop is placed below current price — correct, but it locks in a loss at entry rather than waiting until price has moved back to breakeven before arming the stop.

Regular BE behavior (B9 ArmPendingBe): Click once → button goes amber (armed). The engine watches price via AccountItemUpdate. When price crosses the entry level, then the stop is submitted automatically. Zero exposure until entry is reached.

BE ALL behavior (B39 as designed): No armed state — fires immediately. One click = stop submitted now at avgEntry + buffer × tick. This was specced as "instant BE" intentionally (panic-protect-all). But in practice the user wants the same armed-wait behavior as the regular button.

Director decision required:
Option Behavior Trade-off
A — Keep instant (current) Click = stop submitted immediately at entry price across all accounts Simplest. If price is through entry you take the loss. B35 guard rejects adverse stops.
B — Armed/wait (match regular BE) Click → all accounts armed (amber). Each account's price watcher fires when that account's position reaches its own entry price. Stop submitted per-account on trigger. More complex. Requires ArmPendingBe() equivalent per account in PttGlobalBreakEven. Safest for traders still in drawdown.
C — Two buttons [BE ALL] = instant (current). [ARM ALL] = armed-wait for all accounts. Maximum flexibility. Two separate actions, clear intent. Adds one more button.

B40 — BE ALL: Armed/Wait State Machine + OCO ID Fix
B39 delivered the [BE ALL] button but live testing surfaced two defects that must be fixed before the feature ships:

DW-B39-OCO-01 (P0): OCO ID collision when two accounts share the same 4-char name prefix and TickCount is identical (tight loop). NT8 rejects the second order with "The OCO ID cannot be reused" and cascades the event 3–4×.

DW-B39-BEHAVIOR-01 (P1): BE ALL fired immediately at entry price on click — no armed/wait state. Director decision: Option B — match the regular BE+ button exactly. Click → all accounts arm (amber). Each account's price watcher fires independently when price crosses that account's own entry + buffer. Stop submitted per-account on trigger.

B40 closes both defects using the existing armed-state machinery as a building block — no new engine primitives are invented. The _pendingBeSlots ConcurrentDictionary already supports N accounts in parallel.
Building Block: Current BE+ Armed State Machine (B27 / B32)
The regular BE+ button is a 3-state FSM split across TradeCopierPanel (UI state) and CopyEngine (price watcher):
Idle  ──── click (price already past entry) ─────────────────────────────>  Idle  (fire immediately)
Idle  ──── click (still in drawdown) ──────────────────────────────────>  Armed  (button → amber "BE Armed")
Armed  ──── price crosses entry + buffer ───────────────────────────────>  Idle  (stop submitted, button → idle)
Armed  ──── click again (cancel arm) ───────────────────────────────────>  Idle  (disarmed, no stop)
Component File / Line Role
BeState enum TradeCopierPanel.cs ~326 Idle / Armed / Connected — 3-state FSM
_beState field TradeCopierPanel.cs ~200 Current UI state of the per-instrument BE button
ArmPendingBe(instr, acc, buf) CopyEngine.cs ~1944 Registers AccountItemUpdate price watcher, keyed by accName in _pendingBeSlots
_pendingBeSlots CopyEngine.cs ~135 ConcurrentDictionary<string, PendingBeSlot> — key = accName. Already supports N accounts simultaneously.
OnPendingBeAccountUpdate CopyEngine.cs ~1993 Price watcher — fires MoveStopToBreakEven when price crosses entry. One-shot: removes slot after firing.
IsPriceAlreadyAtBe(...) TradeCopierPanel.cs ~1037 If price already past entry → fire immediately rather than arming. Per-account variant needed for BE ALL.
PendingBeFired event CopyEngine.cs ~152 Action<string, string> — fires per-account when its stop is placed. Panel uses this to reset button to Idle.
DisarmPendingBe(acc) CopyEngine.cs ~1968 Atomically removes slot + unsubscribes watcher. Called when user cancels arm or position goes flat.
Key insight: _pendingBeSlots is a ConcurrentDictionary keyed by accName. Calling ArmPendingBe for Sim101, Sim102, Sim103 simultaneously creates three independent slots — no engine changes needed. BE ALL armed state is a pure UI coordination layer on top of existing engine machinery.
Fix 1 — DW-B39-OCO-01 (P0): OCO ID Collision via Global Sequence Counter
Root cause: BuildBeOcoId (in PttBreakEven.cs) and the equivalent path in CopyEngine.SubmitBeStop both build OCO IDs using accName[0..4] + "-" + (int)(bePrice/tick) + "-" + pairIndex. When two accounts share the same 4-char prefix ("Sim101"[0..4] = "Sim1", "Sim102"[0..4] = "Sim1") and the loop executes within the same TickCount window, the IDs are identical. NT8 rejects the second OCO registration and cascades 3–4 retries.
// BEFORE (collision-prone)
string ocoId = "PTT-BE-" + accName.Substring(0,4) + "-" + priceInt + "-" + pairIndex;
// Sim101 → "PTT-BE-Sim1-30539-0" ← same as Sim102 when loop is tight
// Sim102 → "PTT-BE-Sim1-30539-0" ← COLLISION → NT8 reject

// AFTER (collision-free) — global sequence counter per Execute() call
// In PttGlobalBreakEven:
private volatile int _ocoSeq = 0;
// Increment ONCE at top of Execute() — one sequence number per button press
int seq = System.Threading.Interlocked.Increment(ref _ocoSeq);
// Pass seq into BuildGlobalBeOcoId:
string ocoId = "PTT-BEG-" + seq.ToString("D5") + "-" + accIdx + "-" + pairIndex;
// Sim101 pair 0 → "PTT-BEG-00001-0-0" ← unique
// Sim102 pair 0 → "PTT-BEG-00001-1-0" ← accIdx=1, unique
// Next press → "PTT-BEG-00002-0-0" ← seq incremented, never reused
Rule Compliance
JS-023 (volatile int) volatile int _ocoSeq — allowed. Not a double (NT8-003 does not apply).
JS-021 (no lock) Interlocked.Increment — lock-free atomic increment. Zero lock().
NT8-014 (signal prefix) "PTT-BEG-" prefix — starts with "PTT-". Distinct from "PTT-BE-" (per-instrument). Unambiguous in order log.
CYC impact One new field + one Interlocked call. No branches added. CYC unchanged on all methods.
Scope: The fix lives entirely in PttGlobalBreakEven.cs — the BuildGlobalBeOcoId helper replaces the inline formula. PttBreakEven.cs is unchanged — its per-instrument OCO IDs use account name + price int which is already unique per account for a single instrument. Only the global path (multi-account × multi-instrument in one tight loop) needs the sequence counter.
Fix 2 — DW-B39-BEHAVIOR-01 (P1): BE ALL Armed/Wait — Option B
Director decision: BE ALL must behave exactly like the regular BE+ button — click arms all open positions across all accounts, each waits for its own entry price, stop fires per-account on trigger. The existing per-instrument BE+ is the building block.

Key architectural insight: CopyEngine._pendingBeSlots is already a ConcurrentDictionary<string, PendingBeSlot> — calling ArmPendingBe three times for three accounts creates three independent watching slots with zero engine modification.
New method: CopyEngine.ArmAllPendingBe(int bufferTicks)
/// CYC=5: (1) base, (2) foreach acc, (3) foreach pos,
/// (4) null/flat guard, (5) IsPriceAlreadyAtBe branch.
/// JS-021: no lock. JS-023: _pendingBeSlots is ConcurrentDictionary.
internal int ArmAllPendingBe(int bufferTicks)
{
    int armedCount = 0;
    foreach (var acc in Account.All)                        // (2)
    {
        foreach (var pos in acc.Positions)                // (3)
        {
            if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) continue;  // (4)
            if (IsPriceAlreadyAtBeForAccount(acc, pos, bufferTicks)) // (5)
            {
                SubmitBeStop(acc, pos.Instrument, ComputeBePrice(pos, bufferTicks));
                // Already past entry — fire immediately, no arm needed
            }
            else
            {
                ArmPendingBe(pos.Instrument, acc, bufferTicks);  // reuse existing
                armedCount++;
            }
        }
    }
    return armedCount;  // 0 = all fired immediately, >0 = slots watching
}

Reset to Idle: _pendingBeSlots.IsEmpty (Option B2 — dictionary as source of truth)
On each PendingBeFired event (fires once per account when its stop is placed), the handler checks _pendingBeSlots.IsEmpty. When the dictionary is empty — meaning all armed accounts have triggered — _globalBeState resets to Idle and the button visual updates.

This is Option B2: the ConcurrentDictionary is the source of truth — no separate counter to maintain. If a position goes flat (DW-B32-11 path), the slot is removed by the flat-detection branch, which also decrements the dict — so IsEmpty still triggers correctly when the last account resolves.

Armed  ──── each account's price crosses entry+buffer ───────────────────────>  stop submitted per-account; slot removed
                                                                     when _pendingBeSlots.IsEmpty → Idle
Armed  ──── click again (cancel all arms) ──────────────────────────────────>  Idle  (DisarmPendingBe × all accounts)

PIPELINE_COMPLETE: B41 — Quick Exit: Per-Instrument Bracket Swap  |  Tag: PTT-COPIER B41 | quick-exit | 2026-08-05  |  [Fact] count: 234  |  13/13 V-checks GREEN
Two new buttons — [Quick ▲▼] and [Quick ALL] — that swap the current ATM bracket for a PTT-managed bracket with configurable T1/T2 limit targets computed from the position's average entry price. Per-instrument defaults (MES: T1=4t/T2=8t, MGC: T1=2t/T2=4t). Idempotent: press again at any time to swap to a new bracket configuration — previous PTT-QX orders are cancelled and replaced. T3 row hidden by default, appears when 3 live Working target orders are detected. Two own files: PttQuickExit.cs (per-chart scope) and PttGlobalQuickExit.cs (all accounts/instruments).
Scope Model — mirrors BE / BE ALL exactly
Button Scope Instrument resolved from Works without CopyRule?
[Quick ▲▼] This chart's _instrument — leader + all followers for that rule _instrument field set at panel attach — identical to BE button ✓ Yes — fallback to hardcoded default ticks for instrument
[Quick ALL] Account.All × positions — every account, every instrument with a non-flat position No chart context — identical to BE ALL ✓ Yes — always works, no rule needed
Coincident fill scenario: You press [Quick] on your MES chart while MGC also happens to be filled simultaneously. Only MES gets the bracket swap — _instrument is MES, MGC is invisible to this button. Press [Quick ALL] to cover all instruments at once.
Idempotent Preset Switch — press as many times as needed
Each press is a complete bracket swap. Pressing [Quick] a second time (or after adjusting the ▲▼ spinner to a different offset) cancels the existing PTT-QX orders and resubmits with the new values. There is no "one and done" — you can freely switch between bracket configurations mid-trade. 
── Example: change your mind mid-trade ─────────────────────────────────
Long 4 MES @ 5000.00   ATM Stop @ 4995.00  ATM Target1 @ 5010  Target2 @ 5020

Press [Quick] with spinner at +4t/+8t (1pt/2pt):
  Step 1: SnapshotStop → 4995.00
  Step 2: CancelStaleBrackets(cancelPttQx:false) → wipes ATM targets + stop
  Step 3: Submit PTT-QX-Stop   @ 4995.00  (stop stays same)
  Step 4: Submit PTT-QX-T1     @ 5004.00  (+4 ticks = +1pt)  Sell 2 lots
  Step 5: Submit PTT-QX-T2     @ 5008.00  (+8 ticks = +2pt)  Sell 2 lots
  → bracket is now 1pt/2pt

Change mind — adjust spinner to +8t/+16t (2pt/4pt), press [Quick] again:
  Step 1: SnapshotStop → 4995.00              (still valid)
  Step 2: CancelStaleBrackets(cancelPttQx:true) → wipes PTT-QX-T1/T2 from step above
  Step 3: Submit PTT-QX-Stop   @ 4995.00
  Step 4: Submit PTT-QX-T1     @ 5008.00  (+8 ticks = +2pt)  Sell 2 lots
  Step 5: Submit PTT-QX-T2     @ 5016.00  (+16 ticks = +4pt)  Sell 2 lots
  → bracket is now 2pt/4pt — first bracket cleanly replaced
Key: CancelStaleBrackets receives a new cancelPttQx boolean (alongside the existing cancelPttBe from B33 U2 fix). At Quick Exit submit time: cancelPttQx=true — wipes previous PTT-QX orders. At flat event: both flags true — full cleanup. Existing ATM orders: always wiped (no PTT- prefix).
▲▼ Spinner — Shared Increment, Both Targets Move Together
A single ▲▼ spinner adjusts both T1 and T2 by the same increment simultaneously. The relationship T2 = T1 × 2 is maintained by default (T2 offset = T1 offset × 2). Pressing ▲ once: T1 +1 tick, T2 +2 ticks. Pressing ▼ once: T1 -1 tick, T2 -2 ticks.

Defaults pre-populated when rule is created. User adjusts via ▲▼ per session. Stored on CopyRule fields QuickT1Ticks and QuickT2Ticks. Fallback table in PttQuickExit.cs serves the no-rule path.
T3 Row — Hidden by Default, Auto-Detected from Live Orders
The T3 row ([Quick T3 ▲▼] / [Quick T3 ALL]) starts as Visibility.Collapsed. When SnapshotTargets() returns 3 or more Working target orders, UpdateT3Visibility() sets the row to Visibility.Visible. When position goes flat or targets drop below 3, row collapses again. No dynamic binding — simple Visibility toggle on a pre-built WPF row. T3 defaults to T1 × 3 ticks. Separate QuickT3Ticks = 0 field on CopyRule (0 = hidden). 
// UpdateT3Visibility — called from OnPositionUpdate and on button press
// CYC=2: null guard(1) + count threshold check(2)
private void UpdateT3Visibility(Account acc, Instrument instr)
{
    var targets = CopyEngine.Instance?.SnapshotTargets(acc, instr);
    bool show = targets != null && targets.Count >= 3;
    _quickT3Row.Visibility = show ? Visibility.Visible : Visibility.Collapsed;
}

// CYC=5: null guard(1) + no position guard(2) + long/short(3) + T2 submit(4) + T3 guard(5)

Step 1: pos = leader.Positions.FindByInstrument(instr)

Step 2: snapshotStop = SnapshotStopPrice(leader, instr)
        // reads first Working/Accepted stop order price
        // if none found → snapshotStop = 0 (no stop resubmit — log warning)

Step 3: CancelStaleBrackets(leader, instr, cancelPttBe:false, cancelPttQx:true)
        // wipes ATM bracket + any existing PTT-QX orders
        // does NOT cancel PTT-BE orders (cancelPttBe:false)

Step 4: ocoId = "PTT-QX-" + _qxSeq.ToString("D5")

Step 5: isLong = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long
        entryPx = pos.AveragePrice
        tick    = instr.MasterInstrument?.TickSize ?? 0.25
        t1Price = Math.Round((entryPx + (isLong ? +t1Ticks : -t1Ticks) * tick) / tick) * tick
        t2Price = Math.Round((entryPx + (isLong ? +t2Ticks : -t2Ticks) * tick) / tick) * tick
        t1Qty   = (int)Math.Ceiling(pos.Quantity / 2.0)   // ceil = same as Trim rule
        t2Qty   = pos.Quantity - t1Qty

Step 6: if snapshotStop > 0
          stopOrd = leader.CreateOrder(instr, isLong ? OrderAction.Sell : OrderAction.BuyToCover,
                      OrderType.StopMarket, OrderEntry.Manual, TimeInForce.Gtc,
                      pos.Quantity, 0, snapshotStop, ocoId, "PTT-QX-Stop",
                      DateTime.MaxValue, (CustomOrder)null)
          if stopOrd != null → leader.Submit(new[] { stopOrd })
          else → log "QX: stop CreateOrder null — position unprotected"

Step 7: t1Ord = leader.CreateOrder(instr, isLong ? OrderAction.Sell : OrderAction.BuyToCover,
                  OrderType.Limit, OrderEntry.Manual, TimeInForce.Gtc,
                  t1Qty, t1Price, 0, ocoId, "PTT-QX-T1",
                  DateTime.MaxValue, (CustomOrder)null)
        if t1Ord != null → leader.Submit(new[] { t1Ord })
        else → log "QX: T1 CreateOrder null — skip"

Step 8: t2Ord = leader.CreateOrder(instr, isLong ? OrderAction.Sell : OrderAction.BuyToCover,
                  OrderType.Limit, OrderEntry.Manual, TimeInForce.Gtc,
                  t2Qty, t2Price, 0, ocoId, "PTT-QX-T2",
                  DateTime.MaxValue, (CustomOrder)null)
        if t2Ord != null → leader.Submit(new[] { t2Ord })
        else → log "QX: T2 CreateOrder null — stop still protects"

Step 9: PttBus.RaiseQuickExit(this, new QuickExitEventArgs(instr, entryPx, t1Price, t2Price, isLong, ocoId))

PttGlobalQuickExit.cs — [Quick ALL] own file
Mirrors PttGlobalBreakEven.cs exactly. Loops Account.All × positions. For each non-flat position, resolves T1/T2 ticks: FindRule(instr) → rule ticks if found, else InstrumentDefaults.GetQuickTicks(instr) fallback. Calls PttQuickExit.ExecuteOne(acc, instr, t1Ticks, t2Ticks) per slot. 
// PttGlobalQuickExit.cs — ~55 lines, CYC target: Execute()=3, ExecuteOne()=4
// JS-021: no lock(). JS-002: no return null. JS-033: no async void.
internal sealed class PttGlobalQuickExit
{
    private volatile int _qxSeq = 0;

    internal void Execute()
    {
        foreach (var acc in Account.All)
            foreach (var pos in acc.Positions)
            {
                if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) continue;
                var (t1, t2) = ResolveQuickTicks(pos.Instrument);
                ExecuteOne(acc, pos.Instrument, t1, t2);
            }
    }

    private (int t1, int t2) ResolveQuickTicks(Instrument instr)
    {
        var rule = CopyEngine.Instance?.FindRule(instr);
        if (rule != null) return (rule.QuickT1Ticks, rule.QuickT2Ticks);
        return InstrumentDefaults.GetQuickTicks(instr.MasterInstrument?.Name ?? "");
    }
}
