// PttQuickExit.cs — inner static helper, ~15 lines
// CYC=3: null guard(1) + MES check(2) + MGC check(3)
internal static class InstrumentDefaults
{
    internal static (int t1, int t2) GetQuickTicks(string masterName)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(masterName)) return (4, 8);
        if (masterName.StartsWith("MES", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return (4, 8);
        if (masterName.StartsWith("MGC", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return (2, 4);
        return (4, 8);  // unknown → MES default
    }
}

CancelStaleBrackets Update — CopyEngine.cs
// Add cancelPttQx bool param alongside existing cancelPttBe (B33 U2)
// CYC stays ≤ 4
private void CancelStaleBrackets(Account acc, Instrument instr,
    bool cancelPttBe = false, bool cancelPttQx = false)
{
    if (acc == null || instr == null) return;
    var stale = acc.Orders.Where(o =>
        o.Instrument?.FullName == instr.FullName
        && (o.OrderState == OrderState.Working || o.OrderState == OrderState.Accepted)
        && (cancelPttBe || !o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-"))
        && (cancelPttQx || !o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-QX-"))).ToList();
    if (stale.Count == 0) return;
    acc.Cancel(stale);
}
All existing call sites pass no new args — defaults preserve current behaviour. Quick Exit submit path: cancelPttQx:true (wipe previous QX bracket). Flat event path: both cancelPttBe:true, cancelPttQx:true (full cleanup).

PTTQUICKEXIT.CS SPEC:
  internal sealed class PttQuickExit
  Execute(Account leader, Instrument instr, int t1Ticks, int t2Ticks):
    1. Null/flat guard
    2. SnapshotStopPrice(leader, instr) -> snapshotStop (0 if none found, log warning)
    3. CancelStaleBrackets(leader, instr, cancelPttBe:false, cancelPttQx:true)
    4. ocoId = "PTT-QX-" + Interlocked.Increment(ref _qxSeq).ToString("D5")
    5. Compute t1Price, t2Price from pos.AveragePrice +/- ticks * tickSize (per direction)
       t1Qty = (int)Math.Ceiling(pos.Quantity / 2.0)
       t2Qty = pos.Quantity - t1Qty
    6. Submit PTT-QX-Stop (StopMarket, GTC, full qty, snapshotStop) -- if snapshotStop > 0
    7. Submit PTT-QX-T1 (Limit, GTC, t1Qty, t1Price) -- null-guard, log on null
    8. Submit PTT-QX-T2 (Limit, GTC, t2Qty, t2Price) -- null-guard, log on null
    9. PttBus.RaiseQuickExit(...)
  NT8 rules: NT8-049 arg6=limitPrice arg7=0 for Limit. NT8-007 arg12=(CustomOrder)null.
             NT8-013 DateTime.MaxValue for GTC. NT8-014 signal names "PTT-QX-*".

PTTGLOBALQUICKEXIT.CS SPEC:
  internal sealed class PttGlobalQuickExit
  Execute():
    foreach acc in Account.All
      foreach pos in acc.Positions (skip null/flat)
        (t1, t2) = ResolveQuickTicks(pos.Instrument)
        ExecuteOne(acc, pos.Instrument, t1, t2) -- delegates to PttQuickExit pattern
  ResolveQuickTicks(instr):
    rule = CopyEngine.Instance?.FindRule(instr)
    return rule != null ? (rule.QuickT1Ticks, rule.QuickT2Ticks)
                        : InstrumentDefaults.GetQuickTicks(instr.MasterInstrument?.Name)
  volatile int _qxSeq -- unique OCO seq per Execute() call (prevents OCO ID collision)

◯ Card A  ·  Live Sync — Spinner Reflects Actual Live Order Distances
The ▲▼ spinner currently shows CopyRule.QuickT1Ticks — the configured default. After [Quick] is pressed and live PTT-QX-T1/T2 orders are Working, the spinner must back-calculate and display the actual tick distances from the live order prices to pos.AveragePrice. Three scenarios define when each display mode is correct:
Scenario Live QX orders? Spinner shows Correct?
A — No position No CopyRule.QuickT1Ticks ✓ Pre-configured default
B — Position open, Quick not pressed No CopyRule.QuickT1Ticks ✓ Shows what you'll get on next press
C — Quick pressed, live QX orders Working Yes Back-calc from live order price △ Gap in original spec — fixed here
RefreshQuickDisplay() — new method on TradeCopierPanel
// RefreshQuickDisplay — CYC=3: no t1Ord guard(1) + no pos guard(2) + isLong branch(3)
// Called from: OnOrderUpdate (PTT-QX-T1 → Working), OnPositionUpdate, panel attach.
// Always dispatches on UI thread via Dispatcher.InvokeAsync.
private void RefreshQuickDisplay(Account acc, Instrument instr)
{
    var t1Ord = FindWorkingOrder(acc, instr, "PTT-QX-T1");
    if (t1Ord == null) return; // no live QX orders — leave spinner at CopyRule default

    var pos = acc.Positions.FindByInstrument(instr);
    if (pos == null || pos.Quantity == 0) return;

    double tick    = instr.MasterInstrument?.TickSize ?? 0.25;
    bool   isLong  = pos.MarketPosition == MarketPosition.Long;
    double rawDiff = isLong ? t1Ord.LimitPrice - pos.AveragePrice
                            : pos.AveragePrice  - t1Ord.LimitPrice;
    int    liveT1  = (int)Math.Round(rawDiff / tick);
    if (liveT1 < 1) liveT1 = 1; // clamp — never show 0 ticks

    Dispatcher.InvokeAsync(() => {
        _quickT1Spinner.Value = liveT1;       // updates display only — does NOT re-submit
        _quickT2Spinner.Value = liveT1 * 2;   // maintains T2=T1×2 relationship
    });
}

// Three call sites (add to existing event handlers):
// 1. OnOrderUpdate:  if (e.Order.Name == "PTT-QX-T1" && e.Order.OrderState == OrderState.Working)
//                     → RefreshQuickDisplay(e.Order.Account, e.Order.Instrument)
// 2. OnPositionUpdate: if any PTT-QX-T1 is Working for this instrument
//                     → RefreshQuickDisplay(e.Position.Account, e.Position.Instrument)
// 3. Panel attach / tab switch: RefreshQuickDisplay(_leaderAccount, _instrument)
Important: RefreshQuickDisplay updates the spinner display value only — it does NOT call SetQuickTicks on CopyRule. The CopyRule default is preserved for the next session. The spinner value is the "live view" of the current bracket — not a persistent config change.
■ Card B  ·  PTT Window ↔ Chart Panel — 100% Sync Contract
The PTT Window and the chart panel Quick Exit spinner must always show the same values. The panel is the source of truth (it owns RefreshQuickDisplay). The PTT Window is an event subscriber — it receives the live tick distances via PttBus.QuickExitFired and back-calculates independently. On window open it calls RefreshQuickDisplay directly to cover the "opened late" case.
Event Panel action PTT Window action
User presses [Quick] Fires PttBus.QuickExitFired with payload Receives event → back-calc ticks → update spinner
PTT-QX-T1 → Working RefreshQuickDisplay → spinner updates Already updated by event above — no action needed
Position avg price changes (add/reduce) OnPositionUpdate → RefreshQuickDisplay Subscribes to same OnPositionUpdate → re-calc
PTT Window opened (late) No action On-open: calls RefreshQuickDisplay(_leaderAccount, _instrument) to poll current live orders
Position flat (all QX orders cancelled) Spinner reverts to CopyRule.QuickT1Ticks Same — reverts to CopyRule.QuickT1Ticks

// PttContracts.cs — QuickExitEventArgs (original 6 fields + 1 new)
public sealed class QuickExitEventArgs : EventArgs
{
    public Instrument Instrument  { get; }
    public double     EntryPrice  { get; }  // pos.AveragePrice at press time
    public double     T1Price     { get; }  // absolute price of PTT-QX-T1
    public double     T2Price     { get; }  // absolute price of PTT-QX-T2
    public bool       IsLong      { get; }
    public string     OcoId       { get; }
    public double     TickSize    { get; }  // ← NEW — enables PTT Window back-calc without polling
}

// PTT Window subscriber — back-calc from event payload, no order polling needed:
// liveT1Ticks = (int)Math.Round((isLong ? T1Price-EntryPrice : EntryPrice-T1Price) / TickSize)
// liveT2Ticks = (int)Math.Round((isLong ? T2Price-EntryPrice : EntryPrice-T2Price) / TickSize)
Sync guarantee: After a [Quick] press, both the chart panel and PTT Window receive the same QuickExitEventArgs payload within the same NT8 dispatcher cycle. They independently back-calculate identical tick values from the same prices and tick size. No shared mutable state between panel and window — no race condition possible.
△ Card C  ·  Stop Strategy Gap — Current Limitation + B42 Candidate
When PTT resubmits a stop (BE, Quick Exit, flat cleanup), it passes (CustomOrder)null at CreateOrder arg12. The original ATM bracket may have had a stop strategy overlay — trail steps, auto-BE trigger, chase limit — configured on the ATM template. These overlays are silently dropped. The resubmitted stop is a plain StopMarket at the snapped price. This is an NT8 architectural constraint: Order objects do not expose the CustomOrder that was passed at submission — it is write-only. There is no API to read back the stop strategy from a live ATM order.
CustomOrder field ATM template had After PTT resubmit Gap?
Stop price e.g. 4995.00 ✓ Preserved (SnapshotStopPrice) None
AutoTrailSteps e.g. trail 2 ticks every 4 ticks ✗ Dropped — plain StopMarket Yes
AutoBreakEvenProfitTrigger e.g. move BE at +8 ticks ✗ Dropped Yes
ChaseLimit / IsChaseIfTouched e.g. chase 1 tick ✗ Dropped Yes
B42 Candidate — Portable Stop Strategy Config

Instead of snapshotting the ATM's stop overlay (impossible — write-only API), add user-configured stop strategy fields to CopyRule. Whenever PTT resubmits a stop (BE, Quick Exit, flat), it applies the user's portable overlay:

✓ Block 42  ·  PTT-COPIER-B42  ·  PTTFollowerStrategy: Native ATM Brackets on Followers  ·  ✓ COMPLETE
Today follower entries are copied naked — no stop, no target. B42 fixes this permanently. A thin headless PTTFollowerStrategy runs per follower account in NT8 Control Center. When CopyEngine signals a fill, the strategy calls AtmStrategyCreate() on its own account using the same ATM template the leader had selected. NT8 owns everything after that — trail, auto-BE-after-T1, partial exits, broker-side survival. Zero manual steps per trade.
Why a Strategy is required (ARCH-BRACKET-03 confirmed)
AtmStrategyCreate() is locked to StrategyBase. It is not available on AddOnBase or via Account. CustomOrder at arg12 of Account.CreateOrder() was probed on 2026-08-05 — NT8 accepted the order and ignored the overlay entirely. Zero bracket legs spawned. PATH B is the only path to native automated brackets on followers.
Architecture — one strategy per follower account
AccountWhat runsWho calls AtmStrategyCreateATM behaviour
Leader No change. ChartTrader as today. NT8 native — ATM template selected in ChartTrader ✓ Full ATM — trail, BE, targets, broker-side
Follower-A PTTFollowerStrategy headless in Control Center Strategy calls AtmStrategyCreate(templateName) on its own account at fill signal ✓ Full ATM — identical to leader
Follower-B PTTFollowerStrategy headless in Control Center Strategy calls AtmStrategyCreate(templateName) on its own account at fill signal ✓ Full ATM — identical to leader
One strategy instance per follower account per instrument. Each instance is account-scoped — AtmStrategyCreate() always acts on the account the strategy is attached to. No charts required. Runs headlessly. Configured once, never touched again unless a new follower account is added.
Applies to both Signal mode and Mirror mode
The PTTFollowerStrategy fires on the follower account when its entry order fills — the ATM spawns regardless of whether the entry came from Signal mode or Mirror mode copy path.
Signal design — CopyEngine → PTTFollowerStrategy
CopyEngine captures the ATM template name from the leader's ChartTrader selection at the moment the entry fires. It publishes a PttBus.FillSignal event carrying: Instrument · Account · AtmTemplateName · OrderAction · Quantity. Each PTTFollowerStrategy instance subscribes to this event and ignores signals not matching its own account. When it receives a matching signal it calls AtmStrategyCreate() immediately. 
// PTTFollowerStrategy -- OnStateChange / State.Realtime
// Subscribes to PttBus.FillSignal. Fires only when Account matches this strategy instance.
PttBus.FillSignal += OnFillSignal;

// OnFillSignal handler (fires on fill of copied entry on this follower account)
private void OnFillSignal(FillSignalEventArgs args)
{
    if (args.Account.Name != Account.Name) return;  // not my account
    if (args.Instrument.FullName != Instrument.FullName) return; // not my instrument
    AtmStrategyCreate(
        args.OrderAction,
        OrderType.Market,
        0, 0,
        TimeInForce.Gtc,
        args.EntryOrderId,          // unique entry order ID
        args.AtmTemplateName,       // same template as leader
        Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N").Substring(0, 8), // unique ATM strategy ID
        (code, msg) => { if (code != ErrorCode.NoError) Print("B42 ATM error: " + msg); }
    );
}

Bug Fix  ·  BUG-B42-QX-BE-01  ·  Quick All / BE All any-order interaction
⚠ BUG-B42-QX-BE-01  ·  Quick All then BE All (or BE All then Quick All) — second button does nothing
Pressing Quick All followed by BE All leaves followers unprotected — BE All submits a bare stop with no targets. Pressing BE All followed by Quick All leaves stale PTT-BE-* orders competing with new PTT-QX-* orders. Both sequences must work correctly regardless of order pressed.
Root cause — two directions
SequenceWhat breaksWhy
Quick All → BE All BE All submits bare stop only, no targets re-placed SnapshotTargetsLocal() in PttBreakEven looks for orders named Target1, Target2 (ATM slot names). Quick All replaced those with PTT-QX-T1, PTT-QX-T2. Snapshot finds zero targets → bare stop edge case → no targets re-placed at BE.
BE All → Quick All Stale PTT-BE-Stop + PTT-BE-Target-N compete with new PTT-QX orders CancelQxBrackets() only cancels PTT-QX-* prefix and ATM slot names (Stop1, Target1). PTT-BE-Stop and PTT-BE-Target-* are not in the cancel list — they survive and compete.
Fix — two targeted changes
FileFunctionChange
PttBreakEven.cs SnapshotTargetsLocal() Extend target recognition to also match PTT-QX-T1, PTT-QX-T2, PTT-QX-T3 as valid target orders to snapshot. These are Limit orders — price and qty are readable. BE All then re-places them at the same prices paired with BE stops.
PttQuickExit.cs + CopyEngine.cs CancelQxBrackets() Extend cancel filter to also cancel any Working order whose name starts with PTT-BE- for the given account + instrument. This ensures Quick All always starts from a clean slate regardless of whether BE All ran first.
Invariants preserved: Single-button behaviour is unchanged — BE All alone works exactly as today. Quick All alone works exactly as today. Only the two-button sequences are repaired. No new order naming conventions. No new state. Two filter extensions, nothing else.

Block 43  ·  PTT-COPIER-B43  ·  Per-Follower ATM Template ComboBox
◯ Block 43  ·  PTT-COPIER-B43  ·  Per-Follower ATM Template ComboBox  ·  PENDING_SPEC
The Named ATM TextBox is broken in the NT8 chart host: any keystroke bubbles up to the chart and opens the NT8 instrument search popup. B43 eliminates the TextBox entirely and replaces it with a proper ATM template ComboBox — one per follower row — populated from NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.AtmStrategy.AtmStrategyTemplates. The default selection is the leader’s currently selected template, but each follower can pick any template independently (e.g. Follower-A gets the $200 ATM, Follower-B gets the $400 ATM). The confusing three-way Inherit/Market/Named mode selector is also removed.
⚠ DW-B43-NAMED-TB-01 — P1 OPEN  ·  Named ATM TextBox: keystrokes bubble to NT8 chart, open instrument search popup
Symptom: When the user selects “Named” in the ATM mode ComboBox and tries to type a template name (e.g. MES $200 SL5) into the inline TextBox, each keystroke is captured by the NT8 chart host and opens the NT8 instrument search popup instead of entering text. It is impossible to type a template name by keyboard. The TextBox is effectively unusable.
Root cause (confirmed from source): In the NT8 chart panel host, keystrokes in embedded WPF TextBox controls bubble up through the WPF visual tree to the chart’s global KeyDown handler, which intercepts any printable character and opens the instrument search. The TextBox has no KeyDown / PreviewKeyDown handler to call e.Handled = true and stop the bubbling.
SurfaceFileLocationTextBox variable
Panel (followers dropdown rows) TradeCopierPanel.cs BuildCheckItemTemplate() ~L1541 namedBoxFactory (FrameworkElementFactory)
Window — static rule row TradeCopierWindow.cs BuildRuleRow() L402 namedBox
Window — dynamic rule row TradeCopierWindow.cs BuildDynamicRuleRow() L563 namedBoxDyn
Why a TextBox fix alone is insufficient: Adding KeyDown += (s,e) => e.Handled = true would stop the bubbling but would also prevent all keyboard interaction with the TextBox — the user still could not type. The correct fix is to eliminate the TextBox entirely and replace it with a ComboBox (mouse-driven selection only), which does not suffer from this keyboard-bubbling problem. A ComboBox drop-down is purely mouse/pointer operated — no keyboard events bubble to the chart host.
Design Decision — Replace the two-widget ATM cluster with one ComboBox
Before B43 (broken)

ATM [Inherit ▾] ← ComboBox (Inherit / Market / Named)
       [________] ← TextBox 80px, collapsed until "Named"

// Problems:
✗ Inherit → no brackets (B42 broken)
✗ Named TextBox → keyboard bubbles to chart
✗ User must remember exact template name
✗ Three modes confusing (Inherit ≠ Market ≠ Named)
After B43 (correct)
// Single template ComboBox — same Col 4, same 80px width
ATM [MES $200 ▾] ← populated from AtmStrategyTemplates
       MES $200 ← default = leader’s selected template
       MES $400 ← follower can override per-account
       (none) ← naked copy, no brackets

✓ Mouse-only — no keyboard bubbling
✓ Shows real template names from live NT8 list
✓ Default = leader template (one-click ready)
✓ Per-follower override (e.g. $200 vs $400)

Net change: Col 3 removed, Col 4 repurposed. Still 6 columns. Row width unchanged. OnRowGridLoaded pattern (B10-UI-01) preserved. The column count stays at 6 so OnRowGridLoaded does not need changes.
Why Inherit and Market are removed
Old modeWhat it didB43 replacement
Inherit Passed atmTemplate = null → string.Empty to FillSignalEventArgs → AtmStrategyCreate("") → NT8 silently fails → no brackets spawned. Was conceptually “use whatever the follower has set” but PTTFollowerStrategy is headless with no chart — there is nothing to inherit from. Select (none) in the template ComboBox — same naked-copy behaviour, honest label
Market Forced OrderType.Market on the copied entry order, limitPrice = 0. Had no effect on ATM bracket spawning (template was still null → no brackets). Useful only when leader placed a Limit entry and follower wants a guaranteed Market fill. Not represented in B43 UI. Can be re-added as a separate “Force Market” checkbox in a future block if the need arises. Deferred — no Director use-case reported.
Named Passed TemplateName to FillSignalEventArgs.AtmTemplateName → AtmStrategyCreate(templateName) → brackets spawned. Only mode that worked with B42. Blocked by keyboard-bubbling TextBox bug. Every non-empty selection in the template ComboBox maps to FollowerAtmMode.Named(templateName) — same engine path, better UI
ATM template ComboBox — population & default selection
Source: NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.AtmStrategy.AtmStrategyTemplates — the same static collection ChartTrader’s cbxStrategySelector is bound to. Already referenced in the B11 ATM template writer work. Decompiled: IEnumerable<AtmStrategy>; each item has a Name property (the template name string).

Default selection: When the follower row renders, pre-select the template that the leader currently has active in ChartTrader. Read via visual tree walk to cbxStrategySelector in TradeCopierAddOn.cs (already done in B11). If the walk fails or no template is selected, default to the first item in the list (or (none) if the list is empty).

Per-follower independence: Each follower row has its own ComboBox instance. Once the row renders with the leader default, the user can change each one independently. The selections are captured at “Add Followers” (Panel) or “Apply” (Window) click time — same as today. 
// Panel: BuildCheckItemTemplate() — replace namedBoxFactory with atmTemplateComboFactory
// Col 4 (was: Named TextBox collapsed; now: ATM template ComboBox always visible)

var atmTemplateCbFactory = new FrameworkElementFactory(typeof(ComboBox));
atmTemplateCbFactory.SetValue(Grid.ColumnProperty,       4);
atmTemplateCbFactory.SetValue(ComboBox.WidthProperty,    80.0);
atmTemplateCbFactory.SetValue(ComboBox.MarginProperty,   new Thickness(2));
atmTemplateCbFactory.SetValue(ComboBox.ToolTipProperty,  "ATM template for this follower");
// Loaded handler: populates from AtmStrategyTemplates + sets default to leader's selection
atmTemplateCbFactory.AddHandler(
    FrameworkElement.LoadedEvent,
    new RoutedEventHandler(OnFollowerAtmTemplateComboLoaded));
// SelectionChanged: update item.AtmModeName ("Named:<templateName>" or "Inherit" for none)
atmTemplateCbFactory.AddHandler(
    Selector.SelectionChangedEvent,
    new SelectionChangedEventHandler(OnFollowerAtmTemplateComboChanged));

// Remove the old ATM mode ComboBox factory (Col 3 — was Inherit/Market/Named)
// Remove namedBoxFactory (Col 4 — was TextBox, collapsed)
// Grid stays 6 columns (col 3 definition removed; col 4 repurposed)
// OnFollowerAtmTemplateComboLoaded — runs on UI thread (FrameworkElementFactory Loaded event)
private void OnFollowerAtmTemplateComboLoaded(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
{
    var cb = sender as ComboBox;
    if (cb == null) return;

    cb.Items.Clear();
    cb.Items.Add("(none)");    // maps to FollowerAtmMode.Inherit — naked copy, no brackets

    string leaderTemplate = GetLeaderAtmTemplateName();   // reads cbxStrategySelector

    foreach (var t in NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.AtmStrategy.AtmStrategyTemplates)
    {
        cb.Items.Add(t.Name);
    }

    // Default: leader's current template; fallback: first template; fallback: (none)
    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(leaderTemplate) && cb.Items.Contains(leaderTemplate))
        cb.SelectedItem = leaderTemplate;
    else if (cb.Items.Count > 1)
        cb.SelectedIndex = 1;   // first real template (index 0 = "(none)")
    else
        cb.SelectedIndex = 0;   // (none)
}

// GetLeaderAtmTemplateName — walks visual tree to cbxStrategySelector in ChartTrader
// Returns string.Empty if walk fails or no template selected. CYC=3.
private string GetLeaderAtmTemplateName()
{
    if (_currentChart == null) return string.Empty;
    try
    {
        var ct = _currentChart.ChartTrader;
        if (ct == null) return string.Empty;
        var cb = FindByName<ComboBox>(ct, "cbxStrategySelector");
        return cb?.SelectedValue?.ToString() ?? string.Empty;
    }
    catch { return string.Empty; }
}

Block 44  ·  PTT-COPIER-B44  ·  CopyEngine.Subscribe() wired in Panel
⚠ Block 44  ·  PTT-COPIER-B44  ·  CopyEngine.Subscribe() missing from TradeCopierPanel  ·  P0 DEFECT
CopyEngine.Subscribe() — which wires OnOrderUpdate to every account's order stream — is only called from TradeCopierWindow.OnLoaded. TradeCopierPanel (the chart panel, the primary user interface) never calls it. The engine is completely deaf to order events when the pop-out window is not open. Zero copies fire. COPY ON has no effect. Rules have no effect.
⚠ DW-B44-SUBSCRIBE-PANEL-01  —  P0 CRITICAL  ·  CopyEngine deaf when TradeCopierWindow not open
Confirmed live 2026-08-05. Director placed multiple Market Buy orders on leader account with COPY ON and rule applied. Zero follower orders appeared. NT8 Output showed no PTT-Copy error: lines — because OnOrderUpdate never fired at all.
Root cause — confirmed from source
LocationLineWhat happens
TradeCopierWindow.OnLoaded L125 _engine.Subscribe() called → OnOrderUpdate registered on every Account.All order stream ✅
TradeCopierWindow.OnClosed L156 _engine.Unsubscribe() called → OnOrderUpdate removed ⚠️
TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded — Subscribe() is never called ❌ — engine deaf to all order events
TradeCopierPanel.Detach() L490 Unsubscribe() is never called (nothing to unsubscribe) — not a bug but a gap
Call chain — why OnOrderUpdate never fires
CopyEngine.Subscribe()
    └─ foreach (Account acc in Account.All)
           acc.OrderUpdate += OnOrderUpdate;   <-- only path to the hot copy gate

OnOrderUpdate(sender, e)
    <-- NEVER CALLED because Subscribe() was never invoked from Panel
    ├─ Gate 1: _isCopyEnabled check
    ├─ Gate 2: instrument + master account match
    ├─ Gate 2.5: per-rule enabled
    ├─ Gate B: bracket drag divert
    └─ DispatchCopy → SendCopy → follower.CreateOrder + PttBus.RaiseFillSignal
Workaround (until B44 ships) — open TradeCopierWindow and keep it open
  1. Open the PTT Trade Copier pop-out window (the separate window, not the chart panel).
    This triggers TradeCopierWindow.OnLoaded → _engine.Subscribe() → OnOrderUpdate registered.
  2. Leave the window open while trading. If you close it, Unsubscribe() fires and copying stops.
  3. You can minimize the window. The chart panel remains your primary UI.
  4. Re-apply your rule in the pop-out window (enter instrument name exactly as NT8 reports it, e.g. MES 09-26 — not MES SEP26) and click Apply.
⚠ Instrument name must be the exact NT8 FullName format. Type exactly what appears in the Strategies grid "Instrument" column, e.g. MES 09-26. If unsure, check NT8 Output for the PositionStateChanged instr= diagnostic line that fires after your first fill.
Fix — B44 spec
FileChangeLine
TradeCopierPanel.cs In OnLoaded: add _engine.Subscribe(); after the existing module wire-up block (after the foreach (IPttModule m) loop). Guard: only if not already subscribed (idempotent). After ~L618
TradeCopierPanel.cs In Detach(): add _engine.Unsubscribe(); at the end of the existing unsubscribe block (before the _modules.Clear() call at ~L528). Symmetric with Subscribe(). Before ~L528
CopyEngine.cs Make Subscribe() idempotent: track a _subscribed bool. If already subscribed, no-op. Prevents double-registration if both Panel and Window are open simultaneously. L436
TradeCopierWindow.cs No change needed — Subscribe() on window open becomes redundant (Panel already subscribed) but is harmless once CopyEngine is idempotent. —
BEFORE (broken)
// TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded -- AFTER module setup
// (no Subscribe call -- engine deaf)
foreach (IPttModule m in _modules) {
    m.Initialize(this);
    // ...
}
// ← Subscribe() missing here
AFTER (fixed)
// TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded -- AFTER module setup
foreach (IPttModule m in _modules) {
    m.Initialize(this);
    // ...
}
_engine.Subscribe();  // ← B44: wire OnOrderUpdate
BEFORE (broken)
// TradeCopierPanel.Detach()
foreach (IPttModule m in _modules)
    m.Teardown();
_modules.Clear();
// ← Unsubscribe() missing
AFTER (fixed)
// TradeCopierPanel.Detach()
_engine.Unsubscribe();  // ← B44: unwire OnOrderUpdate
foreach (IPttModule m in _modules)
    m.Teardown();
_modules.Clear();
BEFORE (CopyEngine — not idempotent)
internal void Subscribe()
{
    foreach (Account acc in Account.All)
        acc.OrderUpdate += OnOrderUpdate;
    // ← no guard: double-registration
    //   if called twice
}
AFTER (idempotent)
private volatile bool _subscribed;

internal void Subscribe()
{
    if (_subscribed) return;  // ← B44: idempotent
    _subscribed = true;
    foreach (Account acc in Account.All)
        acc.OrderUpdate += OnOrderUpdate;
}

internal void Unsubscribe()
{
    if (!_subscribed) return;
    _subscribed = false;
    foreach (Account acc in Account.All)
        acc.OrderUpdate -= OnOrderUpdate;
}

✓ DW-B45-APPLY-NO-LEADER-01  —  CLOSED  ·  OnApplyRule now calls TryResolveLeaderAccount() — "No leader" error gone
Confirmed live 2026-08-05. Panel status bar shows "No leader -- select account in ChartTrader." even though Sim101 is visibly selected in the ChartTrader Account dropdown. AddRule is never called. No follower orders fire.
Root cause
NT8 sometimes binds the Account ComboBox with a string SelectedItem instead of an Account object at attach time (HOTFIX-B30-F1). WireLeaderAccount casts SelectedItem as Account → null → _leaderAccount stays null.
Every button handler (Trim, Flatten, BE, QuickExit etc.) recovers via:
_leaderAccount = _leaderAccount ?? TryResolveLeaderAccount();
OnApplyRule is the only handler that does NOT call TryResolveLeaderAccount(). It hits the null guard at L1824 and returns immediately.
Fix — TradeCopierPanel.cs, OnApplyRule (~L1824)
BEFORE (broken)
private void OnApplyRule(...)
{
    if (_leaderAccount == null)
    {
        _statusText.Text = "No leader...";
        return;
    }
AFTER (fixed)
private void OnApplyRule(...)
{
    // B45 T1: same late-resolve as all other button handlers
    _leaderAccount = _leaderAccount
        ?? TryResolveLeaderAccount();
    if (_leaderAccount == null)
    {
        _statusText.Text = "No leader...";
        return;
    }
✓ DW-B45-FOLLOWER-STARTBEHAVIOR-02  —  CLOSED  ·  PttFollowerStrategy now sets StartBehavior=ImmediatelySubmit — no more Disable/re-Enable cycle
Confirmed live 2026-08-05. NT8 Output shows:
Enabling NinjaScript strategy 'PttFollowerStrategy/382222633'...
Disabling NinjaScript strategy 'PttFollowerStrategy/382222633'
Enabling NinjaScript strategy 'PttFollowerStrategy/382222633'...
The StartBehavior=WaitUntilFlat in the strategy output confirms the cause. When Sim102 already has an open position and the strategy restarts (after F5 or NT8 reload), NT8 sees the existing position and temporarily disables the strategy to wait for flat. During that window, PttBus.FillSignal is unsubscribed → any fill signal fired in that brief period is silently dropped → no ATM brackets spawned.
Fix — PttFollowerStrategy.cs, SetDefaults (~L33)
BEFORE (broken)
if (State == State.SetDefaults)
{
    Name            = "PTTFollowerStrategy";
    Calculate       = Calculate.OnBarClose;
    BarsRequiredToTrade = 0;
    IsExitOnSessionCloseStrategy = false;
    // ← StartBehavior not set
    // defaults to WaitUntilFlat
}
AFTER (fixed)
if (State == State.SetDefaults)
{
    Name            = "PTTFollowerStrategy";
    Calculate       = Calculate.OnBarClose;
    BarsRequiredToTrade = 0;
    IsExitOnSessionCloseStrategy = false;
    // B45 T2: never pause on existing position
    StartBehavior   =
        StartBehavior.ImmediatelySubmit;
}
NT8 enum: NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.StartBehavior.ImmediatelySubmit — strategy goes straight to State.Realtime regardless of existing position. ⚠ DW-B47-BE-FOLLOWER-SCOPE  —  P0  ·  BE ALL / Quick ALL cancels follower ATM brackets
Confirmed live 2026-08-07. NT8 Output showed:
[BE] CancelStaleBrackets: cancelled 4 bracket orders
[BE] CancelStaleBrackets: cancelled 3 bracket orders
[BE] CancelStaleBrackets: cancelled 4 bracket orders

CancelStaleBrackets is called from the BE ALL path and iterates every account in the copy rule — including Sim102 (the follower). It treats Sim102's ATM Stop/Target brackets as "stale" and cancels them. 17 bracket order cancellations fired. Sim102 was left with a bare BuyToCover stop and no targets.

Follower accounts must be excluded from the leader's BE/flatten/cancel scope. The BE and Quick buttons must only operate on _leaderAccount.
Fix specification
In CancelStaleBrackets, SubmitBeStop, and any method that iterates accounts for the BE / Quick / flatten paths: filter to account == _leaderAccount only. Follower accounts are managed exclusively by PTTFollowerStrategy — the panel must never reach into them.
◯ DW-B47-AUTO-RULE-01  —  P1  ·  Remove Apply button — auto-apply on checkbox + ATM combo change
Director decision 2026-08-07: The Apply button step is redundant. Rules already persist to XML (%UserDataDir%\PropTraderTools\copy_rules.xml) — the real problem was the B46 strategy-kill loop making setup feel ephemeral. Once B46 ships, the rule persists through restarts automatically.

Desired flow: Open panel → check Sim102 ✅ + pick ATM from same row → rule is live immediately. No Apply button.
Architecture — TryAutoApply() (CYC=3)
private void TryAutoApply()
{
    _leaderAccount = _leaderAccount ?? TryResolveLeaderAccount();
    if (_leaderAccount == null) return;           // branch 1 — not yet ready
    if (_instrument == null) return;               // branch 2 — not yet ready
    var followers = GetSelectedFollowers();
    if (followers.Length == 0)                     // branch 3 — nothing checked
    {
        if (_statusText != null)
            _statusText.Text = "No followers selected.";
        return;
    }
    // Same logic as OnApplyRule — build atmMap, call engine.AddRule, save immediately
    var atmMap   = BuildAtmMap(followers);
    var multipliers = BuildMultipliers(followers);
    _engine.AddRule(_instrument.FullName, _leaderAccount, followers, multipliers, atmMap);
    _engine.SaveRules();   // ← persist immediately (not just on NT8 shutdown)
    if (_statusText != null)
        _statusText.Text = "Rule: " + _instrument.FullName
                         + " leader=" + _leaderAccount.Name;
}
Triggered from two existing handlers: OnFollowerChecked and OnFollowerAtmTemplateComboChanged — both call TryAutoApply() instead of waiting for the button.

The Apply button is hidden, not deleted — kept as a safe fallback for recovery.

B48 — Test File Isolation: NT8 F5 Path Fix PIPELINE_COMPLETE 2026-08-07
Context & Root Cause

NinjaTrader 8's AddOns folder uses a flat, non-recursive scan at F5 compile time. Any *.cs file placed in the flat root of src/PropTraderTools/ is hard-linked to NT8's bin and compiled by NT8's Roslyn fork. xUnit test files (B46Tests.cs, B47Tests.cs, etc.) reference Xunit and Assert — assemblies not available in NT8's host process. Result: CS0246 "The type or namespace name 'Xunit' could not be found" and CS0103 "The name 'Assert' does not exist" at every F5. This was the blocking compilation error the Director saw on 2026-08-07.

Fix scope: Move all B42–B46Tests.cs files from the flat root into a Tests\ subfolder. NT8 does not recurse into subdirectories — the test files become invisible to the NT8 compiler while remaining fully visible to dotnet build via the updated PropTraderTools.csproj entries.

⚠ 2026-08-07 03:25 PM — Compilation Error Forensics
Director's NT8 Grid CSV at 2026-08-07 03:25 PM showed 13 errors all from B46Tests.cs: CS0246 (Xunit, FactAttribute), CS0103 (Assert).
Root Cause
NT8 was running with B46Tests.cs still in the NT8 AddOns hard-link folder (placed there during B46-LaneA before the B48 isolation fix was pulled). The Director had not yet pulled the B48 branch or re-run verify_links.ps1. This is a stale deploy artefact, not a regression — the B48 fix was already in the wave workspace. Once B48 is pulled and F5 is run, the Tests\ isolation removes all xUnit references from NT8's compile path.
Resolution Steps
  1. Pull 001-agent-arena-platform branch to local wave workspace.
  2. Run powershell -File scripts\verify_links.ps1 -Fix — removes stale NT8 hard-links for B46Tests.cs and B47Tests.cs (SKIPPED=7 confirms clean state).
  3. NT8 → Tools → Edit NinjaScript → Compile (F5).
  4. Confirm NT8 Output shows PTT-COPIER B47 | panel-ux-redesign | 2026-08-07 with zero errors.
  5. Proceed with DW-B46-01 acceptance test (DW-B42-05 re-run).

Root cause — REVISED (2026-08-09, screenshots + CSV forensics):

Prior conclusion was wrong. Earlier diagnosis assumed "Sim102 had zero executions." This was because the CSVs only captured Sim101. Sim102 orders were being created — but they never reached the exchange.

Actual root cause: PttFollowerStrategy managed framework conflict.
The log confirms PttFollowerStrategy runs with IsUnmanaged=False and EntriesPerDirection=1. NT's managed order framework owns the strategy's entry order slots. When CopyEngine calls account.CreateOrder() + Submit() externally on Sim102, the framework sees a conflict with the strategy's own entry slot and silently holds the order at Initialized — it never reaches the exchange and never fills.

Cancel hangs permanently (DW-B53-03).
Calling Cancel() on a strategy-owned order from the CopyEngine AddOn context hits a thread/ownership conflict. NT accepts the cancel request but never resolves it — the order stays Cancel pending in the Orders tab forever. The only recovery is an account reset. This is a symptom of DW-B53-01: fix the ownership model and cancel works natively.

Fix decision: remove PttFollowerStrategy entirely (Option B).
CopyEngine places follower entry orders directly as an AddOn — no strategy running on follower accounts at all. On follower entry fill, CopyEngine calls AtmStrategyCreate directly. Cancel goes via acc.Cancel() on AddOn-owned orders — resolves cleanly. Users need zero per-follower strategy setup. The PTT AddOn window is the only thing that needs to be running.

Architecture after B53 LaneA:
Zero strategies need to be running on follower accounts. The PTT AddOn window is the sole active component. It subscribes to Account.All.OrderUpdate, places follower orders as a first-class NT AddOn citizen, owns those orders outright, and invokes AtmStrategyCreate on fill. Cancel, change, and ATM all work through the standard AddOn API — no managed strategy framework involved on the follower side. This is the parasitic infrastructure principle: NT owns ATM, routing, and position tracking. We own one event hook and one order per follower entry.
◆ Design Pillar — Checkbox = Full Activation (B53+)

Checking a follower account checkbox is the complete setup gesture. No Control Center → Strategies tab. No strategy picker. No account/instrument selector. No Run button. The checkbox does everything.

This is the Zero-Launch UX pillar applied to follower accounts. Before B53, the user had to:
  1. Open Control Center → Strategies
  2. Add PTTFollowerStrategy
  3. Set account + instrument + click Run
  4. Repeat per follower account per instrument
After B53, the user ticks the checkbox in the PTT scrollbox — done. CopyEngine owns the follower order slot directly. AtmStrategyCreate fires on fill. Cancel resolves. Everything works through the standard AddOn API.

Analogous to NT's own strategy activation pattern: NT activates a strategy by toggling it on in Strategies tab (a checkbox). PTT activates a follower account by toggling it on in the copier scrollbox (a checkbox). Both are checkbox → active. The UX mental model is identical — one is for strategies, one is for accounts, both use checkmarks as the sole activation gesture.

Future note: If per-follower OnBarUpdate logic is ever needed (e.g., dynamic trailing unique to each follower), a strategy-per-follower pattern would re-enter scope. At that point, checkbox → auto-start of a companion strategy instance would be the correct implementation — not a separate Strategies tab setup. Until that need arises, CopyEngine direct ownership is strictly simpler and correct.

CORE REQUIREMENT — Live-Truth Sync Contract

Every PTT button on every surface must reflect live engine state at all times.
The PTT Add-On window and the ChartTrader panel are two viewports into one engine. Neither surface owns truth. CopyEngine is the single source of truth.

Current failure modes (post-B53, pre-B54):
  • F5 reload desync (DW-B54-03 P0): After F5, CopyEngine singleton resets _isCopyEnabled = false (default). The ChartTrader panel's local _copyEnabled field is a stale carry-over from the previous session. The WPF button visually reads "COPY ON" but the engine is OFF. No SetEnabled(true) call is ever made during OnLoaded. Gate 1 in OnOrderUpdate blocks every copy attempt silently.
  • Window re-open desync: If the Add-On window is closed and re-opened, the new window instance reads its own stale local field rather than querying _engine.IsEnabled.
  • Rule enabled toggle: When a rule's enabled state changes in the engine (e.g. programmatic or from one surface), the other surface's toggle may not reflect it until the user interacts.

The contract (non-negotiable):
  • Engine is authority. CopyEngine.IsEnabled is the ground truth. No surface stores its own authoritative copy of this value.
  • On surface creation / OnLoaded: every surface MUST read current engine state and paint buttons accordingly — ApplyCopyState(_engine.IsEnabled) called unconditionally in OnLoaded.
  • On engine state change: engine fires CopyEnabledChanged (already exists, B20 T2). All subscribed surfaces update via Dispatcher.InvokeAsync — no polling, no timer.
  • On persistence load (F5 / startup): LoadRules() must restore _isCopyEnabled from copy_rules.xml AND immediately call CopyEnabledChanged so any already-loaded surface snaps to restored state.
  • No surface ever sets its own button colour directly. Every visual update goes through ApplyCopyState(bool) — a single private method on each surface. The engine event calls it. OnLoaded calls it. Nothing else does.
DW-B54-03  ·  P0  ·  PTT window + ChartTrader panel buttons NOT in sync with live engine state
DimensionDetail
Symptom After F5 recompile, or after closing + reopening the PTT Add-On window: the Copy ON button appears lit/green but no orders are ever copied. Workaround: click COPY OFF, then COPY ON to force SetEnabled(true). This should never be required — the UI must match reality automatically.
Root cause Three independent failures:

(A) OnLoaded never reads engine state. Both TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded and TradeCopierWindow.OnLoaded initialise the button from a local _copyEnabled field (default = false) rather than from _engine.IsEnabled. On F5, the engine is a new singleton (IsEnabled = false). The panel is a new WPF object (local field = false too) — visually correct by accident, but the WPF button colour from the previous panel instance may persist in the visual tree until the new panel redraws (NT8 WPF reuse quirk).

(B) copy_rules.xml does not persist copy-enabled state. SaveRules() writes CopyRule entries but not the global copy-enabled bool. On reload, the engine always starts disabled regardless of whether the user had Copy ON when NT closed.

(C) CopyEnabledChanged not fired after LoadRules. Even if we fix (B), after LoadRules() restores _isCopyEnabled = true, no event fires — surfaces loaded before the engine completes LoadRules() never get the signal.
Fix — CopyEngine.cs 1. Persist copy-enabled in XML DTO.
Add [XmlElement] public bool CopyEnabled { get; set; } to the serialization DTO (or root element). SaveRules() writes it. LoadRules() reads it and sets _isCopyEnabled before firing the event.

2. Fire CopyEnabledChanged at end of LoadRules.
CopyEnabledChanged?.Invoke(_isCopyEnabled); at the very end of LoadRules(). Surfaces already subscribed by the time LoadRules runs (AddOn.OnInitialize → inject panel → subscribe → then LoadRules) will receive the event. Late-loading surfaces (window opened after LoadRules) use fix #3.

3. ApplyCopyState() on every OnLoaded.
Both TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded and TradeCopierWindow.OnLoaded: subscribe to CopyEnabledChanged (already done, B20), then immediately call ApplyCopyState(_engine.IsEnabled) to snap to current truth. Order does not matter — event covers future changes, direct read covers present state.
Fix — TradeCopierPanel.cs ApplyCopyState(bool enabled) — private method:
_copyEnabled = enabled;
Dispatcher.InvokeAsync(() => {
  _copyToggleBtn.Content = enabled ? "COPY ON" : "COPY OFF";
  _copyToggleBtn.Background = enabled ? GreenBrush : DimBrush;
});

Replace all direct button mutations with calls to ApplyCopyState(). In OnLoaded: after subscribing, call ApplyCopyState(_engine.IsEnabled). DW-B54-01  ·  P0  ·  AtmStrategyCreate AddOn API gated #if NT8_ADDON_ATM (NT8-055 open)
DimensionDetail
Symptom ATM brackets do not appear on Sim102 after follower entry fills. The call to AtmStrategyCreate() in TryAttachAtmToFollower is gated behind #if NT8_ADDON_ATM and never compiles by default. The NT8-055 rule documents that the correct AddOn path for ATM creation is unknown — NinjaScript strategies use AtmStrategyCreate() as a protected virtual method; AddOns do not inherit that path.
Research required Director research item (escalated B53-LaneA). Options to investigate:

Option A — NinjaTrader.NinjaScript namespace ATM via Reflection:
Account.AtmStrategyCreate() exists on the Account type in some NT8 builds. Probe via account.GetType().GetMethod("AtmStrategyCreate").

Option B — NinjaTrader.Cbi.AtmStrategy static factory:
Check if NinjaTrader.Cbi.AtmStrategy exposes a static Create() or Submit() method accessible from AddOn context.

Option C — AtmStrategy via OrderEntryParameter:
Account.CreateOrder() accepts OrderEntryParameter. Probe whether passing an ATM template name there causes NT8 to auto-attach an ATM on fill.

Option D — Defer ATM to user:
User selects ATM template in ChartTrader before placing leader entry. NT8 copies the ATM selection to the follower account order automatically via the AddOn order path. Lowest-effort — test whether NT8 already does this natively for AddOn-placed orders.
Status Director research item NT8-055 rule documented in docs/standards/NT8_COMPILER_RULES.md. Unblock this before any B54 LaneA engineer work on ATM attachment. The #if NT8_ADDON_ATM gate keeps the build clean until the API path is confirmed.

Live-Truth Sync — State Machine (reference)
── CopyEngine (single source of truth) ─────────────────────────────────────

  IsEnabled (volatile bool)          ← authoritative state
  _isCopyEnabled persisted in XML    ← survives F5 / NT restart

  SetEnabled(bool value):
    _isCopyEnabled = value
    CopyEnabledChanged?.Invoke(value) ← all surfaces update

  LoadRules():
    _isCopyEnabled = dto.CopyEnabled   ← restore from XML
    CopyEnabledChanged?.Invoke(_isCopyEnabled) ← snap subscribed surfaces

  SaveRules():
    dto.CopyEnabled = _isCopyEnabled   ← persist before NT close

── TradeCopierPanel / TradeCopierWindow ─────────────────────────────────────

  OnLoaded():
    _engine.CopyEnabledChanged += ApplyCopyState  ← subscribe for future changes
    ApplyCopyState(_engine.IsEnabled)             ← snap to current truth NOW

  OnCopyToggle() / OnGlobalToggle():
    _engine.SetEnabled(!_engine.IsEnabled)        ← engine owns the change
    // DO NOT call ApplyCopyState here — event will do it

  ApplyCopyState(bool enabled):
    _copyEnabled = enabled
    Dispatcher.InvokeAsync(() => {
      btnCopyToggle.Content    = enabled ? "COPY ON" : "COPY OFF"
      btnCopyToggle.Background = enabled ? GreenBrush : DimBrush
    })

  Detach() / OnWindowClosed():
    _engine.CopyEnabledChanged -= ApplyCopyState  ← unsubscribe (already done B20)

── Invariant ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ∀ surface s at any time t:
    s.btnCopyToggle.IsGreen ↔ CopyEngine.Instance.IsEnabled
  Holds after: F5, window re-open, NT cold start, LoadRules, any SetEnabled call.

LANE A  ·  DW-B43-02 P1  ·  GetLeaderAtmTemplateName reads wrong value — Clone ATM pre-population broken
DimensionDetail
Symptom In Clone mode, each follower row's ATM template ComboBox always shows (none) instead of the leader's currently selected ATM template (e.g. "MES $200"). The user must manually select the template on every follower row — the auto-population that Clone mode promises does not work.
Root cause GetLeaderAtmTemplateName() in TradeCopierPanel.cs reads cb.SelectedValue on the cbxStrategySelector ComboBox.

NT8 binds cbxStrategySelector to AtmStrategyTemplates (a static collection of template name strings). SelectedValue is only populated when a SelectedValuePath is set on the ComboBox — if NT8 does not set one, SelectedValue is always null regardless of what is selected.

SelectedItem is the correct read path — it returns the selected string directly from the collection.
Fix In GetLeaderAtmTemplateName(), change line:
return cb?.SelectedValue?.ToString() ?? string.Empty;
to:
return cb?.SelectedItem?.ToString() ?? string.Empty;

One character change. CYC stays at 3. No other files touched. If live test reveals SelectedItem also returns null (WPF timing issue on panel load), add a SelectionChanged subscription to cache the value live — but try the one-liner first.
Test T_B55A_01: GetLeaderAtmTemplateName_ReturnsEmpty_WhenChartIsNull — _currentChart = null → returns string.Empty (already covered by T_B43_04 — verify it still passes, no new test needed for the null path).

T_B55A_01 (new): Mock a ComboBox with SelectedItem = "MES $200" and SelectedValue = null → GetLeaderAtmTemplateName() returns "MES $200".
Note: method is private — test via reflection (same pattern as B53 LaneA tests) or extract to internal for testability.
DW-B50-01 unblock After B55-LaneA ships, Director runs live test: open chart with ATM template "MES $200" selected in ChartTrader → open PTT panel in Clone mode → tick a follower checkbox → follower ATM ComboBox must show "MES $200" pre-populated. If pass → DW-B50-01 CLOSED. If fail → new diagnosis.
LANE B  ·  DW-B47-05 P2  ·  FindRule returns null — JS-002 violation, null contract undocumented
DimensionDetail
Violation FindRule(Instrument) in CopyEngine.cs returns null when _rules is empty or has no entry matching instrument.FullName. JS-002 bans implicit null returns — the contract must be explicit and callers must be provably guarded.

Runtime risk is LOW — every existing call site already has an explicit null guard (if (rule == null) return; or null-conditional ?.FindRule()). This is a code-contract debt item, not a live crash risk.
Fix Option chosen: add [return: MaybeNull] annotation + doc comment. NT8 targets .NET Framework 4.8 — System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.MaybeNullAttribute is available in .NET Standard 2.1 shim (check if available; if not, use inline XML doc). Do NOT change the return type to a nullable value type or introduce Option<T> — that would require changing all 6+ call sites and risks breaking the build on NT8's pre-C#9 compiler (NT8-002 / NT8-003 class).

Minimal safe fix:
  1. Add XML doc comment to FindRule: /// <returns>Matching rule, or null if no rule exists for this instrument. Callers MUST null-check.</returns>
  2. Confirm every call site has explicit null guard — grep for FindRule( across all src/ — each must have if (rule == null) or ?. on the same or next line.
  3. Add 1 new [Fact] that documents and locks the null-return contract: FindRule_ReturnsNull_WhenNoRules — engine with empty rules list, call FindRule(instrument) via reflection, assert result is null.
Call sites to audit All occurrences of FindRule( in src/PropTraderTools/:
— AllAccounts() in CopyEngine.cs — ResolveQuickTicks() in PttQuickExit.cs — PttTightenStop.cs (rule null → hard return)
Each must show explicit guard. ptt-verifier confirms with SCAN-08 (new): grep -n "FindRule(" src/ --include=*.cs then manually verify each result has guard on following line.

DW-B56-01  ·  P0  ·  Follower limit order stuck Initialized — Gate 3 fires only on Submitted, but NT8 limit orders never reach Submitted
DimensionDetail
Symptom Place a limit Buy on leader (Sim101). Follower order (Sim102) appears in Account Data grid with state "Initialized" and stays there indefinitely. When leader fills, follower does not fill. When leader order is canceled or closed, follower's Initialized order does not cancel automatically. The copy appears to fire (follower order is created) but then goes silent.
Root cause Gate 3 in DispatchCopy requires OrderState.Submitted.

NT8 order state lifecycle for a limit order placed via ChartTrader (AddOn CreateOrder):
Initialized → Accepted → Working → Filled / Cancelled

NT8 order state lifecycle for a market order:
Initialized → Submitted → Accepted → Working → Filled

Limit orders placed via AddOn Account.CreateOrder() skip the Submitted state entirely. They go directly Initialized → Accepted. Gate 3 (if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Submitted) return;) therefore blocks every limit order copy attempt after the initial follower order is placed. The engine receives the leader's Accepted, Working, and Filled events but each one is gated out by Gate 3, so no follower fill is triggered and no cancel is triggered when the leader order closes.

Why follower cancel also fails: CancelOneAccount is called from button clicks (Trim [x], Flatten) or the CancelPendingEntries path, but it is NOT called when a leader order transitions to Cancelled state. There is no handler that fires CancelFollowerOrders(leaderOrder) on leader Cancelled — so the follower's Initialized order lingers forever.
Fix Two-part fix in CopyEngine.cs:

Part A — Gate 3: accept Accepted state for limit orders.
Change Gate 3 from:
if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Submitted) return;
To:
if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Submitted && order.OrderState != OrderState.Accepted) return;
OR (cleaner, extracted predicate):
private static bool IsDispatchTriggerState(Order order)
    => order.OrderState == OrderState.Submitted     // market orders
    || order.OrderState == OrderState.Accepted;     // limit orders (skip Submitted)
Gate 3 becomes: if (!IsDispatchTriggerState(order)) return;

Part B — Cancel follower when leader is cancelled.
In OnOrderUpdate, after all gates pass, add a handler for leader Cancelled state:
if (order.OrderState == OrderState.Cancelled)
{
    // Cancel all matching Initialized/Working follower entry orders
    foreach (var acc in matchedRule.Value.FollowerAccounts)
    {
        if (acc == null) continue;
        CancelOneAccount(acc, order.Instrument);
    }
    return;
}
This goes BEFORE the existing Gate B (bracket detection) so a leader cancel propagates to followers regardless of bracket state.

Note: The dedup cache (Gate 5) prevents double-firing if Accepted fires twice. Confirm by testing: place limit → cancel → place again. The second placement must produce a new follower order.
Test coverage T_B56_01: IsDispatchTriggerState returns true for Submitted and Accepted, false for Initialized/Working/Filled/Cancelled.
T_B56_02: DispatchCopy called for leader in Accepted state → SendCopy fires for follower (via reflection / mock account). Previously would have returned at Gate 3.
Acceptance gate F5 → place limit Buy on Sim101 → Sim102 follower order appears Working (not stuck Initialized) → Sim101 fills → Sim102 fills. Then: place limit → cancel on Sim101 → Sim102 entry cancels immediately.
DW-B56-02  ·  P1  ·  Rule rows not refreshed from engine state after F5 — Window and Panel always show hardcoded initial row
DimensionDetail
Symptom PTT Window opens and shows only the static initial rule row (e.g. "MES" hardcoded at construction). ChartTrader panel similarly shows no rules despite rules existing in copy_rules.xml. User added a rule and clicked Apply — the rule was saved and copy worked in the prior session, but after F5 the rule row is not restored in the UI even though the engine loaded it from XML.
Root cause TradeCopierWindow.cs line 270: _rulesPanel.Children.Add(BuildRuleRow("MES")); This hardcodes exactly one rule row at construction time. When LoadRules() fires in OnLoaded (line 126), it populates CopyEngine._rules with the saved rules, but nothing in the Window rebuilds _rulesPanel to match. The Window has no RulesChanged event subscription or post-load refresh call.

Same pattern in TradeCopierPanel.cs: the panel builds its UI rows statically at construction; it does not reconstruct rows from the post-LoadRules engine state.
Fix options Option A (preferred — event-driven):
Add a RulesLoaded event to CopyEngine that fires at end of LoadRules() with the list of loaded instrument names. Both Window and Panel subscribe in OnLoaded and rebuild their rule rows via Dispatcher.InvokeAsync.

Option B (simpler — post-load rebuild):
After CopyEngine.Instance.LoadRules() in OnLoaded, immediately call RefreshRuleRows() which clears _rulesPanel.Children and rebuilds one row per instrument in _engine.GetRuleInstruments() (add this method to CopyEngine: returns IEnumerable<string> of distinct instrument names in _rules). Simpler: no new event, synchronous, easier to verify.

Director choice: Option B is recommended for minimal change surface. Assign to B56 LaneB.
DW-B56-03  ·  P1  ·  Clone mode missing from PTT Window ComboBox — engine enum missing Clone=2 value
DimensionDetail
Symptom PTT Window Copy Mode ComboBox (lines 212–213 of TradeCopierWindow.cs) shows only "Signal (default)" and "Mirror". "Clone" is not present. Director cannot select Clone mode from the Window.
Root cause Two related gaps:

Gap 1 — CopyEngine enum: CopyEngine.cs line 77: internal enum CopyMode { Signal = 0, Mirror = 1 } — Clone = 2 is missing. TradeCopierPanel.cs calls SetCopyMode(CopyMode.Clone) — this currently references an undefined enum member and should be a compile error. If it compiles, it means CopyMode.Clone was added to the panel file as a local extension or the enum was patched without a build. Verify with grep.

Gap 2 — Window ComboBox: TradeCopierWindow.cs lines 212–213 only populate two items. The Window was never updated when Clone mode was added to the Panel in B50.
Fix 1. Add Clone = 2 to CopyEngine.cs enum (if not already present after thorough grep):
internal enum CopyMode { Signal = 0, Mirror = 1, Clone = 2 }

2. Add "Clone" item to Window ComboBox (TradeCopierWindow.cs after line 213):
modeCb.Items.Add("Clone");

3. Handle Clone in OnCopyModeComboChanged in Window (add index 2 case):
case 2: CopyEngine.Instance.SetCopyMode(CopyMode.Clone); break;
4. Sync ATM template visibility: when Clone is selected in Window, the per-rule ATM ComboBoxes should be shown (same as Panel behavior). Implement UpdateAtmColumnVisibility(bool show) in Window matching the Panel pattern.
DW-B56-04  ·  P2  ·  Dedup cache (Gate 5) may block re-placed limit after cancel if orderId recycled
DimensionDetail
Context Director scenario: place limit → cancel → place another limit. The second placement has a new orderId. Gate 5 (IsDedup(order.OrderId.ToString())) caches orderId strings and rejects duplicates. Risk: if NT8 recycles orderIds within a session (e.g. reset counter post-cancel), the second placement is deduped and ignored. Runtime risk is LOW — NT8 typically increments orderId monotonically per session. Confirm by adding orderId to the StatusUpdate log on each DispatchCopy pass-through. If orderId is always unique per placement, this is a non-issue.
Resolution Add StatusUpdate?.Invoke("DispatchCopy: orderId=" + order.OrderId); at Gate 5 pass-through. Director confirms during live test: two consecutive placement events show two distinct orderIds. If IDs are unique — DW-B56-04 CLOSED by observation. If IDs recycle — scope dedup cache eviction to CancelledIds set.

DW-B79 — BE-ALL Bracket Recovery Architecture (v8, HEAD 27dbe9a3)
ROOT CAUSE — Confirmed SIM 2026-08-19

When the leader re-enters after QX→BE-ALL, NT8’s StartAtmStrategy() sweep cancels all follower working orders — including the PTT-BE-Stop-* / PTT-BE-Target-* OCO brackets that MoveStopToBreakEven just placed. The follower is left holding an open position with no bracket protection.

OnOrderUpdate dispatch chain (v8)
Call Responsibility
TryFireFollowerBeRetry(e) Fires MoveStopToBreakEven the instant Target1..Target9 or PTT-QX-T* goes Working on a follower that has a pending BE slot. Atomic TryRemove claim gate — exactly one path wins.
TryEvictFollowerBeSlot(e) Clears the slot and unconditionally resets _beReplaceAttempts counter when follower goes flat (v8 fix: decoupled from slot existence).
TryReplacePttBeBrackets(order) Triggered when PTT-BE-Stop-* is Cancelled and follower has open position. Registers slot + queues 500ms DispatcherTimer fallback. Max 3 attempts per trade per account.
Shared state (CopyEngine fields)
Field Purpose
_pendingFollowerBeSlots
ConcurrentDictionary<string, PendingFollowerBeSlot>		 One slot per account name. Consumed atomically by the first path to call TryRemove (event-driven or timer). Both paths are no-ops if slot already gone.
_beReplaceAttempts
ConcurrentDictionary<string, int>		 Counts slot registrations per account per trade. Cap = 3. Reset unconditionally by TryEvictFollowerBeSlot when flat (not gated on slot presence).
QueueBeRetryFallback design (v7 fix):
OnOrderUpdate fires on NT8’s background order-update thread. A DispatcherTimer created on a background thread uses that thread’s dispatcher, which never pumps — Tick never fires. Fix: wrap timer construction in Application.Current.Dispatcher.InvokeAsync() so the timer runs on the WPF UI thread. Same pattern as RaiseBeBufferChanged.
delayMs=500 (ATM-sweep path — new ATM brackets go Working before the PTT-BE-Stop cancel arrives, so event-driven misses; 500ms fires after ATM fully settled).

DW-B79-CANCEL-01  ·  P1  ·  ✓ CLOSED — Fixed in DW-B79-04  ·  commit 5925b618  ·  “Cancellation rejected” popup eliminated
Symptom: NT8 popup “Cancellation rejected [side] [qty] StopMarket @ [price]” during live trading. Triggered when NT8’s native ATM auto-breakeven modified a stop price mid-position. Unacceptable for commercial release — now fixed.

Root cause (confirmed, CopyEngine.cs L713):
1. NT8 ATM auto-BE sends a price-mod request — stop enters ChangeSubmitted state
2. CancelAllAccountOrders stateOk included ChangeSubmitted → stop added to cancel list
3. Broker receives cancel after stop already filled → rejects → NT8 surfaces as async UI popup
4. catch { } around acc.Cancel() does NOT suppress async OMS rejection events

Fix applied (CopyEngine.cs L706–734, commit 5925b618):
TICKET-1a: Removed OrderState.ChangeSubmitted from stateOk (L719–722). Now 4 terms only.
TICKET-1b: Added toCancel.RemoveAll(o => Filled || Cancelled) race guard before acc.Cancel() (L730–731).

stateOk BEFORE:
Working || Initialized || Submitted || Accepted || ChangeSubmitted
stateOk AFTER:
Working || Initialized || Submitted || Accepted
Safety: No position-protection gap. ChangeSubmitted orders complete modification, land in Working, then cancelled by ATM OCO when PTT-Flatten fills.
Frozen intentionally: ChangeSubmitted read at L2668 in MoveStopToBreakEven — different purpose (reading target prices for OCO pair creation, not cancelling). Not touched.

New test: CancelAllAccountOrders_SkipsChangeSubmittedOrders — IL ldsfld token scan verifies ChangeSubmitted absent from compiled method body; asserts 4 valid states present.

DW-B79-COSMETIC-01 — P3 Deferred — RemoveAll race guard missing from CancelQxBrackets + CancelStaleBracketsLocal
Context: DW-B79-04 fixed CancelAllAccountOrders with two changes: (1) removed ChangeSubmitted from stateOk, and (2) added a RemoveAll(Filled || Cancelled) race guard before acc.Cancel(). The question is whether these fixes apply to all buttons — BE, BE-ALL, QX, QX-ALL — or only Flatten. The answer requires tracing each button to its cancel method.

Cancel method per button:
Button Cancel method called File
Flatten / Flatten-ALL CancelAllAccountOrders CopyEngine.cs L713
QX button / QX-ALL button CancelQxBrackets (2-param + 3-param) CopyEngine.cs L613, L677
BE button / BE-ALL button CancelStaleBracketsLocal PttBreakEven.cs L171
Cancel-entries (Shift+C) CancelOneAccount CopyEngine.cs L2301
Fix 1 — ChangeSubmitted removal: uniformly correct across all buttons.
ChangeSubmitted was only ever present in CancelAllAccountOrders. CancelQxBrackets, CancelStaleBracketsLocal, and CancelOneAccount never included it in their stateOk, so the original popup root cause (NT8 auto-BE sends price-mod → stop enters ChangeSubmitted → included in cancel list → async broker rejection) could not happen through BE button, BE-ALL, QX button, or QX-ALL. No gap — those paths were never broken in this way.

Fix 2 — RemoveAll race guard: NOT applied to QX or BE cancel paths.
The race guard was only added to CancelAllAccountOrders (Flatten path). The QX and BE cancel methods do not have it:
// CancelAllAccountOrders (Flatten path) — DW-B79-04 GUARDED ✓
toCancel.RemoveAll(o => o.OrderState == OrderState.Filled
                      || o.OrderState == OrderState.Cancelled);
try { acc.Cancel(toCancel); } catch { }

// CancelQxBrackets (QX button + QX-ALL) — NO race guard ✗
try { acc.Cancel(stale.ToArray()); } catch { }

// CancelStaleBracketsLocal (BE button + BE-ALL) — NO race guard ✗
try { acc.Cancel(stale.ToArray()); } catch { }
Practical severity: The race requires an order to fill in the narrow window (<1ms) between list construction and the cancel call. The original popup was observed exactly once in hundreds of sessions, on the Flatten/QX path. The BE and QX cancel paths are equally susceptible in theory, though the Flatten path (which cancels all orders including ATM stops) is the highest-exposure path because it runs when an active position is being closed — exactly when ATM auto-BE is most likely to be modifying a stop. No popup has been observed from the QX or BE cancel paths.

Proposed fix (spec only — not ready for pipeline): Apply the same one-line guard to both unguarded methods:
// CancelQxBrackets (CopyEngine.cs L629 and L701) — insert before acc.Cancel:
stale.RemoveAll(o => o.OrderState == OrderState.Filled || o.OrderState == OrderState.Cancelled);

// CancelStaleBracketsLocal (PttBreakEven.cs L190) — insert before acc.Cancel:
stale.RemoveAll(o => o.OrderState == OrderState.Filled || o.OrderState == OrderState.Cancelled);
CYC impact per method: +0 (RemoveAll is not a branch). Three insertions total (2× CancelQxBrackets overloads + 1× CancelStaleBracketsLocal).

Priority: P3 — cosmetic only. No position-protection risk. No popup has been observed from these paths in production. Deferred until a convenient pipeline pass touches any of the three methods.

DW-B72-01 — P3 Deferred — IsAtmBracketName Stop10 over-cancel investigation
Origin: First noted in DW-B79-03 deferred backlog. Carried through DW-B79-04. Not yet added to spec HTML until this session (2026-08-21).

Symptom (theoretical): Orders whose names contain the string "Stop10" may be over-cancelled under certain ATM bracket naming conventions. The concern is whether the instrument-name vs order-name filter logic in CancelAllAccountOrders (or a related method) correctly discriminates between a stop order belonging to this instrument’s ATM bracket and a stop order from a different position whose name happens to contain the instrument ticker substring (e.g. a bracket named "Stop10 NQ" on an ES position).

Practical severity: P3 — no over-cancel incident observed in production. The naming convention filter has not been analytically proven incorrect. Requires a code read of IsAtmBracketName() and the stateOk filter in CancelAllAccountOrders to confirm or close.

Resolution path: Read IsAtmBracketName() implementation. If the filter uses instrument name as a prefix guard (not a substring match), the risk is zero and DW-B72-01 can be CLOSED by observation. If substring match — widen to prefix-only or add instrument.MasterInstrument.Name guard.

Target block: B80 or later (low urgency). No pipeline required until investigation confirms a real defect.

DW-B73-B-01 — P2 CLOSED — Remove redundant UpdateBeAllVisuals(BeState.Idle) from UpdateButtonColors
Root cause:
UpdateButtonColors called UpdateBeAllVisuals(BeState.Idle) at ~L587 immediately before CopyEngine.Instance.RaiseBeAllDisarmed(). RaiseBeAllDisarmed() fires GlobalBeAllDisarmed, which every panel subscribes to — including the calling panel itself — causing UpdateBeAllVisuals(BeState.Idle) to fire twice on the leader panel on every disarm.

Fix: Remove the direct call (UpdateBeAllVisuals(BeState.Idle)) at TradeCopierPanel.cs ~L587. The event subscription already handles it.

DW-B81-01 — PTT-BE-Stop Rejection Does Not Evict _pendingFollowerBeSlots Entry (P1)
Root cause chain:
1. TryReplacePttBeBrackets (L1817) calls TryAdd to register a slot.
2. MoveStopToBreakEven submits PTT-BE-Stop for the follower.
3. NT8 returns Rejected ("Buy stop below market") — market moved in favor before NT8 accepted.
4. TryEvictFollowerBeSlot (L1082) only evicted on OrderState.Filled, not Rejected.
5. Slot persisted in _pendingFollowerBeSlots indefinitely.
6. Next BE press on the same account: TryAdd found existing slot → returned false → TryReplacePttBeBrackets returned early → no brackets placed.
7. Only the single PTT-BE-Stop from MoveStopToBreakEven was submitted → follower had stop but NO targets.

Fix applied:
TryEvictFollowerBeSlot (CopyEngine.cs L1093–1113): expanded guard to evict on OrderState.Rejected when order name is "PTT-BE-Stop".
• isFilled + isRejected booleans declared; flat-guard conditioned on isFilled only (bypassed for Rejected — slot is dead even while position open).
• _beReplaceAttempts reset on both paths (unconditional on terminal).
• CYC: 4 → 6 (+2 guards: terminal-state-guard, name-guard).
• 3 new IL-scan [Fact] tests: T_DW_B81_01_01 (OrderState.Rejected in IL), T_DW_B81_01_02 ("PTT-BE-Stop" string in IL), T_DW_B81_01_03 (OrderState.Filled regression guard).

DW-B82-01 — _beReplaceAttempts Not Reset on Slot Consumption — Brackets Lost After First BE→QX Cycle (P1)
Root cause: _beReplaceAttempts[acc] incremented in TryReplacePttBeBrackets (max 3 allowed) but only reset in TryEvictFollowerBeSlot (position-close path). QX sweep cancels all 3 PTT-BE-Stop-* brackets in a single BE→QX cycle → counter goes 0→3 in one trade. On next entry prevAttempts ≥ 3 gate fires immediately → no slot registered → no brackets placed → follower gets bare PTT-BE-Stop only (stops-only, no targets, no OCO).
This failure affected ALL scenarios from trade 2 onward in any session with at least one prior BE→QX cycle.

Fix (2 lines, CopyEngine.cs):
• Location 1 — TryFireFollowerBeRetry L1067: after _pendingFollowerBeSlots.TryRemove atomic claim, immediately reset counter: _beReplaceAttempts.TryRemove(o.Account.Name, out _);
• Location 2 — QueueBeRetryFallback timer Tick lambda L1156: inside the if (TryRemove) success branch, immediately reset counter: _beReplaceAttempts.TryRemove(capturedAcc.Name, out _);

Rationale: Both paths represent successful slot consumption — the slot is about to be used to fire MoveStopToBreakEven. The attempt counter counted prior attempts on this slot lifecycle; resetting it here ensures TryReplacePttBeBrackets starts from 0 for the next BE cycle on this account.

CYC delta: None — both insertions are in straight-line code (no new branches).
Tests added: 2 new IL-scan [Fact] tests in B82Tests.cs:
• T_DW_B82_01_01: TryFireFollowerBeRetry IL contains exactly 2 TryRemove callvirt instructions (slot + counter reset).
• T_DW_B82_01_02: QueueBeRetryFallback timer Tick lambda IL contains ≥ 2 TryRemove callvirt instructions.

● DW-B83  ◆  PTT-COPIER-B83  ◆  Stale Bracket Accumulation & Counter Exhaustion  ◆  ● DW-B83-01 OPEN (P0)  ·  DW-B83-02 OPEN (P1)
DW-B83-01 — Multiple Live PTT-BE OCO Bracket Groups Per Follower Account (P0)
Symptom: Follower account holds two or more distinct live PTT-BE OCO bracket groups simultaneously on a single open position. Confirmed: Sim102 at 5:44 PM held groups PTT-BE-Sim102-23559720 (4 targets, from prior cycle) and PTT-BE-Sim102-23559723 (3 targets, from current cycle) both live and accepted.

Evidence: NinjaTrader Grid CSV 2026-08-20 05-47 PM, event log lines 63–94: two complete sets of OCO pairs cancelled for Sim102 simultaneously on Flatten Everything at 5:45:55 PM. Also: Sim103 had 2 live PTT-BE-Target-1 / PTT-BE-Stop-1 pairs from two different OCO groups at the same timestamp.

Root cause hypothesis: When TryReplacePttBeBrackets fires on cancel events from prior-cycle stale PTT-BE orders, the attempt counter reaches 3 and blocks further replacements — but the first replacement (attempt 1/3) already succeeded and placed a new bracket group. Meanwhile the old group from the prior cycle was never explicitly cancelled before the new group was placed, because MoveStopToBreakEven does not purge prior PTT-BE OCO groups before submitting new ones. Result: both the stale group and the new group remain live simultaneously.

Risk in live trading: Two stop legs on the same position; whichever fires first closes the position and OCO-cancels its paired target. The orphaned group from the other bracket set will produce rejected orders (position already flat) and potentially an unintended re-entry if NT8 mishandles the orphan.

Required fix direction (spec only — not src until pipeline):
Before MoveStopToBreakEven submits new PTT-BE orders for a follower, cancel any existing live PTT-BE OCO groups for that account+instrument. A pre-cancel sweep using a name-prefix filter (o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-"), state Working/Accepted) should run as step 0 of bracket placement, analogous to the [PTT-QX-GUARD] pre-cancel follower brackets already implemented for QX.

DW-B83-02 — Cancel-Storm Counter Exhaustion in TryReplacePttBeBrackets (P1)
Symptom: TryReplacePttBeBrackets logs max 3 attempts, no new slot (TryFireFollowerBeRetry still holds slot 3) immediately after a successful attempt 1/3 on the same BE-ALL press, without any retry or fallback timer having fired.

Evidence (NT8 Output log 2026-08-20):
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1 → TryReplace attempt 1/3 ✓
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-2 → TryReplace max 3 ✗
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-2 → TryReplace max 3 ✗
(continuing for all remaining prior-cycle PTT-BE cancel events)

Root cause: Every PTT-BE-* order cancel event (regardless of which cycle placed it) calls TryReplacePttBeBrackets. Prior-cycle stale PTT-BE orders still present in the NT8 order book (state Cancelled, visible in [BE-DIAG] order dumps with hundreds of historical orders) fire cancel notifications when Flatten/QX/Close processes them. Each notification increments the shared _beReplaceAttempts[acc] counter. After 3 cancel events from stale prior-cycle orders, the counter is at 3 and all subsequent TryReplacePttBeBrackets calls return immediately — including the fallback timer when it fires, leaving the follower with no OCO brackets.

Relationship to DW-B82-01: DW-B82-01 fixed counter reset on slot consumption (TryRemove success path). This defect is orthogonal: the counter exhausts within a single press due to cancel-storm from prior-cycle orders, before any slot is consumed.

Required fix direction (spec only — not src until pipeline):
TryReplacePttBeBrackets should only increment the attempt counter when the cancellation event corresponds to an order belonging to the current bracket group (i.e., the order was placed after the current slot was registered). One approach: record the slot registration timestamp and reject counter increments from orders whose submission time predates the current slot. Alternative: filter by OCO group ID matching the currently registered slot's group prefix.

DW-B84-01 — Follower BE-ALL Fires acc.Cancel() on ATM Stops (P0) — Root Cause + Deployment History
Root Cause (confirmed by log analysis, 3 independent BE-ALL cycles):
MoveStopToBreakEven Step B calls acc.Cancel(stale) on every Working/Accepted/Submitted/Initialized/TriggerPending order that does not start with "PTT-BE-". On a follower account the ATM stops are named Stop1, Stop2, Stop3 — these pass the notBe guard and are cancelled. NT8 then OCO-cancels the paired targets (Target1/2/3) as a consequence of the stop cancellation. Step C then attempts to submit new PTT-BE-* OCO pairs, which NT8 immediately sweeps because an active ATM strategy is present on the account.

Log Evidence (3 cycles, consistent):
• Cycle 1: [BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 cancel=3 targets=3 newStop=7668.50
• Cycle 2: [BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 cancel=3 targets=3 newStop=7668.75
• Cycle 3: [BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 cancel=5 targets=3 newStop=7668.50
• targets=3 always found at Step A — snapshot is correct and complete every time
• T+500ms: Stop1/Stop2/Stop3 AND Target1/2/3 all Cancelled
• Immediately after Step B: [BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1 → TryReplace attempt 1/3
(The PTT-BE-* orders placed by Step C are swept by NT8 before they go Working.)

Key Insight — Why cancel+replace is architecturally wrong for followers:
The leader uses a different bracket type (AddOn-submitted PTT-BE-* OCO pairs via CreateOrder/Submit). The followers use ATM-owned stops (Stop1/Stop2/Stop3) that are part of an active ATM strategy. Cancelling ATM-owned stops triggers OCO cancellation of the paired targets. NT8 then treats the new PTT-BE-* stops submitted in Step C as foreign orders on an ATM-managed position and sweeps them.

Correct Fix — acc.Change() in-place:
NT8 account.Change(orders[]) modifies the stop price of existing Working orders without cancellation. The ATM strategy treats the change as a normal stop price update and the targets are never touched.
Confirmed by T1 analysis (GAP-001d, B25 spec): acc.Change() does NOT kill the ATM trail or OCO link.

What gets eliminated:
• Step B cancel block (for followers) → replaced with acc.Change(stops)
• Step C OCO creation loop (for followers) → goes away entirely (targets stay as-is)
• TryReplacePttBeBrackets / TryFireFollowerBeRetry / QueueBeRetryFallback retry subsystem becomes unnecessary for the normal BE-ALL path (followers never cancel stops, so no PTT-BE-Stop-* cancel events fire, so the entire retry path is never triggered)

DW-B83 relationship:
DW-B83-01 (stale bracket accumulation) and DW-B83-02 (cancel-storm counter exhaustion) both become moot for the normal BE-ALL path if acc.Change() is adopted — no new brackets are submitted, so nothing accumulates and the attempt counter is never incremented.

NT8 SIM broker dependency confirmed — DW-B84-03:
On SIM accounts, ATM stop orders park permanently at OrderState.Accepted and never transition to Working. NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md (line 1005): "In real-time, some stop orders may only reach Accepted state if they are simulated/held on a broker's server." acc.Change() is valid on Accepted orders — the broker has acknowledged the order. State guard widened in DW-B84-03 (commit 1e0e45b0) to: Working || Accepted || ChangeSubmitted.
CancelSubmitted is explicitly excluded — NT8 rejects acc.Change() on in-flight cancellations.

Deployment history:
• v1 (commit 944da22a) — stops=0: followers ran AFTER leader. Leader Step B acc.Cancel() triggered NT8 ATM cascade putting follower stops into CancelSubmitted before the follower path iterated them. Working-only guard rejected them → stops=0.
• v2 (commit 14e93055) — DW-B84-01: swap execution order (followers before leader) + widen guard to Working || ChangeSubmitted + [BE-DIAG-F] diagnostic dump on stops=0.
• v2.1 (commit 51eae807) — DW-B84-01 v2: followers run before leader confirmed in BreakEven(Account,Instrument,int); ChangeSubmitted accepted (belt-and-suspenders).
• v2.2 (commit 1e0e45b0) — DW-B84-03: widen state guard to also accept Accepted state. Root cause of latest stops=0: NT8 SIM broker holds stops permanently at Accepted, never advancing to Working. Confirmed by NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md line 1005.

DW-B84-02 (commit 51eae807) — infinite loop guard:
ReplaceFollowerCopyOnAtmCancel (L1775): added guard — if the follower already has a position, skip re-placing the entry. This blocks the NT8-internal ATM-arming cancel from triggering an infinite copy loop. The guard sits at L1775: if (HasOpenPosition(cancelledOrder.Account, cancelledOrder.Instrument)) return;
