DW-B84-SIM104 — Sim104 Null at LoadRules Time — Root Cause Identified (P1)
Director confirmed Sim104 IS in the copy rule UI. Sim104 was selected as a follower alongside Sim102 and Sim103. Yet the dispatch log shows only Sim102 and Sim103. This points to a single precise root cause in DtoToRule (CopyEngine.cs L3396–3407):

Root cause — DtoToRule null-slot on load (P1):
When LoadRules() runs at NT8 startup, it resolves follower names against Account.All (line 3399: foreach (var acc in Account.All)). If Sim104's Account object is not yet present in Account.All at load time (e.g. the SIM connection hasn't completed or Sim104 hasn't been initialized), the inner loop finds no match and followers[i] stays null.
AllAccounts() (L2484) silently skips nulls: if (acc != null) yield return acc;
Result: Sim104 is in the XML on disk, present in the UI dropdown, but resolves to null at runtime and is never dispatched to, never included in BE-ALL, never included in any copy event.

Why Sim102 and Sim103 resolve but Sim104 does not:
Sim102 and Sim103 are chart-active accounts with open charts — NT8 initialises them earlier. Sim104 may have no open chart or its connection was established after LoadRules() ran, so its Account object was absent from Account.All at resolution time.

Evidence from CSV (9:17 PM block):
Sim104 accumulated 336 contracts SHORT in ~2 seconds — this is Sim104 running its own independent chart-trader ATM session. The infinite copy loop (DW-B84-02) fired on Sim104's own chart, completely separate from PTT copy engine. Sim104's position was never managed by PTT in this session because the null-slot caused it to be silently skipped.

Fix options (spec-only — requires pipeline):
Option A (lazy re-resolve, minimal): In AllAccounts(), when a slot is null, attempt to re-resolve the name from Account.All at call time rather than silently skipping. If found, update the slot in-place (requires Account[] to be mutable — it is).
Option B (deferred load): Register a callback on Account.AccountStatusChange and re-call DtoToRule / re-resolve null slots when new accounts become available.
Option C (log + warn): At minimum, log a warning when DtoToRule leaves a followers[i] = null slot so the Director sees it in the Output tab at startup.

Immediate workaround for next test:
After NT8 loads, open the PTT panel → re-apply the copy rule (press Apply Rule) after the connection is fully established and all four SIM accounts are visible. This calls AddRule() fresh with live Account references, bypassing the stale LoadRules() null slot. Then verify dispatch shows Sim104 before pressing BE-ALL.

DW-B85-01 — Follower Account Resolves to null in DtoToRule if Not Yet in Account.All at Load Time (P1)
Root cause:
LoadRules() calls DtoToRule() (CopyEngine.cs L3396–3407) which resolves follower names by iterating Account.All. If a follower's Account object is not yet present in Account.All at the moment LoadRules() runs (connection not yet established, account not yet initialized by NT8), followers[i] stays null.
AllAccounts() (L2484) then silently skips nulls: if (acc != null) yield return acc;
Result: the follower is saved correctly in XML, visible in the panel UI, but never dispatched to, never included in BE-ALL, never included in any copy operation at runtime.

Observed instance — Sim104 (session 2026-08-20 10:25 PM):
Copy rule saved with followers Sim102 + Sim103 + Sim104. At startup Sim102 and Sim103 had open charts so NT8 initialised them before LoadRules() ran. Sim104 had no open chart; its Account was absent from Account.All at load time → null slot → dispatch log showed only Sim102 and Sim103. Sim104 accumulated 336 contracts independently via its own chart-trader session with no PTT oversight.

Why TryAutoApply() (checkbox tick) works but LoadRules() does not:
TryAutoApply() calls GetSelectedFollowers() which reads item.Account directly from the live _followerItems list. These Account references are populated when the panel follower list is built — if this happens after the connection is established and all accounts are in Account.All, the references are live and correct. LoadRules() runs at TradeCopierWindow OnLoad time, which may precede full account initialization.

Workaround (no code change required):
After NT8 is fully connected and all SIM accounts are visible in the Accounts list:
1. Open the PTT panel
2. Uncheck the affected follower (e.g. Sim104) → TryAutoApply() fires
3. Re-check it → TryAutoApply() fires again with live Account reference
4. Verify dispatch: [PTT-COPY] dispatch: ... -> Sim104 appears when leader fills
Note: the Apply Rule button is hidden (Visibility.Collapsed) — checkbox tick is the correct equivalent action. Clone (radio button) sets copy mode only — it does not re-apply the follower rule.

Proposed fix (spec-only — requires PTT pipeline):
Option A — Lazy re-resolve (preferred, minimal):
In AllAccounts() (L2482–2486), when iterating FollowerAccounts and a slot is null, look up the saved name for that index from the rule's DTO and attempt to resolve it against Account.All. If found, update the slot in-place. Requires storing the original account name strings alongside the Account[] array in CopyRule.
Option B — Startup log warning (minimum viable):
In DtoToRule(), when followers[i] stays null after the inner loop, emit: [PTT-COPY] WARNING: follower '{name}' not found in Account.All at load time — will be skipped until rule is re-applied.
This at least surfaces the problem in the Output tab instead of silently losing the follower.

COPY ON order — confirmed does not matter:
OnCopyToggle calls _engine.SetEnabled() which flips a volatile bool. The copy rule (which followers are registered) is completely independent of COPY ON state. COPY ON/OFF gates whether dispatches are sent; it does not affect rule registration. Order of pressing COPY ON relative to anything else is irrelevant.

DW-B86-01 — Follower MoveStopToBreakEven Stop Name Guard Does Not Match PTT-QX-Stop* Orders After QX-ALL (P0)
Session evidence — 2026-08-21 12:31 PM:
Sequence: leader entry filled → dispatch Sim102 + Sim103 → QX-ALL pressed → QX replaces ATM brackets → BE-ALL pressed → stops=0 for both followers → [BE-DIAG-F] dump fired → acc.Change() called with empty array → no stop movement. Followers left with position protected only by stale PTT-QX-Stop* orders at original QX price (7702.5), not at BE price (7696.50). Manual flatten required.

Root cause:
After QX-ALL, the PTT engine cancels the ATM-owned stop orders (Stop1…Stop3 / Stop9) on both the leader and followers, then places new PTT-managed brackets named PTT-QX-Stop, PTT-QX-Stop2, PTT-QX-Stop3, PTT-QX-Stop4 (one per QX bracket leg) plus PTT-QX-T1…PTT-QX-T4 (targets).
The follower BE path in MoveStopToBreakEven (CopyEngine.cs L2755–2762) has a strict name guard:
o.Name.StartsWith("Stop", Ordinal) && o.Name.Length == 5 && char.IsDigit(o.Name[4])
This matches exactly Stop1…Stop9. It does not match PTT-QX-Stop, PTT-QX-Stop2, etc.
When BE-ALL is pressed after QX-ALL, all ATM stops are already Cancelled. The only remaining active stops on the follower are the PTT-QX-Stop* orders (Accepted state on SIM). The name guard misses all of them → beSt.Count == 0 → stops=0.

Evidence from [BE-DIAG-F] dump (Sim102, 2026-08-21 12:30):
Stop1 Cancelled • Stop2 Cancelled • Stop3 Cancelled — ATM stops, all cancelled by QX cascade
PTT-QX-Stop Accepted • PTT-QX-Stop2 Accepted • PTT-QX-Stop3 Accepted • PTT-QX-Stop4 Accepted
→ None of these pass the StopN guard → stops=0.

Why this did not show up before (prior session 2026-08-20 10:25 PM):
That session pressed BE-ALL on the original ATM entry without pressing QX first. The stops were still Stop1 (ATM-owned, Accepted state). The StopN guard matched → stops=1 newStop=7669.00 → PASS. DW-B86 only surfaces on the QX then BE workflow path.

Scope of the problem:
Any workflow where QX-ALL runs before BE-ALL will result in stops=0 on all followers and no stop movement. This is the common production workflow: QX to tighten stop/target structure, then BE to protect principal. This is a P0 defect for the QX+BE path — the two most commonly combined commands.

Fix (spec-only — requires PTT pipeline):
In MoveStopToBreakEven (CopyEngine.cs L2755–2762), extend the stop name guard to also match PTT-QX-Stop* orders:
Current guard (L2755–2758):
o.Name.StartsWith("Stop", Ordinal) && o.Name.Length == 5 && char.IsDigit(o.Name[4])
Proposed extension:
Add a second OR branch:
|| (o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-QX-Stop", StringComparison.Ordinal))
This matches PTT-QX-Stop (leg 1), PTT-QX-Stop2, PTT-QX-Stop3, PTT-QX-Stop4, etc.
The full guard becomes:
bool isBeStop =
    // Original ATM stop names: Stop1..Stop9
    (o.Name.StartsWith("Stop", Ordinal) && o.Name.Length == 5 && char.IsDigit(o.Name[4]))
    // After QX-ALL: PTT-QX-Stop, PTT-QX-Stop2, PTT-QX-Stop3 ...
    || o.Name.StartsWith("PTT-QX-Stop", StringComparison.Ordinal);
No other changes required. The acc.Change() call, the try/catch, the diagnostic dump, and the early return are all unaffected.

State guard note:
PTT-QX-Stop* orders are Accepted on SIM (same as ATM stops per NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md line 1005). The existing state guard already accepts Working || Accepted || ChangeSubmitted (DW-B84-03). No state guard change needed — only the name guard needs extending.

Also note — PTT-BE-Stop* case:
After a second BE press (e.g. leader-only BE already ran once and placed PTT-BE-Stop-1… on the leader), followers are still on their QX bracket. This case does not exist on followers (followers never have PTT-BE-Stop-* because their BE path is acc.Change() of existing stops, not cancel+replace). No additional guard needed for PTT-BE-Stop-* on followers.

Sim104 note (same session):
Sim104 shows PTT-QX: flat skip -- Sim104. QX correctly skipped it (no position, DW-B85 null-slot). QX did not place PTT-QX-* brackets on Sim104. Sim104 had no orders for this instrument at BE-ALL time. The BE-DIAG for Sim104 does not appear in the output, confirming AllAccounts() skipped it. Sim104 was flat throughout this session — no independently accumulated position (improvement over 2026-08-20 session).

Leader BE — confirmed working:
Leader (Sim101) had PTT-QX-Stop/Stop2/Stop3/Stop4 from QX. The leader path (Step B cancel + Step C submit) cancelled those 8 orders (MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim101 cancel=8 targets=4 newStop=7696.50) and created 4 new PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3/4 + PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3/4 brackets. All 4 PTT-BE-Stop-* filled @ 7696.50 (12:30:08). Targets OCO-cancelled correctly. Leader path works correctly for the QX+BE workflow.

4-target count explained:
The ATM template in this session uses 4 bracket legs (qty split 1+3+2+1 = 7 contracts). QX reads the live target count from the leader and reports leaderTargets=4. The 4 PTT-BE-DIAG-CANCEL lines for PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3/4 on Sim101 are the expected OCO cancellation when each corresponding PTT-BE-Stop-* fills. Not a defect.

DW-B86 Analysis — Why QX-ALL Worked While BE-ALL Did Not: Structural Comparison
Background (user observation confirmed by source):
QX-ALL was implemented by building on BE-ALL as a base. Both operate on follower accounts. QX-ALL worked correctly. BE-ALL failed on Path B (QX then BE). The structural comparison below explains exactly why.

The fundamental architectural difference:
QX-ALL creates orders on followers — it never needs to find existing ones.
BE-ALL modifies orders on followers — it must first find the existing stop orders by name.
The name guard in MoveStopToBreakEven is the only place where Path B could fail, and it did. QX-ALL has no equivalent lookup step, so it was immune.

Side-by-side source comparison:
Dimension QX-ALL (PttGlobalQuickExit) BE-ALL (PttGlobalBreakEven)
Entry point PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute() PttGlobalBreakEven.Execute(bufferTicks)
How followers are reached rule.FollowerAccounts iterated directly inside Execute()
Followers get ExecuteOne(skipIfFollower:false) called per account		 ArmAllPendingBe() arms only leader accounts.
Followers reached later via BreakEven() → AllAccounts() → MoveStopToBreakEven()
What it does to the follower CreateOrder + Submit
Places new PTT-QX-Stop* + PTT-QX-T* orders on the follower		 acc.Change(beSt[])
Updates existing stop price in-place on whatever stops are already there
Requires finding existing orders? No. Creates new ones unconditionally. Yes. Loops acc.Orders and filters by name guard isBeStop.
Name guard N/A — no lookup Before T1: StartsWith("Stop") && Length==5 && IsDigit[4] only
After T1: adds || StartsWith("PTT-QX-Stop", Ordinal)
Path A (ATM entry → BE) N/A ✓ Always worked. ATM stops are Stop1–Stop9 — matched original guard.
Path B (QX → BE) ✓ QX-ALL always works — creates fresh PTT-QX-Stop* orders; no lookup needed. ✗ Before T1: followers have PTT-QX-Stop* (not Stop1–Stop9) → guard missed → beSt=[] → stops=0.
✓ After T1: new QX branch matches PTT-QX-Stop* → beSt populated → acc.Change() fires correctly.
Why QX works as “base” for BE but BE needed the extra guard QX-ALL was built from BE-ALL’s looping structure (Account.All → positions → followers). The key divergence: QX-ALL submits new orders (no name lookup needed), while BE-ALL modifies existing orders (name lookup is load-bearing). The two implementations share the dispatch structure but not the order-interaction mechanism. BE-ALL’s mechanism is correct and more efficient (no cancel/resubmit), but it depends on the name guard being complete.
Stop naming after QX-ALL on followers (confirmed from PttQuickExit.cs L122):
string stopName = i == 0 ? "PTT-QX-Stop" : "PTT-QX-Stop" + (i + 1);
So for a 4-bracket ATM: PTT-QX-Stop, PTT-QX-Stop2, PTT-QX-Stop3, PTT-QX-Stop4.
All four are caught by StartsWith("PTT-QX-Stop", Ordinal) in the T1 guard extension.

Why acc.Change() is the right mechanism for BE on followers (not cancel+replace):
QX-ALL placed the PTT-QX-Stop* orders via CreateOrder+Submit which sets them up as PTT-managed (not ATM-owned). These are plain StopMarket orders registered with NT8 directly, not inside an ATM strategy bracket tree. acc.Change() is the standard NT8 stop-price update API for exactly this kind of order. No OCO re-wiring is needed because the PTT-QX OCO pairs are already set (the stop and its paired target share an ocoId_i string set at QX time). Moving the stop price via acc.Change() does not break the OCO link.

Confidence in Path B SIM gate:
The structural analysis shows the fix is complete and correct. The only broken part was the name guard. With T1 deployed, BE-ALL’s MoveStopToBreakEven follower path is now structurally equivalent to Path A — the same acc.Change() call fires, the same log line appears, the same DIAG is suppressed. 3 SIM gate cycles are still required as the human-in-the-loop runtime confirmation, but the code fix is complete.

Discovered: 2026-08-23 SIM gate Path A, cycle 3.

Root cause:
The follower path in MoveStopToBreakEven uses acc.Change() to reprice existing ATM stops in-place. The state guard only accepts Working, Accepted, ChangeSubmitted. If BE-ALL is pressed too quickly after entry dispatch — before the follower ATM brackets have transitioned from Submitted/Initialized to Working/Accepted — the guard rejects all stops → beSt.Count == 0 → acc.Change([]) no-op → follower stop does not move. The [BE-DIAG-F] dump fires and the function returns with no retry.

Evidence from cycle 3 [BE-DIAG-F] dump (Sim102, 2026-08-23):
19 orders present for instrument. Stop1/Stop2/Stop3 from cycles 1 and 2 all Filled. Cycle 3 ATM brackets had not yet settled: still in Submitted/Initialized state. State guard rejected all → stops=0 newStop=7684.00 → no bracket protection. Manually flattened via "Flatten Everything" at 3:37:12 PM (CSV confirms Close market order, follower exits at 7684.75–7685.00).

Contributing factor — double dispatch before cycle 3:
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 appeared twice for each follower before the BE-ALL press, indicating rapid re-entry after a cancelled limit order from prior cycle stale state. This left 19 orders in the follower account (cycles 1 and 2 fills + cycle 3 fresh ATM still arming) making the timing window wider than normal.

Workaround:
Wait ~1–2 seconds after entry dispatch before pressing BE-ALL. Gives follower ATM brackets time to transition to Working/Accepted before the state guard runs.

Fix direction:
This defect is superseded by DW-B88. The DW-B88 unified cancel+resubmit path does not call acc.Change() on existing stops — it cancels everything (state-agnostic) and submits fresh PTT-BE-Stop-N orders at newStop. The settlement race cannot occur because the cancel sweep does not require stops to be in any particular state, and the new orders are submitted unconditionally. DW-B87 is closed as a side effect of DW-B88.
OPEN — superseded by DW-B88 (no standalone fix needed) WORKAROUND: wait 1–2s after entry before pressing BE-ALL will be CLOSED when DW-B88 SIM gate passes

DW-B88 — Design: Replace MoveStopToBreakEven Follower + Leader Paths with Unified QX-Engine Cancel+Resubmit
Motivation:
The current MoveStopToBreakEven has two divergent execution paths:
• Follower path: acc.Change() on existing ATM stops (in-place reprice). Vulnerable to DW-B86 (wrong stop names after QX) and DW-B87 (stops not yet settled).
• Leader path: Step B cancel + Step C cancel+resubmit PTT-BE-* orders. Correct but diverges from follower.
Both problems go away if both paths use the same cancel+resubmit engine that QX-ALL already uses and that is proven working.

What does NOT change:
• PttGlobalBreakEven.Execute() — arm/wait logic unchanged
• ArmAllPendingBe(), ArmPendingBe() — unchanged
• The price trigger mechanism — unchanged
• BreakEven(Account, Instrument, int) — followers-before-leader dispatch unchanged
• PttQuickExit.Execute() — completely untouched
• PttGlobalQuickExit — completely untouched
QX-ALL continues to work exactly as today. Zero risk to it.

What changes — one function only:
MoveStopToBreakEven (CopyEngine.cs): the follower acc.Change() block (L2742–2797) and the leader Step B/C cancel+resubmit block (L2800–2963) are both replaced with a single call to PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute(acc, instrument, newStop, targets).
The targets list is already built at Step A (L2691–2724) before any path diverges — it is passed straight in.

New file: PttBreakEvenSwap.cs
~40 lines. Wraps PttQuickExit.Execute() with the following fixed arguments:
• leaderStop = newStop (entry ± buffer, already computed)
• targets = snapshotted targets list from Step A (keeps existing tranche structure)
• skipIfFollower = false (called once per account, not from leader context)
• t1Ticks = 0 (not used — stop price comes from leaderStop, target prices come from the snapshot)
The QX engine uses leaderStop as the stop price when snapshotStop == 0 (which it will be after cancel). Target prices come directly from the snapshotted list, not recomputed from ticks. Tranche quantities preserved exactly.

Cancel sweep coverage (confirmed from source):
CancelQxBrackets calls IsQxCancelCandidate which matches:
• ATM bracket names (Stop1–Stop9, Target1–Target9) via IsAtmBracketName
• PTT-QX-* prefix — covers PTT-QX-Stop* and PTT-QX-T* after QX-ALL
• PTT-BE-* prefix — covers prior PTT-BE-Stop-N / PTT-BE-Target-N
• PTT-Copy* prefix — covers entry orders
State filter accepts Working, Initialized, Accepted, Submitted, TriggerPending. Not state-dependent for the cancel — whatever is cancellable gets cancelled.

QX-ALL first then BE-ALL: confirmed correct:
After QX-ALL the follower has PTT-QX-Stop* orders in Working/Accepted and PTT-QX-T* targets. When the BE-ALL arm trigger fires, PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() calls CancelQxBrackets which explicitly matches PTT-QX-* (line 599). These are cancelled. Fresh PTT-BE-Stop-N orders are placed at newStop (entry ± buffer). Targets reconstructed from the Step A snapshot. Fully correct for QX→BE sequence.

Reversibility:
The old follower acc.Change() block and leader Step B/C block remain in CopyEngine.cs as commented-out code with a // DW-B88: replaced by PttBreakEvenSwap marker. Rollback = delete the PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() call, uncomment the old blocks. One-line change.

Signal names (unchanged from today):
Stop: PTT-BE-Stop-1, PTT-BE-Stop-2, … — same as leader path today.
Target: PTT-BE-Target-1, PTT-BE-Target-2, … — same as leader path today.
Already matched by Step A snapshot filter (PTT-BE-Target- prefix at L2720) so re-arming after a prior BE-ALL also works correctly.

Side effects resolved by DW-B88:
• DW-B86: the PTT-QX-Stop* name guard miss is irrelevant — cancel sweep is name-agnostic via IsQxCancelCandidate.
• DW-B87: the settlement timing race is irrelevant — cancel sweep accepts Submitted/Initialized, resubmit is unconditional.
Both can be marked CLOSED when DW-B88 SIM gates pass.

DW-B88 does NOT affect:
• The arm/wait trigger behaviour — BE-ALL still arms and waits for price
• The retry subsystem (_pendingFollowerBeSlots, QueueBeRetryFallback, TryFireFollowerBeRetry) — these handle the targets=0 path (post-QX no targets yet) and are unchanged
• Buffer ticks logic — unchanged
• Short position direction — unchanged (handled by PttQuickExit.Execute isLong flag)

DW-B89-01 — OCO ID Reuse After In-Session Recompile (P1)
Error:
"The OCO ID 'PTT-BE-Sim101-245037222-2' cannot be reused. Please use a new OCO ID."

Root cause:
NT8 keeps cancelled OCO IDs in memory for the entire NT8 session — they are never evicted, even across AddOn recompiles. CopyEngine._mstbeOcoSeq is seeded with Environment.TickCount on construction (L205). After an in-session recompile, a new CopyEngine is created with a new seed. The old PttBreakEven per-chart path and the new PttBreakEvenSwap path both write OCO IDs in the format PTT-BE-{acc[..8]}-{seq:D5}-{i}. If the new seed lands within 99999 of any value used in the pre-recompile run (possible: TickCount is ms since OS boot, recompile takes <1s), NT8 flags the ID as reused.

The D5 (5-digit zero-padded) format caps the unique space at 100,000 values. With a TickCount seed and multiple OCO pairs per trade, the collision window is non-trivial within a single NT8 session that includes a recompile.

Fix:
Widen the seq field from D5 to D7 (7 digits, 10M values) AND XOR the seed with a larger entropy source. The safest approach that stays within NT8's OCO ID length limit:
private volatile int _mstbeOcoSeq = Math.Abs(Environment.TickCount ^ (int)(DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks & 0x7FFFFFFF));
XORing TickCount (ms since boot) with the low 31 bits of DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks (100ns increments) gives a seed that advances even within a single millisecond, making post-recompile collision probability negligible.

Change OCO ID format from:
"PTT-BE-" + acc.Name[..8] + "-" + seq.ToString("D5") + "-" + i
to:
"PTT-BE-" + acc.Name[..8] + "-" + seq.ToString("D7") + "-" + i

NT8 OCO ID length budget:
Max field length for OCO ID in NT8 is not officially documented but empirically observed at ~40 chars. "PTT-BE-" (7) + "Sim101" (6) + "-" (1) + "0012345" (7) + "-" (1) + "2" (1) = 23 chars — well within budget.

Files to change:
• src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs L205: widen seed entropy
• src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttBreakEvenSwap.cs L84: D5 → D7
• Check PttBreakEven.cs for any D5 format in its own OCO ID path — must match.

Affected files: CopyEngine.cs, PttBreakEvenSwap.cs, possibly PttBreakEven.cs
OPEN (P1) CopyEngine.cs L205 seed + PttBreakEvenSwap.cs L84 D5->D7 must fix before SIM gate re-run
DW-B89-02 — BuyToCover StopMarket Rejected as “Below Market” on Short Entry + buf=0t (P1)
Error:
"Buy stop or buy stop limit orders can't be placed below the market. affected Order: BuyToCover 1 StopMarket @ 7688.5"

Root cause:
Entry was a short (Sell x7 @ 7688.5). With buf=0t, newStop = entry ± 0 = 7688.5. By the time PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() reaches the NT8 acc.Submit() call, price had moved above 7688.5 (i.e. the trade was already against the position). NT8 rejects a BuyToCover StopMarket placed below the current ask price — the stop would trigger immediately, which NT8 treats as invalid for a stop order.

This is not a direction-calculation bug — HOTFIX-BUG-BE-STOP-SHORT in MoveStopToBreakEven L2672 correctly sets direction = +1.0 for shorts so newStop = entry + buf*tick. With buf=0 that equals entry. The issue is that with buf=0 on a short, any adverse tick between entry and BE press puts the stop price below the market, making it unsubmittable as a stop.

Secondary cause:
PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() uses bare catch { /* non-fatal */ } on every acc.Submit() call. When the Stop leg is rejected by NT8, the exception is swallowed silently. The position is left with no stop bracket and no log entry indicating what went wrong. The Target leg (same OCO pair) is then auto-cancelled by NT8, doubling the exposure.

Fix — two parts:
Part A (silent-failure logging — mandatory):
Change every catch { /* non-fatal */ } in PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() to:
catch (Exception ex) { NinjaTrader.Code.Output.Process("[BE-ERR] " + acc.Name + " submit failed: " + ex.Message, NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.PrintTo.OutputTab1); }
This makes every NT8 rejection visible in the Output tab instead of silent. Zero behaviour change, pure observability.

Part B (stop-below-market guard — mandatory):
Before calling acc.Submit(new[] { sOrd }) on a Stop leg, validate the stop price against current market. Add a helper IsStopPriceValid(instr, isLong, stopPrice):
• Long: BuyToCover is not applicable; Stop is Sell, valid at any price (stops below market for longs are fine in NT8).
• Short: stop is BuyToCover StopMarket; NT8 requires stop price ≥ current ask.
If the stop would be rejected, fall back to the 0-targets bare-stop path (which NT8 will also reject if price is above stop) OR log [BE-ERR] stop below market, skipping and leave the position without a stop (matching current silent-failure behaviour but now visible).

Part C (workflow note — non-code):
buf=0t on a short with immediate BE press is a marginal case. Any adverse tick makes the stop unplaceable. The Director should use buf≥1t on short positions to give the stop price a buffer above entry. This is a workflow recommendation, not a code defect. The code must still handle buf=0 gracefully (Part A + B cover this).

Files to change:
• src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttBreakEvenSwap.cs: replace bare catch{} with logging catches (Part A) + add stop-price validity check before Stop submit (Part B)

CYC impact:
Adding the stop-price validity check adds 1 branch per Stop submit. CYC: 8 → 9. Needs extraction of the stop-price check into a private helper IsStopPriceSubmittable(instr, isLong, price) to keep Execute() at CYC ≤ 8 (Jane Street strict standard).
OPEN (P1) PttBreakEvenSwap.cs: catch logging + stop-price guard CYC: extract IsStopPriceSubmittable() helper to stay ≤8 must fix before SIM gate re-run

DW-B90 — Root Cause: TryReplacePttBeBrackets Fires on OCO Partner Cancels (Target Fill), Not Only ATM Sweep Cancels
The trigger mechanism:
When a PTT-BE-Target-N limit fills, NT8 automatically cancels the paired PTT-BE-Stop-N OCO partner. This cancel fires OnOrderUpdate with OrderState.Cancelled on the stop leg. The handler at L955–965 checks:
if (e.Order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-Stop-", StringComparison.Ordinal)) TryReplacePttBeBrackets(e.Order); This filter matches any PTT-BE-Stop-* cancel — whether caused by an ATM sweep (the intended case) or by an OCO partner target fill (the wrong case). NT8 does not distinguish these two cancel reasons at the OrderState level — both arrive as Cancelled.

Why the 3-attempt cap fails:
TryReplacePttBeBrackets increments _beReplaceAttempts[acc] (L1839). However the 500ms fallback timer at L1156 calls _beReplaceAttempts.TryRemove(capturedAcc.Name, out _) before calling MoveStopToBreakEven. That call to MoveStopToBreakEven runs PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() which calls CancelQxBrackets, which cancels the freshly placed PTT-BE-Stop-* orders, which re-fires TryReplacePttBeBrackets, which now reads prevAttempts = 0 (just reset) and increments to 1 — always attempt 1/3. The cap counter is reset faster than it can accumulate. The log confirms: attempt 1/3 on every single iteration, from cycle 1 through cycle ~40.

The cascade in sequence:
1. Target fills → NT8 cancels paired stop (OCO cancel)
2. TryReplacePttBeBrackets fires (wrong — should not fire here)
3. 500ms timer fires → resets counter → calls MoveStopToBreakEven(isRetry:true)
4. PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute() → CancelQxBrackets → cancels all PTT-BE-*
5. Those cancels re-fire TryReplacePttBeBrackets (counter = 0 again)
6. Goto 3. Infinite.

What DW-B79-08 was designed for (not this):
TryReplacePttBeBrackets was built for the case where a leader re-entry triggers NT8's StartAtmStrategy sweep which wipes ALL follower working orders including PTT-BE-* brackets mid-trade. That scenario has no target fill — the full position is still open when brackets are wiped. In the target-fill case, the position is being intentionally reduced — the stop cancel is expected and correct, not a bracket wipe that needs recovery.
P0 — blocking OnOrderUpdate L964: TryReplacePttBeBrackets fires on OCO cancel _beReplaceAttempts reset before cap can accumulate
DW-B90 — Fix: Guard TryReplacePttBeBrackets Against OCO Partner Cancels
The distinguishing criterion:
When a target fills and its OCO stop is auto-cancelled, the account's open position quantity is already reduced by the time OnOrderUpdate fires for the stop cancel. The original full-position case (ATM sweep wipe) leaves position qty unchanged — all contracts still open, no fills have occurred.

Therefore: before calling TryReplacePttBeBrackets, compare the current position quantity against the total quantity protected by the remaining PTT-BE-Stop-* working orders. If pos.Quantity < totalStopQty a target fill has occurred — do not retry brackets.

Simplest correct guard (preferred):
In OnOrderUpdate, at the call site (L964), add a position-qty check before calling TryReplacePttBeBrackets:
if (e.Order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-Stop-", StringComparison.Ordinal)) { // DW-B90: only fire bracket recovery if position is still full size. // If qty reduced (partial target fill), the OCO cancel is expected -- do not retry. var bePos = FindPosition(e.Order.Account, e.Order.Instrument); int remainingStopQty = SumWorkingBeStopQty(e.Order.Account, e.Order.Instrument); bool isOcoCancelFromFill = bePos != null && bePos.Quantity < remainingStopQty + e.Order.Quantity; if (!isOcoCancelFromFill) TryReplacePttBeBrackets(e.Order); } Where SumWorkingBeStopQty is a new private helper that sums the Quantity of all Working/Accepted orders on the account whose name starts with "PTT-BE-Stop-" for the given instrument (excluding the just-cancelled order itself). If pos.Quantity < remainingStopQty + cancelledQty then a fill reduced the position — this is an OCO cancel, not a sweep.

DW-B91-A OPEN Copy Engine

Double dispatch on partial entry fill

SYMPTOM

When a single entry order fills in multiple partial executions (e.g. a 7-lot order fills as 2 lots then 5 lots), OnExecutionUpdate fires once per partial. The copy engine dispatches each partial independently to followers. Each dispatch triggers a full ATM bracket set on each follower account.

Result: followers receive 2 separate entry orders (e.g. Sell 2 then Sell 5) with 2 independent ATM bracket sets, while the leader has 1 entry with 1 ATM bracket set. When BE-ALL fires, Step A snapshots targets from both ATM sets on each follower, producing more OCO tranches than the leader.

EVIDENCE (log 2026-08-23 06:52)
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim102  <-- partial 1 (2 lots)
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim103
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim104
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim102  <-- partial 2 (5 lots)
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim103
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim104

Confirmed by executions CSV: Sell 2 @ 7698.75 (6:52:28) then Sell 5 @ 7698.75 (6:52:33) on all 4 accounts. Two separate entry rows per account. 2-lot row produces ATM bracket set A; 5-lot row produces ATM bracket set B.

ROOT CAUSE

The copy engine dispatches in OnExecutionUpdate keyed on execution events, not on position-confirmed events. A single order that generates N execution events fires N dispatch calls. Each dispatch is treated as an independent entry and places a fresh ATM bracket set.

Contrast: OnPositionUpdate fires once per position-level change (aggregate), not per execution. Routing dispatch through position confirmation would collapse all partials into a single dispatch.

FIX DIRECTION

Gate dispatch in OnExecutionUpdate against a per-order dedup set. Track execution.Order.Id in a ConcurrentDictionary<string,bool> _dispatchedOrders. On first execution for a given order ID: dispatch and record. On subsequent executions for the same order ID: skip dispatch (partial fill of same order).

The set should be scoped to the current bar or cleared on position-flat event to prevent stale IDs accumulating across trades.

Impact: followers receive exactly 1 entry per leader order regardless of how many partial fills NT8 produces. Follower ATM bracket count matches leader. Step A target snapshot produces correct tranche count.

DW-B91-B OPEN Copy Engine

Copy engine exit dispatch re-opens flat follower accounts

SYMPTOM

After BE-ALL fires and PTT-BE stops fill (closing all accounts), the leader's position goes flat. The copy engine sees leader flat and dispatches an exit order (BuyToCover on a short, or Sell on a long) to all follower accounts. By this time, followers are already flat from their own PTT-BE stop fills.

NT8 cannot execute BuyToCover on a flat account; it treats the order as a new long entry. Followers end up with an unintended open position in the opposite direction while the leader is flat.

Observed as: "left with followers only after BE-ALL" -- leader flat, followers unexpectedly long (after short BE) or short (after long BE).

EVIDENCE (log 2026-08-23 06:52-06:53)

Cycle 1 BE-ALL sequence:

-- PTT-BE stops fill on all followers (102/103/104) --
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3/4  <-- OCO cancel = stop filled, follower flat
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3/4
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3/4
-- PTT-BE stop fills on leader (101) --
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim101 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3/4  <-- leader flat
-- copy engine detects leader flat, dispatches exit to followers --
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Buy x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim102 mode=Named name=Entry
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Buy x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim103 mode=Named name=Entry
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Buy x7 MES SEP26 -> Sim104 mode=Named name=Entry
<-- followers already flat; Buy on flat short account = new long position
ROOT CAUSE

The copy engine's OnPositionUpdate handler fires when the leader goes flat. It dispatches an exit to followers unconditionally. It has no awareness that PTT-BE already closed the follower positions independently.

The two exit mechanisms (PTT-BE stop fills vs copy engine exit dispatch) race. PTT-BE is faster (stops fire individually per account), but the copy engine dispatch follows within milliseconds on the leader flat event.

FIX DIRECTION

Add a per-account BE-in-flight flag: ConcurrentDictionary<string,DateTime> _beInFlight (key = acc.Name, value = UTC timestamp of BE-ALL press).

  1. Set flag at the top of MoveStopToBreakEven for each account processed by BE-ALL: _beInFlight[acc.Name] = DateTime.UtcNow.
  2. Gate the exit dispatch in the leader-flat branch of OnPositionUpdate: if _beInFlight contains the follower key and the timestamp is within the last 3 seconds, skip the exit dispatch for that follower.
  3. Clear flag in OnOrderUpdate when the PTT-BE stop for that account transitions to Filled.

Simpler alternative (2-line fix): in the leader-flat dispatch loop, skip any follower whose position is already Flat at the moment the dispatch fires: if (FindPosition(followerAcc, instr)?.Quantity == 0) continue; This has a narrow race window if the follower flat event has not propagated yet, but covers the common case with zero new fields.

PATH B CYCLE 1 RESULT — FAIL (2026-08-23)

Test: BE-ALL only (no QX). Single entry, 3-tranche ATM. BE-ALL pressed immediately.

Entry dispatch: single [PTT-COPY] dispatch: per follower (DW-B91-A working for non-partial fill). BE-ALL placed PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3 + PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 on all 4 accounts correctly. T1 target price reached → PTT-BE-Target-1 filled → OCO cancelled PTT-BE-Stop-1 on all accounts. Result: PTT-BE-Stop-2, PTT-BE-Target-2, PTT-BE-Stop-3, PTT-BE-Target-3 all cancelled on all followers. Remaining 2 tranches unprotected. Followers left with open position, no brackets.

[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1   <-- T1 OCO cancel (correct)
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim101 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-2   <-- recovery wipe (BUG)
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-2
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-3
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-3
...same on Sim102, Sim104, Sim101
ROOT CAUSE

The DW-B90 guard HasFilledBeTarget loses a race against the OCO cancel event.

When PTT-BE-Target-1 fills, NT8 fires two events nearly simultaneously:

  1. OnOrderUpdate(PTT-BE-Target-1, Filled) — records the fill in acc.Orders
  2. OnOrderUpdate(PTT-BE-Stop-1, Cancelled) — OCO partner cancel

If event (2) arrives before event (1) is fully committed to acc.Orders, HasFilledBeTarget scans acc.Orders, finds no Filled PTT-BE-Target-*, returns false, and TryReplacePttBeBrackets fires. The recovery path calls MoveStopToBreakEven(isRetry:true) → PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute → CancelQxBrackets which cancels all remaining live PTT-BE brackets (Stop-2, Target-2, Stop-3, Target-3), then places new brackets at the entry price. The new brackets may also be immediately wiped by the same race on T2 fill.

The DW-B90 guard is correct in design but insufficient in timing. The OCO cancel event is an NT8 async callback. acc.Orders is not guaranteed to reflect the Target-1 fill state at the instant the Stop-1 cancel callback fires.

EVIDENCE TRACE

Sequence from log (2026-08-23):

  1. BE-ALL places PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3 + PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 on all 4 accounts. ✅
  2. Price reaches T1 target. PTT-BE-Target-1 fills on Sim102/103/104/101. ✅
  3. PTT-BE-Stop-1 OCO-cancelled on all accounts. ✅ (correct, expected)
  4. OnOrderUpdate(PTT-BE-Stop-1, Cancelled) fires. HasFilledBeTarget runs → race lost → returns false → TryReplacePttBeBrackets fires. ❌
  5. 500ms fallback queued. After 500ms: MoveStopToBreakEven(isRetry:true) fires.
  6. PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute calls CancelQxBrackets → cancels Stop-2, Target-2, Stop-3, Target-3. ❌
  7. New brackets placed at entry price (not at T1-adjusted entry). Followers may be partially protected or not at all depending on price.

The PositionStateChanged hasPos=True between the Stop-1 cancels and the Stop-2/3 wipes confirms a new entry was started during this window, compounding the bracket chaos.

FIX DIRECTION

The DW-B90 HasFilledBeTarget guard must be race-proof. The OCO cancel of a PTT-BE-Stop is ONLY legitimate in two cases:

  1. OCO cancel from target fill — partner target hit price. Do NOT retry.
  2. ATM sweep cancel — NT8 internal StartAtmStrategy wipe. DO retry.

Distinguishing them reliably:
OCO-cancel always arrives paired with a target fill for the same OCO group. The OCO id is embedded in the order. Instead of scanning acc.Orders for any Filled target (which races), check the specific OCO partner:
HasFilledBeTarget(cancelledStop.OcoId) — look for a Filled PTT-BE-Target-* with the same OcoId as the cancelled stop. An ATM sweep cancel has no such partner.

Simpler alternative (1-line fix):
Check if cancelled stop's OcoId is non-empty. OCO-cancelled orders always have a populated OcoId. ATM sweep cancels arrive with empty OcoId (NT8 sweep does not set the OCO group on the cancel event).
Guard: if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(cancelledStop.Oco)) return; // OCO cancel, not sweep
This requires NT8 API verification: does Order.Oco remain populated after OCO cancel? See NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md for Order.Oco property availability on Cancelled orders.

Alternative B (state-based, no API risk):
Track a per-account ConcurrentDictionary<string,int> _filledBeTargetCount (key = acc.Name, value = count of PTT-BE-Target-* fills). Increment on OnOrderUpdate(PTT-BE-Target-*, Filled). In TryReplacePttBeBrackets, check _filledBeTargetCount[acc.Name] > 0 instead of scanning acc.Orders. The counter update happens synchronously in OnOrderUpdate before the cancel arrives in the next event, eliminating the race. Clear counter on position-flat or new entry.
This is the recommended fix — no NT8 API uncertainty.

Test 1 (QX→BE, previous test) showed double dispatch (2 dispatches per follower). Root cause (separately diagnosed):

  • NT8 event ordering for partial fills: OnOrderUpdate(Filled) fires first, calling EvictDedup which clears both _dedupCache and _entryDispatchedOrders.
  • Then OnOrderUpdate(Submitted) for the second partial fires (NT8 re-submits the remainder), or OnOrderUpdate(Submitted) fires twice for different fill events of the same underlying order ID.
  • After eviction, both caches are empty → IsDedup returns false → IsEntryDispatched returns false → second dispatch proceeds.

Fix direction for DW-B91-A (to be added to pipeline ticket):
Do NOT evict _entryDispatchedOrders in EvictDedup. Instead, evict it in the position-flat handler (TryEvictFollowerBeSlot or PositionStateChanged hasPos=False branch). The dict is keyed by unique NT8 order IDs (GUIDs), so memory accumulation across trades is trivial (<1 KB per trading day). Removing the co-evict line from EvictDedup (L3088) is a 1-line change.

QX-ALL: follower snapshot=0 because Named ATM "Entry" Limit is invisible to IsQxCancelCandidate

QX-ALL SIM RESULT — FAIL (3 consecutive runs, 2026-08-23)

Test: Clean single entry (Sell x7, Named ATM mode). Single [PTT-COPY] dispatch: per follower. leaderTargets=3 correct. QX-ALL pressed while followers have open short position.

Result every run: [PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 cancellable orders on Sim102/103/104. PTT-QX-Stop + PTT-QX-T1/2/3 placed on followers against a position that already has an unsettled ATM bracket state. Followers lose all bracket protection when T1 fills.

[PTT-QX-ALL] follower: Sim102 MES SEP26 leaderStop=7688.25 leaderTargets=3
[PTT-QX-GUARD] pre-cancel follower brackets: Sim102
[PTT-QX] stop resolved: 7688.25 on Sim102
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 cancellable orders for MES SEP26   <-- BUG: "Entry" Limit invisible
[PTT-QX] cancel: 0 queued, 0 race-skipped on Sim102
... same for Sim103, Sim104

Screenshot confirmed: Orders grid shows leader (Sim101) has 4 Working/Accepted PTT-QX orders. Sim102/103/104 show no orders in the grid — only open positions.

ROOT CAUSE

SendCopyWithAtm creates the follower entry as OrderType.Limit named "Entry". In NT8, StartAtmStrategy arms ATM brackets only after this entry Limit fills. Until it fills, the follower account has one order: the unfilled "Entry" Limit. No Stop1, no Target1/2/3 yet.

When QX-ALL fires, BuildQxSnapshot runs IsQxCancelCandidate on every order. The guard matches:

  • IsAtmBracketName → Stop1..Stop9, Target1..Target9
  • PTT-QX-* prefix
  • PTT-BE-* prefix
  • PTT-Copy* prefix

The name "Entry" matches none of these. The unfilled follower entry Limit is invisible to the cancel sweep → snapshot=0 → cancel: 0 queued → QX submits PTT-QX brackets alongside the still-arming ATM strategy.

NT8 then has two bracket systems competing on the follower: the ATM brackets (Stop1/Target1/2/3) armed by StartAtmStrategy when the "Entry" Limit fills, and the PTT-QX-Stop/T1/2/3 orders just submitted by QX. When T1 price is reached, the ATM T1 target fills, NT8 OCO-cancels the ATM Stop1, and TryReplacePttBeBrackets (DW-B92 race) then wipes the PTT-QX brackets too. Result: follower flat on T1 with nothing protecting the remaining tranches.

FIX DIRECTION

Option A — Add "Entry" to IsQxCancelCandidate (1-line fix, recommended):

// In IsQxCancelCandidate (CopyEngine.cs ~L713):
if (o.Name == "Entry")
    return true; // (6) DW-B93: Named ATM follower entry Limit -- cancel before QX places PTT-QX brackets

When QX-ALL fires, the unfilled follower "Entry" Limit is cancelled before PTT-QX orders are placed. The ATM never arms (no entry to attach to). QX takes full ownership of the position protection. Clean state.

Side-effect to verify: IsQxCancelCandidate is also called by PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute via CancelQxBrackets. Adding "Entry" means BE-ALL will also cancel any unfilled follower entry Limit. This is correct behaviour — BE-ALL should not leave an open entry order. Verify there is no path where a legitimate "Entry" Limit should survive a BE-ALL or QX-ALL press.

CYC impact: IsQxCancelCandidate gains one branch: CYC 6 → 7. Still within the JS ≤8 limit.

Option B — Wait for ATM settlement before QX: Poll follower acc.Orders for Stop1..Stop9 / Target1..Target9 Working state before firing QX on each follower. Requires async/timer delay (~100ms). More invasive. Option A is preferred.

DW-B94 — SIM Evidence: Follower PTT-BE Brackets Wiped on Every Target Fill

Observed on every test cycle where price reached any PTT-BE-Target (2026-08-23):

  • 9:30 PM: PTT-BE-Target-1 fills (4 lots, Long). Remaining 3L brackets gone 30s later. Manual close.
  • 10:31 PM: PTT-BE-Target-1 (1 lot) + Target-2 (3 lots, Short) fill. Remaining 3S brackets gone. PTT-Flatten required.
  • 10:38 PM QX log: same pattern confirmed — brackets vanish on follower target hit.

Contrasting: stopped-out path always works. Every BE-stop-out trade (7:02, 7:13, 7:29, 6:58, 6:59, 10:17 PM) worked perfectly — all PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3/4 filled in order on all 4 accounts. The defect is exclusively triggered by the target-fill (winning trade) path.

DW-B92 counter guard confirmed working: No TryReplacePttBeBrackets log line appeared after any target fill. The DW-B92 fix is correct. DW-B94 is a separate, independent bug.

DW-B94 — Root Cause: IsNonFlatDispatchName Does Not Cover ATM Bracket Names

When the leader’s ATM Target1 fills, NT8 OCO-cancels the paired Stop1. That Cancelled event fires OnOrderUpdate on the leader account with e.Order.Name = "Stop1". The call chain then hits TryDispatchLeaderFlat:

// TryDispatchLeaderFlat guard sequence for Name="Stop1", State=Cancelled:

(1) state == Cancelled                          → PASSES (Cancelled is allowed)
(2) isFollower(account)                         → PASSES (Sim101 is leader)
(2.5) IsNonFlatDispatchName("Stop1")            → false  ← BUG: "Stop1" not listed
       IsNonFlatDispatchName only covers:
         (1) orderName.StartsWith("PTT-")       → false
         (2) orderName == "Entry"               → false
       "Stop1".."Stop9" and "Target1".."Target9" are NOT covered
(3) !IsNativeExitName("Stop1")                  → true (not Close/Flatten/Rev/Exit)
    && hasOpenPosition(leader, MES)             → FALSE (NT8 position race —
       NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md line 1721: position not updated until next OnBarUpdate)
    → guard (3) DOES NOT FIRE (hasOpenPosition returns false due to race)
(4) foreach follower: FlattenFollower fires      ← SPURIOUS FLATTEN
    → PTT-Flatten dispatched to Sim102/103/104
    → All PTT-BE-Stop-2/3/4 + PTT-BE-Target-2/3/4 CANCELLED

The same race applies to Target1 OCO-cancelling Stop1 for any tranche. The ATM bracket cancel arrives during the NT8 position update gap, making hasOpenPosition unreliable at that instant.

Why the stop-out path works: When the BE stop fills, the order name is "PTT-BE-Stop-1" — which starts with "PTT-" and IS caught by IsNonFlatDispatchName guard (1). No spurious flatten fires.

DW-B94 — Fix: Add ATM Bracket Names to IsNonFlatDispatchName

File: src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs
Method: IsNonFlatDispatchName (~L1728)
Change: Add 1 branch (CYC 2→3, well within JS CYC≤8)
Jane Street rules: JS-021 no lock · JS-001 no throw · ASCII-only

// BEFORE (CYC=2):
internal static bool IsNonFlatDispatchName(string orderName)
{
    if (orderName != null && orderName.StartsWith("PTT-", StringComparison.Ordinal))
        return true; // (1)
    if (orderName == "Entry")
        return true; // (2)
    return false;
}

// AFTER (CYC=3) DW-B94:
// IsNonFlatDispatchName: CYC=3. Returns true when orderName must NOT trigger follower flatten.
// Combines HOTFIX-B63-FLATTEN-01 (PTT- prefix), HOTFIX-B64-ENTRY-FLATTEN-01 ("Entry"),
// and DW-B94 (ATM bracket names Stop1..Stop9 / Target1..Target9).
// ATM bracket cancel events arrive during NT8 position update gap (NT8_FULL_REFERENCE line 1721)
// and must never trigger a follower flatten -- the position is still live.
// JS-001: no throw. JS-002: returns bool. JS-021: no lock. ASCII-only.
internal static bool IsNonFlatDispatchName(string orderName)
{
    if (orderName != null && orderName.StartsWith("PTT-", StringComparison.Ordinal))
        return true; // (1)
    if (orderName == "Entry")
        return true; // (2)
    if (IsAtmBracketName(orderName))
        return true; // (3) DW-B94: Stop1..Stop9 / Target1..Target9 -- ATM cancel must not flatten followers
    return false;
}

Why this is safe: IsAtmBracketName matches Stop[1-9] and Target[1-9] only. These are NT8 ATM internal bracket names — they never represent a user-initiated close. Adding them to IsNonFlatDispatchName makes the method return true, causing TryDispatchLeaderFlat to return false at guard (2.5) — no follower flatten, no bracket wipe.

No side effects on stop-out path: BE stop-out uses PTT-BE-Stop-* names (already blocked by guard 1). This change adds no new code paths to the stop-out flow.

DW-B93-v2 — SIM Log Evidence (2026-08-23 ~10:35 PM)
[PTT-QX-ALL] follower: Sim102 MES SEP26 leaderStop=7687.25 leaderTargets=3
[PTT-QX-GUARD] pre-cancel follower brackets: Sim102
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 cancellable orders for MES SEP26   ← BUG: should be >0

Note: The original DW-B93 fix (o.Name == "Entry") targeted the case where the follower’s Entry limit is still pending when QX fires. This fix is correct for that timing. DW-B93-v2 is a different failure mode: in SIM, the follower’s Entry limit fills near-instantly, so by the time QX-ALL runs the Entry order is gone and ATM brackets have (or have not yet) been placed.

DW-B93-v2 — Root Cause: Timing Gap Between Entry Fill and ATM Bracket Placement

In Named ATM mode the follower lifecycle is:

  1. PTT dispatches Entry limit to follower (Working/Accepted)
  2. Entry fills (near-instant in SIM)
  3. NT8 detects fill → starts ATM strategy → places bracket orders (Stop1, Target1 etc.)

Steps 2→3 have a small async gap. If QX-ALL fires:

  • Between step 1→2: DW-B93 fix catches the live Entry order (snapshot ≥1) ✅
  • Between step 2→3: Entry is gone, brackets not yet placed → snapshot=0 ❌
  • After step 3: Brackets present, IsAtmBracketName catches them (snapshot ≥4) ✅

The snapshot=0 window is the gap between entry fill and bracket placement. On real brokers with network latency this window may be wider than in SIM.

Priority note: DW-B94 (P0) must be fixed first. Once DW-B94 is resolved and followers no longer get spuriously flattened, DW-B93-v2’s bracket leak (ATM brackets not cancelled before PTT-QX placed) becomes the next blocker for PATH B QX cycles. Resolve DW-B94 first, then re-test QX path to confirm DW-B93-v2 severity.

DW-B93-v2 — Fix Direction (pending DW-B94 resolution)

Two options (engineer to choose after DW-B94 validation):

Option A — Retry snapshot with short delay: In CancelQxBrackets, if snapshot=0 on a follower with an open position, wait 100ms and retry the snapshot scan once. Covers the entry-fill → bracket-placement gap.

Option B — Cancel before placing PTT-QX: Before placing PTT-QX orders on a follower, cancel all working orders on that account for the instrument (regardless of name), then place PTT-QX. More aggressive but race-proof.

Decision deferred until DW-B94 is resolved and re-tested.

✓ DW-B95  ◆  PTT-COPIER-B95  ◆  _entryDispatchedOrders Never Evicted on Leader-Account Position Close  ◆  CLOSED (P1)  ·  ptt-direct-repair
DW-B95 — Regression Introduced By DW-B91-A-v2

DW-B91-A-v2 moved _entryDispatchedOrders eviction from EvictDedup (per-orderId TryRemove) to TryEvictFollowerBeSlot (bulk Clear() on position-flat). The stated intent was to evict the entire set when the instrument position closes, preventing stale dedup entries from blocking re-entry after flat.

The eviction never fires for leader-account closes. TryEvictFollowerBeSlot has a follower-only guard at L1398 that returns early for any non-follower account. The .Clear() at L1406 is unreachable when the leader’s order reaches Filled or Cancelled.

DW-B95 — Root Cause: Clear() Sits Below Follower-Only Guard

Call chain for a leader account order reaching Filled:

// TryEvictFollowerBeSlot (CopyEngine.cs L1387-1419)

L1390  var o = e?.Order;
L1391  if (o == null) return;                       // (1) null guard
L1396  if (!isFilled && !isRejected) return;        // (2) terminal-state guard
L1398  if (!IsFollowerAccount(o.Account)) return;   // (4) FOLLOWERS ONLY -- leader exits HERE
       ...
L1406  _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear();              // UNREACHABLE for leader account

Meanwhile, EvictDedup (L3095-3107) no longer calls _entryDispatchedOrders.TryRemove (removed by DW-B91-A-v2). No other eviction site exists for the leader path. The dictionary grows unbounded across the session.

Severity note: NT8 assigns unique GUID orderIds per order, so in a clean single-session live run, new orders never collide with stale entries and dispatch is not immediately blocked. The risk is latent and edge-case: SIM reconnect / broker reconnect orderId reuse, multi-trade sessions where the same logical order token is recycled, or any future change to orderId format. Classified P1 (correctness violation, not immediately user-visible).

DW-B95 — Proposed Fix: Move Clear() Above Follower Guard

Relocate _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear() above the IsFollowerAccount guard so it fires for any account whose order causes position-flat. The per-account _pendingFollowerBeSlots, _beReplaceAttempts, and _filledBeTargetCount removals stay below the guard (they are follower-specific). Only the instrument-level dedup clear moves up.

// BEFORE (DW-B91-A-v2):
L1398  if (!IsFollowerAccount(o.Account)) return; // (4)
       ...
L1406  _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear();   // unreachable for leader

// AFTER (DW-B95):
       _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear();   // instrument-level reset -- fires for ALL accounts
L1398  if (!IsFollowerAccount(o.Account)) return; // (4) follower-only evictions below
       ...
       // _pendingFollowerBeSlots.TryRemove, _beReplaceAttempts.TryRemove,
       // _filledBeTargetCount.TryRemove remain below guard (follower-scoped)

CYC impact: 0 (no new branches; pure reorder of existing statements).

Introduced by: DW-B91-A-v2 (moved eviction from EvictDedup to TryEvictFollowerBeSlot without accounting for leader-account guard).

✓ DW-B95 — CLOSED

_entryDispatchedOrders.Clear() moved above the IsFollowerAccount guard in TryEvictFollowerBeSlot (L1395). CYC=6, unchanged. Instrument-level dedup reset now fires for all accounts (leader + follower) on position-flat. Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. CSharpier: clean.

✓ DW-B96  ◆  PTT-COPIER-B96  ◆  ChartTrader Limit Entry Never Dispatched (Working State Bypasses IsDispatchTriggerState)  ◆  CLOSED (P0)  ·  ptt-direct-repair
DW-B96 — Failure Mode: Leader Places Limit Entry via ChartTrader → Followers Get Nothing, BE-ALL Fires on Empty Follower Positions
  • Leader places a Limit entry order using the NT8 ChartTrader (not the PTT AddOn panel).
  • NT8 delivers OnOrderUpdate with sequence: Initialized → Submitted → Working (no discrete Accepted event for ChartTrader-originated orders on Rithmic/SIM).
  • DispatchCopy Gate 3 calls IsDispatchTriggerState(Working, Limit) → returns false → early return.
  • No follower copy placed. Leader fills; leader has open position. Followers are flat.
  • BE-ALL fires. MoveStopToBreakEven is called per-account. For each follower: IsFlat(pos) at L3314 is true → silent “flat skip” return. BE-ALL log shows fires but no brackets placed — because followers are flat, not because BE-ALL is broken.
DW-B96 — Root Cause: IsDispatchTriggerState Limit Path Requires Accepted; ChartTrader Delivers Working

The existing logic at CopyEngine.cs:L1658-1660:

// L1655 comment (existing): "AddOn limit orders skip Submitted; they arrive first as Accepted"
internal static bool IsDispatchTriggerState(OrderState state, OrderType type) =>
    (type == OrderType.Market && state == OrderState.Submitted)  // Market: GUID-keyed, Submitted only
    || (type == OrderType.Limit  && state == OrderState.Accepted); // Limit: first exchange ack

This is correct for orders placed via the PTT AddOn API (account.CreateOrder() + Submit()). Those orders first appear in OnOrderUpdate as Accepted.

ChartTrader-originated Limit orders follow a different NT8 state path: Initialized → Submitted → Working. The Accepted state is absent (or only present as a transient internal state not surfaced in OnOrderUpdate on Rithmic/SIM). The Limit dispatch trigger never fires.

Key asymmetry: Market orders are unaffected (trigger on Submitted, which ChartTrader does deliver). Only Limit-type leader entries via ChartTrader are broken.

BE-ALL is NOT independently broken. MoveStopToBreakEven L3314 correctly skips flat follower accounts. The absence of brackets on followers is entirely downstream of no dispatch having occurred.

DW-B96 — Proposed Fix: Extend Limit Trigger to Include Working

Widen the Limit condition in IsDispatchTriggerState to also accept Working. The existing _dedupCache in DispatchCopy (Gate 5, L1769) protects against double-dispatch: AddOn-originated orders that do produce an Accepted event will be deduped when the subsequent Working event arrives with the same orderId + limitPrice key.

// BEFORE (current — L1658-1660):
internal static bool IsDispatchTriggerState(OrderState state, OrderType type) =>
    (type == OrderType.Market && state == OrderState.Submitted)
    || (type == OrderType.Limit  && state == OrderState.Accepted);

// AFTER (DW-B96):
internal static bool IsDispatchTriggerState(OrderState state, OrderType type) =>
    (type == OrderType.Market && state == OrderState.Submitted)
    || (type == OrderType.Limit  && (state == OrderState.Accepted   // AddOn path (unchanged)
                                  || state == OrderState.Working));  // ChartTrader path (DW-B96)

Dedup safety: AddOn-originated Limit orders trigger on Accepted (first event). When Working arrives later for the same orderId, IsDedup(orderId, limitPrice) returns true (already keyed) → DispatchCopy returns at Gate 5. No double-dispatch.

ChartTrader-originated Limit orders skip Accepted entirely. Working is the first event that passes Gate 3. IsDedup returns false (new orderId). Dispatch proceeds normally.

CYC impact: IsDispatchTriggerState CYC 2 → 2. The OR within the Limit branch is a single boolean expression inside the existing ternary; McCabe counts it as the same conditional branch (the Limit ternary arm). Confirm with complexity audit after implementation.

Note on comment update: The L1655 comment should be updated to describe both AddOn path (Accepted) and ChartTrader path (Working). Engineer to update in the same commit.

IMPLEMENTED. Director-approved ptt-direct-repair. IsDispatchTriggerState Limit arm extended to include Working. Comment updated for AddOn path + ChartTrader path. Build: 0 errors. CYC=2, unchanged.

DW-B97 — Residual Gap: _entryDispatchedOrders Not Evicted on Cancelled

The TryEvictFollowerBeSlot guard at L1393 only runs _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear() for Filled or Rejected PTT-BE-Stop orders. A Cancelled entry order (e.g. user cancels a pending Limit before it fills) does not trigger the Clear. The orderId accumulates in _entryDispatchedOrders indefinitely until the next Filled trade.

This is not a blocking defect for normal operation: NT8 assigns a unique new orderId per order, so stale Cancelled entries never collide with fresh entry orderIds. The only effect is unbounded dictionary growth during a session with many cancelled orders (memory, no correctness impact).

Proposed fix (DW-B98, low-priority): Extend EvictDedup to also call _entryDispatchedOrders.TryRemove(orderId, out _) on Filled | Cancelled | Rejected — restoring the original DW-B91-A design. The DW-B91-A-v2 rationale for moving eviction was to prevent Rithmic re-submit double-dispatch; the _dedupCache already covers that path, making the _entryDispatchedOrders per-orderId TryRemove safe to restore. CYC delta: 0.

DW-B98 — Why the Previous Workaround Failed

The previous workaround said: "open PTT window → click Copy ON → re-apply follower checkbox". The user opened the window and clicked Copy ON ("clicking clone again") but did NOT re-check the follower checkbox. That omission means TryAutoApply() never fired, AddRule() was never called, _rules stayed empty, and Gate 2 blocked every order.

⚠ The checkbox check is mandatory. It is the only call path that registers a live rule. Clicking Copy ON alone is not sufficient.

DW-B98 — Correct Workaround (Right Now, No Code Change)
  1. In the ChartTrader panel, find the follower account row. CHECK the follower checkbox.
    This fires: chk.Checked lambda → TryAutoApply() → _engine.AddRule() → _engine.SaveRules(). This is the only action that registers a live rule with real Account object references AND writes the XML.
  2. Watch the status text in the panel. It must say: Rule: [instrument] leader=[account].
    If it says "No leader" or "No instrument" or nothing changes — the rule was NOT registered. Check that ChartTrader has an account selected and a chart is open.
  3. Click the COPY ON button. Button must show green / “COPY ON”.
  4. Place a test Market order on the leader account. Immediately watch NT8 Output Tab 1 for: [PTT-COPY] dispatch: Buy x1 [instrument] -> [follower] mult=1 mode=Inherit name=Entry
  5. If the dispatch line appears → working. If it does not → reply with the exact text in Output Tab 1.

This sequence must be repeated after every F5 until the three code fixes (A/B/C below) go through the pipeline. After the fixes, the panel will auto-restore the rule and Copy ON state from XML on every F5.

DW-B98 — Three Code Fixes (Pipeline Required)

Fix A — CopyEngine.SetEnabled() must call SaveRules():
Persists the Copy ON/OFF state to XML immediately on toggle so it survives F5.

// CopyEngine.cs ~L467 SetEnabled
internal void SetEnabled(bool enabled)
{
    _isCopyEnabled = enabled;
    StatusUpdate?.Invoke("Copy " + (enabled ? "ON" : "OFF"));
    CopyEnabledChanged?.Invoke(enabled);
    SaveRules(); // DW-B98-A: persist enabled state on every toggle
}

Fix B — TradeCopierPanel.OnApplyRule() must call SaveRules():
The hidden Apply button path adds a rule but never saves. Add the save after AddRule().

// TradeCopierPanel.cs ~L2767 OnApplyRule
_engine.AddRule(_instrument.FullName, _leaderAccount, followers, multipliers, atmMap);
_engine.SaveRules(); // DW-B98-B: persist rule immediately

Fix C — TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded() must call LoadRules():
Insert after the Account.All loop (line 698, accounts populated) and before the B67 checkbox-restore block (line 705). This ensures: (1) DtoToRule has live Account references; (2) GetSavedFollowerNames can find rules; (3) B67 fires TryAutoApply which replaces the XML-restored rule with live Account references.

// TradeCopierPanel.cs OnLoaded -- INSERT AFTER line 698, BEFORE line 705 (B67 block)

LoadRules() at CopyEngine.cs:4086 does:

Why is the file missing? The DW-B98 fixes add SaveRules() to SetEnabled(), OnApplyRule(), and TryAutoApply(). But those paths can only write the XML after the user takes a UI action in the new session. The file has never been written in any prior session because:

  1. Before commit e06bce7b, SetEnabled() had no SaveRules() call
  2. Before commit e06bce7b, TryAutoApply() in DW-B98's pre-fix version had no SaveRules() call
  3. The TradeCopierWindow path calls SaveRules(), but the user never opened the Window (always uses ChartTrader injection)

Even with e06bce7b, the first session after apply must manually check a follower checkbox to create the XML. Until then, every LoadRules call is a no-op.

DW-B99 — Blocker B: _persistenceLoaded Never Resets Across F5 Cycles

CopyEngine is a static readonly singleton — the CLR initialises it once per AppDomain and it never dies while NT8 is running:

// CopyEngine.cs L125
private static readonly CopyEngine _instance = new CopyEngine();

// CopyEngine.cs L3867
private volatile bool _persistenceLoaded = false;  // ← instance field ON THE SINGLETON

LoadRules() at CopyEngine.cs:4081-4083:

if (_persistenceLoaded)
    return;                // ← PERMANENT NO-OP after first LoadRules call
_persistenceLoaded = true;

Sequence within a single NT8 session (without full restart):

  1. NT8 starts → _persistenceLoaded = false (singleton fresh)
  2. Panel OnLoaded fires → LoadRules() called → _persistenceLoaded = true, XML not found → no-op
  3. User checks follower checkbox → TryAutoApply() → AddRule() → SaveRules() → XML written for first time
  4. User clicks Copy ON → SetEnabled(true) → SaveRules() → XML updated with CopyEnabled=true
  5. User presses F5 → NT8 destroys/recreates TradeCopierAddOn + TradeCopierPanel → new panel's OnLoaded fires → _engine.LoadRules() called
  6. LoadRules() checks _persistenceLoaded → it is still true from step 2 (singleton never recreated) → immediate return, nothing loaded
  7. XML exists but is never read. _rules still has the in-memory rules from step 3 (NOT cleared on F5 either) → rules appear to survive!

⚠ Wait — step 7 means rules DO survive F5 within the same NT8 session (singleton kept in RAM). The copier should work after the first manual setup, even across F5. This is actually correct behaviour. The problem is a full NT8 restart, not F5.

But on full NT8 restart:

  1. NT8 restarts → AppDomain recycled → singleton recreated → _persistenceLoaded = false, _rules empty, _isCopyEnabled = false
  2. Panel OnLoaded fires → LoadRules() → sets _persistenceLoaded = true → reads XML → restores rules + _isCopyEnabled → B67 block fires TryAutoApply → SHOULD WORK

Conclusion: The _persistenceLoaded guard is NOT a problem after full restart. It IS a problem if LoadRules is called multiple times within the same session (e.g. both Window and Panel attach). This is intentional dedup design and is correct.

● DW-B100  ◆  PTT-COPIER-B100  ◆  SaveRules() Always Silently Fails — XmlSerializer Cannot Serialize Private Classes  ◆  OPEN (P0)  ·  ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED
DW-B100 — Root Cause: private sealed class on DTO Types

XmlSerializer requires that the type it is asked to serialize be publicly accessible. Both DTO types used by SaveRules() are declared private sealed class:

// CopyEngine.cs L3872 -- CURRENT
[Serializable]
private sealed class CopyRuleDto          // ← XmlSerializer cannot access this

// CopyEngine.cs L3893
[Serializable]
private sealed class CopyRulesContainer   // ← XmlSerializer cannot access this

When SaveRules() at CopyEngine.cs:4057 executes:

var serializer = new XmlSerializer(typeof(CopyRulesContainer));  // ← throws here

The XmlSerializer constructor throws InvalidOperationException: "CopyRulesContainer is not accessible because it is private". This is immediately caught by the catch (Exception) block at L4066 which swallows all exceptions silently. File.WriteAllText is never reached. The XML file is never written. Ever.

This is present in every commit going back to B6 (when SaveRules was first written). copy_rules.xml has never been written to disk in any session in the history of this project.

DW-B100 — Evidence
Evidence Result
Filesystem search for copy_rules.xml anywhere on disk (recursive) Zero results — file has never been written
TryAutoApply() executes successfully — status text shows Rule: MES SEP26 leader=Sim101 AddRule() succeeded — rule is in RAM
TryAutoApply() calls _engine.SaveRules() immediately after AddRule() Returns silently — exception swallowed by catch (Exception)
File.WriteAllText() tested directly from PowerShell to the exact same path Succeeds — directory is writable, no permissions issue
CopyRuleDto and CopyRulesContainer access modifier in all commits private sealed class — confirmed in both ee6b1dcf (before) and current HEAD
Copier was working "yesterday" during same NT8 session Rules were live in singleton RAM — never needed XML. Fresh start = rules gone.
DW-B100 — Why the Copier "Was Working Yesterday"

The copier has always worked within a single NT8 session. The flow is:

  1. NT8 starts → singleton fresh → _rules empty
  2. User checks follower checkbox → TryAutoApply() → AddRule() → rule lands in _rules (RAM) ✅
  3. SaveRules() is called but throws silently → no XML written
  4. User clicks COPY ON → _isCopyEnabled=true in RAM
  5. Leader places orders → OnOrderUpdate fires → Gate 1 passes (_isCopyEnabled=true) → Gate 2 passes (_rules has the rule from step 2) → Dispatch fires. Followers get orders. ✅
  6. F5 recompile within same NT8 session → singleton survives in RAM → _rules still populated → copier still works ✅
  7. NT8 closed and restarted → singleton recycled → _rules empty → LoadRules() looks for XML → XML missing → returns → _rules stays empty → Gate 2 blocks everything ❌

The fix commit DW-B98 did not help because the underlying XML write was always failing. The missing LoadRules in panel.OnLoaded (DW-B98-C) was a real gap, but it doesn't matter if the XML never gets written in the first place.

DW-B100 — The Fix: Change private to internal on Both DTO Classes

XmlSerializer works with internal types within the same assembly. Since both DTO classes are inner private types of CopyEngine, they only need to be accessible to the serializer — not to external code. Changing private to internal makes them serializable while keeping them unexposed to other assemblies.

// CopyEngine.cs L3872 -- CHANGE private to internal
[Serializable]
internal sealed class CopyRuleDto          // ← was: private sealed class

// CopyEngine.cs L3893 -- CHANGE private to internal
[Serializable]
internal sealed class CopyRulesContainer   // ← was: private sealed class

Alternative fix (also valid): Move the two DTO classes out of CopyEngine and declare them as public (or internal) top-level classes in the PropTraderTools namespace. This is cleaner architecturally but requires more edits.

Change File Line From To CYC Δ Priority
DW-B100-A CopyEngine.cs 3872 private sealed class CopyRuleDto internal sealed class CopyRuleDto 0 P0 BLOCKER
DW-B100-B CopyEngine.cs 3893 private sealed class CopyRulesContainer internal sealed class CopyRulesContainer 0 P0 BLOCKER

After this fix: SaveRules() will write copy_rules.xml correctly. After the file is written once (by checking a follower checkbox + clicking COPY ON), every subsequent NT8 restart will automatically restore the rule and enabled state via LoadRules() in panel.OnLoaded.
