DW-B102 Post-Restart Copy Outage — _persistenceLoaded Race Between Window and Panel CLOSED
Symptom

After NT8 restart, copier is silent. Leaders receive orders. Followers get nothing. Zero [PTT-COPY] dispatch: lines in Output Tab 1. No error. No log line. Occurs on every NT8 restart after the e06bce7b commit (2026-08-24 08:25 AM). Was working on prior daily restarts at a0217a6d / 83dcc6b0.

Commit Timeline
Commit Date Change Status
ee6b1dcf 2026-08-21 13:41 DW-B85 startup warning; no LoadRules in panel OnLoaded Working ✓
a0217a6d 2026-08-23 20:52 DW-B91-A entry dedup; DW-B91-B flat-follower guard; no LoadRules in panel OnLoaded Working ✓ (manual ritual)
83dcc6b0 2026-08-23 23:58 DW-B96 Limit Working dispatch; DW-B95 entryDispatched.Clear() Working ✓ (manual ritual)
e06bce7b 2026-08-24 08:25 DW-B98: _engine.LoadRules() added to panel OnLoaded L704; SaveRules() added to SetEnabled Race introduced ✗
Root Cause — _persistenceLoaded Token Race

There are two callers of LoadRules():

  1. TradeCopierWindow.OnLoaded at TradeCopierWindow.cs:123 — fires when user opens the Trade Copier popup window
  2. TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded at TradeCopierPanel.cs:704 — fires when the chart loads after NT8 restart (added by e06bce7b)

LoadRules() has a one-shot guard:

// CopyEngine.cs:4082
public void LoadRules(string overridePath = null)
{
    if (_persistenceLoaded)      // ← any second caller hits this and returns immediately
        return;
    _persistenceLoaded = true;   // ← first caller claims the token permanently
    ...
}

Race scenario (most common — user opens Trade Copier window before/during chart load):

  1. NT8 restarts. Chart begins loading. TradeCopierAddOn hooks chart.Loaded.
  2. User clicks Trade Copier menu → TradeCopierWindow opens → Window.OnLoaded fires → LoadRules() called → _persistenceLoaded = true → XML read OK (if it exists).
  3. Chart finishes loading → TradeCopierPanel.OnLoaded fires → _engine.LoadRules() called → guard returns immediately (no-op).
  4. HOTFIX-B67-CHECKBOX-RESTORE block calls GetSavedFollowerNames() → iterates _rules → _rules is empty (Window path may have loaded them but panel never received them as IsSelected checkboxes) → returns empty HashSet → saved.Count == 0 → TryAutoApply() never called.
  5. User does not manually check any follower box.
  6. Order arrives → DispatchCopy Gate 1: if (!_isCopyEnabled) return → silent drop.

Even simpler race (window not open — XML does not exist yet):

  1. Panel calls LoadRules() → File.Exists(path) → false (first run after B102 fix, XML never written before B102) → returns immediately.
  2. Same outcome: _rules empty, _isCopyEnabled = false, TryAutoApply() never fires.
Why It Worked Before e06bce7b

At a0217a6d and 83dcc6b0, panel OnLoaded did NOT call _engine.LoadRules(). The HOTFIX-B67-CHECKBOX-RESTORE block was present but only the Window path called LoadRules(), and that path requires the user to explicitly open the popup window. The panel relied entirely on the user's manual morning ritual:

  1. NT8 restart → panel loads → all checkboxes unchecked → _isCopyEnabled = false
  2. User manually checks Sim102/103/104 → chk.Checked lambda → TryAutoApply() → AddRule() wires _rules
  3. User clicks COPY ON → SetEnabled(true) → _isCopyEnabled = true
  4. Dispatch gates open. Copying works.

This worked every day because the ritual was the persistence mechanism. copy_rules.xml was never written (DW-B100 — private DTO classes prevented XmlSerializer from reflecting the types) but the ritual bypassed the need for XML.

The DW-B98 fix (e06bce7b) tried to automate the ritual via XML restore — but introduced the _persistenceLoaded race before B100 was patched and before the user's first successful SaveRules() write.

Why It May Still Be Broken Even After B102

B102 fixed DW-B100 (private → internal on the DTO classes). This means SaveRules() can now successfully write copy_rules.xml. However:

  • B102 only writes XML when SaveRules() is explicitly called. It is called in SetEnabled() and TryAutoApply().
  • If the user has NOT completed the manual ritual since B102 was compiled (no COPY ON press, no checkbox toggle), copy_rules.xml has never been written.
  • Without the XML file, LoadRules() → File.Exists → false → no rules restored → same dead state.
  • The _persistenceLoaded race between Window and Panel remains as a latent bug even after first successful XML write.
Immediate Workaround (No Pipeline Required)

The manual ritual still works today as long as the user does it after panel loads:

  1. Open chart in NT8. Wait for panel to appear.
  2. Check boxes for Sim102, Sim103, Sim104 — this calls chk.Checked → TryAutoApply() → AddRule() → SaveRules() (now works because B102 fixed the private DTO bug).
  3. Click COPY ON → SetEnabled(true) → SaveRules() writes copy_rules.xml with CopyEnabled=true.
  4. Tomorrow: XML exists. LoadRules() reads it. HOTFIX-B67-CHECKBOX-RESTORE restores IsSelected on matching items. TryAutoApply() fires. Copying works without manual ritual — provided the Panel wins the _persistenceLoaded race vs the Window.

⚠️ The race is still present. If the user opens the Trade Copier window before the chart panel fires its Loaded event, the Window steals the _persistenceLoaded token and the Panel's LoadRules() is a no-op — checkbox restore never fires, manual ritual required again.

Fix Required (Pipeline)

Two changes eliminate the race permanently:

  1. Remove the _persistenceLoaded idempotency guard from LoadRules(). Instead, make LoadRules() always read from disk but use a merge strategy: clear _rules and re-populate from XML on each call (or skip if _rules already has entries from a prior successful load). This allows both Panel and Window to call it safely without one blocking the other.
  2. Alternative (simpler): Remove the _persistenceLoaded guard entirely and rely on the File.Exists check as the sole gate. Each caller reads the same XML independently — idempotent because both calls produce the same _rules state from the same file. Only risk: double-population of _rules (ConcurrentBag does not deduplicate). Mitigate by clearing _rules before populating at the top of LoadRules().
File Change Lines
CopyEngine.cs Remove _persistenceLoaded guard from LoadRules(). Add _rules = new ConcurrentBag<CopyRule>() at top of LoadRules so each call is idempotent (clear + repopulate from XML). ~3 lines changed
CopyEngine.cs Remove private volatile bool _persistenceLoaded field (L3870) — no longer needed. 1 line deleted

Important: The ConcurrentBag.Clear()-then-repopulate pattern requires that LoadRules() not be called concurrently with AddRule(). Both are currently UI-thread-only, so this is safe per NT8-003.

Evidence Chain
  • TradeCopierWindow.cs:123 — CopyEngine.Instance.LoadRules() called in Window's OnLoaded. Window is a NTWindow opened only when the user clicks the menu item — NOT automatically on NT8 restart.
  • TradeCopierPanel.cs:704 — _engine.LoadRules() added by e06bce7b (DW-B98). Panel fires Loaded unconditionally on every NT8 restart during chart startup.
  • CopyEngine.cs:4084-4086 — _persistenceLoaded guard: token is claimed at L4086 before File.Exists is evaluated at L4089. Even if XML is missing and the first caller returns early, the token is permanently claimed. No second caller can reach File.Exists.
  • CopyEngine.cs:3870 — private volatile bool _persistenceLoaded = false. No reset path exists. Once set to true it stays for the singleton lifetime.
  • CopyEngine.cs:620-632 — GetSavedFollowerNames() reads in-memory _rules (not disk): iterates foreach (var rule in _rules). If Window won the race and loaded XML into _rules, HOTFIX-B67 sees a non-empty bag even though Panel's own LoadRules() was a no-op — both callers share the same singleton instance.
  • TradeCopierPanel.cs:711-725 — HOTFIX-B67-CHECKBOX-RESTORE: gated on saved.Count > 0. Fails only when _rules is empty, which happens when: (a) Panel wins the race but XML does not exist yet, or (b) Window wins the race and XML does not exist yet.
  • CopyEngine.cs:4089 — File.Exists(path) guard: if XML was never written (first cold start after B100 compiled, before user has pressed COPY ON or toggled any checkbox), LoadRules() returns immediately regardless of who wins the token race.
  • CopyEngine.cs:467-473 — SetEnabled() calls SaveRules() unconditionally. TradeCopierPanel.cs:2219 — TryAutoApply() also calls SaveRules(). XML is written on the first COPY ON press or any checkbox toggle after B100 is compiled. After that one action the XML exists for all future restarts.
  • CopyEngine.cs:1230, 2176 — Gate 1: if (!_isCopyEnabled) return — blocks all dispatch when copy was never enabled
  • TradeCopierPanel.cs:711 — HOTFIX-B67-CHECKBOX-RESTORE has an outer guard: if (_instrument != null && _leaderAccount != null) wraps the entire restore block. If either is null at Panel Loaded time (chart account selector not yet resolved), the checkbox restore is skipped regardless of _rules content. This is an independent guard from the _persistenceLoaded race and applies to all four failure-map scenarios equally. In practice, _leaderAccount and _instrument are resolved from the chart's ChartTrader account selector, which is populated by NT8 before the Panel Loaded event fires — so this guard passes in the normal case. Noted as an additional precondition, not a separate defect.

Primary conclusion: The blocking failure is specifically XML does not exist on disk. Once the user performs the manual ritual one time after B100 is compiled, the normal-restart path (Panel wins token, no Window open) works correctly on all subsequent restarts. The _persistenceLoaded race is a latent bug but its practical impact after one successful ritual write is very low.

DW-B103 Follower Brackets Wiped After T1 Fill — TryCancelFollowerEntries Missing PTT-* Guard CLOSED
Symptom

After QX-ALL (or BE-ALL) places PTT-QX-* (or PTT-BE-*) brackets on all accounts, when the T1 target fills on the leader, followers immediately lose ALL their remaining brackets (Stop-2, Stop-3, Target-2, Target-3). The leader keeps its brackets. Reproduced with both BE-ALL → PTT-BE brackets and QX-ALL → PTT-QX brackets. Confirmed from NT8 Output Tab 1 log and Positions grid: followers go flat at T1, leader does not.

Kill Chain (confirmed via log + code trace)
  1. QX-ALL fires. Leader (Sim101) gets 3 OCO pairs: PTT-QX-Stop / PTT-QX-T1, PTT-QX-Stop2 / PTT-QX-T2, PTT-QX-Stop3 / PTT-QX-T3. Followers (Sim102/103/104) each get the same 3 OCO pairs.
  2. Price hits T1. PTT-QX-T1 fills on ALL accounts. Each account's OCO pair 1 resolves: PTT-QX-Stop is NT8-cancelled via OCO. Remaining brackets on ALL accounts should be pairs 2 and 3.
  3. NT8 fires OnOrderUpdate for the leader's (Sim101's) PTT-QX-Stop with state = Cancelled.
  4. Gate 2 finds a matching rule: MasterAccount = Sim101. ✓
  5. TryCancelFollowerEntries is called at CopyEngine.cs:1250:
    • State = Cancelled ✓ (passes first gate)
    • IsAtmBracketName("PTT-QX-Stop") → checks for StopN/TargetN pattern (e.g. "Stop1") → "PTT-QX-Stop" does NOT match → returns false
    • Falls through to CancelOneAccount for Sim102, Sim103, Sim104
  6. CancelOneAccount(Sim102, MES SEP26) at CopyEngine.cs:2915:
    • Iterates acc.Orders
    • IsBracketLeg("PTT-QX-Stop2") → checks StartsWith("Stop") or StartsWith("Target") → "PTT-QX-Stop2" starts with "PTT-" not "Stop" → returns false
    • Same result for PTT-QX-Stop3, PTT-QX-T2, PTT-QX-T3
    • All 4 remaining follower brackets are cancelled by acc.Cancel()

Identical kill chain applies to PTT-BE brackets: when PTT-BE-Target-1 fills on the leader, its OCO partner PTT-BE-Stop-1 is NT8-cancelled. IsAtmBracketName("PTT-BE-Stop-1") → false (not "Stop1" pattern) → CancelOneAccount wipes follower PTT-BE-Stop-2/3 and PTT-BE-Target-2/3.

Why the Leader is Unaffected

TryCancelFollowerEntries only calls CancelOneAccount on rule.FollowerAccounts — never on the master account itself. The leader's remaining pairs 2 and 3 are NOT touched because the loop only iterates followers.

Root Cause — Missing PTT-* Guard in TryCancelFollowerEntries

TryCancelFollowerEntries was designed to propagate a leader's entry order cancel (e.g. unfilled limit entry cancelled by user) to the followers' corresponding entry orders. It should NOT fire when the cancelled order is one of PTT's own exit brackets (PTT-QX-*, PTT-BE-*).

The existing guard at CopyEngine.cs:1514 is IsAtmBracketName(order.Name) which only covers NT8 native bracket names (Stop1..Stop9, Target1..Target9). It does NOT cover PTT-prefixed bracket names:

Order Name IsAtmBracketName IsNonFlatDispatchName Should Cancel Followers?
Stop1 true ✓ true ✓ NO
PTT-QX-Stop false ✗ true ✓ NO
PTT-QX-Stop2 false ✗ true ✓ NO
PTT-BE-Stop-1 false ✗ true ✓ NO
Entry false ✗ false ✗ YES (entry cancel)
PTT-Copy false ✗ true ✓ YES (entry cancel)

⚠️ Note: PTT-Copy starts with "PTT-" so IsNonFlatDispatchName returns true — but PTT-Copy cancels should NOT propagate to followers. The correct fix is to use a targeted guard: skip only exit orders, not all PTT-* orders. The safest approach is to add a dedicated guard specifically for PTT-QX-* and PTT-BE-* names.

Fix — One Line in TryCancelFollowerEntries

File: CopyEngine.cs:1510-1523

// CURRENT (broken):
private bool TryCancelFollowerEntries(Order order, CopyRule rule)
{
    if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Cancelled)
        return false;
    if (IsAtmBracketName(order.Name))
        return true; // HOTFIX-B63-COPY-CANCEL-01: Stop1..Stop9 / Target1..Target9 skipped
    foreach (var acc in rule.FollowerAccounts)   // ← PTT-QX-Stop / PTT-BE-Stop-1 reach here!
    {
        if (acc == null) continue;
        CancelOneAccount(acc, order.Instrument);
    }
    return true;
}

// FIX (add one guard after IsAtmBracketName):
private bool TryCancelFollowerEntries(Order order, CopyRule rule)
{
    if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Cancelled)
        return false;
    if (IsAtmBracketName(order.Name))
        return true; // HOTFIX-B63-COPY-CANCEL-01
    if (order.Name != null
        && (order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-QX-", StringComparison.Ordinal)
            || order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-BE-", StringComparison.Ordinal)))
        return false; // DW-B103: OCO cancel of PTT exit bracket must not wipe follower brackets
    foreach (var acc in rule.FollowerAccounts)
    {
        if (acc == null) continue;
        CancelOneAccount(acc, order.Instrument);
    }
    return true;
}

Why not use IsNonFlatDispatchName? IsNonFlatDispatchName returns true for all "PTT-*" names, including PTT-Copy. A cancelled PTT-Copy on the leader (drag cancel path) SHOULD propagate to followers — that is the entry drag cancel propagation. Using IsNonFlatDispatchName would break drag cancels. The targeted fix uses StartsWith("PTT-QX-") and StartsWith("PTT-BE-") — only our own exit bracket prefixes.

Alternative — more exhaustive fix: Extract the intent test into a new predicate IsPttExitBracketName(string name) covering all current and future PTT exit bracket prefixes (PTT-QX-, PTT-BE-, PTT-QX-Stop variants, etc.). This is cleaner for future expansions.

Guard Placement Rationale (source-confirmed 2026-08-24)

Two versions of IsBracketLeg exist in CopyEngine.cs:

Version Lines Includes PTT- prefix? Used by
IsBracketLegStatic 3180-3191 Yes — StartsWith("PTT-") NOT called by CancelOneAccount
IsBracketLeg (instance) 3198-3205 No — B29 explicitly removed "PTT-" CancelOneAccount at L2927

The B29 comment at L3193-3197 explains the removal: "PTT- exit orders (PTT-Trim, PTT-Flatten, PTT-BE-Stop, PTT-Tighten-Stop) are NOT brackets — they should be cancelable by the Cancel button. Copy-cascade prevention for PTT- orders is handled separately by Gate 0.5 in DispatchCopy."

B29 was correct for the Cancel-button path. It did not anticipate the TryCancelFollowerEntries path reaching CancelOneAccount via an OCO-cancel trigger. Gate 0.5 in DispatchCopy prevents PTT-* orders being copied to followers (cascade prevention), but Gate 0.5 is in the dispatch path — it has no effect on the cancel-propagation path through TryCancelFollowerEntries.

Correct guard layer: The fix belongs in TryCancelFollowerEntries (before the follower loop), not in IsBracketLeg and not in CancelOneAccount. Source-confirmed via grep — CancelOneAccount has three callers:

Caller Lines Path Should cancel PTT-QX-*/PTT-BE-*?
TryCancelFollowerEntries L1520 OCO-triggered follower cancel propagation NO — this is the broken path
CancelPendingEntries(Account,Instrument) L2665, L2670 User-initiated cancel: leader direct, then all followers YES — user pressing Cancel should cancel PTT exit brackets
CancelPendingEntries(Instrument) L2909 Instrument-scoped user-initiated cancel YES — same intent as above

A guard placed inside CancelOneAccount to skip PTT-QX-*/PTT-BE-* orders would break both CancelPendingEntries paths — the user's manual Cancel button would no longer cancel PTT exit brackets. This is unacceptable. The guard must be at the TryCancelFollowerEntries level where the decision context (OCO-triggered propagation vs. user intent) is known. CancelOneAccount itself is a clean "cancel all working entry orders on this account/instrument" utility; it correctly has no opinion about why the cancellation is being requested.

DW-B104 Unprotected Unit After QX-ALL — Integer Division Remainder in PttQuickExit Fallback Path CLOSED
Symptom

When pos.Quantity is not evenly divisible by targetCount and no ATM targets were snapshotted (fallback path), one unit remains unprotected after QX-ALL. Confirmed live 2026-08-24: Sim102 held 1 unit long with no bracket after QX-ALL on a 7-unit position with 3 OCO pairs. With copier ON, the gap was multiplied across all follower accounts (Sim102/103/104).

Example: 7 units, 3 pairs — floor division gives Math.Max(1, 7/3) = 2 per pair. 3 pairs × 2 units = 6 protected; 1 unit left naked.

Affected Path

PttQuickExit.Execute() fallback branch — fires when no ATM targets were snapshotted (i.e., position entered without an active ATM template). Prior code: Math.Max(1, pos.Quantity / targetCount) applied uniformly across all pairs with no remainder correction.

Root Cause

Integer floor division truncates the remainder. When pos.Quantity % targetCount != 0, the last OCO pair received the same floor qty as all prior pairs, leaving pos.Quantity - (floor * targetCount) units unprotected. No compensation was applied to absorb the remainder into any pair.

Fix Applied

Extracted CalcTNQty(int totalQty, int targetCount, int i) from the inline fallback expression.

  • All pairs except the last: floorQty = Math.Max(1, totalQty / targetCount)
  • Last pair (when i == targetCount - 1 && totalQty > targetCount): absorbs remainder — Math.Max(1, totalQty - floorQty * (targetCount - 1))
  • Guard preserves pre-existing behaviour when qty <= targetCount (each pair = 1 unit)

Verified: CalcTNQty(7,3,0)=2, CalcTNQty(7,3,1)=2, CalcTNQty(7,3,2)=3 — total = 7 ✓.
CalcTNQty(6,3,2)=2 — total = 6 ✓ (divisible case unchanged).
CalcTNQty(1,3,2)=1 — total = 1 ✓ (qty < targetCount guard intact).

Files Affected

src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttQuickExit.cs — Execute() L131, new CalcTNQty method L270–276. CYC of Execute(): unchanged at 8. CYC of CalcTNQty: 3.

Confirmed In

Live test 2026-08-24 — Sim102 held 1 unit long with no bracket after QX-ALL on 7-unit position (copier active; gap multiplied across all follower accounts). Independent source verification 2026-08-24: all six post-fix checks PASS (see post-pipeline validation session).

DW-B105 — CLOSED B107-T1 TryReplacePttBeBrackets Falsely Triggered by QX-ALL BE-Bracket Sweep → Follower Left Unprotected (Combo C: BE-ALL → QX-ALL)

Discovery

Live test session — Combo C (BE-ALL then QX-ALL) with Copier ON, Sim101 (master) + Sim102/Sim103/Sim104 (followers), MES SEP26, Sell x7, 4-target ATM. After the sequence completed, one follower account (Sim104) was left with an open position and zero brackets. The user had to flatten manually.

Observed Symptom

  • BE-ALL fired first → placed PTT-BE-Stop-1..4 + PTT-BE-Target-1..4 on all 4 accounts. ✓
  • QX-ALL fired next → leader Sim101: 8 BE orders found in snapshot, all cancelled cleanly. ✓
  • QX-ALL follower pre-cancel guard ([PTT-QX-GUARD]) swept follower BE brackets via 2-param CancelQxBrackets.
  • Each PTT-BE-Stop-* cancel on a follower triggered TryReplacePttBeBrackets (designed for ATM-sweep recovery, not QX-ALL intentional cancels).
  • With 4 BE stops per follower, the attempt counter hit 3 after Stop-1/Stop-2/Stop-3 cancels arrived in rapid succession, before the DW-B82-01 reset in TryFireFollowerBeRetry could fire.
  • Sim104: 500ms fallback fired ([BE-RETRY] flat=False), called MoveStopToBreakEven(isRetry:true), but QX targets were already in CancelSubmitted state → targets=0 → bare PTT-BE-Stop (no number, no OCO) submitted.
  • That bare stop was also cancelled ([BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop ×2) → Sim104 position open with zero brackets.
  • Sim102 and Sim103: event-driven PTT-QX-T1 Working retry fired in time and placed OCO BE pairs; those accounts stopped out correctly.

Key Log Lines

[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop-1 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim104 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop-1 instr=MES SEP26    <-- NT8 double-callback
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop-2 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim104 -- max 3 attempts, no new slot (TryFireFollowerBeRetry still holds slot 3)
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop-3 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim104 -- max 3 attempts ...
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop-4 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim104 -- max 3 attempts ...
...
[BE-RETRY] Sim104 -- fallback timer fired, flat=False
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim104 buf=0t        <-- retry runs, but targets=0
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop instr=MES SEP26   <-- bare stop placed and immediately cancelled
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Stop instr=MES SEP26   <-- NT8 double-callback

Root Cause

Two compounding defects in the QX-ALL → follower path when BE brackets are active:

  1. DW-B105-RC1 — TryReplacePttBeBrackets has no QX-intent guard.
    It is called from OnOrderUpdate whenever any PTT-BE-Stop-* transitions to Cancelled on a follower with an open position. It cannot distinguish “ATM sweep wiped my BE stops (recovery needed)” from “QX-ALL intentionally cancelled my BE stops (recovery NOT needed)”. The correct action after QX-ALL cancels BE brackets is: do nothing — QX-ALL will immediately submit PTT-QX-* brackets as the replacement.
  2. DW-B105-RC2 — Attempt counter exhausted by 4-stop rapid cancel burst.
    With a 4-target BE bracket, 4 × PTT-BE-Stop-* cancel callbacks arrive within milliseconds. The 3-attempt limit in TryReplacePttBeBrackets (designed for the 1-stop-cancel recovery case) is exhausted after 3 of them. The DW-B82-01 reset in TryFireFollowerBeRetry only fires when the slot is atomically consumed by the event-driven path, which requires a PTT-QX-T* or Target* order going Working — but by the time that happens for Sim104 (via 500ms fallback), the QX targets are already past Working and the MoveStopToBreakEven call sees targets=0.

Affected Code Paths

  • CopyEngine.OnOrderUpdate → TryReplacePttBeBrackets (line ~2277)
  • TryReplacePttBeBrackets → _beReplaceAttempts counter (line ~2288)
  • TryFireFollowerBeRetry → DW-B82-01 reset (line ~1348)
  • QueueBeRetryFallback 500ms path → MoveStopToBreakEven(isRetry:true) (line ~1469)
  • MoveStopToBreakEven Step A: targets=0 when QX orders are in CancelSubmitted (line ~3369)

Proposed Fix Direction (Director Review Required Before Pipeline)

Option A (preferred — intent guard): Add a ConcurrentDictionary<string, bool> _qxCancelInProgress flag that PttGlobalQuickExit.ExecuteOne sets on the follower account name before calling CancelQxBrackets and clears after. TryReplacePttBeBrackets checks this flag and returns early if set — QX-ALL cancel is intentional, no recovery slot needed. Zero impact on the ATM-sweep recovery path (flag is never set during a native ATM entry).

Option B (counter fix only): Raise the attempt limit from 3 to targetCount × 2 + 1, or reset the counter any time a slot is successfully registered (not just when consumed by event-driven path). Does not address RC1 but eliminates the counter-exhaustion race. Simpler but leaves spurious recovery attempts running during QX-ALL.

Option C (cancel-source tagging): Pass a CancelSource enum (QxAll | AtmSweep | Manual) through CancelQxBrackets and stamp each order before cancel. OnOrderUpdate reads the tag and skips TryReplacePttBeBrackets for QxAll-sourced cancels. Most precise but requires Order-level tag storage (NT8 does not support custom order annotations; would need a ConcurrentDictionary<string, CancelSource> keyed on Order.OrderId).

Severity

  • P1 — HIGH: Unprotected open position. User must manually flatten. Reproducible on Combo C (BE-ALL → QX-ALL) with a multi-target ATM whenever the QX-ALL pre-cancel guard reduces visible target count at BE-retry time, leaving one or more high-qty tranches without a bracket.
  • Confirmed affected: Sim102 (4 of 7 contracts unprotected, manually flattened). Sim103 covered by mixed brackets. Sim104 covered by QX brackets. All three root causes (RC1, RC2, RC3) can fire independently or together depending on per-follower timing.

Status

OPEN — Pipeline authorised. Director approved Option A: _qxCancelInProgress ConcurrentDictionary<string,bool> intent-guard. Ships combined with DW-B106 in a single ticket (one pipeline run). No .cs edits made yet. Spec only.

Sim102 PTT-BE-Stop-1(1) Stop-2(1) Stop-3(1). PTT-BE-Stop-4 absent. 3 of 7 ✗ 4 contracts unprotected — manually flattened
Sim103 PTT-BE-Stop-1(1) Stop-2(1) Stop-3(1) + PTT-QX-Stop4(4) 7 ⚠ Covered by mixed brackets (safe but anomalous)
Sim104 PTT-QX-Stop(1) Stop2(1) Stop3(1) Stop4(4) 7 ✓ Fully covered — QX brackets

The execution grid proves Sim104 was fully stopped out by QX brackets — the 500ms-fallback bare PTT-BE-Stop was indeed swept by the QX-ALL pre-cancel, but PttQuickExit.Execute then placed intact PTT-QX-Stop/Stop2/Stop3/Stop4 which fired correctly at 7674.00. Sim102 is the account with the unprotected 4-contract tranche.

At that moment only 3 of the 4 QX target orders were visible as snapshotable (the 4th was already in CancelSubmitted or beyond, consumed by the QX pre-cancel guard that had run immediately before). Indicates the QX and BE layers partially overlapped on Sim103 — the QX-Stop4 was submitted by PttQuickExit.Execute but not swept by any subsequent cancel, while the BE retry placed Stop-1/2/3 on top. DW-B106 — CLOSED B107-T1 QX-ALL Produces 4 Targets When a 4-Target ATM Is Loaded — Should Always Be Capped at 3 (T1=1pt, T2=2pt, T3=3pt)

Discovery

Live test session — QX-ALL with Copier ON, Sim101 (master) + Sim102/103/104 (followers), MES SEP26, Buy x10, 3-target ATM loaded. QX-ALL fired and produced PTT-QX-T1/T2/T3/T4 (4 targets) instead of the intended PTT-QX-T1/T2/T3 (3 targets at 1pt / 2pt / 3pt). A subsequent QX-ALL run with the same 3-target ATM correctly produced 3 targets, confirming this is a session-state issue, not an ATM configuration issue.

Observed Behaviour

[PTT-QX-ALL] leader: Sim101 MES SEP26 qty=10 t1=4 stop=7677.25
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 8 cancellable orders for MES SEP26   <-- 8 = 4 pairs x 2 orders (should be 6)
[PTT-QX-ALL] follower: Sim102 leaderStop=7677.25 leaderTargets=4   <-- should be 3

The immediately following run (same session, same 3-target ATM) produced: 

[PTT-QX] snapshot: 6 cancellable orders for MES SEP26   <-- correct: 3 pairs x 2 orders
[PTT-QX-ALL] follower: ... leaderTargets=3              <-- correct

Root Cause

Corrected diagnosis (confirmed by user): A 3-target ATM was loaded in both runs. The 4-target count was caused by a stale prior-session order still in Working state on Sim101 at the moment QX-ALL fired.

SnapshotTargetOrders in PttGlobalQuickExit.cs collects all Working/Accepted Limit orders on the leader account matching:

  • Target1..Target9 — current ATM targets
  • PTT-QX-T* — prior QX session targets
  • PTT-BE-Target-* — prior BE session targets

The most likely trigger: a PTT-BE-Target-* or PTT-QX-T* order from a prior session had a partial fill — e.g., 8 of 10 contracts filled, leaving a 2-contract remainder still in Working state. On the next entry, before QX-ALL fired, Sim101's acc.Orders contained: Target1, Target2, Target3 (current ATM) + one stale PTT-BE-Target-* or PTT-QX-T* partial remainder (prior session) → snapshot count = 4.

ResolveTargetCount in PttQuickExit.cs returns the snapshot count verbatim — no cap, no staleness check: 

// PttQuickExit.cs line 255
private static int ResolveTargetCount(List<...> own, int leaderCount)
    => own?.Count > 0 ? own.Count : (leaderCount > 0 ? leaderCount : 2);

Target prices are always correct (computed from t1Ticks * (i+1)). Only the count is inflated by the stale order.

Affected Code

  • PttGlobalQuickExit.SnapshotTargetOrders (line 172) — returns the raw ATM target list, count unbounded.
  • PttQuickExit.ResolveTargetCount (line 255) — no max-3 cap applied.
  • PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute (line 81) — leaderTargets = targets.Count forwarded verbatim to followers.

Intended Behaviour (Spec)

  • QX-ALL always places exactly 3 OCO pairs: T1, T2, T3.
  • Target prices: entry ± 1pt (4 ticks), ± 2pt (8 ticks), ± 3pt (12 ticks).
  • Per-tranche quantities: taken from the current ATM snapshot entries [0..2] if available, otherwise CalcTNQty(pos.Quantity, 3, i).
  • Stale prior-session PTT-QX-T* or PTT-BE-Target-* orders (partial fills, cancellation lag) must not contribute to targetCount.

Proposed Fix

Two independent fixes are required. Both should ship in the same ticket.

Fix 1 — Hard cap in ResolveTargetCount (defence-in-depth):
Regardless of how the snapshot is assembled, ResolveTargetCount must never return more than 3. Change the fallback default from 2 to 3 at the same time: 

// PttQuickExit.cs — ResolveTargetCount
private static int ResolveTargetCount(List<...> own, int leaderCount)
{
    int raw = own?.Count > 0 ? own.Count : (leaderCount > 0 ? leaderCount : 3);
    return Math.Min(raw, 3);  // QX-ALL contract: always exactly 3 targets
}

Fix 2 — Exclude PTT-QX-T* and PTT-BE-Target-* from SnapshotTargetOrders target-count logic (root-cause fix):
The snapshot is called at QX-ALL fire time, when the ATM is freshly loaded. Only native ATM targets (Target1..Target9) should drive the count. The PTT-QX-T* and PTT-BE-Target-* branches exist to preserve per-tranche quantities when QX-ALL or BE-ALL replaces a prior QX/BE bracket — but in those cases the ATM targets are gone and only the PTT orders are present. The correct discriminator: if any native Target* orders exist in the snapshot, the count should be taken from those only (they represent the current ATM). If no native Target* orders exist (post-QX or post-BE state), then PTT-QX-T* / PTT-BE-Target-* count is used. This prevents stale partial-fill residue from inflating the count.

Practically: Fix 1 alone is sufficient to prevent the observable symptom (4 targets instead of 3), since the correct ATM always has exactly 3 native targets. Fix 2 is the cleaner architectural guard. Both should be implemented.

Severity

P2 — MEDIUM. Triggered by a partial-fill residue from a prior session leaving a stale Working Limit order on the leader account. Intermittent — only occurs when a prior PTT-QX-T* or PTT-BE-Target-* order has an unfilled remainder at the moment QX-ALL fires. No unprotected position results. However the extra bracket violates the QX-ALL 3-target contract and interacts adversely with DW-B105 (more OCO stops = deeper _beReplaceAttempts counter exhaustion when BE-ALL fires on top).

Status

OPEN — Pipeline authorised. Director approved both Fix 1 (hard cap Math.Min(raw,3) in ResolveTargetCount) and Fix 2 (native-target discriminator in SnapshotTargetOrders). Ships combined with DW-B105 in a single ticket. Verification criterion: code inspection + Combo C live re-test (no separate stale-order re-test required). No .cs edits made yet. Spec only.

DW-B107 — CLOSED B108-T1 MoveStopToBreakEven Step A Snapshots Stale Prior-Session PTT-BE-Target-* Orders → Followers Submit 4 OCO Pairs on a 3-Target ATM (BE-ALL Path)

Closed B108-T1. SnapshotBeTargets extracted, two-pass native-first collect + cap-at-3 applied.

Discovery

Live test session — BE-ALL with Copier ON, Sim101 (master) + Sim102/103/104 (followers), MES SEP26, Buy x7, 3-target ATM. BE-ALL fired, position subsequently stopped out. Output log showed Sim102/103/104 each cancelling PTT-BE-Target-1 through PTT-BE-Target-4 (4 targets each). Sim101 (leader) correctly showed PTT-BE-Target-1 through PTT-BE-Target-3 (3 targets). No unprotected position — all accounts closed cleanly via stop fill.

Relevant log excerpt (Sim102 representative; Sim103/104 identical pattern): 

[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-1 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-1 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-2 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-2 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-3 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-3 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-4 instr=MES SEP26  <-- extra
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-4 instr=MES SEP26

Double-fire per order is expected NT8 sim behaviour: OnOrderUpdate fires twice for the same OrderState.Cancelled transition. It is diagnostic noise, not a second cancellation. Sim101 (leader) showed Target-1..3 only — confirming the leader snapshot is correct and the anomaly is follower-specific.

Root Cause

DW-B107-RC1 — MoveStopToBreakEven Step A has no native-vs-PTT discrimination and no count cap.

MoveStopToBreakEven (CopyEngine.cs ~L3380) collects target orders via its own inline Step A snapshot loop. The isAtmTarget predicate accepts three name families:

  • Target1..Target9 — native ATM targets
  • PTT-QX-T* — QX replacement targets
  • PTT-BE-Target-* — prior BE re-arm targets

If a stale PTT-BE-Target-4 from a prior session is still in Working state in acc.Orders when BE-ALL fires on followers, it is included in the targets list passed to PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute. The swap then submits an extra OCO pair (PTT-BE-Stop-4 + PTT-BE-Target-4) for the stale tranche.

This is the same class of defect as DW-B106, which fixed the QX path (SnapshotTargetOrders in PttGlobalQuickExit.cs and ResolveTargetCount in PttQuickExit.cs) with native-vs-PTT discrimination and a Math.Min(raw, 3) cap. The BE path (MoveStopToBreakEven Step A) was not updated in B107-T1 and retains the unguarded flat list.

Why Sim101 was correct: The leader runs native ATM brackets (Target1/Target2/Target3), not PTT-BE-Target-* names. A stale PTT-BE-Target-4 would not be present on the leader between sessions. Followers use PTT bracket names throughout, so stale names persist in acc.Orders across sessions until the NT8 sim resets.

Severity

P2 — Functionally benign in this test. The extra OCO pair stops out with the others; the position is fully closed; no contracts are left unprotected. However the wrong bracket count is a correctness violation and could cause issues in edge cases (e.g. partial fills on the extra pair, unexpected [BE-DIAG] attempt-counter exhaustion on the next trade).

Reproduction

  1. Run at least one BE-ALL trade on followers in a prior NT8 session (creates PTT-BE-Target-* history in acc.Orders).
  2. Start a new trade without restarting NT8 (stale PTT-BE-Target-4 remains Working in sim).
  3. Enter long on Sim101, copier ON. Press BE-ALL.
  4. Observe: Sim102/103/104 each emit PTT-BE-Target-1..4 cancel at stop-out; Sim101 emits Target-1..3 only.

Proposed Fix

Apply the same two-pass native-vs-PTT discrimination to MoveStopToBreakEven Step A that DW-B106 applied to SnapshotTargetOrders:

  1. Two-pass collect in MoveStopToBreakEven Step A: Collect nativeTargets (name starts with Target + digit) and pttTargets (PTT-QX-T* / PTT-BE-Target-*) separately. Use nativeTargets if any exist, else fall back to pttTargets. Consistent with SnapshotTargetOrders logic.
  2. Cap at 3 after merge: Apply targets = targets.Count > 3 ? targets.GetRange(0, 3) : targets; (or equivalent inline while (targets.Count > 3) targets.RemoveAt(targets.Count - 1); to avoid LINQ per JS rules) after the snapshot loop, before passing to PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute.

No .cs edits made. Director decides pipeline next steps.

DW-B109-01 — P1 — CANNOT REPRODUCE
DW-B109-01 — SuperDOM & Basic Entry orders NOT copied — CANNOT REPRODUCE on re-test

Reported: 2026-08-22  ·  Severity: P1 (functional gap — copier misses leader orders from SuperDOM and Basic Entry)  ·  Status: CANNOT REPRODUCE — Director re-tested, all three UIs now copy correctly  ·  Closed: 2026-08-22

✓ Re-test result (Director, 2026-08-22): Orders placed from ChartTrader, SuperDOM, and Basic Entry all copy correctly to follower accounts. The original single-session failure could not be reproduced on a subsequent live session. No code change was made. Root cause remains unconfirmed (possible NT8 session state issue or connection transient at time of original report).

Original Observed Behaviour (session 2026-08-22, single occurrence)

Orders placed on the leader account from ChartTrader were copied correctly to followers. Orders placed from SuperDOM or Basic Entry on the same leader account were silently not copied. No error. No popup. No [PTT-COPY] dispatch: log line in Output Tab 1. The copier behaved as if the order never happened. On re-test in the same session, copying worked from all three UIs.

Root Cause Analysis

CopyEngine.OnOrderUpdate subscribes to acc.OrderUpdate — this fires for every order on the account regardless of originating UI. The copy does not fail at Gate 1 (copy enabled), Gate 2 (rule match), or Gate 0.5 (exit-signal filter — IsExitSignalName(null) returns false per line 1695). It fails at Gate 3 inside DispatchCopy: IsDispatchTriggerState(order.OrderState, order.OrderType).

IsDispatchTriggerState (CopyEngine.cs line 1674) was written to handle exactly two documented paths: 

internal static bool IsDispatchTriggerState(OrderState state, OrderType type) =>
    (type == OrderType.Market && state == OrderState.Submitted)    // ChartTrader/AddOn Market (GUID-keyed)
    || (type == OrderType.Limit
        && (state == OrderState.Accepted   // AddOn Limit path
            || state == OrderState.Working)); // ChartTrader Limit path (DW-B96)

SuperDOM and Basic Entry were never included in the documented state-sequence knowledge base. Their market orders likely arrive at OnOrderUpdate in a state that is not Submitted — the hypothesis is Accepted (first event for a manually-placed Market order). This causes Gate 3 to return false and the order is silently ignored.

State-Sequence Table — All NT8 UI Sources

UI Source Order type First OnOrderUpdate state (confirmed / hypothesis) Gate 3 result Copied?
ChartTrader Market Submitted (GUID-keyed — B9 confirmed) PASS ✓ Yes
ChartTrader Limit Accepted (2026-08-25 DW-B109-DIAG probe, Combo C session) — dispatch fires between Accepted and Working events. GUID stable throughout (59ff2dca…). Note: prior F-test noted "Working" but probe log shows dispatch fires at Accepted. PASS (Accepted matches IsDispatchTriggerState) ✓ Yes
AddOn CreateOrder + Submit Market Submitted (NT8_API_SURFACE.md confirmed) PASS ✓ Yes
AddOn CreateOrder + Submit Limit Accepted (B56-LaneA confirmed) PASS ✓ Yes
SuperDOM Market UNKNOWN — not captured (probe not run, re-test passed) PASS (re-test) ✓ Yes (re-test 2026-08-22)
SuperDOM Limit UNKNOWN — not tested UNKNOWN ? (not tested)
Basic Entry Market UNKNOWN — not captured (probe not run, re-test passed) PASS (re-test) ✓ Yes (re-test 2026-08-22)
Basic Entry Limit UNKNOWN — not tested UNKNOWN ? (not tested)

What NT8 Docs and Reference Confirm

  • The programmatic (AddOn) submit path: Submit() → PendingSubmit → Submitted → Accepted → Working (NT8_API_SURFACE.md line 169).
  • CreateOrder() parameter orderEntry is OrderEntry.Automated (AddOn) or OrderEntry.Manual (NT8 UI windows). The NT8 reference confirms SuperDOM and ChartTrader use OrderEntry.Manual internally (NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md line 2113).
  • The order.Name assigned to SuperDOM/Basic Entry entry orders is not documented in the NT8 official reference. ChartTrader Buy/Sell assigns "Entry" (when ATM armed) or null/"" (plain market). SuperDOM/Basic Entry names are unknown.
  • DW-B96 established that ChartTrader Limit orders skip Accepted entirely and arrive as Working-first. The analogous question for SuperDOM Market orders is: do they skip Submitted and arrive as Accepted-first? The HOTFIX-MARKET-DEDUP-01 analysis (NO-PIPELINE-REPAIRS.md lines 1419–1437) explains why NT8/Rithmic changes OrderId GUID → numeric at Accepted — if SuperDOM Market orders behave the same way, dispatching on Accepted would double-dispatch unless the dedup guard catches the GUID → numeric key change.
  • NT8 developer forum (community-confirmed): orders placed via SuperDOM appear in acc.OrderUpdate with the same event chain as strategy orders. The first visible state for a market order depends on the broker/connection layer (Rithmic, IQFEED, Sim) and may differ from Submitted.

Order Name Assignment (known and unknown)

UI / Source order.Name Gate 0.5 impact Source
ChartTrader Buy/Sell (ATM armed) "Entry" Passes (not blocked) NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md line 2066; live B9
ChartTrader Close button "Close" Blocked — exit NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md; T_B63_04
SuperDOM Buy/Sell Unknown — probe required Likely passes (null/"" return false from IsExitSignalName) Not documented; not in ADDON_KNOWLEDGE.md
Basic Entry window Unknown — probe required Likely passes Not documented

IsExitSignalName(null) returns false (line 1695–1696). IsExitSignalName("") also returns false (all five StartsWith checks fail on empty string). Gate 0.5 is not the blocking gate. Gate 3 is the only blocker.

Design Requirement (spec-level decision)

The B1 spec scoped the copier to the ChartTrader panel as the primary UI surface. This was an implementation scope decision for early blocks, not a product decision. The intent of a trade copier is unambiguously to copy all leader entry orders, regardless of the NT8 UI window used to place them.

Spec decision: the engine MUST copy leader entry orders originating from any NT8 UI surface (ChartTrader, SuperDOM, Basic Entry, keyboard hotkey, ATM strategy auto-entry).

Open Research Questions (still unknown, for future probing)

The re-test confirms the engine works in practice. The following questions remain unresolved at the architecture level and should be answered before any structural change to IsDispatchTriggerState:

  • What order.OrderState is the first OnOrderUpdate event for a SuperDOM Market order? (Submitted hypothesis vs. Accepted hypothesis)
  • What order.Name does NT8 assign to SuperDOM and Basic Entry entry orders? (affects Gate 0.5)
  • Is order.OrderId a GUID or numeric string at the first event for SuperDOM/Basic Entry? (affects dedup guard safety)
  • Do SuperDOM Limit orders arrive as Working (same as ChartTrader, per DW-B96) or Accepted (AddOn path)?
  • What was the cause of the original single-session failure? (NT8 restart? connection drop? UI not yet subscribed at session start?)

⚠ Recommended: Run the TEMP-DIAG probe (diagnostic log before Gate 3) during a non-live session to answer the state-sequence questions definitively. This is low-cost insurance even though copying currently works. If a second instance of this failure is ever reported, the probe results will short-circuit the investigation.

If the failure recurs, the most likely fix is widening IsDispatchTriggerState to admit Accepted for Market orders. Kept here as a reference:

DW-B110 — P0 — CLOSED B110-T1
✓ DW-B110 — CancelQxBracketsForFollowers Race Bypasses DW-B105 _qxCancelInProgress Guard — CLOSED B110-T1

Discovered: 2026-08-25  ·  Severity: P0 (follower accounts receive conflicting PTT-BE + PTT-QX bracket orders simultaneously; unprotected-position risk)  ·  Status: CLOSED — B110-T1  ·  Test: Combo C (BE-ALL → QX-ALL) with Copier ON, Sim101+Sim102/103/104, MES SEP26, 3-target ATM

✓ Closure note (B110-T1): Fix confirmed by live re-test 2026-08-28. CancelQxBracketsForFollowers removed from PttQuickExit.Execute leader path. Execute CYC reduced 8→7; cancelFollowers guard(3) removed from docstring; branches renumbered. DW-B79-03 follower pre-cancel path (inside ExecuteOne) is sufficient — sets _qxCancelInProgress before cancel, preventing TryReplacePttBeBrackets recovery storm. Combo C code-review PASSED (all 4 file checks clean). Live re-test exposed a new independent defect — see DW-B111 below. Pipeline: B110-T1 — commit 5865dc69.

Observed Symptom

  • BE-ALL fired first → 6 PTT-BE orders per account (Stop-1/2/3 + Target-1/2/3). ✓
  • QX-ALL pressed → leader Sim101: snapshot=6, cancel=6. ✓
  • Followers: [BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim10X — attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued fires for Sim104, Sim102, Sim103 despite DW-B105 guard.
  • [PTT-QX-GUARD] then fires for each follower: snapshot=0, cancel=0 (expected — already cancelled).
  • PTT-QX brackets submitted for all 3 followers. ✓
  • [BE-RETRY] fires: Sim102 and Sim103 via event-driven path (PTT-QX-T1 Working); Sim104 via 500ms fallback timer.
  • MoveStopToBreakEven called on all 3 followers → new PTT-BE orders submitted on top of existing PTT-QX brackets.
  • Final state: PTT-BE-Target-* cancelled on all followers (3 per account). PTT-BE-Stop-* status unknown (likely Working or filled → stopped out). Position outcome unclear.

Key Log Lines (2026-08-25 Combo C)

[PTT-QX] cancel: 6 queued, 0 race-skipped on Sim101          <-- leader cancel done
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE-Target-2                      \
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE-Target-1                       |-- follower BE cancels fire
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Target-1 ... Stop-3/2/1        |   BEFORE follower ExecuteOne
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim104 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim102 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim103 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
[PTT-QX-ALL] follower: Sim102 ... leaderTargets=3             <-- follower ExecuteOne starts HERE
[PTT-QX-GUARD] pre-cancel follower brackets: Sim102           <-- _qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd here
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 ... cancel: 0 queued on Sim102           <-- already cancelled, correct
... (same for Sim103, Sim104)
[BE-RETRY] Sim102 PTT-QX-T1 Working -- event-driven BE retry firing
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 buf=0t                       <-- PTT-BE placed on top of PTT-QX
[BE-RETRY] Sim103 PTT-QX-T1 Working -- event-driven BE retry firing
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim103 buf=0t
[BE-RETRY] Sim104 -- fallback timer fired, flat=False
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim104 buf=0t
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 (3 cancels)
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 (3 cancels)
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim104 PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 (3 cancels)      <-- PTT-BE-Stop-* fate unknown

Root Cause

The DW-B105 guard (_qxCancelInProgress) was designed to protect against cancels that originate from the follower’s own ExecuteOne call. It works correctly in Combo E (QX-ALL direct, no prior BE-ALL) because there are no PTT-BE orders present when ExecuteOne runs and sets the guard.

However, in Combo C (BE-ALL → QX-ALL):

  1. PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute() calls ExecuteOne(Sim101, skipIfFollower=true) for the leader first.
  2. Inside that leader call, PttQuickExit.Execute(Sim101, skipIfFollower=true) runs Step 3: CancelQxBrackets(leader, instr, snapshot) (cancels Sim101’s 6 PTT-BE orders) — then at line 106–107:
    if (skipIfFollower)
        CopyEngine.Instance?.CancelQxBracketsForFollowers(instr);     This iterates all followers (Sim102/103/104) and calls CancelQxBrackets(follower, instr) for each. All 9 follower PTT-BE orders are cancelled here, synchronously, before the follower loop starts.
  3. NT8 fires OnOrderUpdate(Cancelled) for each of the 9 follower PTT-BE-Stop-* cancels. TryReplacePttBeBrackets is called. Guard (3b) checks _qxCancelInProgress.ContainsKey("Sim102") — returns false because TryAdd for followers has not been called yet (follower ExecuteOne has not started).
  4. TryReplacePttBeBrackets passes all guards → registers recovery slot + 500ms fallback for each follower.
  5. Follower loop runs: ExecuteOne(Sim102, skipIfFollower=false) → TryAdd("Sim102") → CancelQxBrackets (no-op) → TryRemove → PTT-QX submitted. ✓
  6. BE-RETRY fires (from step 4) → MoveStopToBreakEven submits PTT-BE orders on top of PTT-QX.

The guard (3b) is structurally sound but set too late. The cancels it was designed to intercept come from CancelQxBracketsForFollowers inside the leader execution path, which runs before any follower ExecuteOne has a chance to set the guard.

Why Combo E (QX-ALL direct) Passes

In Combo E there are no PTT-BE-Stop-* orders on followers before QX-ALL fires. CancelQxBracketsForFollowers at L107 finds nothing to cancel on followers. No OnOrderUpdate(Cancelled) event fires for PTT-BE-Stop-*. TryReplacePttBeBrackets is never called. Guard (3b) is never tested. The guard appears to work because the condition that exposes its race never occurs.

Proposed Fix Direction (spec-level, no code)

The fix must ensure _qxCancelInProgress is set for all follower accounts before CancelQxBracketsForFollowers is called in the leader path. Two candidate approaches:

  1. Pre-arm all followers in PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute() before calling ExecuteOne(leader): iterate rule.FollowerAccounts, call _qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd(follower.Name, true) for each, then run leader ExecuteOne, then clear each follower entry after its own ExecuteOne returns. Pro: minimal change, correct guard order. Con: follower list must be available before the instrument is known (solvable by iterating positions first).
  2. Pre-arm followers inside PttQuickExit.Execute() at the CancelQxBracketsForFollowers call site (L106–107): before calling CancelQxBracketsForFollowers(instr), iterate the rule’s follower accounts and TryAdd each; after the cancel, TryRemove each (or let follower ExecuteOne TryRemove). Pro: guard and cancel are co-located. Con: PttQuickExit already has access to CopyEngine.Instance; no structural obstacle.
  3. Remove CancelQxBracketsForFollowers from the leader path entirely. DW-B79-03 already handles per-follower cancel inside ExecuteOne with the try/finally guard. The L107 call may be fully redundant post-DW-B79-03. If confirmed redundant: delete the call and the guard race disappears. Pre-condition: verify no Combo D (QX-ALL → BE-ALL) regression by confirming follower pre-cancel still works via ExecuteOne alone.

Director to choose approach before ptt-architect Phase 1.

DW-B111 — P0 — CLOSED B112-T1
DW-B111 — _beReplaceAttempts Counter Reset in Timer Callback Causes Infinite BE-Retry Loop on Sim103

Discovered: 2026-08-28  ·  Severity: P0 (unbounded retry storm — PTT-BE orders placed and immediately swept on every 500ms tick; position cycles between unprotected and over-bracketed indefinitely)  ·  Status: OPEN — pipeline not yet started  ·  Test: QX-ALL → BE-ALL with Copier ON, Sim101+Sim102/103/104, MES SEP26, 3-target ATM

Observed Symptom

  • QX-ALL completes cleanly: all 4 accounts receive PTT-QX-Stop + PTT-QX-T1/T2/T3 Working. [PTT-QX-GUARD] fires for Sim102/103/104. ✓
  • BE-ALL fires. Sim103 sees only 2 of 3 PTT-QX targets: [BE-DIAG] Sim103 -- partial targets=2 leader=3, registered BE retry slot + 200ms fallback.
  • PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute submits PTT-BE-Stop-1/2 + PTT-BE-Target-1/2 for Sim103 (2 pairs).
  • 200ms fallback fires → [BE-RETRY] Sim103 -- fallback timer fired, flat=False → [BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim103.
  • PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute calls CancelQxBrackets(Sim103) → sweeps prior PTT-BE orders → submits new PTT-BE-Stop-1/2 + PTT-BE-Target-1/2.
  • Sweep cancel events arrive → [BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim103 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued.
  • Loop locks in: every 500ms: timer fires → counter reset → MoveStopToBreakEven → CancelQxBrackets sweeps prior PTT-BE → TryReplacePttBeBrackets reads counter=0 → “attempt 1/3” → new slot + 500ms timer → repeat.
  • orders-for-instr counter grows by +4 every cycle: 108 → 112 → 116 → 120 … (cancelled orders accumulate in NT8 sim order book).
  • The prevAttempts >= 3 gate in TryReplacePttBeBrackets is never reached. Loop runs indefinitely until NT8 is restarted.
  • Near end of log: Sim101, Sim102, Sim104 BE orders also begin cancelling (cascade). All 4 accounts affected.

Key Log Lines (2026-08-28, repeating cycle)

[BE-RETRY] Sim103 -- fallback timer fired, flat=False
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim103 buf=0t
[BE-DIAG] Sim103 orders-for-instr=108         <-- grows +4 each cycle
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim103 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-2 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-1 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim103 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-2 instr=MES SEP26
[BE-RETRY] Sim103 -- fallback timer fired, flat=False     <-- 500ms later, repeat

Cycle count: approx. 20+ iterations observed before log truncated. orders-for-instr reached 172 at last visible cycle.

Root Cause — Two Interacting Mechanisms

Mechanism 1 (Primary): Counter reset neutralises 3-attempt guard

QueueBeRetryFallback timer callback at CopyEngine.cs L1465 (DW-B82-01): 

// DW-B82-01: reset on slot consumption
_beReplaceAttempts.TryRemove(capturedAcc.Name, out _);   // <-- L1465
// ...
MoveStopToBreakEven(slot.Account, ...);                  // <-- L1475

The reset fires before MoveStopToBreakEven on every timer iteration. MoveStopToBreakEven calls PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute which calls CancelQxBrackets, sweeping previous PTT-BE orders. Those sweep cancels trigger TryReplacePttBeBrackets which reads _beReplaceAttempts["Sim103"] = 0 (just reset) and logs “attempt 1/3”. The guard if (prevAttempts >= 3) return; at L2299 is never reached.

Mechanism 2 (Cycle driver): PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute unconditional cancel sweep

PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute at PttBreakEvenSwap.cs L70 calls CopyEngine.Instance.CancelQxBrackets(acc, instr) unconditionally on every invocation. This sweep cancels the PTT-BE orders placed by the previous retry cycle. Those cancels are what trigger TryReplacePttBeBrackets each iteration. Without Mechanism 1, the 3-attempt guard would halt the loop after 3 cycles. Mechanism 1 is the root cause; Mechanism 2 is the expected behaviour that exposes it.

Why DW-B82-01 was placed at L1465: DW-B82-01 was intended to reset the attempt counter when a slot is consumed by the timer callback, so that on the next trade the follower starts with a fresh counter (rather than inheriting the previous trade’s count). The reset is correct in concept but placed in the wrong location: it resets the counter mid-trade (before MoveStopToBreakEven) instead of post-trade (when the position closes). The correct reset locations already exist: TryFireFollowerBeRetry at L1354 (QX path) and TryEvictFollowerBeSlot at L1409 (position-flat terminal path).

Why the initial trigger was partial targets (targets=2, leader=3): Sim103’s SnapshotBeTargets call returned only 2 PTT-QX-T orders when BE-ALL fired (the 3rd had not yet reached Working state in Sim103’s order book). This is expected NT8 async behaviour. The partial-target retry path at MoveStopToBreakEven L3461 is the correct mechanism for handling it. The bug is that the recovery loop that path spawns has no working rate limit.

Proposed Fix Direction (spec-level, no code)

Primary fix: Remove the _beReplaceAttempts.TryRemove(capturedAcc.Name, out _) call at CopyEngine.cs L1465 from the QueueBeRetryFallback timer callback.

  • The DW-B82-01 reset at L1354 (TryFireFollowerBeRetry) already handles the QX-path reset on slot consumption.
  • The DW-B82-01 reset at L1409 (TryEvictFollowerBeSlot) already handles the terminal reset when the position closes.
  • Removing L1465 leaves the attempt counter intact across timer-driven retry cycles, allowing the prevAttempts >= 3 guard to halt the loop after 3 attempts (3 × 500ms = 1.5s max storm duration).
  • Risk: If the partial-target retry legitimately needs more than 3 attempts (e.g. very slow NT8 sim), the loop would stop too early. Mitigate by increasing the attempt cap from 3 to 5 for the timer path only — or by detecting “targets now complete” and resetting the counter only in that case.

Optional secondary fix: In PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute, skip the CancelQxBrackets sweep when the call is a retry (add an isRetry parameter or check whether the orders being submitted have a name that already exists in Working state). This reduces the number of spurious cancel events that trigger TryReplacePttBeBrackets. Director to decide if primary fix alone is sufficient.

Relationship to DW-B110

DW-B112 — _qxCancelInProgress Guard Cleared Before Async Cancel Events Arrive — Combo C Unprotected Position

Discovered: 2026-08-28  ·  Severity: P0 (follower accounts left with open position and no brackets after QX-ALL; Director manually flattened 2 unprotected contracts)  ·  Status: OPEN — pipeline not yet started  ·  Test: Combo C (BE-ALL → QX-ALL) with Copier ON, Sim101+Sim102/103/104, MES SEP26, 3-target ATM

Observed Symptom

  • For each follower (Sim102/103/104): [PTT-QX-GUARD] fires, _qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd sets guard, CancelQxBrackets sweeps PTT-BE orders, TryRemove clears guard in finally — all synchronous. snapshot=0 confirmed (orders already in CancelSubmitted). ✓
  • THEN — NT8 delivers OnOrderUpdate(Cancelled) for the swept PTT-BE orders AFTER the finally has already cleared the guard: [BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-1 … [BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim102 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
  • [BE-RETRY] Sim102 PTT-QX-T1 Working -- event-driven BE retry firing → MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 → PTT-BE orders placed on top of PTT-QX brackets.
  • Same for Sim103 and Sim104. All three followers receive both PTT-QX and PTT-BE brackets simultaneously.
  • 500ms fallback timers for all three fire: TryRemove=false (slot already consumed) — no infinite loop (unlike DW-B111). ✓
  • As targets fill (OCO partner cancels): PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 cancelled for Sim102; PTT-BE-Target-1/2 cancelled for Sim103 and Sim104 (only 2 pairs placed due to partial-target at retry time).
  • Result: Sim103 and Sim104 left with open short position (1/3 of contracts) and zero brackets. Director manually flattened the unprotected positions.

Key Log Lines (2026-08-28, Combo C)

[PTT-QX-GUARD] pre-cancel follower brackets: Sim102       <-- TryAdd sets guard
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 cancellable orders for MES SEP26    <-- orders now CancelSubmitted
[PTT-QX] cancel: 0 queued, 0 race-skipped on Sim102      <-- no-op (already cancelled)
                                                           <-- TryRemove clears guard here (finally)
                                                           <-- PttQuickExit.Execute runs, PTT-QX submitted
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Target-1  <-- async event arrives AFTER guard cleared
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-1
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim102 -- attempt 1/3, slot registered, 500ms fallback queued
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE order cancelled: PTT-BE-Stop-3
...
[BE-RETRY] Sim102 PTT-QX-T1 Working -- event-driven BE retry firing
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 buf=0t     <-- PTT-BE placed on top of PTT-QX brackets

Root Cause — Guard Closes Before Async Events Arrive

The DW-B79-03 guard pattern in PttGlobalQuickExit.ExecuteOne (PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L145–163) is: 

CopyEngine.Instance?._qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd(acc.Name, true);   // guard SET
try {
    CopyEngine.Instance?.CancelQxBrackets(acc, instr);              // cancel submitted (ASYNC to NT8)
} finally {
    CopyEngine.Instance?._qxCancelInProgress.TryRemove(acc.Name, out _);  // guard CLEARED (synchronous)
}
// PttQuickExit.Execute runs, PTT-QX orders submitted
// ... NT8 delivers OnOrderUpdate(Cancelled) HERE -- guard is already gone

Account.Cancel() in NT8 is asynchronous: it submits the cancel request and returns immediately. NT8 delivers OnOrderUpdate(OrderState.Cancelled) on a background thread at some point after the call returns — typically after several hundred microseconds to a few milliseconds in sim. The finally block executes synchronously and immediately, so _qxCancelInProgress["Sim102"] is removed before the cancel events arrive.

When OnOrderUpdate(Cancelled) fires for PTT-BE-Stop-1 on Sim102, TryReplacePttBeBrackets checks _qxCancelInProgress.ContainsKey("Sim102") — returns false — and proceeds to register a recovery slot. The 500ms fallback or event-driven path then fires MoveStopToBreakEven, placing PTT-BE orders on top of the PTT-QX brackets already submitted.

Relationship to DW-B110 and DW-B111

Defect Cancel source Guard state at event delivery Loop? Status
DW-B110 (original) CancelQxBracketsForFollowers in leader path — fires before any follower TryAdd Guard never set for followers No (single shot, BE-RETRY fires once) CLOSED B110-T1 (call removed)
DW-B111 PttBreakEvenSwap.Execute sweep inside BE-RETRY loop Guard not in play (BE path, not QX path); _beReplaceAttempts reset neutralises limit Yes — infinite OPEN
DW-B112 (this defect) Follower’s own ExecuteOne CancelQxBrackets — guard set and cleared synchronously, async events arrive after Guard cleared before events arrive No (single shot; event-driven path consumes slot, 500ms fallback returns TryRemove=false) OPEN

DW-B112 is the residual Combo C failure after the B110-T1 fix. B110-T1 correctly eliminated the leader-path pre-cancel race. DW-B112 is a separate, deeper race: the guard architecture itself has a fundamental async delivery gap.

Proposed Fix Direction (spec-level, no code)

The guard must remain active until NT8 has delivered all OnOrderUpdate(Cancelled) events for the swept orders. Three candidate approaches:

  1. Extend guard window past PTT-QX submission. Move TryRemove from the finally block in ExecuteOne to the end of PttQuickExit.Execute, after all PTT-QX orders have been submitted. This gives NT8 time to deliver the cancel events while the guard is still set. Risk: if PttQuickExit.Execute throws, the guard is never cleared — mitigate with a try/finally inside Execute.
  2. Structural PTT-QX presence check in TryReplacePttBeBrackets. Before registering a recovery slot, check whether any PTT-QX-* orders are already Working or Submitted for this account and instrument. If so, QX-ALL has already protected the account — skip recovery. This eliminates the timing dependency entirely. Risk: small window where PTT-QX orders are submitted but not yet Working; a 50–100ms NT8 propagation delay means the check might return false even though QX-ALL is in flight.
  3. Defer TryRemove using a short timer (e.g. 100ms). Instead of clearing the guard in the finally, queue a 100ms dispatcher timer. This covers NT8’s async cancel event delivery window (< a few ms in sim) with margin. Risk: artificial delay; must not block the next trade’s TryAdd.

Recommended approach: Option 2 (structural PTT-QX presence check) is the most robust because it is timing-independent. Option 1 is the minimal surgical change.

✓ Director Decision (2026-08-28): Option 2 chosen.
Fix approach: add a structural guard in TryReplacePttBeBrackets that checks whether any PTT-QX-* orders are already Working or Submitted for the account+instrument. If any such orders exist, QX-ALL has already protected the position — skip recovery entirely. This eliminates the timing dependency without relying on the _qxCancelInProgress guard window.

Risk acknowledgement: Small window where PTT-QX orders are submitted but not yet Working. The architect must specify how to handle this window (e.g. Submitted state also counts as protection).

Note: DW-B111 and DW-B112 are to be fixed in the same B111-T1 pipeline ticket. DW-B111’s primary fix (remove L1465 TryRemove) does not conflict with DW-B112 Option 2.

Unprotected Position — Why Two Accounts, Not Three

Sim102 received 3 PTT-BE-Target cancels (Target-1/2/3) — all 3 OCO pairs were placed and the BE stops filled, exiting the position cleanly. Sim103 and Sim104 received only 2 PTT-BE-Target cancels each, meaning MoveStopToBreakEven placed only 2 OCO pairs (partial-target path: SnapshotBeTargets returned 2 of 3 PTT-QX-T orders at retry time). The 3rd contract tranche on Sim103 and Sim104 had no bracket — unprotected.

The partial-target issue on retry is a secondary consequence of DW-B111’s root cause (same SnapshotBeTargets timing gap). Fixing DW-B111 (attempt counter) and DW-B112 (guard window) together should eliminate both the loop and the unprotected-position outcome.

DW-B113 — PTT-BE Brackets Swept Every Cycle — Open Position After Cap (Combo D)
Observed Symptom

After BE-ALL following QX-ALL (Combo D), Sim102 ends with an open position and no bracket after the BE-retry cap (5) is exhausted. Each MoveStopToBreakEven call places PTT-BE-Stop + PTT-BE-Target orders which are immediately swept every cycle. The cap correctly halts the storm but the terminal state is unprotected.

Key Log Signature
[BE-RETRY] Sim102 -- fallback timer fired, flat=False
[BE] MoveStopToBreakEven: Sim102 buf=0t
[BE-DIAG] Sim102 orders-for-instr=175   <-- grows +4 each cycle
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE-Stop-1 cancelled
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE-Target-1 cancelled
[BE-DIAG-CANCEL] Sim102 PTT-BE-Target-2 cancelled
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim102 -- attempt 1/5
... (repeats until attempt 5/5)
[BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim102 -- max 5 attempts, no new slot
Root Cause

Upstream cause is DW-B115: Sim102 ATM copy is incomplete (fewer contracts and fewer targets than leader). When BE-ALL places PTT-BE brackets against a 2-target position structure, the ATM internal OCO sweep cancels the newly placed brackets every time — the bracket count does not match the ATM’s expected structure. The retry loop correctly detects the cancel and re-arms, but the underlying mismatch means every placement is swept immediately. DW-B111’s cap halts the storm; it cannot fix the terminal unprotected state.

Relationship
  • Downstream of DW-B115 (ATM copy fidelity) — fix DW-B115 first
  • Also worsened by DW-B116 (CountLeaderTargets overcounting) triggering unnecessary retries
  • DW-B111 cap is working correctly — it prevents the infinite storm but cannot protect a position whose bracket structure is fundamentally mismatched

DW-B115 — ATM Copy Fidelity Failure — Follower Accounts Get Different Contract Count and/or Fewer Targets Than Leader
Observed Symptom

After entry copy, Sim102 (and sometimes other followers) shows a different contract count and/or fewer working ATM target orders than the leader Sim101. In one instance Sim102 had no T3. In another, all followers had 3 targets while the leader was counted as having 5 by CountLeaderTargets. The snapshot in Account Data shows e.g. Sim101=10 qty with 3 targets, Sim102=7 qty with 2 targets. This persists throughout the trade and causes all downstream BE/QX logic to operate on a mismatched position structure.

Root Cause Hypotheses
  • H1 (most likely): Entry copy dispatch fires before the ATM strategy is fully armed on the follower account. NT8 ATM arming is asynchronous — the OCO target orders may not be submitted yet when the copy dispatch runs, leaving the follower with a partial bracket structure.
  • H2: The ATM strategy name resolution differs per account (e.g. Sim101 uses “MES 200 SL4” but Sim102 resolves a different strategy variant), producing a different target count.
  • H3: A partial fill on T1 before the copy fires causes the follower to enter with a reduced quantity, and the ATM arms with proportionally fewer target tranches.
Impact
  • Drives DW-B113 — unprotected position after BE-retry cap
  • Contaminates all multi-account Combo tests until resolved
  • P0 live-trading risk: follower account has mismatched position size and bracket structure from trade inception
Diagnostic Step Needed

On a fresh NT8 session: enter position with copier ON. Immediately after entry (before any button press), check Account Data for all 4 accounts:

  • Do all accounts show the same quantity?
  • Do all accounts show the same number of Working orders?
  • What ATM strategy name appears on each account?
If Sim102 differs: reproduce 3 times to confirm consistency, then paste the entry dispatch log lines for diagnosis.

All accounts end flat — position protection is maintained. Risk is confined to BE-ALL path (triggers unnecessary partial-target retry slot + DW-B113 sweep loop). Not a live-trading P0. Needs further investigation on a clean NT8 session to determine if reproducible and whether it is a timing artifact or an ATM copy structural defect.

DW-B116 — CountLeaderTargets Returns leader=5 for a 3-Target ATM
Observed Symptom

With a standard 3-target ATM on Sim101, CountLeaderTargets returns 5, causing partial targets=3 leader=5 on all followers even when they have complete coverage. This triggers unnecessary BE-retry slots on every follower for every BE-ALL press.

Key Log Signature
[BE-DIAG] Sim102 -- partial targets=3 leader=5, registered BE retry slot + 200ms fallback
[BE-DIAG] Sim103 -- partial targets=3 leader=5, registered BE retry slot + 200ms fallback
[BE-DIAG] Sim104 -- partial targets=3 leader=5, registered BE retry slot + 200ms fallback
Root Cause

CountLeaderTargets at CopyEngine.cs:3321 iterates leader.Orders (the full historical order list) and counts every Working / Accepted / Submitted Limit order matching Target1..9, PTT-QX-T*, or PTT-BE-Target-*. In a session with accumulated order history, stale PTT-BE-Target-* orders from prior cycles temporarily sit in CancelSubmitted or Accepted state when CountLeaderTargets runs, and are counted alongside the 3 real ATM targets — yielding 4 or 5 instead of 3.

Live-trading risk: This can fire in a live session if a second BE-ALL is pressed shortly after a T1 fill while old PTT-BE-Target-* orders are still transitioning through CancelSubmitted.

Fix Direction

CountLeaderTargets should count only Working state orders, excluding CancelSubmitted and Accepted transitional states, and should exclude PTT-BE-Target-* names entirely (BE targets on the leader are residues, not authoritative ATM structure). Only native Target1..9 in Working state should be counted.

Status: OPEN — P1. Confirmed from log analysis 2026-08-26 (3-target ATM reported as leader=5). Also a live-trading P1 risk (second BE-ALL after T1 fill). Fix is small and targeted: narrow CountLeaderTargets state filter to Working only and exclude PTT-BE-Target-* names. Requires pipeline ticket.
CLOSED — B112-T1 (code-review confirmed) — Live: CONFIRMED Combo D 2026-08-26. Fix: CountLeaderTargets narrowed to Working-state native Target1..9 orders only. PTT-BE-Target-* and PTT-QX-T* patterns removed from isTarget predicate. Accepted and Submitted states removed from stateOk. Return capped at Math.Min(count,3). Stale-order overcounting eliminated. Live-trading second-BE-ALL risk eliminated. Tests T_B112_01..05 pass. CYC=4 (project convention), McCabe=6, unchanged.

[PTT-QX-GUARD] pre-cancel: Sim102
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 cancellable orders  <-- Wave 1 brackets already in CancelSubmitted
[PTT-QX] cancel: 0 queued
<-- PTT-QX-T1/T2/T3 submitted -->
<-- re-armed Wave 2 Target3 arrives Working mid-submit -->
<-- NT8 OCO conflict: PTT-QX-T3 cancelled -->

-- Wave 3: further re-arm during Sim103/Sim104 QX sequence --
[DW-B117-DIAG] Sim103 Target1 Working (third time)
[DW-B117-DIAG] Sim104 Target1 Working (third time)
Root Cause (confirmed)

The pre-cancel in ExecuteOne (PttGlobalQuickExit.cs) calls CancelQxBrackets on the follower. This successfully cancels the follower’s ATM brackets (Target1/2/3 go to CancelSubmitted, hence snapshot=0 in the subsequent BuildQxSnapshot).

Cancelling NT8 ATM bracket orders triggers NT8’s ATM engine to re-arm. NT8 detects that its strategy’s brackets were cancelled and automatically creates a new set of bracket orders. This re-arm produces Target1 and Target2 Working (wave 2) but not Target3 — the ATM engine only partially re-arms, likely because the third tranche is delayed or suppressed by internal ATM state after a forced cancel.

The PTT-QX submit loop then places PTT-QX-T1, PTT-QX-T2, PTT-QX-T3. The re-armed wave-2 Target3 (delayed) arrives Working during the submit loop and conflicts with PTT-QX-T3. NT8’s OCO management cancels PTT-QX-T3.

Additionally, re-armed Target1 and Target2 remain Working alongside PTT-QX-T1 and PTT-QX-T2 (Account Data shows both pairs coexisting — two T1 limit orders and two T2 limit orders per follower).

Critical insight: cancelling ATM brackets to make room for PTT-QX is the cause of the problem, not the solution. Every cancel triggers another re-arm. Post-cancel cleanup (Option A as originally described) would cause another re-arm cycle — identical to the DW-B111 infinite storm pattern.

Why Option A (post-submit cancel) is UNSAFE

Cancelling the re-armed ATM brackets after PTT-QX submission would trigger another NT8 ATM re-arm. That re-arm would produce yet more ATM brackets. Cancelling those would trigger another re-arm. This is a re-arm loop — the same structural failure as DW-B111. Option A as originally written is REJECTED.

Correct Fix Direction — Cancel-After (revised Option A)

Do NOT pre-cancel follower ATM brackets. Submit PTT-QX first. Cancel ATM brackets after PTT-QX settles Working.

Remove the pre-cancel step in ExecuteOne (PttGlobalQuickExit.cs) for the follower path. Allow the follower ATM brackets to remain in place during PTT-QX submission. Then, in OnOrderUpdate, when a PTT-QX-T* order goes Working on a follower account, cancel the corresponding native ATM bracket (IsAtmBracketName) for that account and instrument. By the time PTT-QX-T1/T2/T3 have all settled Working, all three native brackets are cleanly cancelled — one-for-one as each QX order confirms.

Why this avoids re-arm: NT8’s ATM engine does not re-arm when individual brackets are cancelled one at a time in response to a replacement order already being Working. The ATM sees the position as already managed by the new orders. The re-arm only fires when all brackets are batch-cancelled with no replacement in place.

State flag required: _qxPendingFollowerCleanup — a ConcurrentDictionary<string, (Instrument, DateTime)> keyed by account name. Set in ExecuteOne after the submit loop. Cleared in OnOrderUpdate when all 3 native brackets have been cancelled (or after a 2-second TTL). The TTL prevents the flag persisting into future trades.

Files affected: PttGlobalQuickExit.cs (remove pre-cancel, set cleanup flag), CopyEngine.cs (add _qxPendingFollowerCleanup field + cleanup logic in OnOrderUpdate). Pipeline required — 3 changes across 2 files, new state flag, new OnOrderUpdate branch.

Relationship & Severity Escalation
  • Independent of DW-B116 / B112-T1 — occurs on clean sessions
  • Structural sibling of DW-B111: both involve NT8 re-arm triggering a cascade when brackets are cancelled
  • Live-trading risk: P0 BLOCKER — up to T2+T3 tranches on affected followers have no PTT-QX stop and no PTT-BE stop (both swept). Position partially or fully unprotected. Reproduced on BOTH Combo C and Combo D (2026-08-26).
  • Severity escalated P1 → P0 after Combo C confirmed T2+T3 both missing and Director had to manually close 3 contracts.
  • QX-ALL is UNSAFE for live trading until B113 fix is shipped.
