DW-B119 — Original Defect Record (ARCHIVED)
Discovered

2026-08-27  ·  B113 live SIM re-test (Combo D). Reproduced on all 3 consecutive test runs (Test 1 first pass, Test 2 run 1, Test 2 run 2). 100% reproduction rate in NT8 Sim.

Observed Symptom

[PTT-QX-CLEANUP] log lines are completely absent from every test run after QX-ALL. The cancel-after cleanup dispatch (TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket) never fires on any follower account. Native ATM brackets (Target1/2/3) survive alongside PTT-QX-T* orders, creating OCO conflict risk. Position was protected in Test 2 (stop fired, T1/T2 filled, stop-out confirmed by Director) but protection is non-deterministic — the OCO conflict can cancel PTT-QX-T* or PTT-QX-Stop on any run.

Root Cause (confirmed)

_qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryAdd is called at PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L170–173 — after executor.Execute returns at L167.

In NT8 Sim, executor.Execute calls SubmitOrder internally. NT8 dispatches order state callbacks (OnOrderUpdate) synchronously on the same call stack during SubmitOrder in simulation mode. This means OnOrderUpdate fires for each PTT-QX-T* Working event during executor.Execute, before control returns to the TryAdd call. When TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket runs inside OnOrderUpdate, it calls _qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryGetValue — the map is still empty — guard returns false — method returns immediately. No cleanup fires.

Evidence: Sim103 and Sim104 both had snapshot=6, cancel=6 (all six native brackets correctly cancelled) yet still produced zero [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines. The absence is not related to cancel count — the cleanup map was simply never armed before the Working events fired.

Fix — Move TryAdd Before executor.Execute

File: src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttGlobalQuickExit.cs

Move _qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryAdd from inside the try{} block (after Execute) to before the try{} block (before Execute), immediately after _qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd. 

BEFORE (B113-T1 — broken):
  CopyEngine.Instance?._qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd(acc.Name, true);
  try
  {
      executor.Execute(...);
      CopyEngine.Instance?._qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryAdd(   // <-- TOO LATE
          acc.Name, (instr, DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(2)));
  }
  finally { ... TryRemove ... }

AFTER (B114-T1 — fix):
  CopyEngine.Instance?._qxCancelInProgress.TryAdd(acc.Name, true);
  CopyEngine.Instance?._qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryAdd(       // <-- BEFORE Execute
      acc.Name, (instr, DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(2)));
  try
  {
      executor.Execute(...);
      // TryAdd removed from here
  }
  finally { ... TryRemove ... }

CYC impact: None — ExecuteOne CYC stays at 2. Files touched: PttGlobalQuickExit.cs only (3-line move). Test update required: B113Tests.cs T_B113_01 currently asserts TryAdd fires after Execute (wrong ordering) — must be updated to assert TryAdd fires before Execute. Method rename: QxPendingFollowerCleanup_SetAfterExecuteOne_ForFollower → QxPendingFollowerCleanup_SetBeforeExecuteOne_ForFollower.

Pass Criterion After Fix

After B114-T1 sync and F5: run QX-ALL on 3-follower setup. Expected: [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] Sim102/103/104 cancelled Target1/2/3 — 9 lines total (3 followers × 3 targets) in Output Tab 1. Zero [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines = fix did not work (DW-B122 regression).

Relationship
  • Root defect in B113-T1 implementation: TryAdd placement was specified after Execute in the architecture plan — the NT8 synchronous sim dispatch behaviour was not anticipated.
  • DW-B120 (partial ATM arm) is partially mitigated by this fix: once cleanup map is armed before Execute, surviving native brackets that transition to Working after Execute will be cancelled one-for-one as PTT-QX-T* go Working.
  • Live-trading risk: P0 BLOCKER — QX-ALL is not safe for live trading until this fix is deployed and live-confirmed.
Original status (archived): OPEN — P0. Fixed in B114-T1. See closure card above.

DW-B120 — P1 — OPEN — Follower ATM Only Partially Armed When QX-ALL Fires
Discovered

2026-08-27  ·  B113 live SIM re-tests. Reproduced on all 3 consecutive runs. Sim102 affected every run. Sim103 affected on 2 of 3 runs. Sim104 and Sim101 not affected.

Observed Symptom

[PTT-QX] snapshot: 3 cancellable orders on affected followers (expected 6 for a 3-target ATM: 3 targets + 3 stops). Only 3 of the 6 ATM brackets are in a cancellable state (Working/Accepted) when BuildQxSnapshot runs. The other 3 are still in Initialized/Submitted and are excluded from the snapshot. Those 3 brackets later transition to Working and can OCO-conflict with PTT-QX orders.

Root Cause

Followers that fill later than others have ATM brackets that are still initializing when QX-ALL fires. NT8 ATM bracket creation is asynchronous relative to the entry fill. When the leader fires QX-ALL immediately after confirming its own position, some followers may have received their fill confirmation but NT8 has not yet promoted all bracket orders to Working/Accepted.

Mitigation After DW-B119 Fix

Once DW-B119 is fixed (cleanup map armed before Execute), the 3 surviving native brackets that transition to Working after Execute will be cancelled one-for-one as each corresponding PTT-QX-T* confirms Working. This handles the majority of the OCO conflict risk.

Residual risk: If a surviving native bracket goes Working before its corresponding PTT-QX-T* (i.e. native T2 is Working before PTT-QX-T2 is submitted), NT8 OCO may cancel PTT-QX-T2 before it ever reaches Working. The cleanup map is only triggered by PTT-QX-T* Working events — if PTT-QX-T2 is cancelled before Working, no cleanup fires for that tranche.

Status after DW-B119 fix: Monitor in next SIM gate. If snapshot=3 still causes unprotected tranches after DW-B119 fix, escalate to P0 and address in B115.

DW-B121 — P0 — _qxPendingFollowerCleanup TTL Too Short — Native ATM Brackets Survive
Discovered

2026-08-27  ·  Combo D live gate (enter → QX-ALL immediately, no prior BE-ALL). Confirmed across all 3 consecutive Combo D runs. 100% reproduction rate.

Observed Symptom

[PTT-QX-CLEANUP] log lines are completely absent from every Combo D test run after QX-ALL, even after the DW-B119 fix (B114-T1) moved TryAdd before executor.Execute. PTT-QX-T* orders are Working (confirmed in Account Data screenshot — 14 Working Sells on Sim102). Native ATM Target1/2/3 brackets survive alongside PTT-QX targets, creating OCO conflict risk. Position remains open with mixed native + PTT-QX bracket structure.

Root Cause (confirmed)

The cleanup map TTL is set at PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L162: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(2). PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute() processes 4 accounts sequentially: Sim101 (leader), then Sim102, Sim103, Sim104 in order. Each account does: cancel N orders + submit 3 PTT-QX orders = several round-trips to NT8 SIM. Total elapsed time for the full loop is 200–500ms in a clean session, but can exceed 1–2s in a loaded SIM session (orders-for-instr=96–106 at test time).

For Sim102 (which always has DW-B120 snapshot=3), the cleanup map entry is TryAdd’d during Sim102’s turn. After that, Sim103 and Sim104 still need to execute. By the time NT8 asynchronously fires OnOrderUpdate(Working) for Sim102’s 3 residual native brackets, the 2s TTL has already elapsed. TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket checks entry.Expiry <= DateTime.UtcNow at CopyEngine.cs L2400 and returns early without cancelling.

Distinct from DW-B119: DW-B119 = map empty when Working fires (TryAdd was after Execute — fixed B114). DW-B121 = map has the entry but TTL expired before Working fires.

Evidence
  • Log ends at [PTT-QX] cancel: 6 queued, 0 race-skipped on Sim104 — no further events logged (complete log confirmed by Director).
  • Account Data screenshot: PTT-QX Limit orders at 7742.50/7741.50/7740.50 are Working (confirmed). 14 Working Sells on Sim102 — more than the 3 PTT-QX target orders alone, confirming native brackets also Working.
  • No [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines despite PTT-QX-T* confirmed Working.
  • TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket is called on every OnOrderUpdate (L1246) — guard at L2400 entry.Expiry <= DateTime.UtcNow is the only path to silent return without logging.
Fix

File: src/PropTraderTools/Features/PttGlobalQuickExit.cs
Location: L162 (ExecuteOne follower path, inside TryAdd call)
Change: Increase TTL from 2 seconds to 10 seconds. 

BEFORE (B114 — TTL too short):
  CopyEngine.Instance?._qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryAdd(
      acc.Name,
      (instr, DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(2))   // <-- expires before Working fires
  );

AFTER (B115 fix):
  CopyEngine.Instance?._qxPendingFollowerCleanup.TryAdd(
      acc.Name,
      (instr, DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(10))  // <-- covers full 4-account sequential loop
  );

Risk: Near-zero. The TTL is a safety expiry for orphaned map entries on exception paths only. A longer TTL means an orphaned entry stays in the map longer before expiring harmlessly — no functional difference on the normal path. The normal path removes the entry explicitly at T3 (CopyEngine.cs L2442).

CYC impact: None. ExecuteOne CYC stays at 2. Files touched: PttGlobalQuickExit.cs only (1-character change: 2 → 10).

Pass Criterion After Fix

After B115 sync and F5: enter position → QX-ALL immediately → wait 5 seconds. Expected: 9 [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines in Output Tab 1 (Sim102/103/104 × Target1/2/3). Zero native Target1/2/3 remaining Working after cleanup fires.

Relationship
  • Downstream of DW-B120 (snapshot=3) — only accounts with late-arming ATM brackets trigger this path.
  • DW-B119 (B114) fixed the map-empty race. DW-B121 fixes the TTL-expiry race. Both are required for cleanup to fire.
  • DW-B120 root cause (asynchronous ATM arming on followers) is a separate structural issue requiring further investigation.

DW-B122 — P0 — CLOSED — LIVE CONFIRMED — Guard Missing Accepted State
Discovered

2026-08-27  ·  Combo D live gate. Persisted across ALL test runs even after DW-B119 (map-empty fix, B114) and DW-B121 (TTL 2s→10s). Root cause isolated by code trace: guard at CopyEngine.cs TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket L2392 checked OrderState.Working only.

Root Cause

PTT-QX-T* orders are submitted via the NT8 AddOn path (account.CreateOrder() + Submit(), OrderEntry.Manual). In NT8 SIM, AddOn-submitted Limit orders arrive in OnOrderUpdate as Accepted first, before transitioning to Working. The cleanup guard: 

// BEFORE (bug):
if (
    e.Order.OrderState != OrderState.Working   // fires on Accepted but immediately returns
    || ...

The method was called on every OnOrderUpdate event (confirmed at CopyEngine.cs L1246), but returned immediately on the Accepted event because condition (a) was not satisfied. By the time Working arrived (if it arrived before OCO resolved), the native ATM brackets were already in an OCO conflict state. Net result: [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] never logged, native Target1/2/3 brackets survived alongside PTT-QX-T* orders on all follower accounts.

Distinct from DW-B119: map-empty race (TryAdd ordering) — fixed B114.
Distinct from DW-B121: TTL expiry race — fixed same session.
DW-B122: map has entry, TTL valid, but guard rejects Accepted state. All three were required for cleanup to fire.

Evidence
  • Zero [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines in Output Tab 1 across ALL Combo D runs.
  • PTT-QX-T* orders confirmed Working in Account Data (14 Working Buys on Sim102 short test).
  • TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket called on every OnOrderUpdate (L1246) — but condition (a) returned early on Accepted.
  • Parallel confirmation: TryFireFollowerBeRetry (L1365-1368) already checks != Working && != Accepted for same PTT-QX-T* order type — proving the NT8 AddOn Accepted-first lifecycle is known and handled elsewhere.
Fix (Director-approved direct edit)

File: src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs
Method: TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket, guard condition (a)
Change: One condition added. No logic change — pure state acceptance expansion. 

BEFORE (bug -- Working only):
    e.Order.OrderState != OrderState.Working
    || e.Order.Name == null ...

AFTER (fix -- Working OR Accepted):
    e.Order.OrderState != OrderState.Working
    && e.Order.OrderState != OrderState.Accepted
    || e.Order.Name == null ...

Cleanup now fires on whichever arrives first: Accepted or Working. Consistent with TryFireFollowerBeRetry (L1365-1368).

CYC impact: None. TryCleanupReArmedAtmBracket CYC stays at 5.
Files touched: CopyEngine.cs only (1 condition added to compound guard).

Pass Criterion

After F5 in NT8: enter position → QX-ALL immediately → wait 5 seconds.
Expected: 9 [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines in Output Tab 1 (Sim102/103/104 × Target1/2/3). Zero native Target1/2/3 remaining Working. All 3 followers: PTT-QX-T1/T2/T3 Working only.

DW-B123 — P0 — Multi-Generation ATM Bracket Dedup Missing — Garbage Qty Split
Discovered

2026-08-28  ·  Post-DW-B122 analysis / Combo D gate preparation. Identified via DIAG-DW-B115-01 log inspection: [DW-B115-DIAG] leader targets: Sim101 count=4 when expected count=3 for a 3-target ATM position.

Root Cause

NT8 native chart ATM strategy with TimeInForce=DAY (market order entry) creates a new bracket object per partial fill instead of modifying the existing bracket in-place. GTC follower accounts update bracket quantities in-place, so this only affects the leader (Sim101) on partial fills.

Result: acc.Orders contains both the stale generation (gen-1, Target1 qty=1) and the current generation (gen-3, Target1 qty=3) simultaneously. SnapshotTargetOrders collected all Working/Accepted Target[N] Limit orders without dedup, yielding count=4 instead of count=3.

The inflated count then fed CalcTNQty, producing a garbage qty split: 1/3/2/1 instead of the correct 1/1/1 per target tranche.

Evidence
  • [DW-B115-DIAG] leader targets: Sim101 count=4 posQty=3 T1=? T2=? T3=? — count exceeds target count.
  • gen-1 Target1(qty=1) and gen-3 Target1(qty=3) both present in acc.Orders simultaneously.
  • Only occurs on DAY-order entries with partial fills. GTC followers are not affected (in-place update).
Fix (Director-approved hotfix — HOTFIX-APPLIED 2026-08-28)

File: src/PropTraderTools/PttGlobalQuickExit.cs
Location: SnapshotTargetOrders method, L306–319
Approach: Option B — dedup nativeTargets by LimitPrice, keeping highest Qty per price level. 

// BEFORE (bug): collect all Working/Accepted Target[N] Limit orders
// -- stale gen-1 + current gen-3 both collected, count=4

// AFTER (fix): dedup by LimitPrice, keep highest Qty per price (Option B)
// O(N) Dictionary<double,int> pass:
var deduped = new Dictionary<double, int>();
foreach (var t in nativeTargets)
{
    if (!deduped.TryGetValue(t.LimitPrice, out int existing)
        || t.Quantity > existing)
        deduped[t.LimitPrice] = t.Quantity;
}
// count = deduped.Count = 3 (correct)

CYC impact: SnapshotTargetOrders CYC 4 → 5 (one extra foreach + conditional). Within Jane Street CYC ≤8 limit.
Files touched: PttGlobalQuickExit.cs only.

DW-B120 Interaction (important)

With DW-B123 fix active, CalcTNQty fallback (used when Sim103 count=0 due to DW-B120 async lag) now receives leaderTargetCount=3 (correct) instead of 4. This does not fix DW-B120 (count=0 is still expected on Sim103); it removes the secondary garbage-qty error that would have occurred on Sim103’s fallback calculation.

• Sim104 count=3 — followers clean.
T1 qty matches across Sim101 == Sim102 == Sim104. 9 [PTT-QX-CLEANUP] lines present.

DW-B124 — P0 — FIXED (B116 Ph4a) — Pending Combo C Live Gate — CalcTNQty Fallback Produces Wrong Split When BE-ALL Consumes Native ATM Brackets Before QX-ALL (Combo C)
DW-B124 — P0 — FIXED — B116 Ph4a. Pending Combo C live gate.
Discovered

2026-08-28  ·  Combo C live gate (BE-ALL → QX-ALL). Observed: Sim102 and Sim103 received PTT-QX-T1=2, T2=2, T3=3 instead of the correct leader split T1=4, T2=2, T3=1. Sim104 received only PTT-QX-T1(qty=4) with T2 and T3 never submitted. Director had to manually flatten Sim102/Sim103 residual (5 contracts each).

Root Cause

BE-ALL moves/cancels all native ATM bracket orders on followers (Target1/2/3 + Stop1/2/3) and replaces them with PTT-BE brackets at break-even price. When QX-ALL fires immediately after, SnapshotTargetOrders scans acc.Orders for Working/Accepted Target[N] Limit orders. The native ATM brackets are already gone (cancelled by BE-ALL); only the PTT-BE brackets remain — but PTT-BE orders have names like PTT-BE-Target-1, not Target1, so they are not matched by the target snapshot filter.

Result: count=0 (Sim102/103) or count=1 (Sim104, partial) on all followers. CalcTNQty falls back to proportional arithmetic based on posQty alone, producing: 

posQty=7, leaderTargetCount=3:
  CalcTNQty fallback: T1=round(7*4/7)=4? NO -- actual: T1=2, T2=2, T3=3
  (arithmetic split of remainder: 7 / 3 = 2 rem 1, last tranche gets +2)

Sim104 count=1 (only T1 native visible): snapshot had 4 orders,
  cancel queued 4 orders, PTT-QX submitted T1(qty=4)+Stop(qty=4) only.
  T2 and T3 native orders not yet in Working state at snapshot time.
  PTT-QX-T2 and PTT-QX-T3 never submitted for Sim104.

This is distinct from DW-B120 (async ATM arm lag at QX time with no prior BE-ALL). DW-B124 is specifically triggered by BE-ALL preceding QX-ALL: BE-ALL actively removes the native target orders that SnapshotTargetOrders relies on.

DW-B112 Guard (confirmed working)

The DW-B112 guard ([PTT-QX-GUARD]) fired correctly on all 3 followers. Zero [BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets attempt X/5 lines. Zero [BE-RETRY] lines. The infinite loop is not present. DW-B124 is a separate defect in the qty calculation path, not in the guard path.

Key Distinction vs DW-B120

DW-B120: count=0 due to async ATM arm lag (no prior BE-ALL). Mitigation: DW-B119+DW-B121+DW-B122 fix chain handles the cases where natives arrive late. CalcTNQty fallback uses leaderTargetCount=3 (correct after DW-B123).

DW-B124: count=0 because BE-ALL actively cancelled the native targets and replaced them with PTT-BE orders (different Name prefix). No amount of TTL extension or map-arm ordering fixes this — the natives are genuinely gone. The correct fix is: when BE-ALL has fired, QX-ALL should read the leader’s per-target qty directly from the leader DIAG data rather than attempting a per-follower snapshot.

Fix Direction (to be planned in B116 pipeline)

When SnapshotTargetOrders returns count=0 on a follower in the Combo C path, CalcTNQty must use the leader’s per-target qty array directly (T1=leaderT1, T2=leaderT2, T3=leaderT3 scaled by followerPosQty / leaderPosQty) rather than an arithmetic remainder split. The arithmetic split (7 ÷ 3 = 2 rem 1) distributes the remainder to the last tranche, producing T3=3 instead of T3=1.

Alternative fix: include PTT-BE-Target-* orders in the snapshot filter (so followers with active PTT-BE brackets get count=3 from PTT-BE orders). This is simpler but requires verifying the PTT-BE order name pattern matches the Target[N] indexing used by CalcTNQty.

Both options require full pipeline (B116 Ph1–Ph5). Director approval required before any .cs edit.

Ph1 — Architecture Plan — Option B: Leader Qty Array Passthrough
Problem (DW-B124 root cause, code-confirmed 2026-08-28)

In PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute (L89), SnapshotTargetOrders returns an empty list for followers after BE-ALL because PTT-BE-Target-* orders are in-flight (not yet Working/Accepted) at QX-ALL fire time. This empty list flows into PttQuickExit.Execute, which falls back to CalcTNQty(7,3,i) → T1=2, T2=2, T3=3 (wrong). Leader correct split is T1=4, T2=2, T3=1.

Fix: Option B — Two New Private Static Helpers
Helper Signature CYC Purpose
ScaleLeaderTargets (leaderTargets, followerPosQty, leaderPosQty) → List 3 Proportionally scale leader qty array to follower pos qty. Last target absorbs rounding.
ResolveFollowerTargets (followerSnapshot, leaderTargets, followerPosQty, leaderPosQty) → List 3 Return follower snapshot if non-empty; else call ScaleLeaderTargets; else return empty (DW-B120 path preserved).

Call site in Execute: followerTargets = ResolveFollowerTargets(followerTargets, targets, followerPosQty, pos.Quantity); inserted immediately after the DIAG block. Execute CYC stays at 8 (no inline branch added).

Data Flow (after fix)
PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute
  L47:  leaderTargets = SnapshotTargetOrders(leader)  --> [(price1,4),(price2,2),(price3,1)]
  L89:  followerTargets = SnapshotTargetOrders(follower)  --> []  (BE-ALL consumed brackets)
  NEW:  followerTargets = ResolveFollowerTargets([], leaderTargets, fPosQty=7, lPosQty=7)
        --> ScaleLeaderTargets fires  --> [(price1,4),(price2,2),(price3,1)]  scale=1.0
  L133: ExecuteOne(follower, targets=[(4),(2),(1)], leaderTargetCount=3)
        --> PttQuickExit: targets[i].Qty used directly  --> T1=4 T2=2 T3=1  CORRECT

  • DW-B120 (Sim103 async lag, no BE-ALL) path: empty snapshot + empty leaderTargets → returns empty → CalcTNQty fires as before. Unchanged.

Root Cause

ResolveFollowerTargets branch (1): if (followerSnapshot.Count > 0) return followerSnapshot; Sim102 had count=2 at snapshot time — two PTT-BE-Target-* orders had just reached Working/Accepted state, but the third had not yet. The partial snapshot [(price1,2),(price2,1)] passed branch (1) and was returned unchanged. ScaleLeaderTargets was never called. PttQuickExit.Execute received the partial list: T1=2, T2=1, T3 missing (loop iteration i=2 falls off the list end). Result: T3 order never submitted; 4 contracts left open at T3 level.

This is the DW-B116-K04 deferred item from the B116 final review: "Partial-snapshot variant (count=1, Sim104 sub-case): follower snapshot with 1 PTT-BE-Target-* Working at snapshot time returns that partial snapshot unchanged via ResolveFollowerTargets branch (1)." Live evidence confirms this occurs at count=2 as well as count=1.

DW-B124 Fix Status (Confirmed Partial)
  • DW-B124 fix works for count=0: Sim103 (count=0) correctly received T1=4 T2=2 T3=1 via ScaleLeaderTargets. ✓ CONFIRMED.
  • DW-B124 fix works for count=3: Sim104 (count=3, full snapshot) correctly received T1=4 T2=2 T3=1 direct from snapshot. ✓ CONFIRMED.
  • DW-B124 fix does NOT handle count=1 or count=2 (partial): Sim102 (count=2) returned partial snapshot unchanged. ✗ NEW BLOCKER — DW-B125.
Fix Direction — B117 Pipeline

ResolveFollowerTargets branch (1) must be extended to reject partial snapshots. A snapshot is partial when followerSnapshot.Count > 0 && followerSnapshot.Count < leaderTargets.Count. In this case, ScaleLeaderTargets must still be called (same as count=0). The partial orders are stale/racing; the leader snapshot is the authoritative source.

Proposed fix to ResolveFollowerTargets: 

// BEFORE (B116):
if (followerSnapshot.Count > 0) return followerSnapshot;  // (1)

// AFTER (B117 proposed):
// Only trust follower snapshot if it has the same count as the leader.
// Partial snapshots (count < leaderTargets.Count) are treated as empty.
if (followerSnapshot.Count > 0
    && (leaderTargets.Count == 0 || followerSnapshot.Count == leaderTargets.Count))
    return followerSnapshot;  // (1) full snapshot or no leader to compare against

CYC of ResolveFollowerTargets increases from 3 to 4 (one additional AND condition). Still CYC ≤ 8. ScaleLeaderTargets unchanged. Execute CYC unchanged at 8. Full pipeline B117 required. No .cs edits without Director approval.

DW-B124 Updated Assessment

DW-B124 (count=0 case) is fixed and confirmed by Sim103 behaviour in this run. DW-B125 (count=1 or count=2 partial case) is the new sole P0 blocker for Combo C gate. The two defects share the same logical root (partial/empty snapshot bypasses leader qty), but have different trigger conditions (count=0 vs 0 < count < leaderCount).

Sim103 was left 4 contracts SHORT after QX-ALL completed, requiring manual Close. The position was entered at +7L. By the time PTT-QX stop orders filled, the position was already partially reduced by PTT-BE fills, causing the QX stop orders to oversell.

Timeline of Race (11:31 PM timestamps from CSV)
11:31:03 PM  PTT-BE brackets submitted (Target-1, Stop-1 all accepted/working)
11:31:08 PM  QX-ALL fires
             QX submits PTT-QX-Stop(4), PTT-QX-Stop2(2), PTT-QX-Stop3(1) = 7-lot stop orders
             QX begins cancelling PTT-BE orders (Cancel submitted state)
11:31:08 PM  PTT-BE-Target-1 (Sim103) PARTIALLY FILLS: Sell 1 @ 7735.25
             → position: 7L − 1 = 6L (already reduced before QX stops fire)
11:31:11 PM  PTT-BE-Stop-1 (Sim103) FILLS: Sell 3 @ 7734.75
             → position: 6L − 3 = 3L (reduced further)
11:31:11 PM  PTT-QX-Stop fills: Sell 4 @ 7734.75
             → position: 3L − 4 = -1S (SHORT by 1)
11:31:12 PM  PTT-QX-Stop2 fills: Sell 2 → -3S
11:31:12 PM  PTT-QX-Stop3 fills: Sell 1 → -4S
11:31:23 PM  Director manually closes: Buy 4 @ 7735.00 → Flat

Net: PTT-QX submitted 7 Sell orders based on posQty=7, but PTT-BE had already exited 4 contracts (1 via Target-1 partial + 3 via Stop-1). QX had no visibility into these fills.

Root Cause

PttGlobalQuickExit determines qty to sell using posQty (current position quantity) snapshotted before the PTT-QX bracket orders are submitted. During the ~200ms window between QX order submission and PTT-BE cancel confirmation, PTT-BE orders execute at market. The QX stop orders are already in-flight with the original posQty — they cannot be adjusted retroactively once submitted.

This race exists whenever BE-ALL and QX-ALL are pressed within the BE settlement window (< ~3-5 seconds). If the BE stop price is near the current market, it is likely that one or more PTT-BE stop/target legs fill before the PTT-BE cancel chain completes.

Severity Assessment
  • P1 (not P0): Leaves a residual short position that must be closed manually. Does not cause an un-closeable state or runaway loss.
  • Reproducibility: Depends on market price proximity to PTT-BE stop level at QX-ALL fire time. If stops are far from market (BE-ALL just pressed), race window is narrow. If price has already moved to the stop, race is near-certain.
  • Workaround: Wait >5 seconds after BE-ALL before pressing QX-ALL to allow PTT-BE brackets to settle (target or stop fills complete).
  • DW-B112 guard interaction: DW-B112 correctly suppressed PTT-BE recovery during this race ([BE-DIAG] TryReplacePttBeBrackets: Sim102/103/104 -- PTT-QX orders Working/Submitted, skipping recovery). No double-exit. The only issue is the QX orders were sized for the full position without accounting for BE fills already in progress.
Fix Direction (deferred — requires Director decision)

Two options:

  1. Option A — Re-read position at submit time: In PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute, re-read Position.Quantity immediately before submitting each PTT-QX order bracket (rather than using the snapshot taken at QX-ALL fire time). This narrows the race window but does not eliminate it.
  2. Option B — Cancel PTT-BE first, await confirmation, then submit QX: Add an async cancel-and-wait step before QX bracket submission. Only submit QX orders after all PTT-BE Cancel submitted → Cancelled transitions are confirmed. This eliminates the race but adds latency to the QX path. Requires NT8 order event await pattern.

Recommended: Option B (eliminates race, not just narrows it). Full B118 pipeline required. No .cs edits without Director approval.

DW-B125 Gate Impact

DW-B126 is independent of DW-B125. DW-B125 is about wrong target quantities in the follower QX bracket. DW-B126 is about oversell due to BE fills consuming position before QX can execute. Gate #4 for DW-B125 must use a clean test setup where BE-ALL is not pressed before QX-ALL, or where sufficient time elapses (>5 seconds) for BE brackets to settle before QX fires. Alternatively, use a test where the position is entered without BE-ALL (plain ATM bracket → QX-ALL only).

Status: OPEN — DW-B126. P1. BE/QX race condition.
Director to decide: defer (use workaround) or schedule B118 pipeline (Option B fix). Workaround: wait >5 seconds after BE-ALL before pressing QX-ALL.
Gate #4 prerequisite: DW-B125 test must be run WITHOUT pressing BE-ALL first (or with sufficient settling time) to isolate the DW-B125 scenario cleanly.

DW-B127 — P1 — OPEN — QX Fires on Position Entry Transition (hasPos False→True Race): ATM Brackets Cancelled on Fresh Entry → Unmanaged Position (Combo C Gate #4)
DW-B127 — P1 — OPEN — QX Trigger Fires During PositionStateChanged False→True Transition
Discovery

Discovered during Combo C Gate #4 (2026-08-27, ~11:38 PM). This is a separate defect from DW-B125 and DW-B126. It occurs in a specific timing window during rapid position entry.

Root Cause

The QX-ALL trigger evaluates hasPos using a PositionStateChanged event handler. In Gate #4, the prior exit sequence cleared the old position, firing hasPos=False. At the same tick (or immediately after), a new copy-entry filled and raised hasPos=True. QX-ALL was still pending execution from the original button press; it evaluated the state as “leader has position” (the new position) and fired immediately against the fresh entry’s ATM brackets.

Result: ATM stop-loss and target orders on the new entry were cancelled by QX. PTT-QX limit targets and stop-markets were submitted instead — correct mechanically but unexpected. The position was not exited (PTT-QX submits limit targets, not market exits). Director had to manually manage the resulting 7-lot long position (MES SEP26 @ 7737.25).

Trigger Sequence (reconstructed)
Step Event QX State
1 Director presses QX-ALL on original position QX executing: submit market close + cancel ATM brackets
2 Original position fills/clears; PositionStateChanged hasPos=False QX completion in progress
3 CopyEngine fires new copy-entry; 7-lot long fills at 7737.25; PositionStateChanged hasPos=True QX re-evaluates: sees hasPos=True → fires against new entry
4 QX cancels new entry’s ATM brackets; submits PTT-QX targets/stops QX “complete” — but position is long, not flat
5 Director observes 7-lot long with PTT-QX limits working; manual management required N/A
Why This Is Different From DW-B125 and DW-B126
Defect Root Cause Symptom
DW-B125 Partial PTT-BE snapshot returned directly instead of ScaleLeaderTargets → wrong qty split T1/T2 undersized, T3 missing in QX bracket
DW-B126 PTT-BE fills during QX cancel window reduce position before QX stops land → oversell Residual short position after QX completes
DW-B127 PositionStateChanged False→True transition during QX execution triggers QX re-fire against new entry New entry ATM brackets cancelled; position not exited; manual intervention required
Reproduction Conditions
  • QX-ALL is pressed to exit a position
  • The old position clears quickly (within 1–2 seconds)
  • CopyEngine simultaneously fires a new copy-entry that fills before QX state resets
  • The PositionStateChanged False→True event fires while QX execution context is still active

Likelihood: Low in normal trading (QX is not typically pressed during live market rapid re-entry). Higher in gate testing where entries are placed immediately after the previous exit.

Fix Direction
Option A (Guard): After QX fires, set a _qxJustFired flag (timestamp-based, 5-second window). In PositionStateChanged, if _qxJustFired is set and hasPos transitions False→True, skip QX re-trigger. The flag clears after 5 seconds or after QX explicitly resets.

Option B (State Machine): Add a QxCooldown state to the QX FSM. QX enters QxCooldown after completion; in this state, PositionStateChanged events do not trigger QX. Cooldown exits after N seconds or on explicit Director cancel.

Recommended: Option A (simpler, lower risk, directly addresses the race window). Requires B118 pipeline. CYC impact: +1 to OnPositionUpdate guard branch.
Gate Impact

DW-B127 is independent of DW-B125. DW-B125 is about wrong target quantities; DW-B127 is about QX firing at the wrong time entirely. Gate #5 for DW-B125 must use a test setup where the old position is fully cleared and no new copy-entry can fire before QX state resets. Recommended: use a manual entry (not a copy-engine-triggered entry) for Gate #5 to avoid the False→True transition window.

Workaround

Do not re-enter the market immediately after pressing QX-ALL. Wait at least 5–10 seconds for QX state to fully reset before placing a new entry. Disable CopyEngine auto-copy temporarily if testing gate scenarios back-to-back.

Status: OPEN — DW-B127. P1. QX re-fires on position entry transition during cooldown window.
Severity: P1 (financial risk — new position's protective brackets are cancelled; position becomes unmanaged until manual intervention).
Fix: Option A guard in OnPositionUpdate / PositionStateChanged handler. Requires B118 pipeline.
Workaround: Wait ≥10 seconds after QX-ALL before any new entry. Disable CopyEngine auto-copy during gate tests.
Gate #5 Design — DW-B125 Controlled Partial-Snapshot Trigger
Problem

In Gates #3 and #4, the DW-B125 partial-snapshot scenario (follower count=1 or count=2, where count < leaderCount=3) never occurred spontaneously. All followers consistently showed count=0 (no brackets yet) or count=3 (all brackets settled). The partial-snapshot window is too narrow to hit by chance with a single-fill 7-lot entry.

Root Cause of Non-Trigger

Gate #2 hit count=2 because the entry filled in two separate fills (5+2 lots), causing PTT-BE brackets to settle asynchronously. Gates #3/#4 used entries that filled as a single lot-block, causing all 3 PTT-BE brackets to settle simultaneously — giving count=3 before QX could evaluate. The partial-snapshot window only exists during multi-fill entry or broker-side order splitting.

Gate #5 Approach
  • Option A (preferred — manual entry stagger): Enter the position in two separate market orders (e.g., qty=4 then qty=3) within ~1 second. PTT-BE will begin placing brackets after the first fill. Press QX-ALL immediately after the second fill but before all 3 targets have settled. This creates a count=1 or count=2 window.
  • Option B (instrument change): Switch to a less liquid micro contract or off-hours session where fills are slower. Partial bracket settlement is more likely in low-liquidity environments.
  • Option C (diagnostic shortcut): Temporarily modify [DW-B115-DIAG] log output to also record the timestamp of each bracket settle event. Use this to find the exact window size and time Gate #5 accordingly.

Gate #5 prerequisite: Resolve DW-B126 and DW-B127 first (or explicitly defer them), so the gate result is a clean DW-B125 signal without confounding race conditions. Use a manual entry (not CopyEngine auto-copy) for the new entry to avoid DW-B127.

Gate #5 recommended procedure:
1. Fresh NT8 restart. All 4 accounts flat.
2. Enter via two sequential market orders (4 lots + 3 lots) on leader (Sim101). CopyEngine copies both.
3. Immediately press QX-ALL — within 1–2 seconds of the second fill — before all 3 PTT-BE brackets have settled.
4. Watch for [DW-B115-DIAG] lines showing count=1 or count=2 on any follower.
5. Verify PTT-QX orders show T1=4 T2=2 T3=1 on all followers regardless of count.
6. Wait 10 seconds. Confirm all 4 accounts flat.

DW-B127 — Root Cause Correction (2026-08-28) — Automatic Re-trigger Does NOT Exist in Current Code
DW-B127 — Root Cause Revised — Not an Automatic Re-trigger
Finding (2026-08-28 source read)

Source inspection of TradeCopierPanel.OnPositionStateChanged (L664) and TradeCopierWindow.OnPositionStateChanged (L193) confirms both handlers call only UpdateButtonColors. Neither handler calls PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute() or any QX trigger. QX-ALL is only fired by OnQuickAllClick (Panel L1863) — a direct button press.

Therefore: DW-B127 as originally documented (QX auto-fires on PositionStateChanged hasPos=True) does not exist in the current codebase. The original Gate #4 incident was a Director double-press of QX-ALL on a new position that filled within the prior QX's execution window — a manual sequence, not an automatic re-trigger. The live session (2026-08-28) confirmed this: the Director manually pressed QX-ALL twice on two consecutive positions, and both exits were clean.

Revised Status

The real risk in the Gate #4 scenario is not an automatic re-trigger but a stale QX execution window: if QX-ALL is pressed while the prior QX is still cancelling brackets (the cancel-after cleanup map is still populated), the new QX fires against a position whose brackets are mid-cancel. This overlaps with DW-B126 (race between bracket state and QX execution) and should be addressed by the same B118 fix (sequential cancel-then-submit guard).

DW-B127 status revised: DOWNGRADED to P2.
Automatic re-trigger does not exist. Original diagnosis was incorrect.
The stale-window risk is real but low-severity: it requires pressing QX-ALL twice within ~1 second, which is outside normal trading procedure.
B118 pipeline will address the underlying race via the DW-B126 cancel-first fix, which also covers this scenario.
DW-B128 — P1 — CLOSED (B119 FINAL_PASS) — CopyEngine Reversal Entry Guard Deployed (Root Cause Revised 2026-08-28 — Bracket-Event Storm)
✓ DW-B128 — P1 — CLOSED (B119 FINAL_PASS) — Reversal Entry Guard Deployed to CopyEngine.cs
Discovery

Observed during live session 2026-08-28. A sequence of [PTT-COPY] dispatch lines alternating Sell and Buy at qty=10 appeared in the output log. The concern: followers might receive Buy dispatches when flat, opening an unwanted long position.

The DW-B122 guard (!= Working && != Accepted) and the existing dedup cache prevented fills from landing — actual position fills in the CSV matched expected qty. However the dispatch lines were emitted.

⚠ Root Cause — REVISED (CSV Forensics 2026-08-28)
Original diagnosis was incorrect.

The original spec stated the trigger was: leader manually reverses direction (short → flat → long) while followers are already flat. The CSV files disprove this.

What the CSV actually shows: Only two trades filled during the entire 2026-08-28 session — both Sells. The Director never manually entered a long while short. The alternating Buy/Sell dispatch lines were emitted but never filled — the DW-B122 guard absorbed all of them.

Actual root cause: bracket-event storm. The ATM bracket generated multiple OnOrderUpdate events from a single entry (partial fills, bracket state transitions). Each event triggered a new DispatchCopy call. The dispatch actions appeared to alternate Buy/Sell as bracket legs fired in sequence. These were not genuine leader reversals.

This is a separate unresolved defect: DW-B131 — bracket-event storm causes redundant DispatchCopy calls per fill event. Currently masked by DW-B122 but not structurally fixed. Logged below.
What B119 Actually Guards (and Why It Stays)

The B119 fix guards a different but valid and dangerous scenario: the leader genuinely enters opposite direction while the follower is flat. That can happen (leader shorts, closes via QX, immediately goes long on a new signal) and would open an unwanted position on followers who already exited. B119 code stays deployed. The guard is correct, lock-free (JS-021), CYC=8, and adds real protection. The original motivation in the spec was based on a misdiagnosis; the fix itself is sound.

Trigger Conditions (Revised)
Scenario What Fires Protection
Leader genuinely reverses (short → long), follower already flat DispatchCopy with opposite OrderAction ✓ B119 suppresses: [PTT-COPY-GUARD] skip reversal entry
ATM bracket fires repeated OnOrderUpdate events from partial fills (actual 2026-08-28 event) Multiple DispatchCopy calls per fill event; appeared as alternating directions in log ⚠ DW-B122 blocks while follower has Working orders. DW-B131 is the open defect.
Guard Coverage Summary (Revised)
Guard Coverage Gap

DW-B122 guard (!= Working && != Accepted) Blocks redundant dispatches while follower has Working/Accepted orders; absorbs bracket-event storms in normal conditions Does not block if follower is fully flat with no working orders. DW-B131 covers this gap.
B119 — IsReversalToFlatFollower ✓ Blocks genuine directional-reversal copy to flat followers Only fires on direction change. Same-direction repeated dispatches pass through to DW-B122 as intended.
Status: CLOSED (B119 FINAL_PASS). B119 guard deployed and correct. The original misdiagnosis does not invalidate the fix — it guards a real and dangerous scenario. The actual 2026-08-28 event (bracket-event storm) is tracked as DW-B131.

DW-B129 — P0 — CLOSED — Leader QX Stop Not Submitted When All Orders Cancelled By B118 Guard
Discovery

Observed during B118 Combo D live gate, 2026-08-28. After pressing BE-ALL then QX-ALL within 1–2 seconds: the B118 cancel-first guard correctly cancelled all 6 PTT-BE orders on Sim101 (leader). However, after cancellation, SnapshotTargetOrders found count=0 and stop resolved: 0. PttQuickExit submitted no QX stop order for the leader. Sim101 was left long 7 contracts with no bracket and no stop. Required manual close.

Followers (Sim102/103/104) were unaffected — their PTT-BE-Stop was already gone, CancelPttBeOrders returned 0, and they proceeded to normal QX with stop resolved: 7721. All 3 followers exited correctly.

Root Cause

The B118 fix correctly cancels PTT-BE orders before QX runs. However, when the leader has a full multi-target PTT-BE bracket (PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 + PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3), cancelling those orders leaves the leader order book completely empty — the original ATM bracket was already replaced by BE, and BE is now also cancelled. SnapshotTargetOrders returns count=0. PttQuickExit.ResolveStop() returns 0. The QX guard correctly blocks a stop-at-zero submission, so no order fires. Leader is left open.

Trigger Conditions
  • BE-ALL pressed on leader with 3-target ATM (creates PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 + PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3 = 6 orders)
  • QX-ALL pressed within ~1–2 seconds (before BE stop fills)
  • B118 guard cancels all 6 PTT-BE orders on leader
  • SnapshotTargetOrders returns count=0 → stop=0 → no QX submitted
  • Leader left with open position, no orders, no protection
Log Evidence (2026-08-28)
[PTT-QX-ALL] CancelPttBeOrders: acc=Sim101 count=6
[PTT-QX-ALL] WaitForPttBeCancelled: acc=Sim101 waiting count=6
... (6x [BE-DIAG-CANCEL] PTT-BE-Target-1/2/3 + PTT-BE-Stop-1/2/3) ...
[PTT-QX-ALL] WaitForPttBeCancelled: acc=Sim101 completed
[PTT-QX-ALL] leader: Sim101 MES SEP26 qty=7 t1=4 stop=0
[DW-B115-DIAG] leader targets: Sim101 count=0 posQty=7
[PTT-QX] stop resolved: 0 on Sim101
[PTT-QX] snapshot: 0 cancellable orders for MES SEP26
[PTT-QX] cancel: 0 queued, 0 race-skipped on Sim101
<-- NO QX ORDER SUBMITTED. LEADER LEFT OPEN. -->
Fix Direction — B120 Pipeline

In PttGlobalQuickExit.cs, after WaitForPttBeCancelled on the leader path: if SnapshotTargetOrders returns count=0 AND pos.Quantity > 0, call acc.Flatten(pos.Instrument) directly (NT8 Account.Flatten API) to guarantee exit regardless of order state. Log: [PTT-QX-FLATTEN] leader fallback flatten.

Alternative: if beCancelCount > 0 (B118 guard fired and cancelled at least one order), always route through the flatten fallback instead of SnapshotTargetOrders. This is simpler and avoids any ambiguity about what orders remain.

P0 — Pipeline B120 required. Leader is unprotected with open position after BE-ALL + QX-ALL (rapid sequence). Manual intervention required every time this scenario is triggered.

Root Cause

The ptt-architect and ptt-engineer assumed Account.Flatten(Instrument) exists. It does not. Per NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md §2910 (scraped 2026-08-20), the only overload is: 

Flatten(ICollection<Instrument> instruments)

The NT8 reference example for a single instrument is: 

Account.Flatten(new [] { Instrument.GetInstrument("ES 12-15") });

Note: CopyEngine.FlattenOneAccount() does not call Account.Flatten() at all — it uses CreateOrder + Submit for a named "PTT-Flatten" market order with full guard logic (in-flight dedup, cancel-before-flatten, position re-check after cancel). The B120 architect chose the simpler Account.Flatten API but got the signature wrong.

Fix — One Line
Location Current (wrong) Corrected
PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L103 acc.Flatten(pos.Instrument); acc.Flatten(new[] { pos.Instrument });

Single-element array satisfies ICollection<Instrument>. No other change. CYC unaffected. No new allocations in the hot path (this branch only fires on fallback). NeedsLeaderFallbackFlatten, log, and continue are all unchanged.

B120Tests.cs Impact

The 3 xUnit [Fact] tests in B120Tests.cs test NeedsLeaderFallbackFlatten(int, int, int) — a pure static method with no NT8 API dependency. They are unaffected by this fix.

NT8 Rule Added
NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md confirmed (L2910): Account.Flatten signature is Flatten(ICollection<Instrument>) only. There is no single-instrument overload. Always wrap: new[] { instrument }.

DW-B131 — P2 — OPEN — CopyEngine Bracket-Event Storm: ATM OnOrderUpdate Fires Multiple DispatchCopy Calls Per Fill (Masked by DW-B122)
DW-B131 — P2 — OPEN — Bracket-Event Storm From Partial Fills (Real Root Cause of 2026-08-28 Alternating Dispatches)
Discovery

Identified during CSV forensics on the 2026-08-28 live session log. Originally misdiagnosed as DW-B128 (leader manual reversal). The CSV evidence shows only two actual filled trades (both Sells); the alternating Buy/Sell dispatch lines that appeared in the output log were never filled. This means DispatchCopy was called multiple times per fill event by the ATM bracket's OnOrderUpdate handler, generating a bracket-event storm.

Root Cause

NT8 ATM brackets fire OnOrderUpdate for every state transition on every order in the bracket: Initialized → Accepted → Working → PartialFill → Filled. For a 3-target ATM this can generate 15–30 events from a single entry. CopyEngine.OnOrderUpdate calls DispatchCopy on every event that passes Gate 0 (is an entry-direction order). The result is 15–30 dispatch attempts per leader entry, not 1.

In normal conditions this is absorbed by:

  • DW-B122 guard: once the first dispatch fires and follower has a Working/Accepted order, all subsequent dispatches are blocked.
  • Dedup cache: same orderId events are deduplicated.

The gap: if the follower processes its copy order very quickly (goes from Accepted → Working → Filled before the next dispatch arrives) or if a partial fill leaves the follower momentarily flat before the next dispatch, DW-B122 does not fire and a second copy goes through. This is a latent race condition.

Evidence (2026-08-28 Log)

Multiple [PTT-COPY] dispatch lines for the same instrument, alternating Buy/Sell, all at qty=10, within a 1-second window. CSV shows none of the alternating dispatches resulted in fills. DW-B122 blocked all of them in this session.

Current Mitigation (Incomplete)
Guard Protection Level Residual Risk
DW-B122 (!= Working && != Accepted) ~95% — absorbs storms while follower has active orders Latent: follower momentarily flat between fills could allow second dispatch
Dedup cache (Gate 5) Blocks same orderId; does not block different orderIds from same entry bracket ATM bracket legs have different orderIds
Fix Direction (Future Pipeline)

Structural fix: gate OnOrderUpdate dispatch on order state — only dispatch on the first Filled or PartialFilled transition for each orderId, not on every state change. Use a _dispatchedOrderIds ConcurrentHashSet keyed by orderId. Mark on first dispatch; skip on repeat. CYC impact: +1 to the guard block only; extract to helper to stay at CYC=8.

P2 — OPEN. Not a blocker today (DW-B122 masks it). Assign to a future pipeline (B121+) after B120 (DW-B129) is closed.
Financial risk: low in current conditions. Elevated if DW-B122 is ever removed or bypassed.

Go-to-Market Architecture — v1 Free-First Stack → v2 Paid Upgrades
Director decisions locked in this session (2026-08): Start as free/cheap as possible. Upgrade tools from v1 revenue (~$500 threshold). LemonSqueezy as Merchant of Record (handles all global VAT). ConfuserEx obfuscation for v1 → .NET Reactor for v2. Zip import distribution for v1 → installer for v2. NT Ecosystem listing after GTM-2 (product stable). Version numbering: v1.0 → v1.1 → v1.2 → v2.0 (no "beta" label ever).
Full GTM Stack — v1 (free-first) vs v2 (upgraded)
Layer v1 Launch (free / minimal cost) v2 Upgrade (funded by revenue) Switch difficulty
IP Obfuscation ConfuserEx — free, open-source. Renames internal symbols, encrypts strings, anti-dump. Compatible with NT8 AddOn DLL loading. .NET Reactor (~$200 one-time). Stronger protection + native code conversion + built-in license SDK. 🟢 Trivial — change one post-build step. Re-ship DLL zip. Zero user impact.
License enforcement Cryptolens free tier — up to 50 activations free. Remote dashboard, feature flags per key, 7-day offline grace. Cryptolens paid (~$20/mo at 50+ customers) or switch to .NET Reactor's built-in licensing. 🟢 Trivial — Cryptolens → Cryptolens paid is a billing change only. Cryptolens → Reactor needs one code change in LicenseClient.
Distribution Zip import — native NT8 workflow (Tools → Import NinjaScript). Zero installer build time. What all NT8 ecosystem tools use. Inno Setup installer (free tool) — wizard prompts for license key, copies DLL, registers auto-updater. 🟢 Easy — existing zip customers keep working. Installer is additive only.
Checkout LemonSqueezy — 5% per sale, $0/month. Merchant of Record (handles all global VAT). Webhook fires license key delivery. Stay on LemonSqueezy or move to Stripe once you have an accountant for VAT. 🟡 Low — swap payment links on website. License keys (Cryptolens) are independent of checkout platform.
Website GitHub Pages or Vercel — free. Static HTML + Tailwind. No backend needed. Framer or Webflow for polished marketing site. 🟢 Trivial — domain points to new host. Content migrates.
Legal Sole trader registration (your country, $0–$50). ToS + Refund Policy on website (required by LemonSqueezy). LLC / Ltd company once revenue is meaningful (protects personal assets). 🟢 Easy — form a company when ready. Your product and customers transfer over.

── Build → Obfuscate → Package ──────────────────────────

FeatureFlags — Sealed Record Design (Jane Street JS-003 compliant)
// Illegal states unrepresentable (JS-003)
// Immutable at construction — no mutation after init
internal sealed record FeatureFlags(
    bool MultiRule,      // Pro+
    bool TrimFlatten,    // Pro+
    bool BreakEven,      // Pro+
    bool AtrSizing,      // Elite only
    bool ClickTrader,    // Elite only
    bool MirrorMode,     // Elite only
    bool QxGlobalExit    // Elite only
)
{
    public static FeatureFlags Starter() =>
        new(false,false,false,false,false,false,false);

    public static FeatureFlags Pro() =>
        new(true,true,true,false,false,false,false);

    public static FeatureFlags Elite() =>
        new(true,true,true,true,true,true,true);

    // Called once on LicenseClient.Validate() response
    public static FeatureFlags FromFeatureList(
        IReadOnlyList<string> feats) => new(
        MultiRule:   feats.Contains("multi_rule"),
        TrimFlatten: feats.Contains("trim_flatten"),
        BreakEven:   feats.Contains("break_even"),
        AtrSizing:   feats.Contains("atr_sizing"),
        ClickTrader: feats.Contains("click_trader"),
        MirrorMode:  feats.Contains("mirror_mode"),
        QxGlobalExit:feats.Contains("qx_global_exit"));
}
// CopyEngine holds one immutable flags instance
// Set once in OnInitialize(), never mutated
private FeatureFlags _flags = FeatureFlags.Starter();

// Gate pattern — every feature checks its flag
public void Trim(Instrument instr, ...) {
    if (!_flags.TrimFlatten) {
        StatusUpdate("Trim requires Pro tier");
        return;
    }
    // ... existing Trim logic
}

public void AddRule(CopyRule rule) {
    if (!_flags.MultiRule
        && _rules.Count >= 1) {
        StatusUpdate("Multi-rule requires Pro tier");
        return;
    }
    // ... existing AddRule logic
}

// UI hides locked buttons (grey + tooltip)
// Engine double-gates as safety net

LicenseClient — Full Architecture Spec (ptt-architect input)
Scope boundary: LicenseClient is a new static class in a new file src/PropTraderTools/LicenseClient.cs. It has exactly one public entry point: Validate(key, productId) → FeatureFlags. It never throws (JS-001). It never uses lock() (JS-021). All file I/O uses the NT8 NinjaTrader.Core.Globals.UserDataDir path. The NuGet dependency is SKM.NET.Standard (Cryptolens SDK, .NET Standard 2.0 compatible with net48).
Full class contract
// FILE: src/PropTraderTools/LicenseClient.cs
// Jane Street: JS-001 (no throw), JS-021 (no lock)
// Single-threaded — called once on OnInitialize()
// Never called again during the session

internal static class LicenseClient
{
    // Cryptolens product ID (set per product in dashboard)
    // Embedded as a constant — obfuscated in DLL
    private const string ProductId = "PTT_COPIER_V1";

    // Cache file path inside NT8 user data dir
    private static string CachePath =>
        Path.Combine(
            NinjaTrader.Core.Globals.UserDataDir,
            "PropTraderTools",
            "license_cache.json");

    // Main entry point. Called once in OnInitialize().
    // Returns FeatureFlags — never throws.
    public static FeatureFlags Validate(string licenseKey)
    {
        // Guard 1: empty/null key → Starter, log message
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(licenseKey))
            return FeatureFlags.Starter();

        // Try remote first, fall back to cache
        var remote = TryRemoteValidate(licenseKey);
        if (remote != null) {
            WriteCache(licenseKey, remote);  // refresh cache
            return remote;
        }

        // Remote failed (offline/network error)
        var cached = TryReadCache(licenseKey);
        return cached ?? FeatureFlags.Starter();
    }

    // Returns null on any failure — never throws
    private static FeatureFlags TryRemoteValidate(string key)

    // Returns null if cache missing/expired/wrong key
    private static FeatureFlags TryReadCache(string key)

    // Writes cache; silently swallows IO exceptions
    private static void WriteCache(string key, FeatureFlags flags)
}
Remote validate — Cryptolens SDK call
// NuGet: SKM.NET.Standard
// using SKM.V3; using SKM.V3.Methods; using SKM.V3.Models;

private static FeatureFlags TryRemoteValidate(string key)
{
    try {
        var result = Key.Activate(
            token:     "[CRYPTOLENS_ACCESS_TOKEN]",
            parameters: new ActivateModel {
                Key       = key,
                ProductId = 1234,  // your Cryptolens product ID
                Sign      = true,
                MachineCode = Helpers.GetMachineCode()
            });

        if (result?.Result != ResultType.Success)
            return null;

        // Feature names are set in Cryptolens dashboard
        // per license key, stored as DataObjects
        var feats = result.LicenseKey?.DataObjects?
            .Select(d => d.Name)
            .ToList() ?? new List<string>();

        return FeatureFlags.FromFeatureList(feats);
    }
    catch { return null; }  // JS-001: swallow, return null
}
Cache format (license_cache.json)
// Simple JSON — no NuGet needed (manual serialize)
{
  "key":       "XXXX-YYYY-ZZZZ-WWWW",
  "features": ["multi_rule", "trim_flatten"],
  "cached_utc": "2026-08-15T10:00:00Z",
  "expires_utc": "2026-08-22T10:00:00Z"  // +7 days
}

// TryReadCache:
// 1. File not found → return null
// 2. Key mismatch → return null (different key)
// 3. expires_utc < UtcNow → return null (expired)
// 4. Parse features → return FeatureFlags
// Any exception → return null (JS-001)
All error states — what the user sees in the Add-On status log
ConditionRemote resultCache resultFeatureFlags returnedStatus log message
No license key entered — — Starter() "No license key — Starter tier active"
Valid key, online ✓ Success Cache refreshed From server "License valid — [TierName] tier active"
Valid key, offline, cache fresh null (network error) ✓ Hit, not expired From cache "Offline — license from cache (N days remaining)"
Valid key, offline, cache expired (>7 days) null null (expired) Starter() "License cache expired — connect to internet to reactivate"
Invalid key null (server rejects) null (key mismatch) Starter() "License key invalid — check key and try again"
Revoked key (you revoke in dashboard) null (server rejects) null (key mismatch) Starter() "License inactive — contact support"
Where the user enters their license key: A single TextBox + [Activate] button added to TradeCopierWindow (the Add-On window, not ChartTrader panel — panel has no room). On [Activate] click: key is written to PropTraderTools/license.txt (plain text, one line), LicenseClient.Validate() is called, result applied to CopyEngine._flags. No NT8 restart required — flags update live. On next NT8 start: key read from license.txt, validate called in OnInitialize() automatically.

confuserex.crproj (add to repo root)
<project outputDir="Obfuscated"

NT8 AddOn constraint: TradeCopierAddOn (the AddOnBase subclass) must NOT have its class name renamed — NT8 discovers it by type scanning the DLL. Add an exclusion rule in the .crproj for this type. All internal types (CopyEngine, LicenseClient, FeatureFlags) can be aggressively renamed.
NT8 Encryption Method — Can We Use It? (Research Note)
Director question answered: NinjaTrader itself uses Dotfuscator (by PreEmptive Solutions) to protect its own DLLs. This is a commercial obfuscator licensed to NinjaTrader Inc. We cannot use their license. However, the technique is identical to what we spec above — .NET obfuscation + string encryption + symbol renaming. ConfuserEx (v1) and .NET Reactor (v2) give us the same protection class as Dotfuscator.
Tool Who uses it Cost Can we use it? Protection level
Dotfuscator Professional NinjaTrader Inc (their own DLLs) ~$1,500–$4,000/yr (enterprise license) ✗ Their license, not transferable. We'd need our own license. Rename + string encrypt + control flow + anti-tamper. Excellent.
Dotfuscator Community Bundled free with Visual Studio $0 (included in VS) ⚠ Technically available but basic rename only. No string encryption, no anti-tamper. Not sufficient for IP protection. Symbol rename only. Weak — decompilers can still read logic.
ConfuserEx (our v1 choice) Independent NinjaScript add-on developers, open source community $0 — open source (MIT) ✓ Yes — free, no license restrictions, NT8 AddOn DLL compatible Rename (aggressive) + string encrypt + anti-tamper + anti-dump. Same class as Dotfuscator Pro for .NET binaries.
.NET Reactor (our v2 choice) Commercial software vendors protecting .NET products ~$200 one-time ✓ Yes — commercial license, royalty-free distribution, NT8 compatible Rename + string encrypt + native code conversion (IL → x86/x64 native, defeats decompilers entirely) + built-in licensing SDK. Stronger than Dotfuscator Pro for our use case.
SmartAssembly (RedGate) Enterprise .NET apps ~$500+/yr ⚠ Can use but expensive. No advantage over .NET Reactor for our case. Strong. Overkill for a trading add-on.
Bottom line: We cannot use NinjaTrader's Dotfuscator license — it's theirs. But we don't need to. ConfuserEx gives us the same protection class for $0 in v1. .NET Reactor in v2 actually exceeds Dotfuscator for our case because of native code conversion — once IL is converted to native x86/x64 machine code, there is nothing for a .NET decompiler to recover. The source code is invisible to any tool including ILSpy, dnSpy, and dotPeek. NT8 compatibility note: Both tools preserve the AddOnBase public class name (required for NT8 DLL scanning). All internal classes can be aggressively renamed. This is already handled in the ConfuserEx .crproj exclusion rule above.

— FAQ / OBJECTION HANDLING —
Does it require a chart to be open?
No. It's an NT8 Add-On, not an indicator. It loads when NinjaTrader connects and runs invisibly in the background. No chart, no template, no startup ritual.
Will this get my prop firm account banned?
No. All orders are placed through the standard NinjaTrader order submission path — the same path ChartTrader uses. The prop firm sees normal orders from your account. There is nothing to detect.
Does it copy the exact same quantity, or can I scale?
You can set a per-follower quantity multiplier. If your master trades 2 contracts, a follower with multiplier 0.5× will trade 1. Each follower has its own setting.
What happens if my internet drops mid-trade?
Exactly the same as it would without the copier — NinjaTrader loses connectivity. When you reconnect, existing positions are still open in each account. The copier resumes on the next new order.
Is the source code visible?
No. The DLL is obfuscated — all internal class names, method names, and string literals are encrypted. Opening it in ILSpy or dotPeek shows unreadable symbol names. Your logic is protected.

api/webhook.js — skeleton
// Vercel serverless function
// Environment vars (set in Vercel dashboard):
//   LEMON_WEBHOOK_SECRET  — verify request signature
//   CRYPTOLENS_TOKEN      — your API access token
//   CRYPTOLENS_PRODUCT_ID — numeric product ID
//   RESEND_API_KEY        — email delivery
//   DOWNLOAD_URL          — link to latest zip

export default async function handler(req, res) {
  // 1. Verify LemonSqueezy HMAC signature
  if (!verifySignature(req)) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'invalid signature' });
  }

  const { event, data } = req.body;
  if (event !== 'order_created') {
    return res.status(200).json({ skipped: true });
  }

  // 2. Determine tier from product variant name
  const tier = getTier(data.attributes.variant_name);
  // tier: 'starter' | 'pro' | 'elite'

  // 3. Create key in Cryptolens
  const key = await createCryptolensKey(tier);

  // 4. Send email with key + download link
  await sendEmail({
    to:      data.attributes.user_email,
    name:    data.attributes.user_name,
    key,
    tier,
    downloadUrl: process.env.DOWNLOAD_URL,
  });

  return res.status(200).json({ ok: true });
}
createCryptolensKey — feature flags per tier
// POST https://api.cryptolens.io/api/key/CreateKey
const TIER_FLAGS = {
  starter: [],
  pro:     ['multi_rule', 'trim_flatten', 'break_even'],
  elite:   ['multi_rule', 'trim_flatten', 'break_even',
            'atr_sizing', 'click_trader',
            'mirror_mode', 'qx_global_exit'],
};

async function createCryptolensKey(tier) {
  const features = TIER_FLAGS[tier];
  const resp = await fetch(
    'https://api.cryptolens.io/api/key/CreateKey', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      token:       process.env.CRYPTOLENS_TOKEN,
      ProductId:   process.env.CRYPTOLENS_PRODUCT_ID,
      NewCustomer: true,
      DataObjects: features.map(f => ({ Name: f, StringValue: '1' })),
    })
  });
  const json = await resp.json();
  return json.Key; // e.g. "XXXX-YYYY-ZZZZ-WWWW"
}

Website Design System — NT-Aligned Visual Language
Design Rationale — Why We Mirror NinjaTrader's Aesthetic
Our product lives inside NinjaTrader. Our website should feel like it belongs to the same world — not a generic SaaS landing page. NinjaTrader's own website (ninjatrader.com) uses a strict visual language: pure black backgrounds, white bold headlines, and orange used sparingly as a CTA accent — never as a decorative splash. Matching that language signals to prop traders browsing the NT ecosystem that this is a professional, purpose-built tool — not a side project.
What NT does NOT do
No gradients
No glows or neon effects
No orange backgrounds behind text
No rounded-corner hero blobs
No emoji or decorative icons
No full-color feature illustration cards
No "fintech startup" teal/purple palette
No excessive whitespace padding (tight, dense layout)
What NT DOES do
Pure black canvas (#000 / #0a0a0a)
White bold headline text (no off-white)
Orange used only for CTA buttons and section eyebrows
All-caps spaced-letter label above every headline
Thin 1px border cards on near-black backgrounds
Geometric sans headline font, heavy weight
Grey body text (#9ca3af range)
Platform screenshot as right-side hero asset

Every color used across all 7 website HTML files must resolve to one of these tokens. No one-off hex values. No rgba with arbitrary opacity. No hardcoded blue leftovers.

DW-B130 — P0 — CLOSED — Director Design Decision: COPY OFF on Restart is Correct
✓ CLOSED — 2026-09-XX — Director confirmed: copier should reset to COPY OFF on every NT8 restart

Investigation outcome: Tested live. The copier did not copy on restart because:

  1. CopyEnabled defaults to false in CopyRulesContainer [CopyEngine.cs L4264]. It restores whatever state was persisted at last SetEnabled() call.
  2. Mode (Signal/Mirror/Clone) is not persisted — resets to Signal on restart. Switching mode triggers TryAutoApply() which re-registers from UI checkboxes — which are empty on restart (instrument not yet bound).
  3. The correct session workflow is intentionally: restart → select chart → check follower boxes → click COPY ON. This gives a clean, known-good copy state each session.

Director feedback (direct quote): "it should probably be reset every restart since we want a fresh copy so we know what we are copying"

B121 null-slot fix (IsFollowerAccount) is still valid and still deployed — it protects the case where accounts are in a rule but not yet in Account.All at load time. That fix is correct. The restart test was invalid because no rule was active.

DW-B130: CLOSED — Design decision. No pipeline needed. Copier reset on restart is correct behavior.
Symptom (Director-reported, post-B120 F5)

Setup: Sim101 = leader, Sim102 + Sim103 + Sim104 = followers.
Observed: Only Sim101 (leader) and Sim104 receive orders. Sim102 and Sim103 are silently skipped.

Root Cause Analysis (code-confirmed, B121 investigation session)

Two compounding bugs on the XML restore path (LoadRules → DtoToRule):

Bug A — Null slots in FollowerAccounts[] at F5 time:
LoadRules() calls DtoToRule(dto) which calls FindFollowerAccount(name) for each follower name. If an account is not yet in Account.All at F5 load time (SIM accounts connect asynchronously), followers[i] is null and a WARNING is logged. Sim104 connects first (or is already in Account.All); Sim102/103 do not. The CopyRule.FollowerAccounts[] array ends up with null slots for Sim102 and Sim103.

Bug B — IsFollowerAccount false-negative on null slots:
IsFollowerAccount(acc) [CopyEngine.cs L723-732] checks rule.FollowerAccounts[] with guard if (f != null && f.Name == acc.Name). Because Sim102/103 slots are null, IsFollowerAccount returns false for both of them. This has two effects:

  • PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute(): Sim102/103 are NOT skipped in the Account.All outer loop (they appear as non-followers). They get the leader QX path applied independently, which is wrong.
  • DispatchCopy: calls AllAccounts(instrument) which uses B127 lazy-resolve. AllAccounts DOES correctly re-resolve null slots on each dispatch. However, if the first dispatch fires before Sim102/103 are in Account.All, the lazy-resolve logs a WARNING and skips — and no order is sent to those accounts on that dispatch.

Why Sim104 works:
Sim104 resolves successfully at DtoToRule time (already in Account.All). Its slot is non-null. IsFollowerAccount returns true for Sim104 (skipped correctly in leader loops). AllAccounts yields Sim104 on every dispatch.

Source references (code-confirmed):

CopyEngine.cs L4314-4377 : DtoToRule -- null slot on FindFollowerAccount miss + WARNING log
CopyEngine.cs L4383-4391 : FindFollowerAccount -- returns null if name not in Account.All
CopyEngine.cs L4326-4339 : DtoToRule followers[] loop -- null assigned with warning
CopyEngine.cs L723-732   : IsFollowerAccount -- null guard means null slots are invisible
CopyEngine.cs L3419-3463 : AllAccounts -- B127 lazy-resolve handles null slots on dispatch
CopyEngine.cs L449        : CopyRule ctor -- FollowerAccountNames = followerAccountNames ?? DeriveFollowerNames(followers)
CopyEngine.cs L4367-4376 : DtoToRule calls CopyRule.Create with explicit FollowerAccountNames (names preserved)
PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L52-53 : IsFollowerAccount gate -- null slots bypass this guard
Why AllAccounts Lazy-Resolve Is Insufficient Alone

B127 lazy-resolve in AllAccounts() handles the dispatch path correctly IF the account is in Account.All at dispatch time. But:

  • If the first trade fires before Sim102/103 are connected, that dispatch is permanently missed.
  • IsFollowerAccount() cannot be fixed by lazy-resolve — it only reads FollowerAccounts[] (null slots) and does NOT consult FollowerAccountNames[]. This is the structural gap.
  • The fix must make IsFollowerAccount() also consult FollowerAccountNames[] (name-based fallback when slot is null), OR ensure null slots are healed before IsFollowerAccount is called.
Fix Design (pipeline: B121)
Option A (preferred — minimal change): Extend IsFollowerAccount() to also check rule.FollowerAccountNames[] when the corresponding FollowerAccounts[i] slot is null. If acc.Name == names[i], return true. This makes the null-slot follower correctly identified as a follower without needing Account.All resolution. 
// Proposed IsFollowerAccount fix (name-based fallback for null slots):
foreach (var rule in _rules)
    for (int i = 0; i < rule.FollowerAccounts.Length; i++)
    {
        var f = rule.FollowerAccounts[i];
        if (f != null && f.Name == acc.Name) return true;
        // B127 null-slot fallback: check by name
        if (f == null && rule.FollowerAccountNames != null && i < rule.FollowerAccountNames.Length
            && rule.FollowerAccountNames[i] == acc.Name) return true;
    }
return false;

Option B (defensive hardening at load time): After LoadRules(), run a background poll (or subscribe to an account-connection event) to re-resolve null slots as accounts come online. This heals the rule array before any dispatch fires. More complex; Option A is preferred.

Clarifying Question for Director

Before pipeline B121 starts: Is the rule configured via the live UI checkbox toggle (TryAutoApply) or is it loading from saved XML on F5? If using the live path at F5 time, accounts should already be in Account.All and the null-slot issue may not apply. If loading from XML, this is the confirmed root cause. Check NT8 Output Tab for [PTT-COPY] WARNING: follower '...' not found in Account.All at load time messages — their presence confirms the null-slot bug.

Test Criteria for B121 Fix
  • F5 reload with Sim101/102/103/104 rule saved → zero WARNING lines for 102/103 in Output Tab.
  • Place leader order on Sim101 → all four accounts copy: Sim101, 102, 103, 104.
  • Press Quick ALL → IsFollowerAccount correctly blocks 102/103/104 from the leader loop.

DW-B130b — P0 — CLOSED — QxGlobalExit Elite Tier Active via dev_mode.txt Bypass (B121)
Symptom (Director-reported, post-B120 F5)

Quick ALL button does nothing. NT8 Output Tab shows: [PTT-QX-ALL] Blocked: Global Quick Exit requires Elite tier

Root Cause Analysis (code-confirmed)

Complete causal chain: 

PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L38:   if (!CopyEngine.Instance.Flags.QxGlobalExit) -> BLOCKED
FeatureFlags.cs L18-19:      Starter(): QxGlobalExit = false
FeatureFlags.cs L22-23:      Pro():     QxGlobalExit = false
FeatureFlags.cs L24-25:      Elite():   QxGlobalExit = true   <-- only Elite unlocks it
CopyEngine.cs L154:          _flags = FeatureFlags.Starter()   <-- initialized at Starter
TradeCopierAddOn.cs L73-74:  SetFlags(LoadAndValidateLicense())
TradeCopierAddOn.cs L629-646: LoadAndValidateLicense() -> LicenseClient.Validate(key)
LicenseClient.cs L20-34:     Validate(key): reads cache; if no cache -> TryRemoteValidate(key)
LicenseClient.cs L37:        TryRemoteValidate(string key) => null  <-- STUB. Always null.
LicenseClient.cs L33:        return FeatureFlags.Starter()   <-- fallback when stub returns null

The license validation system is a stub. TryRemoteValidate is commented as "SKGL integration deferred" and unconditionally returns null. Unless a pre-built license_cache.json with "features":["qx_global_exit"] exists on disk, the engine always boots at Starter() tier. Quick ALL will never work in this state.

Note: TryReadCache() DOES read an existing cache file, so a manually-crafted cache file could activate Elite. But there is no tooling to create one.

Fix Design for Development / Testing (pipeline: B121, can bundle with DW-B130)

Option A (development bypass — for Director use):
Add a FeatureFlags.Development() factory that returns Elite flags unconditionally. In LoadAndValidateLicense(), check for a dev_mode.txt sentinel file in the PTT user data directory. If present, return FeatureFlags.Elite() without any Cryptolens validation. This is removed (or guarded by a build constant) before commercial release.

Option B (minimal dev fix — preferred for B121):
Create the license_cache.json file manually at %NT8UserDataDir%\PropTraderTools\license_cache.json with content: 

{"key":"DEV","expires_utc":"2030-01-01T00:00:00Z","features":["multi_rule","trim_flatten","break_even","atr_sizing","click_trader","mirror_mode","qx_global_exit"]}

This activates Elite tier via the existing TryReadCache() code path. No code changes needed for testing. Director action required: place this file before next F5.

Option C (pipeline code fix):
Implement TryRemoteValidate with Cryptolens SDK. Deferred to commercial release block. Not required for B121.

Quick Diagnostic (Director action)

Press Quick ALL button with an open position. If Output Tab shows [PTT-QX-ALL] Blocked: Global Quick Exit requires Elite tier → DW-B130b confirmed. Place the license_cache.json file above, press F5, retry.

MISSION BRIEF:
Fix two bugs discovered post-B120 F5 that block all SIM gate testing:

BUG 1 — DW-B130: Copier fires only on Sim101 + Sim104, skips Sim102 + Sim103.
Root cause: IsFollowerAccount() only checks non-null FollowerAccounts[] slots.
When LoadRules/DtoToRule runs at F5 time and SIM accounts are not yet in
Account.All, those slots are null. IsFollowerAccount() returns false for those
accounts. They are skipped by AllAccounts() on the first dispatch AND treated
as non-followers by PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute().

Fix: Extend IsFollowerAccount() to also check FollowerAccountNames[] for null
slots. If rule.FollowerAccounts[i] is null AND rule.FollowerAccountNames[i] ==
acc.Name, return true. CYC stays <=8. No new fields needed.

BUG 2 — DW-B130b: Quick ALL always blocked because QxGlobalExit flag requires
Elite tier which is never activated (LicenseClient.TryRemoteValidate is a stub
returning null; no license_cache.json exists in dev environment).

Fix: Add dev-bypass path in LoadAndValidateLicense() in TradeCopierAddOn.cs:
check for a dev_mode.txt sentinel file at the PTT user data directory. If
present, return FeatureFlags.Elite() unconditionally. This is a dev-only bypass
that does NOT alter the production license flow.

  src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs         (IsFollowerAccount method, L723-732)
  src/PropTraderTools/TradeCopierAddOn.cs   (LoadAndValidateLicense, L629-646)

QTY SPLIT HELPER (new private method in TradeCopierPanel.cs):
  // Build2TargetList: returns a pre-built 2-entry targets list for the 2t buttons.
  // T1 gets ceiling qty (heavy side per Director spec).
  // Prices not used by Execute -- only Qty is read from the pre-built list;
  // prices are computed from entryPx + ticks inside Execute. Pass 0.0 for Price.
  // CYC=1. JS-002: never null. JS-021: no lock.
  private static List<(double Price, int Qty)> Build2TargetList(int totalQty)
  {
      int t1Qty = (totalQty + 1) / 2; // ceiling division
      int t2Qty = totalQty - t1Qty;
      return new List<(double, int)> { (0.0, t1Qty), (0.0, t2Qty) };
  }

OnInstr2tClick handler (replaces OnInstrQxClick):
  private void OnInstr2tClick(object sender, RoutedEventArgs e)
  {
      if (_instrument == null) return;                                    // (1)
      _leaderAccount = _leaderAccount ?? TryResolveLeaderAccount();       // (2)
      if (_leaderAccount == null) return;                                 // (3)
      var pos = _leaderAccount.Positions.FirstOrDefault(
          p => p.Instrument?.FullName == _instrument.FullName);
      int qty = pos?.Quantity ?? 1;
      var targets = Build2TargetList(qty);
      NinjaTrader.Code.Output.Process(
          "[PTT-QX-2T] button: " + _leaderAccount.Name
              + " " + _instrument.FullName
              + " qty=" + qty + " T1=" + targets[0].Qty + " T2=" + targets[1].Qty,
          NinjaTrader.NinjaScript.PrintTo.OutputTab1);
      new PttQuickExit().Execute(_leaderAccount, _instrument, 4, targets);
  }
  CYC=3: null guard(1) + null guard(2) + null guard(3). JS-021: no lock.

DW-B133 — P1 — CLOSED B123 — QAll2t Button Fires 3 Targets (Inherits ATM Snapshot Count) Instead of Forced 2

Symptom (Director-observed, post-B122 live test)

Pressing "QAll2t" with a 3-target ATM active on Sim101 produces 3 bracket pairs, not 2.
Output Tab showed: [DW-B115-DIAG] leader targets: Sim101 count=3 posQty=7 T1=4 T2=2 T3=1

Root Cause (code-confirmed)

OnInstrQAll2tClick calls new PttGlobalQuickExit().Execute() (no-arg overload).
Inside Execute() [PttGlobalQuickExit.cs L62], SnapshotTargetOrders(acc, pos.Instrument) reads the live ATM bracket orders currently on the account. With a 3-target ATM strategy ("MES $200 SL6"), targets.Count = 3.
This is passed to ExecuteOne() → PttQuickExit.Execute() where ResolveTargetCount(targets, leaderTargetCount) at [PttQuickExit.cs L254] returns Math.Min(own.Count, 3) = 3.
The "2-target fixed" intent of the QAll2t button is never communicated to PttGlobalQuickExit. 

OnInstrQAll2tClick -> new PttGlobalQuickExit().Execute()   [no forcedTargets arg]
PttGlobalQuickExit.Execute() L62: targets = SnapshotTargetOrders(acc, instr) -> count=3 (from live ATM)
PttQuickExit.ResolveTargetCount(own=3, leaderCount=0) -> Math.Min(3,3) = 3
Loop fires 3 OCO pairs, not 2.
Fix Design (pipeline: B123)

Option A (preferred — new overload, minimal scope):
Add Execute(List<(double Price, int Qty)> forcedTargets) overload to PttGlobalQuickExit. This overload skips SnapshotTargetOrders() and passes forcedTargets directly to ExecuteOne() (and scales them for ExecuteFollowers via ResolveFollowerTargets).
OnInstrQAll2tClick in TradeCopierPanel then calls:
new PttGlobalQuickExit().Execute(Build2TargetList(qty))
where qty is resolved from the leader position (same as OnInstr2tClick).

Option B (simplest deferral):
Keep QAll2t calling the existing no-arg Execute() (fires 3 targets, mirrors ATM). This is functionally safe — the position exits, just with 3 targets not 2. Defer to a later block if the Director prefers. The button still exits all accounts; only the target count differs.

Architect decides Option A vs B in B123 Ph1.
