FilesCopyEngine.cs (SyncFollowerBracket, HandleBracketChange, FindFollowerBracketOrder)
PipelineB124 (planned) — pending Director approval
Symptom (Director-observed)

While in a trade with COPY ON and followers active, dragging a Target (profit target limit order) or Stop Loss (stop order) bracket on the leader account's chart updates the leader's order price but the follower accounts (Sim102/103/104) retain their original bracket prices. The followers are left with unmodified risk/reward levels that diverge from the leader.

Root Cause (code-confirmed, two-layer gap)

Layer 1 — The listener fires but acc.Change() is a silent no-op for ATM brackets:
CopyEngine.OnOrderUpdate already routes to TryHandleBracketDrag → HandleBracketChange → SyncFollowerBracket → acc.Change(new Order[] { fo }). However, the NT8 ATM engine owns native ATM bracket orders (Stop1/Stop2/Target1/Target2). acc.Change() called from an AddOn context on ATM-owned brackets is a confirmed silent no-op — no exception, no effect, stop/target price unchanged. This is the same root cause fixed by HOTFIX-MSTBE-CANCEL-RESUBMIT (CopyEngine.cs L3598–3601) for the break-even path. 

// CopyEngine.cs L3598-3601 (confirmed existing knowledge):
// Root cause: NT8 ATM engine owns Stop1/Stop2 brackets and ignores acc.Change() from AddOn
// context -- no exception, no effect. Confirmed: [MSTBE] Change() OK Stop1 logged while
// stop remained at original price in Orders tab.

Layer 2 — FindFollowerBracketOrder matches by FromEntrySignal which is null for ATM brackets:
When leader drags a native ATM bracket, leaderOrder.FromEntrySignal == null. FindFollowerBracketOrder(acc, null, isStop) iterates follower orders checking order.FromEntrySignal != null — ATM follower brackets also have FromEntrySignal == null, so the null==null comparison passes the filter. The method then differentiates stops vs. targets by OrderType and IsStopLeg().
ATM stop orders use name format "12s Buy STP" (confirmed CopyEngine.cs L3518–3519) — name starts with digits, not "Stop". IsBracketLegStatic checks StartsWith("Stop") which fails for STP-suffix names, so the leader drag event for ATM stops does not even reach HandleBracketChange because IsWorkingBracket returns false.
Targets (named "Target1", "Target2", ...) do pass IsBracketLegStatic, so their drag events reach HandleBracketChange but are silently ignored by the acc.Change() no-op (Layer 1).

What Happens at Each Gate (call stack trace)
-- Target drag (e.g. Target1 price moved on leader) --
OnOrderUpdate (L1274)
  Gate 1: _isCopyEnabled == true -> pass
  Gate 2: FindMatchingRule -> leader account + instrument matched -> pass
  Gate B+C: TryHandleDrag -> TryHandleBracketDrag
    IsWorkingBracket: OrderState==Working && IsBracketLegStatic("Target1"=StartsWith("Target")) -> TRUE
    HandleBracketChange:
      isStop = IsStopLeg("Target1") -> FALSE (no STP suffix, no "Stop" prefix, no FromEntrySignal)
      rawPrice = leaderOrder.LimitPrice (new dragged price)
      foreach follower:
        SyncFollowerBracket:
          FindFollowerBracketOrder(follower, null, isStop=false)
            -> finds follower order with FromEntrySignal==null, OrderType==Limit, !IsStopLeg -> found
          fo.LimitPrice = newPrice
          acc.Change(new[] { fo })   <-- SILENT NO-OP: ATM bracket owned by NT8 ATM engine
          StatusUpdate logs "bracket synced target -> X" -- but follower price UNCHANGED

-- Stop drag (e.g. "12s Buy STP" moved on leader) --
OnOrderUpdate
  Gate B+C: TryHandleDrag -> TryHandleBracketDrag
    IsWorkingBracket: IsBracketLegStatic("12s Buy STP")
      StartsWith("Stop") -> FALSE
      StartsWith("Target") -> FALSE
      StartsWith("PTT-") -> FALSE
      FromEntrySignal -> null -> FALSE
      -> IsBracketLegStatic returns FALSE
    IsWorkingBracket -> FALSE -> TryHandleBracketDrag returns false -> no sync attempted
NT8 API Confirmed Facts (from NT8_FULL_REFERENCE.md)
  • Account.Change(IEnumerable<Order>) (L2365–2403): changes order price for AddOn-submitted orders. Silent no-op for NT8 ATM-engine-owned brackets (Stop1/Target1) — confirmed empirically.
  • Account.OrderUpdate event (L2456–2506): fires on every order state change and price change when a bracket is dragged in chart. The listener is already wired (CopyEngine.cs L1264).
  • ATM stop name format: "12s Buy STP" (suffix "STP") — CopyEngine.cs L3518–3519. Not "Stop1" prefix.
  • Correct pattern for moving ATM brackets: cancel + resubmit at new price (not acc.Change()). Source: HOTFIX-MSTBE-CANCEL-RESUBMIT pattern at CopyEngine.cs L3598.
Fix Design Options

Option A — Cancel + Resubmit follower bracket at new price (recommended)
When the leader drags a bracket to a new price, detect the price delta in HandleBracketChange and for each follower: (1) cancel the existing ATM bracket order, (2) resubmit a new PTT-prefixed limit/stop order at the scaled new price, (3) the PTT-prefixed order is not owned by the NT8 ATM engine so acc.Submit() will work. This is the same pattern used by PTT-QX and PTT-BE.
Two sub-gaps to fix:

  1. STP-suffix stop detection: extend IsBracketLegStatic to recognise ATM stop name format "...STP" suffix (same as IsStopLeg already does, but IsBracketLegStatic does not — it only checks StartsWith("Stop")). This ensures ATM stop drag events reach HandleBracketChange.
  2. Cancel+resubmit in SyncFollowerBracket: replace fo.LimitPrice = newPrice; acc.Change() with cancel-then-resubmit when the follower bracket is an ATM-owned order (detected by IsAtmBracketName(fo.Name)). PTT-prefixed orders can still use acc.Change() (they are AddOn-submitted, so Change works).

Option B — Price scaling
When dragging, the leader moves by N ticks. The follower may have a different position size. The new price for the follower should be the same absolute price level as the leader (not proportionally scaled by qty) because Stop Loss and Profit Target are price levels, not quantity-dependent. The existing HandleBracketChange already copies the leader price directly (tick-rounded) to the follower — this is correct behaviour. No qty scaling needed.

Option C — Defer (reject)
This is a meaningful operational gap. When a Director moves the stop to lock in profits or moves a target for a partial exit, followers are left exposed. P1 severity. Should be fixed.

Files in Scope
CopyEngine.cs -- two changes:
  1. IsBracketLegStatic (L3532): add EndsWith("STP", OrdinalIgnoreCase) clause
     so ATM stop drag events ("12s Buy STP") reach HandleBracketChange.
  2. SyncFollowerBracket (L2040): replace acc.Change() no-op with cancel+resubmit
     pattern for ATM-owned bracket orders (names: Stop1..Stop9, Target1..Target9, ...STP).
     PTT-prefixed orders continue to use acc.Change() (AddOn-submitted, Change works).

SyncFollowerBracket: CYC 5 → 7 (ATM-owned branch: cancel + resubmit = 2 new branches). If CYC would exceed 8, extract SyncAtmFollowerBracket helper. Architect decides in Ph1.

B130 Test B resultPARTIAL — PTT-TGT-Drag orders on Sim102/103/104 were auto-cancelled when "Flatten Everything" was called. This confirms the Flatten path (QX/BE-ALL triggered close) does not orphan drag-derived stops. The remaining open question is whether an ATM target fill (NT8 OCO execution, not explicit flatten) triggers the same auto-cancel of PTT-TGT-Drag orders outside the OCO group.
Root Cause

SyncAtmFollowerBracket (B129 LaneB fix) cancels the follower's ATM STP bracket via acc.Cancel(new Order[] { fo }) and resubmits a new standalone StopMarket order named "PTT-STP-Drag" via acc.CreateOrder + acc.Submit. Similarly, SyncAtmFollowerTarget (B130 LaneA) resubmits a Limit order named "PTT-TGT-Drag". Both new orders are not part of the original ATM OCO pair. NT8's ATM engine manages STP and target brackets as an OCO group; the new drag-derived orders are outside that OCO group. The OCO auto-cancel behavior when the ATM target fills is untested.

Impact
  • Risk 1 (PTT-STP-Drag orphan): When the ATM target fills on a follower, the ATM engine's OCO cancellation applies to the original STP bracket — which was already cancelled during the stop drag. The "PTT-STP-Drag" stop is outside the OCO group and may remain Working after the target fills, creating an orphaned open stop order.
  • Risk 2 (PTT-TGT-Drag orphan): Similarly, "PTT-TGT-Drag" (from target drag, B130 LaneA) is a standalone Limit order. If the ATM stop fills (position goes flat via stop), the PTT-TGT-Drag target may remain Working.
  • B130 Test B observation: PTT-TGT-Drag was auto-cancelled on explicit Flatten. This suggests PttFlatten.cs calls Cancel on all working orders. The OCO-fill path is a different code path. Observation incomplete.
Fix Design (updated post-B130 Test B)

B130 Test B result partially de-risks this defect. The Flatten path is confirmed safe. The ATM fill path requires one more observation. Fix design options:

  • Option A (Defensive — recommended for B131): In OnPositionUpdate (or OnOrderUpdate on Fill/Cancelled), when a follower account goes flat (position quantity = 0), sweep all orders named "PTT-STP-Drag" or "PTT-TGT-Drag" with state Working and cancel them. This is safe because flat = no position to protect, so any lingering drag order is an orphan.
  • Option B (Wait for observation): Run a dedicated SIM session where the ATM target fills normally (no manual flatten). Observe whether orphan occurs. If no orphan, close DW-B134-OCO as SAFE.

Recommended path: Run Option B first (dedicated observation session, B131 SIM gate 0). If orphan confirmed, implement Option A in B131 LaneA. If no orphan in 3 ATM-target-fill cycles, close as SAFE.

Root Cause

The B129 LaneB fix added EndsWith("STP") to IsAtmSTPOrder, targeting the "Buy STP" / "Sell STP" ATM name format. The Director’s actual template (MES $200 SL 6) generates orders named Stop1, Stop2, Stop3 — a completely different format.

Layer 1 (IsBracketLegStatic): already covers StartsWith("Stop") and StartsWith("Target") — so Stop1 / Target1 PASS Layer 1. This is NOT the bottleneck.

Layer 2 (SyncFollowerBracket routing): calls IsAtmSTPOrder to decide whether to cancel+resubmit. Stop1 does NOT end with "STP" → IsAtmSTPOrder returns false → falls back to acc.Change() → silent no-op for ATM-owned brackets → follower bracket unchanged.

private bool IsAtmSTPOrder(Order o) =>

    || o.Name.StartsWith("Stop", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
// CYC: 1→1 | Risk: confirm no non-ATM orders start with "Stop"

// Option B (IsBracketLegStatic as gate) — align routing with Layer 1:
// Use IsBracketLegStatic result as the routing signal instead of IsAtmSTPOrder.

Conclusion: cancel+resubmit (B129 LaneB design) IS the architecturally correct AddOn approach. The only fix needed is routing: extend IsAtmSTPOrder to cover StartsWith("Stop") names (Option A). No design change required — routing bug only.

FilesCopyEngine.cs — DispatchCopy L1930–1948, IsReversalToFlatFollower L3510–3515, _lastLeaderDirection L331
PipelineB124 (planned) — pending Director approval
Symptom (confirmed from output log)
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell x10 MES SEP26 -> PA-APEX-422136-03 ...
[PTT-COPY-GUARD] skip reversal entry: PA-APEX-422136-03 MES SEP26 follower flat
[PTT-COPY-GUARD] skip reversal entry: PA-APEX-422136-04 MES SEP26 follower flat
[PTT-COPY-GUARD] skip reversal entry: PA-APEX-422136-05 MES SEP26 follower flat
[PTT-COPY] dispatch: Buy x10 MES SEP26 -> PA-APEX-422136-03 ...
[PTT-COPY-GUARD] skip reversal entry: PA-APEX-422136-03 MES SEP26 follower flat
...

The guard fires immediately after a dispatch (sometimes on the same direction) and on every subsequent direction change. Followers are left flat while the leader accumulates positions on live Apex accounts.

Root Cause (code-confirmed)

DispatchCopy (CopyEngine.cs L1930) implements the DW-B128 reversal guard via IsReversalToFlatFollower(currentAction, lastAction, followerIsFlat):

return currentAction != lastAction && followerIsFlat; (L3515).

After every dispatched trade, _lastLeaderDirection[instr.FullName] is written with the last dispatched OrderAction (L1985). When the leader closes a trade and opens in the opposite direction, the guard sees: 

currentAction = Sell (new entry)
lastAction    = Buy  (prior closed trade)
followerIsFlat = true  (close just flattened the follower)
IsReversalToFlatFollower -> true -> GUARD FIRES -> copy BLOCKED

The guard was designed for DW-B128: prevent accidental copy when the leader's closing fill event briefly fires as a reversal signal (e.g. leader fills a short-close order while follower has already been flattened). The fix worked for that race, but the guard is now too broad — it also fires when the Director intentionally opens a new trade in the opposite direction after cleanly closing the prior one.

Additionally, the guard persists across sessions because _lastLeaderDirection is never cleared on COPY OFF / NT8 restart / rule change. On the first re-entry of a new session in the opposite direction from the last trade of the previous session, the guard fires even before the first close event of the new session.

What DW-B128 Was Protecting Against (must be preserved)

The race condition: leader closes a long position via Close/Flatten order (fills). NT8 fires OnOrderUpdate(Filled) for the close order. TryDispatchLeaderFlat runs and flattens followers. Then NT8 fires another OnOrderUpdate event for the same fill with a different state — or the close order itself has OrderAction.Sell which looks like a new short entry. The guard prevents this close-order event from being mistakenly copied as a new Sell entry to already-flat followers.

The root distinction: a close order name is "Close", "Flatten", "Exit*", or similar (caught by IsNativeExitName). A new entry order name is "Entry" (Named ATM mode). The guard should only fire for orders that look like entries but are actually close signals — not for genuine new entry orders.

Fix Design

Option A (minimal — recommended): Clear _lastLeaderDirection when leader position goes flat.
When TryFirePositionState fires hasPos=False for the leader instrument, also clear _lastLeaderDirection[instr.FullName]. The next entry dispatch will have hasLastDirection=false → guard cannot fire (guard is bypassed when hasLastDirection=false, per L1934: "On first entry (hasLastDirection=false) guard cannot fire -- copy always proceeds"). This preserves the DW-B128 protection (guard still fires during the close-order race window when position is still open) while eliminating the false-positive on clean re-entry after a completed close.

Option B (targeted): Only fire guard when order name is a known close signal.
Add a check: if IsNativeExitName(order.Name), skip DispatchCopy entirely (already blocked by IsExitSignalName Gate 0.5). The guard is not needed for named-mode "Entry" orders, since those are unambiguously new entries. Risk: this approach requires careful reasoning about all order name variants and may miss edge cases.

Architect decides Option A vs B in B124 Ph1.

CYC Impact (Option A)

TryFirePositionState: add one _lastLeaderDirection.TryRemove on the hasPos=False path. CYC 3 → 4 (one new branch for the leader check). Still ≤ 8.

Gap A — Second Order Not Copied

When a leader places two entry orders back-to-back on the same instrument while COPY ON, the second order either:

  • Blocked by DW-B135 reversal guard (if direction changed between order 1 and order 2) — same root cause as DW-B135.
  • Blocked by _entryDispatchedOrders dedup: when order 1 fills, TryEvictFollowerBeSlot calls _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear() on Filled events for the leader. However, if order 1 is still Working (not yet filled) when order 2 fires, _entryDispatchedOrders may still contain order 1's ID. Order 2 has a new ID so dedup would not block it. However, if order 1 Cancels (leader cancelled order 1 to replace with order 2), EvictDedup at L3413 calls _entryDispatchedOrders.Clear() on Cancelled — so the dedup clears. This path should allow the second order through.
  • Most likely cause: DW-B135 is the dominant blocker. When the Director cancels order 1 (Working limit) and places order 2 in the same direction, the guard has lastAction = Buy, new currentAction = Buy, currentAction == lastAction → guard does NOT fire. But if order 1 filled and direction then changed for order 2, guard fires.
Gap B — Closing Second Leader Order Cancels Other Followers

TryCancelFollowerEntries (CopyEngine.cs L1621) fires whenever the leader's any order reaches Cancelled state and the order name is not an ATM bracket (IsAtmBracketName guard) or a PTT exit bracket. When the leader cancels order 2 (e.g. a Working limit entry), TryCancelFollowerEntries calls CancelOneAccount on all followers for the instrument. CancelOneAccount cancels all Working/Initialized entry orders for the instrument on each follower — regardless of which leader order they correspond to. This means followers' copy of order 1 (still Working) gets cancelled when the leader cancels order 2. 

Leader: order1 (Working) + order2 (Working) -- two separate entries
Leader cancels order2
  -> TryCancelFollowerEntries fires for order2
  -> CancelOneAccount(Sim102, MES) -> cancels ALL Working entry orders on Sim102
  -> Sim102 copy of order1 CANCELLED (collateral cancel)
  -> Sim102 now flat even though leader still has order1 Working

The same logic applies when the leader fills one order and closes via its ATM Close button: the close order fill triggers TryDispatchLeaderFlat which flattens all followers, even those that copied order2 (which the Director did not intend to close).

Root Cause Summary

The copier is designed for a single-entry model: one leader order per instrument at a time. Both TryCancelFollowerEntries and TryDispatchLeaderFlat operate on instrument scope (not order-ID scope). They have no mechanism to track which follower entry corresponds to which leader order when multiple leader entries coexist on the same instrument.

Fix Design

Short-term (minimal): Document the single-entry constraint explicitly.
The copier does not support two simultaneous entries on the same instrument on the leader. Only one Working entry per instrument per leader account is supported at a time. The Director should finish (fill or cancel) the first entry before placing the second.

Long-term (Pipeline B125+): Order-ID-scoped cancel propagation.
TryCancelFollowerEntries should only cancel follower orders that were copied from the specific leader order being cancelled, not all entries for the instrument. This requires an order-ID mapping in the follower binding (FollowerBinding struct already exists but only tracks FromEntrySignal, not leader orderId). Architect decision in Ph1.

CYC Impact (short-term: doc-only)

CYC = 0. No code changes. Document constraint in spec and in panel UI tooltip.

Ticket 1 — LaneA: DW-B135 Reversal Guard False-Positive (P0)

Root cause (code-confirmed 2026-08-31): IsReversalToFlatFollower fires on every direction change because _lastLeaderDirection[instr.FullName] is never cleared when the leader goes flat. After a completed close, the next entry has currentAction != lastAction && followerIsFlat = true → guard fires, copy blocked.

Fix (Option A — minimal): In TryFirePositionState (CopyEngine.cs), on the hasPos=False path for the leader instrument, call _lastLeaderDirection.TryRemove(instr.FullName, out _). On the next entry dispatch, _lastLeaderDirection.TryGetValue will return false → hasLastDirection=false → guard bypass per L1934. DW-B128 protection fully preserved (guard still fires during the close-order race window when position is still open; only cleared once the position is confirmed flat).

  • File: CopyEngine.cs — TryFirePositionState (currently CYC 3)
  • Change: Add _lastLeaderDirection.TryRemove on leader-flat branch. CYC 3 → 4. Still ≤ 8.
  • Test: [Fact] B129_DW135_GuardClearedAfterLeaderFlat — verify that after simulating a leader-flat event, the next entry dispatch proceeds without the reversal guard firing.
  • Test: [Fact] B129_DW135_DW128ProtectionPreservedDuringRaceWindow — verify guard still fires when position is open and direction changes (close-order race).
Ticket 2 — LaneB: DW-B134 ATM Bracket Drag Sync (P1)

Root cause (code-confirmed 2026-08-31, OQ-01/02/04 answered): Two-layer gap:

  1. Layer 1 (STP suffix): ATM stop bracket names end in "…STP" (e.g. "Buy STP"). IsBracketLegStatic only checks StartsWith("Stop") — does not match STP-suffix names. Stop drag events never reach HandleBracketChange.
  2. Layer 2 (ATM ownership): Even when Layer 1 is bypassed, acc.Change() on ATM-owned stop/target brackets is a confirmed silent no-op. The ATM engine owns those orders and ignores external Change() calls.

Fix design:

  • Layer 1 fix: In IsBracketLegStatic, add || orderName.EndsWith("STP", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) so STP-suffix stop names trigger the bracket-change path. CYC 3 → 4.
  • Layer 2 fix: In SyncFollowerBracket, replace the single acc.Change() call with a cancel+resubmit sequence for ATM-owned brackets: cancel the existing follower bracket order, then create+submit a new PTT bracket at the updated price. Extract SyncAtmFollowerBracket(followerAcc, order, newPrice) helper if CYC would exceed 8.
  • OQ-03 (OPEN — architect must answer in Ph1): After cancel+resubmit, the orphaned PTT bracket (original order, now cancelled) must not trigger a spurious TryCancelFollowerEntries on the follower. Architect must confirm the cancellation path for PTT-submitted orders is gated by IsAtmBracketName or equivalent so the orphan cancel does not cascade.
  • Test: [Fact] B129_DW134_STPSuffixStopDragReachesBracketChange — verify IsBracketLegStatic returns true for "Buy STP" after fix.
  • Test: [Fact] B129_DW134_SyncFollowerBracketCancelResubmit — verify cancel+resubmit fires instead of acc.Change() for ATM-owned brackets.
Execution Order

Ticket 1 (DW-B135) is the blocker. It is simpler (1 line + 2 tests) and resolves the P0 live-trading risk. Ticket 2 (DW-B134) can run in parallel in a separate lane once the architect has answered OQ-03. Both share the same file (CopyEngine.cs) so sequencing is recommended: LaneA FINAL_PASS → LaneB start (to avoid merge conflicts on CopyEngine.cs).

=== DEFECT BRIEF (DW-B135) ===

Root cause (code-confirmed 2026-08-31):
  File: src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs
  Symbol: _lastLeaderDirection  (ConcurrentDictionary, L331)
  Symbol: IsReversalToFlatFollower (L3510)
  Symbol: TryFirePositionState (L2283)
  Symbol: DispatchCopy (L1930 — reads _lastLeaderDirection, writes it at L1985)

  _lastLeaderDirection[instr.FullName] is written on every entry dispatch (L1985).
  It is NEVER cleared when the leader position goes flat.
  IsReversalToFlatFollower (L3510): returns currentAction != lastAction && followerIsFlat.
  After a completed close, on the very next entry in the opposite direction:
    currentAction != lastAction = true  (direction changed)
    followerIsFlat = true               (follower correctly flat after close)
    => guard fires => copy blocked.
  This is a false-positive. The guard was designed for DW-B128 (close-order race window),
  not for clean re-entry after a completed close.

Fix (Option A — minimal, architect must confirm):
  In TryFirePositionState (CopyEngine.cs L2283):
    On the hasPos=False path, add:
      if (IsLeaderAccount(account)) _lastLeaderDirection.TryRemove(instr.FullName, out _);
    Where IsLeaderAccount(account) checks account == _leaderAccount (or equivalent).
  Effect: next entry dispatch has hasLastDirection=false => guard cannot fire (guard is bypassed
  per L1934 when hasLastDirection=false). DW-B128 protection fully preserved: guard still fires
  during the close-order race window (position is still open, hasPos=True, direction key still set).
  CYC TryFirePositionState: 3 → 4 (one new branch). Still ≤ 8.

Architect must confirm:
  1. IsLeaderAccount(account) check: confirm the correct predicate to identify leader vs follower.
     Options: account == _leaderAccount, or account.Name == _leaderAccount.Name.
  2. Thread safety: _lastLeaderDirection is ConcurrentDictionary. TryRemove is lock-free. Confirm OK.
  3. TryFirePositionState is called on NT8 UI thread (PositionStateChanged). Confirm no lock needed.
  4. The hasPos=False event fires AFTER the position is fully closed (not during the close order fill).
     Confirm this is safe and does not clear the key during a partial fill.
  5. Confirm no other callers of _lastLeaderDirection that would be affected by this removal.

Root Cause Confirmed (H2)

FindFollowerBracketOrder matched follower bracket orders by FromEntrySignal string equality. PTT-placed follower brackets carry FromEntrySignal = null or ""; ATM leader brackets carry a non-null signal name from the ATM entry. Comparison: null != "signal_name" evaluated true → follower order was skipped every iteration → FindFollowerBracketOrder returned null → SyncFollowerBracket exited at the early-return guard before any cancel+resubmit fired. This explains why Stop1/Target1/Target2 were always silent while Target3 (which had a matching FromEntrySignal from a prior sync) succeeded.

Fix Applied (B131 LaneA)
  • New SignalOrNameMatches predicate (L2361, CYC=3): private static; checks signal equality first (branch 1), falls back to name equality when leaderName is non-null (branches 2-3). Handles the case where follower bracket has null FromEntrySignal by matching the ATM order name directly.
  • FindFollowerBracketOrder extended (L2375, CYC=4): optional string? leaderName = null parameter added; loop guard replaced from raw != to !SignalOrNameMatches(order, fromEntrySignalName, leaderName). Default param = backward-compatible with all prior callers.
  • SyncFollowerBracket call site updated (L2139): now passes leaderOrder.Name as 4th argument to enable name-based fallback. CYC=7 unchanged (no new branches).
  • 4 xUnit tests (B131Tests.cs): Stop1 name-fallback (Test 1), Target1 name-fallback (Test 2), Target3 signal-match regression (Test 3), Buy STP signal-match regression (Test 4). All 4 pass. 7 total B131 tests + 8 B130 + 13 B129 all passing.

Status✓ P1 CLOSED — B131 LaneB PIPELINE_COMPLETE. VERIFY_PASS. FINAL_PASS.
EvidenceCSV 10:56 AM order log (original defect): Sim102 had 3 PTT-TGT-Drag at 7687/7685.5/7681.5. Fix prevents accumulation: each drag event cancels prior Working PTT-TGT-Drag before creating new one at updated price.
Root Cause

SyncAtmFollowerTarget created a new PTT-TGT-Drag Limit order on each drag event via acc.CreateOrder + acc.Submit without first checking whether an existing PTT-TGT-Drag Working order was present on the follower account for the same instrument. Each drag event appended a new limit order to the follower's order book at the new drag price while prior PTT-TGT-Drag orders remained Working at old prices.

Fix Applied (B131 LaneB)
  • Block A-Prime inserted (L2270-L2288, before Block A): foreach (var o in acc.Orders.ToList()) sweeps follower orders; filter: o.OrderState == OrderState.Working && o.Name == "PTT-TGT-Drag" && o.Instrument?.FullName == fo.Instrument?.FullName; each matching order cancelled via acc.Cancel(new Order[] { o }) inside try/catch (no rethrow, logs via StatusUpdate).
  • Block A and Block B unchanged: existing acc.Cancel(new Order[] { fo }) (Block A) and acc.CreateOrder + acc.Submit (Block B) byte-for-byte identical to B130.
  • SyncAtmFollowerTarget CYC=8: at Jane Street strict limit. 8 branches enumerated in leading comment.
  • Sub-defect T1/T2 not syncing: fixed by DW-B138 LaneA fix (same root cause — FromEntrySignal mismatch). T1/T2 follower bracket lookup now succeeds via SignalOrNameMatches name fallback.
  • 3 xUnit tests (B131LaneBTests): second drag cancels prior PTT-TGT-Drag (Test 1), first drag creates exactly 1 (Test 2), no prior drag = no extra cancels (Test 3). All 3 structural placeholders pass (NT8 Account sealed — runtime SIM required for behavioural confirmation).

Observed Symptom (B131 SIM session 2, 2026-08-31 12:41-12:45 PM)

Leader: Sell 7 MES open on Sim101 with ATM brackets Stop1(4)+Stop2(2)+Stop3(1), Target1(4)+Target2(2)+Target3(1).
Followers (Sim102, Sim103): native ATM brackets fully Working (green = OCO-linked, strategy-owned).
At 12:41:46: Director dragged T3 on Sim101. SyncAtmFollowerTarget fired for each follower.

Expected: Target3 follower bracket (qty=1) cancelled and replaced by PTT-TGT-Drag @ new price. Stop3 follower bracket preserved. Stop1/Stop2/Target1/Target2 untouched.
Actual: For Sim102/Sim103: entire OCO group cancelled — Stop1(4)+Target1(4)+Stop2(2)+Target2(2) ALL cancelled on first drag of T3. Then Target3/Stop3 pair also cancelled+replaced separately. PTT-TGT-Drag qty=4 and qty=2 created (target-side only, no stop replacement). After first drag: zero stop orders on Sim102 and Sim103.

Root Cause

SyncAtmFollowerTarget locates the matching follower bracket order via FindFollowerBracketOrder (or direct scan) and calls acc.Cancel(new Order[] { followerBracket }).

The follower bracket orders are native ATM orders placed by NT8 when PTT copied the entry: they are OCO-linked (green in NT8 grid = OCO group active). When acc.Cancel() is called on any member of an OCO group, NT8 automatically cancels all other members of the same OCO group. This is standard NT8 OCO behaviour — not a PTT bug in the Cancel call itself, but an architectural gap in how PTT interacts with OCO orders.

Because all 3 target brackets (T1, T2, T3) are in a single OCO group with their corresponding stops (Stop1, Stop2, Stop3), cancelling T3 cancels the entire group. PTT then creates PTT-TGT-Drag (target-side only, no OCO linking, no stop). Result: followers are long/short with no stop protection at all.

NT8 API Fact (confirmed — do not re-investigate)

Account.Change() is a silent no-op on ATM-owned brackets (empirically confirmed B129 SIM gate). Cannot use Change() to price-adjust an ATM bracket without cancelling.
Account.Cancel() on OCO-linked orders cancels the full OCO group (confirmed B131 SIM session 2 observation).
Therefore the only viable path is: cancel the target bracket (accepting OCO-cancel-all), then immediately create replacement stop orders using acc.CreateOrder()+Submit() at the leader’s current stop prices for the same bracket group index.

Fix Implemented (B132 LaneA PIPELINE_COMPLETE)

FileCopyEngine.cs — SignalOrNameMatches L2510–2517
Status✓ P0 CLOSED (pipeline) — B133 LaneA FINAL_PASS 2026-08-31 — SIM Test A PENDING (CONDITIONAL)
RelatedDW-B141 (P0 SIM re-queued B133 Test A — now testable), DW-B143 (P1 CLOSED — companion fix LaneB), DW-B138 (CLOSED pipeline — root causes fixed)
Root Cause

SignalOrNameMatches at L2510: 

internal static bool SignalOrNameMatches(Order order, string? signalName, string? leaderName)
{
    if (order.FromEntrySignal == signalName) // ATM brackets: null == null = TRUE → WRONG
        return true;
    if (leaderName == null) return false;
    return order.Name == leaderName;         // NAME CHECK NEVER REACHED for ATM orders
}

ATM brackets have null FromEntrySignal. C# reference equality: null == null = true. FindFollowerBracketOrder iterates all follower orders and returns the first Working order where SignalOrNameMatches is true. For ATM brackets this is always the first Working order in iteration order (typically Target1 or Stop1), regardless of which bracket the leader dragged (e.g. Target3). This causes the wrong bracket to be cancelled via acc.Cancel(fo), which NT8 OCO-group-cancels ALL brackets in the group (Stop1/Stop2/Stop3/Target1/Target2/Target3). The B131 LaneA leaderName fallback (line 3) was designed correctly but is never reached at runtime because line 1 always short-circuits for ATM orders.

Fix (B133 LaneA — one-line change)
// Before (L2510):
if (order.FromEntrySignal == signalName)
    return true;

// After:
if (signalName != null && order.FromEntrySignal == signalName)
    return true;

This one-line guard prevents null == null from matching. With signalName != null guarded, ATM orders with null signals fall through to line 3 (order.Name == leaderName) which correctly matches by order name (e.g. "Target3" == "Target3"). The B131 LaneA name fallback now activates for ATM orders as originally intended.

Fix Applied (B133 LaneA — PIPELINE_COMPLETE)
  • CopyEngine.cs L2513 (B133 LaneA): if (signalName != null && order.FromEntrySignal == signalName) — null-guard in place. null==null no longer returns true. VERIFY_PASS + FINAL_PASS confirmed.
  • DW-B141 Phase C: Now testable — re-queued as B133 SIM Test A. DW-B142 no longer corrupts the path before Phase C can exercise.
  • DW-B143: Companion fix deployed (B133 LaneB). Both ship together.
  • DW-B138 diagnostic: _diagnosticMode stays true through B133 SIM re-validation.

FileCopyEngine.cs — FindFollowerBracketOrder ~L2533 (state filter line)
Status✓ P1 CLOSED (pipeline) — B133 LaneB FINAL_PASS 2026-09-05 — SIM Test B PENDING (CONDITIONAL)
HypothesisOriginally H1 in B132 LaneB plan. Confirmed by TP4 trace: fo=NULL while follower orders show Submitted/Accepted state.
RelatedDW-B138 (parent — stop drag silent), DW-B142 (companion P0 — null==null; together these two fixes fully resolve DW-B138 at runtime)
Root Cause (confirmed by TP4 trace)

FindFollowerBracketOrder state filter at ~L2533: 

// Before (~L2533):
if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Working)
    continue;   // Skips Accepted AND Submitted orders

Leader bracket is accepted through IsWorkingBracket if Working || Accepted. But FindFollowerBracketOrder only passes Working. When a drag event fires while follower orders are in Accepted state (transition from newly submitted PTT-placed or ATM orders), follower lookup returns null → SyncFollowerBracket returns early → no PTT-STP-Drag dispatch. TP4 trace confirmed: fo=NULL with followerOrders=[...,Stop1:Submitted,Target1:Submitted,...].

Note: Submitted state is NOT included in the fix. Cancelling a Submitted ATM bracket via acc.Cancel() may not be reliably supported. Accepted is safe (NT8 confirms broker acceptance; cancel operations succeed on Accepted orders). IsWorkingBracket already accepts Working || Accepted for leader-side gate — mirroring this on the follower side is the minimal safe fix.

Fix (B133 LaneB — one-line change)
// Before (~L2533):
if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Working)
    continue;

// After:
if (order.OrderState != OrderState.Working && order.OrderState != OrderState.Accepted)
    continue;

Observed Symptom (B134 SIM Test A, 2026-09-07)

First drag of Target3 on Sim101: TP4 fo=Target3 ✓. PTT-TGT-Drag placed on Sim102/Sim103/Sim104 as BLUE (standalone Limit, outside OCO group). ATM Target3 bracket cancelled on each follower account — replaced by PTT-TGT-Drag.

Second drag of Target3 on Sim101: TP4 fo=NULL on all followers. FindFollowerBracketOrder iterates follower orders, applies leaderName guard: if (leaderName != null && order.Name != leaderName) continue;. leaderName="Target3". No order named "Target3" exists on follower (it was cancelled on first drag). PTT-TGT-Drag is named "PTT-TGT-Drag". Guard skips it. fo=NULL → sync returns early, no action.

Color confirmation: After first drag, followers show PTT-TGT-Drag in BLUE (standalone, not OCO-linked). Remaining ATM brackets (Stop1-3, Target1-2) stay GREEN (OCO-linked). This confirms the leaderName guard cannot match the blue replacement order by exact name.

Root Cause

DW-B145 (B134 Ticket 2) added an exact leaderName guard to FindFollowerBracketOrder to prevent fo=Target1 when Target3 is dragged. The guard works perfectly for first drags (ATM bracket "Target3" exists on follower, matches exactly). But on a second drag, the first drag already cancelled the ATM bracket and replaced it with "PTT-TGT-Drag". The guard does not know that "PTT-TGT-Drag" is the replacement for "Target3" — it only matches by exact name. Result: second drag always returns fo=NULL for any bracket that has already been dragged once.

CYC Constraint

FindFollowerBracketOrder is currently at CYC=8 (AT LIMIT — JS ceiling). Adding a new condition to the guard at L2551 adds 1 branch → CYC=9 (OVER LIMIT). Helper extraction is MANDATORY before any fix can be applied. The B135 ptt-architect must design a private helper method (e.g. MatchesLeaderName(Order order, string? leaderName, bool isStop)) that encapsulates the existing exact guard plus the new PTT-prefix fallback. Extracting the helper reduces FindFollowerBracketOrder CYC by 1, creating room for the new branch.

Fix Design (for B135 architect)
  • Option A (PTT-prefix fallback): When leaderName is a known ATM bracket name (e.g. "Target3"), also accept the corresponding PTT-prefixed replacement order: "PTT-TGT-Drag" (for target, isStop=false) or "PTT-STP-Drag" (for stop, isStop=true). Encapsulate in MatchesLeaderName(order, leaderName, isStop) helper. Pro: minimal change, clear intent. Con: relies on exact PTT order name strings (coupling).
  • Option B (type-based matching): When no exact-name match found, fall back to matching by OrderType (Limit for target, StopMarket for stop) and order action. Pro: no string coupling. Con: regression risk if multiple Limit/StopMarket orders exist per follower account.
  • Option C (PTT name StartsWith): Relax guard to: exact name match OR (leaderName is ATM bracket name AND order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-")). Simplest. Requires that only one PTT-prefixed order exists per bracket type per follower at any time (guaranteed by Block A-Prime pre-sweep in SyncAtmFollowerTarget).
  • Recommended: Option A or C. Architect determines exact approach in B135 Ph1. Helper extraction required regardless of which option is chosen.

When NT8 fires two TP3-HBC events back-to-back for the same drag (Accepted then Working transitions), the second event catches PTT-TGT-Drag in ChangeSubmitted state. Root cause: When Stop1 fires and CancelExistingPttStpDrag places PTT-STP-Drag #1, NT8 promotes that order Submitted→Accepted asynchronously. Stop2 fires before this promotion completes. CancelExistingPttStpDrag filter was Working||Accepted only — PTT-STP-Drag #1 in Submitted state is NOT cancelled. Stop2 places PTT-STP-Drag #2. Result: 2× PTT-STP-Drag per follower. Fix: Extend filter to Submitted||Working||Accepted at CopyEngine.cs L2400. PTT-STP-Drag is an AddOn-created order — safe to cancel in Submitted state (same pattern used throughout codebase). CYC: 6-7→7-8 (≤8). Direct repair applied without pipeline (1-line change, build 0E/0W, B137 tests 16/16 PASS, sync 0 MISMATCH 2026-09-08).

DW-B152-B — P1 NEW — Cancel-In-Flight Race — B139 Pipeline Required
IDDW-B152-B
PriorityP1
StatusOPEN — B139 pipeline required
DiscoveredB138 SIM (2026-09-08)
ComponentCopyEngine.cs — SyncAtmFollowerBracket Block B + CancelExistingPttStpDrag
Root cause3-stop ATM template fires 3 sequential TP3-HBC events nearly simultaneously. CancelExistingPttStpDrag submits a cancel for the existing PTT-STP-Drag (correct), but Block B immediately places a new PTT-STP-Drag without waiting for the cancel to resolve. NT8 cancel is async (CancelPending → CancelSubmitted → Cancelled). The next stop leg event arrives before the cancel completes; a second PTT-STP-Drag is placed. DW-B152 filter fix caught the first race (Stop1→Stop2 Submitted gap) but not the second (Stop2→Stop3 cancel-in-flight gap).
EvidenceB138 grid log: per-follower: qty=4 PTT-STP-Drag (Submitted→Accepted→CancelSubmitted→Cancelled) + qty=2 PTT-STP-Drag (Submitted→Accepted, survives until flatten). qty=2 only cancelled by Flatten Everything. No qty=1 PTT-STP-Drag (Stop3 leg) visible in log — Stop3 event fired but Block B either did not place or the order was not visible before flatten.
Fix approachPipeline required. Two candidate approaches: (A) In SyncAtmFollowerBracket Block B: before placing new PTT-STP-Drag, scan for any existing PTT-STP-Drag in non-terminal state (Submitted||Working||Accepted||CancelPending||CancelSubmitted) — if found, skip placement (cancel already in-flight will resolve; correct order placed on next drag). (B) Switch subsequent stop drags (PTT-STP-Drag already placed) from cancel+resubmit to in-place modify via Account.Change(). Architecture plan (Ph1) must decide between A and B.

DW-B142-DRAG — P1 — OPEN — ca8ad16 B142-DIRECT-9 SIM — Second target drag silent on followers — IsAtmSTPOrder missing PTT-TGT-Drag-N clause
✗ DW-B142-DRAG — P1 OPEN — ca8ad16 B142-DIRECT-9 SIM (2026-09-02): Second target drag does NOT sync followers — first drag PASS, second+ drag SILENT on all followers (Sim102/103/104)
Discovered: 2026-09-02 — B142-DIRECT-9 SIM output analysis — Director report: targets sync first move only
Defect IDDW-B142-DRAG
SeverityP1 — followers not synced on repeated target drags — first drag correct, second+ drag silent
Commitca8ad16 (B142-DIRECT-9)
Status✗ P1 OPEN — root cause confirmed by log trace analysis — fix designed (spec only) — pipeline required
RelatedB142-DIRECT-4 (stop analogue — PTT-STP-Drag- clause added to IsAtmSTPOrder for stops) — DW-B141 (Phase C stop replacement) — DW-B146/DW-B148 (earlier second-drag fo=NULL fixes, now resolved)
Symptom

After the first target drag all three follower accounts (Sim102/Sim103/Sim104) correctly receive PTT-TGT-Drag-1/2/3 orders via SyncAtmFollowerTarget. On every subsequent target drag, TP3-HBC fires (followerCount=3, newPrice updated), TP4-SFB fires (fo=PTT-TGT-Drag-N, correct), but the follower orders are updated via acc.Change() (no-op on AddOn-created limit orders) instead of the required cancel+resubmit path. The log confirms PTT-TGT-Drag-N:ChangeSubmitted transitions on followers — meaning acc.Change() was called and acknowledged — but NT8 does not actually move the limit price. No new PTT-TGT-Drag-N is created at the new price. Stops work correctly past the first drag because their analogue guard (StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-")) was added in B142-DIRECT-4.

Root Cause (confirmed by log + code analysis)

File: src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs — IsAtmSTPOrder (line 2237) and SyncFollowerBracket branch (3b) (line 2325).

On a second target drag, FindFollowerBracketOrder correctly resolves fo = PTT-TGT-Drag-N via MatchesLeaderName branch (3) (leaderName="TargetN" → suffix extraction → order.Name == "PTT-TGT-Drag-N"). The state filter now includes ChangeSubmitted (B142-DIRECT-9) so fo is non-null even during rapid drags. Control returns to SyncFollowerBracket with fo = PTT-TGT-Drag-N and isStop = false.

Branch (3b) tests !isStop && IsAtmSTPOrder(fo). IsAtmSTPOrder checks four clauses: 

internal static bool IsAtmSTPOrder(Order order) =>
    order.Name != null
    && (
        order.Name.EndsWith("STP", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)       // Buy STP / Sell STP
        || order.Name.StartsWith("Stop", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) // Stop1/2/3
        || order.Name.StartsWith("Target", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) // Target1/2/3
        || order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal)  // PTT stop replacement (B142-DIRECT-4)
        // ✗ MISSING: || order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-TGT-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal)
    );

fo.Name = "PTT-TGT-Drag-3". None of the four clauses match: EndsWith("STP") ✗, StartsWith("Stop") ✗, StartsWith("Target") ✗, StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-") ✗. IsAtmSTPOrder returns false. Branch (3b) is skipped. SyncAtmFollowerTarget (cancel+resubmit) is never called.

Control falls through to the trailing-stop guard and then to the generic fo.LimitPrice = newPrice; acc.Change(new Order[] { fo }); path. acc.Change() on an AddOn-created limit order is confirmed as a no-op by NT8 (empirically confirmed B129 SIM gate; also confirmed by B140 for ATM-owned brackets). The follower order transitions through ChangeSubmitted back to Working at the original price. No price movement occurs.

Contrast with stops: fo.Name = "PTT-STP-Drag-1". StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-") ✓ → IsAtmSTPOrder = true → branch (3) taken → SyncAtmFollowerBracket (cancel+resubmit) called → stops work correctly on second+ drag. The PTT-STP-Drag- clause was added in B142-DIRECT-4 but its target analogue PTT-TGT-Drag- was never added.

Fix Design (one-line, spec-level — pipeline required for src edit)

Add PTT-TGT-Drag- clause to IsAtmSTPOrder, mirroring the B142-DIRECT-4 stop clause exactly. This makes branch (3b) fire when fo = PTT-TGT-Drag-N, routing to SyncAtmFollowerTarget (cancel + resubmit) on every subsequent target drag. 

// BEFORE (CopyEngine.cs ~L2237)
internal static bool IsAtmSTPOrder(Order order) =>
    order.Name != null
    && (
        order.Name.EndsWith("STP", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("Stop", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("Target", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal)
    );

// AFTER (add one clause — symmetric with PTT-STP-Drag- added in B142-DIRECT-4)
internal static bool IsAtmSTPOrder(Order order) =>
    order.Name != null
    && (
        order.Name.EndsWith("STP", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("Stop", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("Target", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal)
        || order.Name.StartsWith("PTT-TGT-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal)  // ✓ ADD: second+ target drag
    );

CYC impact: IsAtmSTPOrder is a CYC=1 expression body (compound || expressions do not add McCabe branches per project convention). Adding one || StartsWith() clause leaves CYC=1. SyncFollowerBracket CYC unchanged (no new branch added; existing branch (3b) already covers this path).

Downstream behaviour: When fo = PTT-TGT-Drag-N hits branch (3b), SyncAtmFollowerTarget(acc, fo, newPrice, leaderOrder) is called. Block A-Prime cancels any stale PTT-TGT-Drag-N (the old one at the prior price). Block A cancels fo directly. Block B creates a new PTT-TGT-Drag-N at newPrice. Phase C (ExecutePhaseCStopReplacement) runs; it looks for the leader's Stop{N} — on a second drag that ATM stop is already PTT-STP-Drag-N and FindLeaderStopPrice will return 0.0 (searches for "Stop1" by name, which is Cancelled). Phase C produces no additional stop (correct — the stop is already placed and Working as PTT-STP-Drag-N). Net result: follower target moves to new price. No regressions.

Target leg PTT-TGT-Drag-3 ✗ false (no matching clause) ✓ true (StartsWith PTT-TGT-Drag-) acc.Change (no-op) → AFTER FIX: cancel+resubmit ✓

ArchitectureGuard in DispatchCopy (CopyEngine.cs ~L2146–2149 + L4768–4775): hasLastDirection && IsReversalToFlatFollower(currentAction, lastAction, flat). IsReversalToFlatFollower = currentAction != lastAction && followerIsFlat. Direction key written at L2198: _lastLeaderDirection[instr.FullName] = currentAction. Key cleared in TryFirePositionState via TryRemove(_lastLeaderDirection) on leader flat event.
▲ Three Candidate Root Causes
PATH A — Spurious Sell write (direction key corruption)

Between trade-1 close and trade-2 entry, some order passes all 5 gates in DispatchCopy and writes direction = Sell to _lastLeaderDirection (L2198). On the next Buy entry: lastAction=Sell, currentAction=Buy, currentAction != lastAction is true, followerIsFlat is true → IsReversalToFlatFollower = true → guard fires → follower blocked. Gate 0.5 should block PTT-* prefixed, Close, Exit*, Target*, Rev* — but an unanticipated order name may slip through. Confirmed only by log showing a [PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell... line between trade-1 close and trade-2 entry attempt.

PATH B — _lastHasPos CAS race (leader TryRemove suppressed)

_lastHasPos dedup box is keyed by instr.FullName only (L3470) — shared across ALL accounts for the same instrument. Race: if a FOLLOWER fill event fires TryFirePositionState first for the same instrument (hasPos=false, OrderState.Filled), the CAS wins on the follower (prior=2 sentinel → new=0), isLeaderAcct=false → TryRemove is skipped. Dedup box now holds 0. When leader fires next: prior=0, new=0 → CAS returns early at L3472 → TryRemove(_lastLeaderDirection) NEVER runs → _lastLeaderDirection["MES"] = Buy survives into the next cycle. HOWEVER: for the guard to fire on a same-direction second Buy trade, lastAction must be Sell (not Buy) — so Path B alone cannot explain the symptom unless combined with a separate Sell write. Path B suppresses the TryRemove cleanup but does not by itself insert a Sell direction. Path B is a contributing condition, not the sole root cause.

PATH C — Stale ATM object cache (dispatch path switches to Inherit)

Clone button click captures _cloneAtmObject — the live AtmStrategy object at click time. After trade closes, NT8 may invalidate or dispose the AtmStrategy object. On the next order: GetCloneAtmMode() checks _cloneAtmObject — if disposed/null-equivalent, returns Inherit. With Inherit mode, ResolveAtmMode returns Inherit → SendCopy is called instead of SendCopyWithAtm. However: the symptom is “dispatched to leader only” (followers don’t even get the entry), not “dispatched without ATM”. This rules out Path C as the primary cause unless SendCopy on the Inherit path has a separate conditional that skips follower dispatch. Requires code trace to confirm.

▲ DIAGNOSTIC STATUS — Log capture required
KEY LOG LINES TO IDENTIFY:
  • [PTT-COPY] dispatch: Buy ... -> Sim10X — first trade dispatch (confirms first trade OK)
  • [PTT-COPY] dispatch: Sell ... -> Sim10X — if present: confirms spurious Sell write → PATH A active
  • [PTT-COPY-GUARD] skip reversal entry: ... — the blocking line on second entry attempt
  • PositionStateChanged instr=... hasPos=False — if present: confirms flat event fired → PATH B candidate
  • Any dispatch: line between trade-1 close and trade-2 attempt that contains a direction other than the entry direction

Decision logic: If a dispatch: Sell line exists between close and second-entry attempt → PATH A. If no such line → PATH B (TryRemove suppressed + separately-sourced Sell write). If followers receive the entry but no ATM brackets → PATH C contribution.

▲ Fix Design (post-log, per path)
PATH A FIX Audit what order name is writing direction=Sell at L2198 between trade-1 close and trade-2 attempt. Add that order name to IsExitSignalName (Gate 0.5) OR ensure DispatchCopy returns before L2198 for that order. CYC impact: +0 (one new StartsWith or Contains check in existing chain). JS-021 compliant.
PATH B FIX Key _lastHasPos per account + instrument (not just instrument). Change: _lastHasPos key = e.Order.Account.Name + "|" + instr (L3461/3470). Follower CAS wins no longer suppress leader TryRemove. CYC impact: +0 (same branch count, key string only). Uses ConcurrentDictionary — JS-021 compliant.
PATH C FIX Add null/disposed check in GetCloneAtmMode and refresh _cloneAtmObject from live ChartTrader state on each DispatchCopy call if the stored reference is no longer valid. Also verify SendCopy (Inherit path) does not have a conditional that skips follower dispatch — if it does, that branch must be removed or the Inherit-path follower dispatch restored.
LOOP RULE: Do NOT start any fix until the log confirms which path is active. After log confirms → write fix design into spec HTML → direct repair (fast path) → sync + F5 + SIM.

IDDW-LB-SFB-01
SeverityP1
SymptomClone mode + BE ALL: when the leader’s PTT-BE-Stop-N order goes Working, IsBracketLegStatic (via IsWorkingBracket) returns true because the old clause StartsWith("PTT-") matched any PTT- order. This triggers HandleBracketChange → SyncFollowerBracket on the leader’s PTT-BE-Stop Working event. In SIM, follower order objects (fo) are null at this stage (bracket not yet Working on follower), causing a null-ref cascade and PTT-Flatten storm.
Root causeIsBracketLegStatic in CopyEngine.cs used StartsWith("PTT-") to identify PTT drag-replacement bracket names. This was correct for PTT-STP-Drag- and PTT-TGT-Drag- (the actual drag bracket substitutes) but also matched PTT-BE-Stop, PTT-Flatten, PTT-Trim, PTT-Tighten-Stop, etc. — all of which are NOT bracket legs.
FixNarrowed IsBracketLegStatic in CopyEngine.cs from StartsWith("PTT-") to two specific clauses: StartsWith("PTT-STP-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal) and StartsWith("PTT-TGT-Drag-", StringComparison.Ordinal). Only the actual drag-replacement bracket order names are classified as bracket legs.

Perpetual Session Loop — $continue Protocol V3.0 — Direct-Repair Loop — diagnose → repair → SIM verify → pipeline only on SIM PASS — no pause, no wait gates — updated 2026-09-02
$continue Loop — Perpetual Session Protocol (V3.0 — 2026-09-02 — Direct-Repair Loop: no wait gates, $continue travels with every test request)

Every copier-spec session begins with a $continue prompt (which includes the test results from the prior session). The session diagnoses, applies a direct repair, syncs+F5, then outputs a test request + next $continue prompt together. The Director tests in NT8 SIM, then pastes the pre-written $continue into a new session with the results appended. The full PTT pipeline (5 phases) runs only after a defect’s SIM test passes. The loop runs until the codebase reaches STABLE.

V3.0 CORE RULE — NO PAUSE, NO WAIT GATES. The session never stops and waits for Director input mid-session. Every session ends in one shot: diagnose → repair → sync+F5 gate → output test request + pre-written $continue prompt. The Director tests, then pastes $continue + results into a NEW session. Pipeline runs only after SIM PASS is confirmed in the $continue prompt.
PIPELINE GATE — WHEN TO RUN FULL 5-PHASE PTT PIPELINE:
  • Direct repair loop (default): diagnose → direct src edit → sync+F5 → SIM test → iterate until SIM PASS.
  • Full pipeline trigger: only when a defect’s SIM test returns PASS. No pipeline before SIM PASS. Ever.
  • Architectural change: if a fix requires a new method, type, or cross-file refactor → full pipeline regardless of SIM state.
  • Single-clause or single-line fix: direct repair always. No pipeline needed unless SIM also passes.
Session Structure — V3.0 (every session, always in this order)
STEP 0 Rules Catalog Gate — read RULES_CATALOG.md lines 1-30, state GATE PASS or BLOCKED. Mandatory, never skippable.
STEP 1 Read $continue prompt. Parse: active task ID, last commit, test results (PASS / FAIL / OBS). If results are PASS → go to STEP 5 (close + pipeline). If results are FAIL/OBS/none → go to STEP 2.
STEP 2 Diagnose. Read the relevant source files and log output. Confirm root cause before touching any code. State the root cause explicitly.
STEP 3 Direct repair. Apply the minimal src edit. Update the DW card in the spec (add fix design). Run powershell -File scripts\ptt-sync-and-verify.ps1 — must be 0 MISMATCH. Instruct Director to press F5 in NT8.
STEP 4 Output test request + $continue prompt together. End session. The test request states exactly what to test and what to look for in the NT8 output. The pre-written $continue prompt includes task ID, commit, and a placeholder for results. Director pastes both into their workflow — tests, then pastes $continue + results into a new session.
STEP 5 (SIM PASS path only) Update spec: close DW item, update status to CONFIRMED FIXED. Commit: git add -f specs/ src/PropTraderTools/CopyEngine.cs; git commit -m "fix(ptt): DW-{ID} {summary}"
STEP 6 (SIM PASS path only) Launch full PTT pipeline via ptt-orchestrator. Output the ptt-orchestrator prompt (all 5 phases verbatim). Output next $continue prompt referencing the pipeline output.
$continue Prompt Format (canonical)
$continue — PTT Copier Defect Loop (4-Task Sequential)

CURRENT TASK: [{N}] {DW-ID}
LAST COMMIT:  {sha}  {commit-label}
STATUS:       {one-line summary of what was fixed and what to test}

TEST RESULTS: {PASS | FAIL | OBS | PENDING}
{paste NT8 log output here if FAIL or OBS}
